# TortalPortal Lite — full option catalog (PRE-VERIFICATION)

12 research reports, 8 design domains, 177 options.

> These are the design agents' own feasibility/enforcement marks.
> The adversarial verification pass has NOT run. Treat every mark as a claim.


---

## 1. Simple Pair (vanilla baseline)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

Two portals sharing one byte-identical tag, each holding the other's ZDOID — the only shape vanilla itself builds.

**How it works.** Encoding: two portal ZDOs P and Q. `P.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, T)` and `Q.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, T)` where T is the same ordinal string (ZDOVars.s_tag = "tag".GetStableHashCode(), assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78617). Then `P.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, Q.m_uid)` and the mirror on Q (ZDO.SetConnection :73656-73666). Server-side write recipe, copied from Game.SetConnection :100637-100651: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(Portal, target); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);` — do this for both ends. ZDO.SetConnection already calls IncreaseDataRevision() and ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() (:73661-73664), so the portal chunk file is flagged for save. A bare tag write does NOT set that flag, so a tag-only change needs an explicit `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702).

Vanilla reconciliation (Game.ConnectPortals :100589-100626, verified body): pass 1 iterates ZDOMan.GetPortalList() and clears any connection whose target ZDO is null, whose target's s_tag string differs, or whose target's own Portal connection is ZDOID.None. A mutual pair passes all three. Pass 2 only touches portals whose connection IsNone(). So a correct pair is a fixed point — the 5 s coroutine (:100580-100587, started only under `if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` at :100074) confirms and re-confirms it forever at zero cost, because ZDOExtraData.SetConnection early-returns false when type+target are unchanged so no DataRevision bump and no network traffic.

You do not need to own the ZDO to write it (no ZDO setter checks ownership) but you should claim it to win the revision race against the owning client, and expect ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926, every 2 s) to hand ownership back to any peer within ~96 m.

**Player experience.** Player walks up to a portal; hover reads `Teleport tag:"forest" [$piece_portal_connected]` (TeleportWorld.GetHoverText :143453-143464) and the mesh glows because UpdatePortal's 0.5 s InvokeRepeating lights m_connected/m_target_found (:143491-143509). Walking into the collider fires TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143672-143681), Teleport() re-reads the connection ZDOID live (:143539), computes `targetPos + targetRot*forward*1.0 + up*1.0` (:143542-143545) and calls TeleportTo(distantTeleport:true). Black screen with the swirl for a minimum of 8 s (Player.UpdateTeleport :15349), then they stand 1 m in front of the far portal facing the same way the far portal faces. Walking straight back in returns them — but only after ~2 s of m_teleportCooldown, and only if they step OUT of the destination trigger first, because OnTriggerEnter is enter-only.

**Failure modes.**
- If one member is destroyed, the survivor holds a dangling ZDOID until the next 5 s pass; ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO (:76963-77000) does not touch the partner. During that window TargetFound() returns false and the player gets a silent no-op (Teleport returns at :143519 with no message).
- Three or more portals sharing one tag: floor(N/2) pairs form and exactly one member is permanently orphaned. It never rotates in, because the surviving pairs keep re-confirming themselves in pass 1 and pass 2 only touches IsNone() portals. Which one is stranded depends on Dictionary bucket order in m_portalObjects and is not stable across restarts.
- Every untagged portal in the world shares the default tag "" (ZDO.GetString defaultValue is "", never null), so a freshly placed unnamed portal auto-pairs with a random unnamed portal anywhere on the map.
- Tag equality is bare C# `string !=` (:100601, :100611) — ordinal, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant. "Base", "base" and "Base " are three separate networks with no diagnostic anywhere.

**Citations.** Game.ConnectPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589-100626 · Game.SetConnection — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100637-100651 · Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100580-100587 (started at Game.Start :100074) · ZDO.SetConnection — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73656-73666 · ZDOVars.s_tag — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78617 · TeleportWorld.Teleport — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143517-143549 · TeleportWorld.GetHoverText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143464 · ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702

**Open questions.**
- Which prefabs are in Game.m_portalPrefabs / PortalPrefabHash (:99828, :100021)? Inspector data. In-game: log ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)?.name for every entry at Game.Start postfix on the dedicated server.

## 2. Fan-In Star (many spokes → one hub)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small-medium

N spoke portals all point at a single hub; the hub points back at exactly one designated return. Fully stable under pure vanilla with no Harmony patch and no re-write tick.

**How it works.** This is the headline result of the whole catalogue: vanilla's reconciler never checks reciprocity, so a non-reciprocal star is a fixed point.

Encoding. Choose one tag string T. Write `s_tag = T` on the hub H and on every spoke S1..SN. Then, for each spoke: claim + `Si.SetConnection(Portal, H.m_uid)` + ForceSendZDO. For the hub: `H.SetConnection(Portal, Sr.m_uid)` for one chosen return spoke Sr (or an anchor, see the Anchor-Terminated option). Ordering matters only in that every member must end the write batch with a non-None connection before the next 5 s tick.

Why pass 1 leaves it alone (verified at :100594-100606): for spoke Si the test is `zDO == null || zDO.tag != T || zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None` evaluated against H. H exists, H.tag == T, H.connection == Sr ≠ None. All three fail → no teardown. For H the same test against Sr: Sr exists, tag matches, Sr.connection == H ≠ None. No teardown. There is deliberately NO check that the target points back (compare ZDOMan.ConvertPortals :77832, the legacy migration, which DID require `A.target == B && B.target == A`). Pass 2 (:100607-100622) skips every portal whose connection is not IsNone(), so nothing is re-paired. The star survives indefinitely with vanilla's own coroutine actively re-validating it.

Cost per tick: zero. The mod does not need a faster timer, does not need to patch anything, and does not race the server's own 5 s pass. It only needs to re-assert after a member is destroyed or after a world reload (see failure modes).

Scale limit: none from the connection layer. The practical limit is that every spoke must carry the identical tag string, so all N+1 portals show the same name on hover.

**Player experience.** Twelve outpost portals scattered across the Black Forest and Swamp all read `tag:"hub"`. A player at the Swamp outpost walks in, sits through the 8 s loading swirl, and steps out 1 m in front of the great hall portal at the base — the same destination every time, from every outpost. There is no ambiguity and no random shuffling: the twelfth outpost built yesterday goes to the same hall as the first. Walking into the hall portal sends them to whichever spoke the admin designated as the return (say, the Swamp outpost), which is why in practice the hub is paired with a Switchboard so the return is the spoke you last came from. All twelve outpost portals and the hall portal glow and read `[$piece_portal_connected]`, so nothing looks unusual.

**Failure modes.**
- Destroying the hub H strands every spoke: on the next ≤5 s pass every spoke's target resolves to null and pass 1 nulls all N connections, then pass 2 randomly pairs the spokes with each other inside tag T. A 12-spoke network instantly becomes 6 random pairs. The mod must subscribe to ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed (public Action<ZDO>, :76033, invoked :76975) and re-provision or re-scramble the tag immediately.
- Destroying the designated return spoke Sr nulls only H's outbound; pass 2 then pairs H with any other unconnected same-tag portal, silently hijacking the star's exit. Mitigate by pointing H at an Anchor instead of a real portal.
- A player retagging any spoke removes it from group T; its own connection is cleared by TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag (:143595) and it is re-paired inside its new tag group. Detect by polling s_tag on ZDOMan.GetPortalList(), or by prefixing ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC/RouteRPC on the "RPC_SetTag" method hash — but note a client that OWNS the portal ZDO executes RPC_SetTag purely locally and no packet reaches the server (ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC :83588 skips RouteRPC when targetPeerID == m_id), so polling is mandatory and interception is only a bonus.
- World reload collapses the star. See the reload note in prerequisites/openQuestions and the Directed Ring entry for the mechanism.

**Prerequisites.** A load-time re-assert pass, because the disk format cannot express a star (ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData :75461-75478 gives each ZDO exactly one hash slot; after reload ZDOMan.ConnectPortals :77850-77893 re-links surviving hash pairs reciprocally and Game.instance.ConnectPortals :76523 randomly pairs the rest). Re-write the star in a postfix on Game.ConnectPortals or right after OnWorldReady.

**Citations.** Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 predicate — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100600-100604 (no reciprocity check) · Game.ConnectPortals pass 2 guard — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100609 · ZDOMan.ConvertPortals (legacy reciprocal check, for contrast) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77832 · ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76033, invoked :76975 · ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC local-dispatch shortcut — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83588-83594 · TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag clears own connection — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143595

**Open questions.**
- Does a client standing at a spoke pick up a server-side connection rewrite without a zone reload? Teleport() re-reads the ZDO at transit (:143539) so logically yes, but TargetFound() (:143640) also needs that client to actually hold the hub ZDO. In-game: rewrite a spoke's target to a portal in an unvisited region and see whether the first walk-through silently fails (gate 1 returns with no message) and the second succeeds.

## 3. Fan-Out Star (one hub → many simultaneously) — RULED OUT

`RULED-OUT` · `NOT-ENFORCEABLE` · effort: small

A single portal cannot hold more than one destination; the connection slot is one readonly ZDOID.

**How it works.** Structural impossibility, not an unimplemented feature. `ZDOExtraData.s_connections` is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` — one value per ZDO — and `class ZDOConnection` declares exactly `public readonly ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType m_type;` and `public readonly ZDOID m_target = ZDOID.None;` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75524-75534). There is no list, no array, no per-type slot. `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection(zid, type, target)` (:74951-74961) overwrites that single entry.

Consequences that are easy to get wrong:
- A ZDO holding a Portal connection can never simultaneously hold a SyncTransform connection, so a portal cannot be parented to a moving object while also being routed.
- `ConnectionType` is `[Flags] { None=0, Portal=1, SyncTransform=2, Spawned=3, Target=0x10 }` (:74747-74755) — Portal/SyncTransform/Spawned are overlapping small integers, not independent bits. Only `Target` is a real flag. So you cannot OR two route types into one slot to fake two destinations.
- Writing `Portal|Target` (0x11) onto a live portal does NOT create a second slot; `ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID` requires exact type equality (:75094-75102), so `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` returns None and vanilla will treat that portal as unconnected and re-pair it in pass 2.
- TeleportWorld.Teleport reads exactly one ZDOID (:143539) with no fallback, no list, and no selection UI.

Everything the assignment calls "fan-out" must therefore be realised as one of: a **Portal Bank** (N physical portals at the hub, one destination each), a **Switchboard** (one portal, repointed between transits), or a **Carousel** (one portal, repointed on a timer). A true simultaneous one-to-many is unreachable by any ZDO write, and would require a client mod to present a destination picker — which is exactly what full TortalPortal's PortalUIManager does client-side.

**Player experience.** Nothing to experience — this shape cannot be built. The nearest server-only substitutes are: a room of six portals each labelled for a different biome (Portal Bank), or one portal in the middle of the room whose destination the player changes with an emote before stepping in (Switchboard).

**Failure modes.**
- A mod that writes a second connection onto the hub silently overwrites the first with no error, because SetConnection returns true and bumps the revision — the previous destination is simply gone.
- A mod that writes Portal|Target to try to stash a second route makes the portal read as unconnected to every client (HaveTarget :143631 and TargetFound :143640 both query bare Portal), and vanilla's pass 2 will then randomly re-pair it inside its tag group.

**Citations.** class ZDOConnection (single readonly target) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75524-75534 · ZDOExtraData.s_connections Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection> — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74794-74797 · ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74747-74755 · ZDOExtraData.SetConnection (overwrites) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74951-74961 · ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID exact-type match — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75094-75102 · TeleportWorld.Teleport single-ZDOID read — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143539

## 4. Directed Ring / Cycle

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small-medium

A→B→C→…→A, every member on one tag; one-way circular travel that vanilla's reconciler accepts indefinitely.

**How it works.** Encoding. N portals P0..P(N-1), all with `s_tag = T`. For each i: claim ownership, `Pi.SetConnection(Portal, P((i+1) % N).m_uid)`, ForceSendZDO. N single writes, no reciprocals.

Stability. Pass 1's predicate for Pi is evaluated against P(i+1): non-null ✓, tag == T ✓, `P(i+1).GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != ZDOID.None` ✓ (it points at P(i+2)). Every edge survives. Pass 2 finds nothing IsNone(). The ring is a fixed point of vanilla's own 5 s reconciler (:100594-100622). This is the direct consequence of the missing reciprocity check and it holds for any N ≥ 2 — note N = 2 collapses to the ordinary pair, and N = 1 becomes the Self-Loop.

Ordering under a live server. Write the whole ring in one batch inside one frame. If you write only some edges and a 5 s tick lands mid-batch, the not-yet-written members read IsNone() and pass 2 will randomly pair them inside T, after which your remaining writes are fighting an already-formed pair (which you can simply overwrite — SetConnection is unconditional). Safest is a prefix on `Game.ConnectPortals` that returns false while a managed rewrite is in flight, or just doing the batch synchronously.

Ownership. Each write must be preceded by `SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` for a durable result; ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) runs every 2 s and gives ownership of any portal within a peer's active area back to that peer, so the mod either re-claims on each write or installs the Wonderland `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix guard (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313) keyed on portal prefab hash.

Do NOT reposition ring members: `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752-73756) so a moved portal stays filed under its creation-time sector in m_portalObjects and HandleDestroyedZDO (:76980) will fail to remove it, leaking a dead ZDO into GetPortalList() forever.

**Player experience.** Five portals named `tag:"caravan"` at Meadows/Black Forest/Swamp/Mountain/Plains outposts. A player at the Meadows portal walks in and arrives at the Black Forest one. To get back to Meadows they must go all the way round: Black Forest → Swamp → Mountain → Plains → Meadows, four more 8 s loading screens and four deliberate walk-ins (after arrival the destination portal's trigger has already been entered, so they must step out and back in, and the 2 s m_teleportCooldown must elapse — Player.TeleportTo :15315). Every portal hovers as connected and glows normally; nothing in the vanilla UI hints that the link is one-way. Players discover the direction by experiment, which is either the whole point (a pilgrimage route, a raid ingress) or a support ticket.

**Failure modes.**
- Destroying any one member breaks the ring into a chain, and a chain is unstable: the node whose target vanished has its connection nulled by pass 1, and the node pointing AT that node then sees `target.connection == None` and is also nulled by pass 1 on the following tick. The damage propagates backwards one hop per 5 s until pass 2 randomly re-pairs whatever is left. A 7-node ring degrades to random pairs within ~30 s of one portal being demolished.
- World reload destroys rings >2. ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478, read directly) writes `s_connectionsHashData[source] = {Portal, h}` then `s_connectionsHashData[target] = {Portal|Target, h}`, one slot per ZDO, iterating s_connections in dictionary order — each later edge overwrites the previous entry for a shared node. For A→B→C→A you end with A={Portal|Target,h3}, B={Portal,h2}, C={Portal,h3}. On load ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893) matches C↔A by h3 and writes both directions reciprocally, and B has no matching Target so it is left unconnected and Game.instance.ConnectPortals (:76523) pairs it at random. Net: one bidirectional pair plus one wanderer.
- Mod uninstalled: whatever configuration survived the last save is re-linked reciprocally at load and then the vanilla 5 s pass leaves it alone. The ring does not come back; the world settles into ordinary pairs plus one orphan if N is odd.

**Prerequisites.** A world-load re-assert (postfix on Game.ConnectPortals, or a one-shot at OnWorldReady after ZDOMan.LoadChunks has run) — mandatory, not optional.

**Citations.** Game.ConnectPortals pass 1/pass 2 (verified body) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589-100626 · ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75461-75478 · ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (load-time hash relink, writes BOTH directions) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77879-77885 · ZDOMan.LoadChunks ordering — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76515 and :76523, DirtyPortalObjects=false at :76527 · ZDO.SetSector portal exemption — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73752-73756 · ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76901-76926

**Open questions.**
- Exact enumeration order of s_connections during RegenerateConnectionHashData determines WHICH pair survives a reload. It is a BinarySearchDictionary/Dictionary order, effectively arbitrary. In-game: build a 3-ring, save, restart, and log which two nodes came back paired — then just re-assert unconditionally rather than trying to predict it.

## 5. Bidirectional Ring — RULED OUT (twin counter-rotating rings are the substitute)

`RULED-OUT` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

A node cannot hold both a clockwise and an anticlockwise neighbour; two portals per station is the only way to get a two-way loop.

**How it works.** A truly bidirectional ring needs each node to store two targets. It cannot: one ZDOConnection per ZDO (:75524-75534). Any second write overwrites the first.

Substitute — twin counter-rotating rings. Place TWO portals at each station, on two different tags. Station i gets portal Ci on tag `T_cw` and portal Ai on tag `T_ccw`. Write `Ci.SetConnection(Portal, C((i+1)%N).m_uid)` for the clockwise ring and `Ai.SetConnection(Portal, A((i-1+N)%N).m_uid)` for the anticlockwise ring. Both rings are independently stable for the same reason a single Directed Ring is: within each tag group every target is non-null, tag-matched and itself non-None.

Cost: 2N portals for N stations, and 2N ZDO writes per re-assert. Both rings must be re-asserted after a world reload for the same RegenerateConnectionHashData reason.

Degenerate case worth knowing: with N = 2 the twin rings collapse to two ordinary pairs between the same two stations, which is exactly what two vanilla portal pairs on two tags already give you — no mod needed.

A cheaper approximation with N+1 portals: build one Directed Ring plus a single Switchboard portal at each station that the player repoints to "previous station" on demand. That gets two-way travel with 2N portals anyway, so the twin ring is usually simpler.

Note that the two tags must be genuinely distinct strings or vanilla will merge the two rings into one 2N-member tag group and the reconciler will happily keep whatever edges you wrote (it does not care about cycles) — but any member that ever loses its connection will be re-paired across the ring boundary by pass 2's random pick (Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664-100679).

**Player experience.** At each of five outposts there is a pair of portals a few metres apart, one signed `caravan-e` and one signed `caravan-w`. Stepping into the east one takes you one stop clockwise; the west one takes you one stop anticlockwise. Both glow, both hover as connected. Players learn the convention from the tags, and a wrong choice costs one extra 8 s hop rather than a four-hop detour.

**Failure modes.**
- Demolishing one portal of a twin breaks only that ring's direction at that station, and the break propagates backwards one hop per 5 s exactly as in the single ring.
- A player retagging `caravan-w` to `caravan-e` merges the two groups; the retagged portal's connection is cleared by RPC_SetTag (:143595) and pass 2 can pair it with any unconnected clockwise member, producing a bridge between the two rings that will look like a routing bug.

**Prerequisites.** Directed Ring

**Citations.** class ZDOConnection single readonly target — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75524-75534 · Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100664-100679 · TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag clears own connection on retag — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143595-143597

## 6. Open Chain / Relay with a Terminator

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

A→B→C→…→Z as a one-way relay; the last hop MUST terminate in a self-loop, an anchor, or a wrap to the head, or vanilla unravels the whole chain backwards.

**How it works.** Encoding. Chain members P0..Pn all on tag T. `Pi.SetConnection(Portal, P(i+1).m_uid)` for i < n. The tail Pn is the whole problem.

Why a naive chain unravels. If Pn's connection is ZDOID.None, pass 1 evaluating P(n-1) hits the third clause `zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None` and nulls P(n-1) (:100601-100604). On the next tick P(n-2) sees P(n-1) as None and is nulled. The chain dissolves from the tail backwards at one hop per 5 s, and pass 2 randomly re-pairs the freed members inside T. This is the single most common way a hand-built topology quietly turns into vanilla soup.

Three legal terminators:
1. **Self-loop**: `Pn.SetConnection(Portal, Pn.m_uid)`. Pass 1 on Pn resolves the target to itself — non-null, tag equals its own tag, connection non-None — so it survives. Runtime-stable, but erased by every save (RegenerateConnectionHashData writes `hashData[Pn]={Portal,h}` and then immediately overwrites it with `{Portal|Target,h}` because m_target != None, :75472-75475, leaving a Target with no source), so re-assert at load.
2. **Wrap to head**: `Pn.SetConnection(Portal, P0.m_uid)` — this is exactly the Directed Ring and is the most robust choice.
3. **Anchor**: point Pn at a non-portal ZDO carrying the same tag and a non-None connection (see the Anchor-Terminated One-Way option). Best of the three: the anchor is never iterated by ConnectPortals because it is not in m_portalObjects, so it can never be torn down or re-paired.

All writes take the standard claim/write/force-send triad. Batch the whole chain in one frame.

**Player experience.** A five-stage descent into the Mistlands: portals tagged `descent` at (1420,-3310), (1980,-3720), (2510,-4060), (2990,-4380) and a final one at the Queen's approach (3310,-4610). The player steps into stage 1, black screen, arrives 1 m in front of stage 2, steps out of the volume, turns around, steps back in, black screen, stage 3. Each hop costs about 10 s of real time (8 s minimum distant-teleport hold plus the 2 s cooldown before the next TeleportTo is accepted, Player.UpdateTeleport :15349 and Player.TeleportTo :15315). There is no way back up the chain — walking into stage 3 sends them to stage 4, not stage 2. The final portal loops onto itself, so stepping into it after arriving gives an 8 s black screen and deposits them back where they were standing: a deliberate dead end.

**Failure modes.**
- Forgetting the terminator: silent, delayed, total. The chain looks correct for 5 s and then dissolves backwards over the following 5n seconds.
- A destroyed mid-chain member splits the chain and the upstream half unravels; the downstream half survives if its own terminator is intact.
- Arrival lands the player 1 m in front of the next portal, potentially INSIDE that portal's trigger volume. Because OnTriggerEnter is enter-only (:143672-143681) and m_teleportCooldown gates re-entry for 2 s, they do not bounce — but any design that widens the trigger or shortens the cooldown would produce an infinite relay. Do not attempt to shorten either; m_exitDistance is a compiled Inspector field with no ZDO backing (:143413).
- World reload: hash-pair matching recovers at most one bidirectional pair out of the chain and randomly re-pairs the rest.

**Prerequisites.** One of: Self-Loop Dead End, Anchor-Terminated One-Way, or Directed Ring

**Citations.** Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 third clause (target connection None) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100601 · ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData self-loop overwrite — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75472-75475 · Player.TeleportTo 2 s cooldown — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15302-15327 · Player.UpdateTeleport 8 s distant-teleport floor — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15349 · TeleportWorld.m_exitDistance (compiled Inspector field) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143413 · TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (enter-only) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143672-143681

## 7. Self-Loop Dead End & Paired Decoy

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

A portal pointing at its own ZDOID: reads as connected, glows, and teleports the player back to where they already stood.

**How it works.** Encoding. One write: `P.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); P.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, P.m_uid); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(P.m_uid);`

Why vanilla keeps it. Pass 1 resolves the target ZDOID to P itself: `zDO == null` false, `zDO.GetString(s_tag) != @string` false (a string is equal to itself), `zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None` false. All three clauses fail, so no teardown (:100600-100604). Pass 2 skips it because its connection is not IsNone() (:100609). A self-loop is a stable runtime fixed point.

What the client does with it. HaveTarget() is `connection != ZDOID.None` → true, so the hover reads `[$piece_portal_connected]` and Update() lerps the emission colour to m_colorTargetfound (:143511-143515). TargetFound() resolves GetZDO(P) → non-null → true, so m_target_found lights whenever a teleportable player is within m_activationRange. On transit, Teleport() reads P's own position and rotation and moves the player to `P.pos + P.rot*forward*1.0 + up*1.0` (:143542-143545) — roughly where they were already standing — via a full distantTeleport, so they eat the 8 s black screen for nothing.

Paired decoy layout. Build a room of, say, six identical portals all carrying the same visible tag. Five of them are self-loops; one is the real edge into the network. Since s_tag, the glow, and the hover string are identical across all six, a vanilla client has no way to tell them apart short of walking in. Note the six must NOT share a tag with anything else you care about, or a destroyed decoy would free a slot that pass 2 fills from the real network.

Alternative decoy that is less punishing: point the decoys at a nearby Anchor two metres behind the portal, so the player is "teleported" to the far side of the room rather than into their own footprint.

**Player experience.** Six identical black-marble portals in a vaulted hall, every one hovering `tag:"vault" [$piece_portal_connected]` and pulsing with the connected emission. The player picks one, walks in, gets the full swirl and black screen for eight seconds, and fades back in standing one metre in front of the same portal in the same hall. No message, no error, nothing in the log they can see. They try another. On the fourth try the screen fades in over the Mountains. This is a genuine puzzle/toll mechanic that a 100% vanilla client renders correctly and cannot short-circuit — the destination is only read at the instant of transit.

**Failure modes.**
- Erased by every world save. RegenerateConnectionHashData writes the source slot for P then immediately overwrites it with the Target slot because m_target != None (:75472-75475), leaving a Target hash with no matching source. On load, ZDOMan.ConnectPortals finds no pair and Game.instance.ConnectPortals then re-pairs P at random inside its tag group. MUST be re-asserted at world load.
- If the self-looped portal is the only member of its tag group it is left permanently unconnected after a reload (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal returns null for an empty candidate list, :100674-100678) — which is actually a safe failure, just not a self-loop.
- Players may report it as a bug ('the portal ate my eight seconds'). If the decoy room is not signposted in-fiction it reads as a broken server.
- Using self-loops as hub terminators leaves the hub's exit pointing at the hub — walk into the hub and you stay at the hub. Usually you want an Anchor instead.

## 8. Anchor-Terminated One-Way / Dead Drop

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Point a portal at a fabricated non-portal ZDO: an arrival point with no portal at it, permanently invisible to vanilla's reconciler.

**How it works.** This is the strongest primitive in the whole catalogue, because the anchor is never iterated by Game.ConnectPortals.

Create the anchor. `ZDO a = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, hash);` where `hash` is a NON-portal prefab hash (something harmless and persistent). CreateNewZDO (:76674-76692) allocates the ZDOID, sets owner to the server session and calls AddIfPortal(zdo, hash) — which returns immediately because the hash is not in Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash (:77734), so the anchor goes into the ordinary sector array, not m_portalObjects. Then replicate ZNetView.Awake's fabrication block yourself (:82613-82620), all five lines: `a.Persistent = true; a.Type = ZDO.ObjectType.Default; a.Distant = false; a.SetPrefab(hash); a.SetRotation(facing);` — omit SetPrefab and m_prefab stays 0, the client's CreateObject returns null and the server destroys it as invalid; omit Persistent and AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) skips it and it is gone on restart.

Make it a legal target. Pass 1 evaluates the PORTAL, not the anchor, so you need the anchor to satisfy the portal's three clauses: `a.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, T)` matching the portal's tag, and `a.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, a.m_uid)` (a self-loop on the anchor) so that `a.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != ZDOID.None`. The anchor's own self-loop is never evaluated by anything, because the anchor is not in GetPortalList(). Then `P.SetConnection(Portal, a.m_uid)` and ForceSendZDO both.

Why the client accepts it. TeleportWorld.Teleport does `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connection)` and reads only GetPosition() and GetRotation() (:143539-143545). There is no prefab validation anywhere on that path. TargetFound() only needs GetZDO != null, and if the client lacks the anchor it calls RequestZDO and the server force-sends it (:143646-143654, ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO :77689-77692).

The anchor's rotation is the arrival facing and its +forward is the 1 m push direction.

**Player experience.** A portal in the Mistlands outpost tagged `drop` glows and reads connected. A player steps in, black screen, and fades in on a stone shelf at (4180, 62, -5220) in the Ashlands — an open ledge with no portal on it, no way back, and nothing to interact with. The only way home is to walk, sail, or die. A second player at the same outpost portal gets the identical one-way delivery. Because there is no portal at the destination, there is no glow, no hover text, and no ambiguity — the endpoint simply is not a portal.

**Failure modes.**
- The anchor must stay alive in ZDOMan or the link dies at the next SAVE, not just at runtime: RegenerateConnectionHashData only persists a connection when BOTH endpoint ZDOs resolve in m_objectsByID (:75468). Give the anchor Persistent = true and never destroy it.
- At world load ZDOMan.ConnectPortals re-links the hash pair RECIPROCALLY (:77879-77885), so the anchor comes back pointing at the portal instead of at itself. That is harmless in play (nobody can walk into an anchor) but it means the anchor's self-loop must be re-asserted if you rely on it as a terminator for other members.
- Never use a portal prefab hash for the anchor. AddIfPortal would register it in m_portalObjects (:77732-77750) and vanilla would iterate it, tear down its self-loop when the hash data goes stale, and re-pair it.
- The client will try to instantiate the anchor prefab when the player's active area covers it. Choose a prefab that is cheap, silent and harmless.
- ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex clamps any zone beyond roughly ±16320 m to Sector 0 (:115755-115774), the same bucket the server's pinned reference position maps to. Do not place anchors out there.

- Does a vanilla client cleanly handle a portal whose destination ZDO has a prefab it must instantiate (an anchor)? Teleport only reads pos/rot, but ZNetScene will still CreateObject for that ZDO when in range. In-game: try an anchor with a harmless real prefab (a marker piece) versus an unregistered hash and watch the client log for CreateObject failures.
- Is there a prefab in ZNetScene whose instantiation is a genuine no-op on the client? In-game: dump ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefabNames() on the server and pick one.

## 9. Directed In-Tree (local → regional → world hub)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

A tiered fan-in: every leaf points at its local hub, every local hub at its regional hub, the regional hubs at the world hub. Travel is inward only; outward needs banks.

**How it works.** Encoding. One tag T for the entire tree — every node from leaf to root must carry the identical s_tag string, because pass 1 tears down any edge whose two ends disagree (:100601). Write one edge per node: `leaf.SetConnection(Portal, localHub.m_uid)`, `localHub.SetConnection(Portal, regionalHub.m_uid)`, `regionalHub.SetConnection(Portal, worldHub.m_uid)`, and finally `worldHub.SetConnection(Portal, <anchor or designated return>)`.

Stability. Identical argument to the Fan-In Star, applied recursively: each node's target is non-null, tag-matched and itself non-None. Every internal edge survives pass 1 and pass 2 never fires. The only node that needs care is the ROOT, whose own connection must be non-None or the entire tree unravels level by level at one level per 5 s.

The crucial asymmetry. A tree edge in a graph is undirected; a portal edge is not. Because a ZDO holds one ZDOID, a hub CANNOT simultaneously point at its children. So the "tree" you can build is strictly an in-tree — all arrows toward the root. Travel is one hop per walk-in: leaf → local hub (8 s), then walk into a DIFFERENT portal at the local hub to continue. If the local hub portal itself points at the regional hub, walking into the same portal you arrived at continues inward. That produces a genuinely nice "express line" feel: keep stepping into the portal in front of you and you ratchet inward to the world hub.

Outward travel requires a Portal Bank at each hub: at the world hub, one portal per regional hub; at each regional hub, one portal per local hub; at each local hub, one portal per leaf. Those bank portals need their own tags (one tag per bank slot, paired with an anchor or with a dedicated arrival portal at the child site). Total portal count for a 3-tier tree with branching factor b: inward edges N, outward bank portals N, so 2N.

Tick rate: none. Write once, re-assert on member destruction and on world load.

**Player experience.** A player at a Plains farmstead walks into the farmstead portal (`tag:"realm"`). Eight seconds later they are at the Plains regional waystation, standing in front of the portal they arrived from. They step out, step back in, and eight seconds later they are in the world hub's arrival hall. Total: two walk-ins, ~20 s, and they have crossed the map. To go home they cross the hall to the departures colonnade — twelve portals, one per waystation, each signed with its region — step into `realm-plains`, arrive at the Plains waystation departures rack, step into `realm-plains-farm`, and they are home. Inbound is one express line with no choices; outbound is a wayfinding exercise through two labelled racks.

**Failure modes.**
- The root's connection is the single point of failure for the whole tree. Point it at an Anchor, never at a player-destructible portal.
- All nodes share one tag string, so a player retagging any single portal removes it from the tree; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag also clears that portal's own connection (:143595), and the node that pointed AT it is then torn down by pass 1 on the next tick. A tiered network needs a tag-normalisation tick (re-assert s_tag on every managed portal) or the Displaced Routing option.
- Because every tier shares one tag, hover text is identical everywhere. Players cannot tell a leaf from the world hub without external signage. Signs (ZDOVars.s_text, server-writable) are the practical mitigation.
- World reload flattens the whole tree into pairs. Mandatory re-assert.

**Prerequisites.** Fan-In Star; Portal Bank / Departures Hall; Anchor-Terminated One-Way (for the root terminator)

## 10. Nested / Layered Airlock (vestibule pattern)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

An outer portal drops you into a sealed vestibule containing the real network's portals; the vestibule is the only ingress and the mod controls what is inside it.

**How it works.** Encoding is a composition of two independent tag groups that never touch.

Outer layer: portals O1..On out in the world, all on tag `T_out`, each written `Oi.SetConnection(Portal, V_in.m_uid)` where V_in is a single arrival portal inside the vestibule room. V_in carries `s_tag = T_out` and points at an Anchor placed at the vestibule floor (so V_in satisfies pass 1 and stepping into V_in is a no-op that dumps you back in the vestibule). This is a Fan-In Star with an anchor terminator, and it is vanilla-stable.

Inner layer: inside the vestibule, a Portal Bank B1..Bm on tags `T_in_1`..`T_in_m`, each paired with a remote portal at the corresponding destination. These are ordinary pairs — vanilla maintains them for free.

The nesting property is that the two layers share no tag, so vanilla's reconciler can never bridge them: FindRandomUnconnectedPortal only considers candidates whose s_tag is string-equal to the orphan's (:100669). An outer portal that loses its connection can only be re-paired with another outer portal, never with an inner one. That containment is the whole point — it is the closest thing the ZDO layer offers to an access-control boundary.

Deeper nesting is just recursion: the vestibule's bank leads to sub-vestibules, each with its own tag namespace. Depth is unbounded; cost is one physical portal per edge.

The mod's leverage inside the vestibule: it can null a bank portal's connection to close a wing (`Bk.SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)`), but must also break Bk's tag or pass 2 re-pairs it within 5 s — see Tag-Scramble Lockdown. Alternatively repoint Bk at a jail Anchor (Black-Hole Sink) which is stable and needs no tag surgery.

**Player experience.** Every outpost portal in the realm is signed `gate`. They all lead to one round stone chamber lit by four braziers, with no exit door and a single portal on the far wall (also `gate`) that does nothing useful if you step into it. Ringing the chamber are eight portals: `gate-mead`, `gate-forest`, `gate-swamp`, `gate-mtn`, `gate-plains`, `gate-mist`, `gate-ash`, `gate-deep`. A player from the Swamp outpost arrives in the chamber, reads the ring, steps into `gate-mtn`, and eight seconds later is at the Mountain waystation. When the admin closes the Ashlands during an event, `gate-ash` stops glowing and hovers `[$piece_portal_unconnected]` — visibly shut, not mysteriously broken.

**Failure modes.**
- A player building their OWN portal and naming it `gate` joins the outer star's tag group; if its connection is None, pass 2 will pair it with… nothing, because every legitimate outer member already has a non-None connection. It sits unconnected. But if the mod's re-assert tick blindly enumerates tag `gate` it may adopt the intruder. Filter managed membership by a mod-private ZDO key or by position, not by tag alone.
- Destroying V_in strands the whole outer star (all N outer portals get nulled, then randomly re-paired with each other, producing an outpost-to-outpost mesh nobody designed). Protect V_in: it should be out of reach, and the mod should re-provision it from ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed.
- The vestibule is not a security boundary against a modified client — a hacked client can invoke Game's routed `RPC_SetConnection` (registered on every peer at Game.Start :100066-100070, handler :100653-100662, zero sender validation) and rewire any portal to any ZDO. Server-side detection is a per-tick connection audit.

**Prerequisites.** Fan-In Star; Portal Bank / Departures Hall; Anchor-Terminated One-Way

## 11. Portal Bank / Departures Hall (the mesh approximation)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

N physical portals side by side, each a plain vanilla pair to a different fixed destination — the only way to give one place many exits.

**How it works.** Encoding is deliberately boring: N ordinary pairs. Bank slot k gets `s_tag = T_k` (a distinct string per slot) and its remote twin gets the same T_k; write the mutual connection on each pair or simply let vanilla's pass 2 form it (two same-tag unconnected portals pair on the next 5 s tick with no mod involvement at all).

What the mod adds over doing nothing: (a) provisioning — CreateNewZDO a portal-prefab ZDO at a surveyed coordinate with the five ZNetView.Awake lines (:82613-82620) so admins do not have to hand-place; (b) tag ownership — re-asserting T_k every tick so a player cannot retag a bank slot and hijack it; (c) labelling — writing adjacent Sign ZDOs' s_tag/s_text; (d) detecting a slot's twin being destroyed and repointing that slot at a "temporarily closed" Anchor instead of letting vanilla pair it with something random.

Bank as a mesh approximation. A full mesh over S sites needs every site to reach every other. With banks that is S×(S−1) portals total (each site holds S−1 outbound slots) — quadratic but perfectly stable and entirely vanilla. A hub-and-bank hybrid is linear: each site gets ONE outbound portal into a Fan-In Star at the hub, and the hub holds one bank slot per site for the return. Total 2S portals for full any-to-any reachability in two hops. That hybrid is the recommended real-world shape.

Do NOT try to save portals by giving two bank slots the same tag: three same-tag portals strand one permanently, and four form two pairs by dictionary-bucket order that is not stable across restarts.

**Player experience.** A long timber colonnade behind the great hall with fourteen portals in a row, each with a rune sign above it: Haldor, Bonemass, the Elder, Moder's altar, the north dock, the iron mine, the copper camp, and so on. Every portal glows and hovers with its own distinct tag. The player walks the line, reads the signs, picks `hall-haldor`, steps in, and eight seconds later is standing at the trader's fire next to the return portal which is also tagged `hall-haldor`. Stepping back into it brings them home. This is the shape players already expect from vanilla — the mod's contribution is that nobody can accidentally retag `hall-haldor` into `hall` and swap two destinations, and a demolished twin shows as `[$piece_portal_unconnected]` instead of silently re-pairing with the copper camp.

**Failure modes.**
- Full mesh is quadratic. 20 sites = 380 portals = 380 ZDOs in m_portalObjects, all resident in server RAM permanently (portals are never released — ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS only reassigns ownership, :76872-76883) and all flattened into a fresh List<ZDO> on every GetPortalList() call, i.e. every 5 s. Measurable but not alarming; cache the list if you poll faster.
- A destroyed twin leaves the local slot unconnected and, because its tag is unique, FindRandomUnconnectedPortal returns null and it stays unconnected forever — a safe, honest failure that the hover text reports.
- If an admin reuses a tag string across two banks, the four portals form two pairs by dictionary order and the mapping silently reshuffles on the next server restart.
- Any mass re-tag or mass re-link across a large bank must be throttled: every ZDO.SetConnection bumps DataRevision and ForceSendZDO pushes to every peer. Wonderland's StructureUpkeep caps routed broadcasts at 256 per sweep for exactly this reason.

**Prerequisites.** Simple Pair

## 12. Switchboard (one physical portal repointed on demand)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

A single hub portal whose destination the player selects via emote or map ping; the server rewrites one ZDOID and the very next transit uses it.

**How it works.** Encoding. Hub H and destinations D1..Dn all on one tag T. Every Di points at H (a Fan-In Star, so all inbound legs are permanently stable). H points at whichever Dk is currently selected.

The repoint is three lines: `H.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); H.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, Dk.m_uid); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(H.m_uid);` — plus `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, Dk.m_uid)` targeted at the requesting player, because TargetFound() (:143640-143654) requires that client to actually HOLD the destination ZDO; if it does not, the first walk-through calls RequestZDO and returns false with no message at all.

Why the repoint survives reconciliation. After the switch, pass 1 on H tests Dk: non-null ✓, tag == T ✓, Dk.connection == H ≠ None ✓ → survives. Pass 1 on the PREVIOUS destination Dj tests H: H.connection == Dk ≠ None ✓ → Dj's inbound leg is untouched. So flipping the hub's outbound never disturbs any inbound leg. Verified directly against the pass-1 body at :100594-100606. No Harmony patch, no faster tick.

Latency. TeleportWorld.Teleport re-reads `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` at the instant of transit (:143539) — nothing is cached — so a repoint applies to the very next walk-in. The 0.5 s UpdatePortal InvokeRepeating only drives the glow (:143491-143509), not routing.

Input channel. A vanilla client has exactly two reliable ways to tell the server anything: an emote (poll ZDOVars.s_emoteID / s_emote on the character ZDO, Wonderland's EmoteSignals pattern) or a map ping, which is `Chat.SendPing` → routed `"ChatMessage"` at targetPeerID 0 carrying the clicked world Vector3 (:42058-42068) and therefore always reaches the server even with one player online. Ping is the better fit: middle-click the map at a destination, server picks the nearest managed portal to that coordinate and repoints the hub. Confirm with PlayerNotify.Toast.

Single-writer caveat: the hub has ONE connection globally. Two players selecting different destinations within a few seconds of each other will fight. Serialise with a short per-hub lock (≈15 s) and toast the loser.

**Player experience.** One portal in the great hall, signed `gate`. The player opens the map, middle-clicks the Mountain waystation, and a moment later gets a top-left toast: `Gate set: Mountain Waystation`. They walk into the portal, eight seconds of swirl, and step out at the waystation. Another player who middle-clicks the Swamp while the first is mid-transit gets `Gate busy — try again in 12s`. Every waystation portal in the realm is also signed `gate` and always leads back to the hall, so the return trip never needs a selection. The hub portal's glow and hover text never change; only where it goes changes.

**Failure modes.**
- First transit after a repoint to a never-visited region silently fails: TargetFound returns false at gate 1 and Teleport returns WITHOUT calling player.Message (:143519-143522). No error, no message, nothing. Always pre-push the destination ZDO with the targeted ForceSendZDO(peerID, id) overload before toasting success.
- Map pings are public — Chat.SendPing broadcasts to every peer, so everyone sees the requesting player's ping marker and a 5 s map pin. It is also trivially spammable; debounce per player.
- Ownership churn: ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926, every 2 s) hands the hub's ZDO to whichever player is standing next to it, so the server's SetOwner claim is transient. The connection VALUE survives (it was already ForceSendZDO'd) but the next repoint must re-claim. For heavy use, install the Wonderland ZDO.SetOwner prefix guard (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313) filtered on portal prefab hash, and allow uid==0 and uid==GetSessionID() through.
- A player already standing inside the hub's trigger when the repoint lands will NOT re-trigger — OnTriggerEnter is enter-only (:143672-143681). They must step out and back in. This is the real constraint on switchboard responsiveness, not the 0.5 s glow poll.
- A hacked client can repoint the hub itself via the unauthenticated routed RPC_SetConnection (:100653-100662). Audit the hub's connection every tick and revert.

**Prerequisites.** Fan-In Star

## 13. Carousel (auto-rotating hub destination)

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

One portal whose destination the server cycles on a timer — a lottery, not a route.

**How it works.** Mechanically identical to the Switchboard minus the player input: a timer in the subsystem's OnUpdate writes `H.SetConnection(Portal, D[(k++) % n].m_uid)` + ForceSendZDO every P seconds. All Di point at H so the inbound legs are stable, and pass 1 never objects for the same reason as the Switchboard.

The reason this is caveated rather than recommended: the destination is resolved at the instant of transit (:143539), not at the instant the player decides to walk in. If the carousel period is short relative to the player's approach, the destination they saw advertised (on a sign, in a toast) is not the one they get. There is no way to latch the destination to the player, because there is one connection slot and it is global. The honest framings are:
- Long period (≥5 minutes) with a server-written Sign next to the portal naming the current destination (write ZDOVars.s_text; Sign.UpdateText repaints on a 2 s InvokeRepeating when the ZDO DataRevision changes). Then the advertised destination is accurate for practically the whole period.
- Short period as a deliberate randomiser — a "wild gate" that drops you somewhere unpredictable.

One useful hardening: pause the rotation whenever any connected character's ZDO position is within ~8 m of the hub (poll ConnectedCharacters + ZDO.GetPosition, or ZdoSpatialQuery), so the destination cannot flip under someone's feet. That converts the worst race into a bounded one.

Per-tick cost is one ZDO write plus one ForceSendZDO broadcast. Because ZDOExtraData.SetConnection returns false for an unchanged value (:74954-74957), re-asserting the same destination is free; only real changes generate traffic.

**Player experience.** A weathered portal at the crossroads signed `wildgate`, with a rune stone beside it that reads `Currently: the Sunken Crypt at Swamp North`. Every ten minutes the stone's text changes and the gate leads somewhere else. A player who reads the stone and steps in within the next nine minutes gets what it promised. A player who reads it, wanders off to fight a troll, and comes back eleven minutes later gets the Mountain cave instead, with no warning — the gate looked identical the whole time. If the admin sets the period to 30 seconds instead, the gate becomes a genuine lottery and players treat it as one.

**Failure modes.**
- Destination-at-transit race: unavoidable and structural. The player cannot reserve a destination and the server cannot hold one per player.
- If the rotation lands on a destination the player's client does not hold, their first walk-in silently no-ops (gate 1 at :143519 returns without a message). Broadcast ForceSendZDO(newTarget) to all peers on each rotation, or accept occasional silent failures.
- A rotation that fires while a player is mid-teleport is harmless — Teleport() already captured the position and Player.UpdateTeleport pins m_teleportTargetPos (:15343).
- Very short periods generate a ZDO write plus a full-broadcast ForceSendZDO every period; at 1 s with many carousels this becomes real traffic since ZDOMan.SendZDOs re-serialises the entire ZDO with no delta encoding (:77053-77062).

## 14. Invisible Tag Sharding via rich-text-stripped suffix

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

Append `<x>` to a portal's tag: vanilla's hover strips it from display but the reconciler still compares the full string, so two portals that look identically named refuse to pair.

**How it works.** The mechanism is a genuine asymmetry between what routes and what displays, and both halves are verified in code.

Routes on the RAW string. Game.ConnectPortals compares `item.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` with bare `string !=` (:100601) and FindRandomUnconnectedPortal filters on `portal.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) != tag` (:100669). No trimming, no normalisation, no stripping.

Displays a STRIPPED string. TeleportWorld.GetHoverText does `text = tagInfo.text.RemoveRichTextTags()` (:143459), and RemoveRichTextTags is `Regex.Replace(text, "<[\\/a-zA-Z0-9= \"\\\"''#;:()$_-]*?>", string.Empty)` (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703 — read directly). The character class covers letters, digits, `/`, `=`, space, quotes, `#`, `;`, `:`, `(`, `)`, `$`, `_`, `-`. So `<a>`, `<p17>`, `<f:red>`, `<s_2>` are all stripped.

Therefore: `s_tag = "base<f:red>"` hovers as `base` on every vanilla client but is a different routing namespace from `"base"` and from `"base<f:blue>"`.

Uses. (a) Per-faction or per-player namespaces that players never see. (b) Shard isolation across a large server. (c) Per-portal uniquification for a server-enforced lockdown (see Tag-Scramble Lockdown) where every portal gets `<p{n}>` and nothing can pair, while the hover text is unchanged. (d) Preventing a visitor's identically-named portal from joining a managed network.

Budget. TeleportWorld.Interact calls `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` (:143482) and TextInput.Show assigns `m_inputField.characterLimit = charLimit` then `m_inputField.text = text` (:61515-61521). Ten characters total including the suffix if a player is ever to retype it. Keep display names ≤ 5 chars, or accept that the mod must re-apply the suffix after every player retag. RPC_SetTag itself applies no cap (:143587-143602) so the SERVER can write any length.

Alternative carrier: a zero-width space (U+200B). Invisible in both the hover and the edit field, one char of budget, and not touched by the regex. Less provable from code than the `<>` form, so verify in-game.

**Player experience.** Two guilds each build a portal they both call `home`. Guild A's portals carry `home<a>` and Guild B's carry `home<b>`, written by the server on placement based on the piece's ZDOVars.s_creator. Both guilds hover their portals and read exactly `Teleport tag:"home" [$piece_portal_connected]`. A guild-A member who walks into their `home` portal always arrives at guild A's hall, never guild B's, and no amount of retyping the tag will cross the boundary because the server re-applies the suffix within a second. From the players' side it simply looks as though portals only connect to their own guild's — which is exactly the feature.

**Failure modes.**
- A player who opens the tag dialog sees the RAW tag in the edit field, including the suffix, because TextInput.RequestText pre-fills with sign.GetText() = GetTagInfo().text = the raw s_tag (:143551-143554, :143556-143570). It is hidden in hover, not in the editor.
- 10-character budget in the client editor. Whether GuiInputField clamps a programmatically assigned .text longer than characterLimit is a Unity behaviour question — if it does, a player opening and confirming the dialog on a server-written long tag saves back a TRUNCATED tag, silently destroying the shard suffix.
- A retag by the player wipes the suffix AND clears that portal's connection (:143595), so the portal drops out of its shard and pass 2 may pair it with whatever else shares its now-bare tag. A normalisation tick (re-write s_tag and call ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()) is mandatory.
- Angle brackets are not the only hazard: Chat.OnNewChatMessage replaces '<' and '>' with spaces, so never round-trip a sharded tag through a chat-based tool.
- Support burden: when two portals that visibly share a name refuse to connect, nothing anywhere explains why. Log the raw tags in the mod's audit trail.

## 15. Per-Player Private Networks

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Every player's portals silently share a namespace of their own, keyed on the builder recorded in the piece ZDO.

**How it works.** Identity source. Every player-placed piece records its builder: `Piece.SetCreator` writes ZDOVars.s_creator (a long equal to that player's PlayerProfile UID, identical to ZDOVars.s_playerID on their character ZDO) and s_creatorIndex (an index into ZNet.World.m_playerHistory, which the server persists in the .fwl and fills from socket-verified PlatformUserIDs). A portal's builder is therefore readable server-side, offline, forever.

Namespacing. On a tick (2-5 s is ample), enumerate ZDOMan.GetPortalList(); for each portal read `creator = zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator, 0L)` and the current s_tag. Strip any existing managed suffix, then write `s_tag = <displayTag> + "<p" + shortCode(creator) + ">"` using the Invisible Tag Sharding mechanism, followed by `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (a tag write alone does NOT set DirtyPortalObjects, so the rename is lost at the next save otherwise — :73832/:76702/:77621). Portals whose creator is 0 (world-gen, admin-spawned, or placed before the field existed — SetCreator only writes when `GetCreator() == 0 && m_nview.IsOwner()`, :136415-136424) go into a shared "public" namespace.

Result. Vanilla's own reconciler now enforces the partition for free: FindRandomUnconnectedPortal only considers exact-tag matches (:100669), so player A's `forest<pA1>` can never be paired with player B's `forest<pB7>`. Two players can both name a portal `forest` and never interfere.

Sharing. To let A grant B access to one portal, rewrite just that portal's suffix to a shared group code (`<gAB>`). Because the routing suffix is data the server owns, sharing is a one-line rewrite plus a ConnectPortals call for instant re-pairing (`Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` is public, :100589).

Grant/revoke must also handle the in-flight connection: changing a portal's suffix out from under an existing pair leaves the PARTNER holding a now tag-mismatched target, which pass 1 tears down within 5 s — correct behaviour, just not instantaneous. Call ConnectPortals() yourself to make it immediate.

**Player experience.** Astrid and Bjorn both build a portal at their own farm and both call it `farm`. In vanilla they would have paired with each other and spent an evening confused; here each pairs only with their own second `farm` portal at their own mine. Both hover as `tag:"farm"`. When Astrid wants Bjorn to be able to reach her mine, she emotes /point at the portal and a top-left toast reads `Portal shared with the nearest player: Bjorn`. Within a second Bjorn's `farm` portals and Astrid's shared one are in the same group, and the next time Bjorn steps into his farm portal he may come out at Astrid's mine.

**Failure modes.**
- s_creator is 0 for admin-spawned and world-gen portals, and for anything placed under conditions where SetCreator's `GetCreator() == 0 && IsOwner()` guard did not fire. Treat 0 as public, never as 'owned by nobody in particular'.
- s_creator is written by the PLACING CLIENT, so it is a client self-report. It is cross-checkable only via s_creatorIndex into ZNet.World.m_playerHistory (socket-verified PlatformUserIDs, :81271-81280, :81436-81461) — and that index is -1 when the placer was not yet in the history.
- A player retagging their portal wipes the suffix and clears the connection. The normalisation tick restores it within one tick, but pass 2 may have paired the portal into the bare-tag public group in the interim. Reduce the window by calling Game.instance.ConnectPortals() immediately after normalising.
- The whole partition is one ZDO string write per portal — a hacked client can simply write s_tag itself via ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77139), which validates nothing beyond the DataRevision. Server-side this is detect-and-revert, not prevention.
- 10-char editor budget: a player's display tag effectively shrinks to ~5 characters once a suffix is applied.

**Prerequisites.** Invisible Tag Sharding via rich-text-stripped suffix

## 16. Team / Faction Networks

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Guild-scoped namespaces derived from a mod-side roster rather than from the builder, so membership can change without rebuilding.

**How it works.** Same sharding mechanism as Per-Player Private Networks, but the suffix is derived from a roster the mod maintains rather than directly from s_creator. Roster key must be durable: ZDOVars.s_playerID (the profile UID, written once into the character ZDO by Player.SetPlayerID, :10129-10136) or the socket-verified PlatformUserID from `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()` — never ZNetPeer.m_uid (a per-connection id) and never ZNetPeer.m_playerID (permanently 0, because no vanilla client ever invokes the "PlayerID" RPC).

Portal→faction resolution, in priority order: (1) a mod-private ZDO key written by the mod when the portal was claimed (e.g. `zdo.Set("tpl_faction".GetStableHashCode(), factionId)` — arbitrary int-keyed ZDO data round-trips through save and network for free); (2) s_creator looked up in the roster; (3) the ward the portal stands inside — PrivateArea's roster is fully server-readable from the ward ZDO as `zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_permitted)` plus the raw string keys `"pu_id"+i` (long) and `"pu_name"+i` (string), written by PrivateArea.SetPermittedPlayers (:137338-137347). Option (3) is attractive because it reuses a UI players already understand, but the ward radius is a compiled Inspector field (PrivateArea.m_radius, class default 10f, :137132) and must be measured or configured; PrivateArea.CheckAccess itself is useless server-side because m_allAreas is always empty and it therefore returns true vacuously (:137547-137593).

The rest is identical: normalisation tick writes `s_tag = display + "<f" + factionCode + ">"`, SetDirtyPortals(), and vanilla's tag-equality filter partitions the world.

Cross-faction gateways: give one designated portal per faction a SHARED suffix (`<fx>`) and wire them as a Fan-In Star into a neutral hub. Faction members reach the neutral hub from their own network, and from the hub a Portal Bank reaches the other factions' public halls.

**Player experience.** The Wolves and the Ravens each have a hall. Wolf portals all hover as `hall`; Raven portals also all hover as `hall`. A Wolf stepping into any `hall` portal always arrives at the Wolf hall. In the neutral market square stand two portals, `market` and `market`, one per faction, both leading to the same neutral rotunda; from the rotunda a colonnade of eight labelled portals reaches every faction's public hall. When a player is promoted from Raven to Wolf, the admin runs one command; within about two seconds every portal they built repoints, and their old `hall` portals now take them to the Wolf hall instead. Nothing they can see on the portal changed.

**Failure modes.**
- Faction membership changes must re-normalise every affected portal in one batch; doing it piecemeal leaves half-migrated networks where pass 1 tears down cross-suffix edges (correctly) and pass 2 re-pairs the freed ends randomly inside their new group.
- A mass migration is a mass broadcast: every changed ZDO bumps DataRevision and ForceSendZDO pushes to all peers. Budget it (Wonderland's StructureUpkeep caps at 256 routed broadcasts per sweep for exactly this reason).
- Ward-derived membership is only as good as PrivateArea.m_radius, which the decompile cannot supply, and PrivateArea's permitted list is itself plain ZDO data any client can rewrite via RPC_ZDOData.
- PrivateArea.RPC_ToggleEnabled and RPC_TogglePermitted ignore the routed-RPC sender entirely and act on a payload playerID (:137399-137421), so ward membership is spoofable by any client. Treat it as a convenience, not authorisation.
- Vanilla's own portal system has no concept of a faction; if the mod is uninstalled, every portal is left carrying a visible-but-stripped suffix and the world settles into whatever pairs those raw strings produce — the faction partition actually SURVIVES uninstall until someone retags, which may be surprising.

**Prerequisites.** Invisible Tag Sharding via rich-text-stripped suffix; Per-Player Private Networks

## 17. Tag-Scramble Lockdown (server-ENFORCED portal shutdown)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small-medium

Give every portal a unique invisible tag suffix so no two can ever pair — a shutdown a modified client cannot lift, unlike the NoPortals global key.

**How it works.** Why the obvious approach fails. Writing `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` on every portal does NOT lock anything: pass 2 of Game.ConnectPortals re-pairs every same-tag unconnected portal within 5 s (:100607-100622). And `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` is CLIENT-HONOURED only — TeleportWorld.Teleport reads the key on the traveller's machine (:143523) — and worse, ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey / RPC_RemoveGlobalKey perform ZERO sender validation (:116022-116037), so any connected client can clear the lockdown with one packet.

The enforced version. For every portal P in ZDOMan.GetPortalList(): stash the original tag in a mod-private ZDO key (`P.Set("tpl_tag_saved".GetStableHashCode(), original)`), then write `P.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, original + "<L" + P.m_uid.ID + ">")` and `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`. Every portal is now the sole member of its own tag group. FindRandomUnconnectedPortal's candidate list is empty for every portal and it returns null (:100674-100678), so pass 2 can never pair anything. Then null every connection: `P.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); P.SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(P.m_uid);`

The result is enforced at the ZDO layer — TeleportWorld.Teleport's gate 1 (`if (!TargetFound()) return;`, :143519) is the ONLY one of its four gates that is server-controllable, and a None connection fails it unconditionally on any client, modified or not.

And because the suffix is stripped from the hover by RemoveRichTextTags (:143459), every portal still displays its original name; only `[$piece_portal_unconnected]` and the dead glow reveal the shutdown. Lifting it is the reverse pass: restore s_tag from the stash, SetDirtyPortals(), and call `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` to re-pair instantly.

Throttle: this is a world-wide write. On a 400-portal world that is 800 ZDO writes and 400 full-ZDO broadcasts to every peer. Budget it across ticks (≤256 broadcasts per sweep) unless the server is empty.

**Player experience.** Ten seconds before a server-wide raid event, every portal in the world goes dark. Hover text still reads `Teleport tag:"base"` — the name the player chose — but the bracket now says `[$piece_portal_unconnected]` and the stone no longer glows. Walking in does nothing at all: no black screen, no `$msg_blocked`, no message of any kind, because gate 1 returns silently (:143519-143522). Players with cheat clients get exactly the same result. When the event ends the portals light up again within a second and every original pairing is restored, including custom hub topologies, because the mod re-asserts them explicitly rather than letting vanilla re-roll.

**Failure modes.**
- Absolutely silent to the player. Pair it with a PlayerNotify.Toast broadcast ("The ways are shut") or the shutdown reads as a server bug.
- Losing the stash loses the tags. Write the stash to the ZDO (round-trips through save automatically) rather than to a mod-side file keyed by ZDOID — ZDOIDs are renumbered on every world load (ZDO.Load does m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID), :74552), so a ZDOID-keyed file is worthless after a restart.
- A restore that runs while vanilla's 5 s pass is mid-flight can produce transient random pairings. Prefix Game.ConnectPortals to return false for the duration of the restore batch, then call it once explicitly.
- Do not use the connection-nulling half alone. Without the tag scramble it is undone in ≤5 s by vanilla itself.
- Mod uninstalled mid-lockdown: the scrambled tags persist in the save, every portal stays a singleton group, and every portal in the world is permanently dead until someone retags them by hand. This is the most dangerous option in the catalogue for that reason — always restore before shutdown (Plugin.OnDestroy).

**Prerequisites.** Invisible Tag Sharding via rich-text-stripped suffix

## 18. Black-Hole Sink (all portals → one destination)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

Repoint every portal at a single jail/lobby anchor: portals keep working, but everything arrives in the same room.

**How it works.** A softer, stabler alternative to the Tag-Scramble Lockdown that needs no tag surgery at all.

Create one anchor Z at the lobby coordinate (see Anchor-Terminated One-Way for the full CreateNewZDO recipe). Then for every portal P you want swallowed: `P.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, T_sink)`, `P.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, `P.SetConnection(Portal, Z.m_uid)`, `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(P.m_uid)`; and on the anchor `Z.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, T_sink)` plus `Z.SetConnection(Portal, Z.m_uid)`.

Stability. Every portal's pass-1 test is evaluated against Z: non-null ✓, tag == T_sink ✓, Z.connection == Z ≠ None ✓. No teardown. Pass 2 finds nothing IsNone(). One anchor swallows an unbounded number of portals with no per-tick cost — this is Fan-In taken to its extreme, and it is the cheapest world-wide topology write in the catalogue because it needs one target ZDOID for every source.

If you want the sink to be reversible without stashing tags, do NOT rewrite s_tag: instead give the anchor the tag of whichever group you are swallowing and run one anchor per tag group. More anchors, zero tag churn, trivially reversible by restoring each portal's connection from a mod-private ZDO key holding the pre-sink target's position (not its ZDOID — ZDOIDs renumber on load).

Uses: a jail (portal offenders into a warded pen), a maintenance mode, a raid-night funnel where everyone who portals ends up at the muster point, or a PvP mechanic where a captured region's portals all dump into the capturing faction's holding cell.

**Player experience.** A player steps into their base portal expecting the mine. Black screen, eight seconds, and they fade in inside a stone rotunda with no exit portal, a sign reading `THE WAYS ARE WARDED — SPEAK TO A JARL`, and half a dozen other confused players. Every portal in the world behaves the same way. The portals still glow, still hover as connected, and still give the full teleport experience — they simply all arrive at one place. Unlike the tag scramble, players immediately understand something deliberate has happened.

**Failure modes.**
- If the anchor is destroyed or fails to persist, every swallowed portal is nulled by pass 1 and then randomly re-paired inside T_sink — producing an instantaneous world-wide random portal shuffle, the worst possible failure. The anchor MUST have Persistent = true and a real SetPrefab (ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO sets neither, :76684-76692).
- Players can be sunk mid-journey and have no way back; provide an egress (a portal in the rotunda on its own tag paired to a release point, or a server-driven RPC_TeleportPlayer).
- At world load ZDOMan.ConnectPortals matches hash pairs reciprocally (:77879-77885) and only ONE portal can win the anchor's single Target slot; the rest are unconnected and then randomly re-paired by Game.instance.ConnectPortals (:76523). Re-assert the sink at OnWorldReady, unconditionally.
- Mod uninstalled: the sink survives only until the next world reload, at which point the world settles into random pairs within T_sink. If every portal shares T_sink, that is a complete randomisation of the server's entire portal graph. Restore before shutdown.

**Prerequisites.** Anchor-Terminated One-Way / Dead Drop; Fan-In Star

## 19. Roulette / Periodic Shuffle

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

Leave a large group on one tag and let vanilla's own UnityEngine.Random pairing do the work — optionally forcing a re-roll on a timer.

**How it works.** Zero-mod version: place N portals all carrying the same tag string. Vanilla's pass 2 (:100607-100622) pairs them using `list[UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, list.Count)]` from the shared global Unity RNG (:100678), producing floor(N/2) arbitrary pairs plus one permanent orphan if N is odd. Because pass 1 never tears down a healthy pair, the arrangement then freezes until something breaks.

Forced re-roll: on a timer, for every member `P.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); P.SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(P.m_uid);` then call `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` (public, :100589) once to re-pair immediately rather than waiting up to 5 s. Every member is IsNone() so pass 2 re-pairs all of them with fresh random picks.

Subtlety that bites: Game.SetConnection defers to the owning client over RPC_SetConnection when the portal is owned by a CONNECTED peer (:100641-100650), leaving the server's own copy reading the OLD connection. Pass 2 in the same tick then sees `!IsNone()` and skips that portal, so a portal a player is standing next to takes two or more ticks to re-roll. Avoid by doing the null writes yourself with explicit SetOwner (which makes GetPeer(serverSessionID) null and forces the immediate local path) rather than going through Game.SetConnection.

Also reproduce vanilla's `IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal` guard if you re-implement pass 2 yourself (:100609, :100671) — it exists precisely because a deferred write leaves the server's copy reading None and would otherwise let the same portal be paired twice in one pass.

The orphan is a feature: designate a known-odd count so exactly one portal in the roulette is always dead, and let players hunt for it.

**Player experience.** Seven identical standing stones scattered across the Black Forest, all tagged `wyrd`. Three pairs are live and one stone is dark. Every hour at the top of the hour every stone briefly goes dark and then relights in a new configuration — the stone that took you to the river camp now takes you to the mountain pass, and a different one is the dead stone. Players build their evening's route around whatever the current roll is, and there is no way to predict it from inside the game because it is drawn from the shared UnityEngine.Random stream.

**Failure modes.**
- Not deterministic and not seedable from the mod's side. If you need deterministic pairing, postfix the private Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (AccessTools.Method(typeof(Game), "FindRandomUnconnectedPortal")) and overwrite __result with your own pick — the minimal, lowest-risk intervention that leaves the two-phase commit, ownership handling and logging intact.
- The orphan's identity is not stable across a restart, because iteration order is m_portalObjects dictionary-bucket order (:77648-77656).
- A re-roll that lands a player's destination in an unvisited region makes their first walk-in silently fail (TargetFound → RequestZDO, :143646-143654).
- Every re-roll is 2N ZDO writes plus 2N full-ZDO broadcasts. At N=40 hourly that is fine; at N=400 every minute it is not.
