## 20. Displaced Routing — own the pairing, free s_tag for display

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium-large

Harmony-prefix Game.ConnectPortals to return false and run your own pairer keyed on a mod-private ZDO string; s_tag becomes a pure label with no routing meaning.

**How it works.** The master enabler. Every constraint elsewhere in this catalogue — one tag per network, identical hover names across a tier, invisible suffixes, 10-character budgets, players accidentally retagging a hub out of existence — exists only because vanilla routes on s_tag. Take that over and all of them dissolve.

Implementation. `[HarmonyPatch(typeof(Game), nameof(Game.ConnectPortals))] static bool Prefix() => false;` (the method is public and instance-level, :100589). Wrap it with SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch. The coroutine keeps running and keeps calling a now-empty method every 5 s — harmless. Alternatively `Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")`, which is valid because Start used the string overload (:100074), but the prefix is safer and reversible.

Then run your own pass on a timer you choose (1-5 s). Read routing from a mod-private key: `int ROUTE = "tpl_route".GetStableHashCode(); string route = zdo.GetString(ROUTE, "");` — arbitrary int-keyed ZDO strings persist through save and network automatically (ZDO.Set/GetString :73721/:73967) and are invisible to the player and to any other mod. Encode whatever you want: `"hub:realm/spoke"`, `"ring:caravan/3"`, `"bank:hall-haldor"`.

Write edges with the same triad (SetOwner / SetConnection / ForceSendZDO). Reproduce vanilla's useful bits: pass 1 self-heal against destroyed targets, and the IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal double-pair guard if you ever defer a write.

What this buys: arbitrary directed graphs with per-portal display names of arbitrary length (RPC_SetTag applies no cap, :143587-143602 — only the client's TextInput widget does, :143482); true trees where every tier can be labelled differently; per-portal metadata; one-way links that cannot be torn down; and immunity to player retagging (a retag changes only the label).

A related, riskier trick worth knowing: `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` returns the LIVE m_portalObjects dictionary (:77643-77646), so a portal removed from it becomes invisible to vanilla's pairer without a patch. Do not do this — the portal chunk file is written wholesale from m_portalObjects (:77621-77635), so a hidden portal is also an unsaved portal.

**Player experience.** Players see richer portals than vanilla allows. The hall portal hovers `Teleport tag:"Grand Hall of Hrafnsborg"` — a 25-character name no vanilla client could have typed. The four waystations read `North Waystation`, `East Waystation` and so on, all distinct, and all four still lead to the Grand Hall because routing has nothing to do with what is written on them. A player who retypes their portal's name to something rude changes only the sign; the route is untouched and the portal keeps working. Caveat: the moment a player opens the tag dialog on a long name, the edit box's 10-character limit may clamp it, so the mod re-writes the label from its own record on the next tick.

**Failure modes.**
- Mod uninstalled = total collapse, and this is the single biggest trade in the catalogue. Vanilla's ConnectPortals resumes on the next 5 s tick, sees a world of arbitrary directed edges, tears down every edge whose two ends have different s_tag strings (which, with per-portal display names, is nearly all of them), and randomly re-pairs everything inside whatever tag groups remain. A 200-portal curated network becomes 100 random pairs in one tick. Mitigate by writing a sane s_tag alongside the route key so the fallback is at least sensible, and by restoring a vanilla-legal configuration in Plugin.OnDestroy.
- A hacked client can still rewire any portal via the unauthenticated routed Game RPC_SetConnection (:100653-100662) or by writing the ZDO directly through RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77139). Your own pass re-asserts within one tick, which is the practical answer.
- Your pairer now owns the two-phase-commit problem vanilla solved. If you ever defer a write to an owning client, reproduce IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal or you will double-pair.
- Never cache ZDO object references across ticks. ZDOPool.Release/Get recycles ZDO objects on destruction and ZDO.Reset sets m_uid = ZDOID.None (:78286-78311, :73536-73545) — vanilla itself violates this in m_currentlyConnectingPortals. Cache ZDOIDs and re-resolve with ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id) every tick.
- Other mods that patch Game.ConnectPortals will conflict.

## 21. Asymmetric Round-Trip ("one-way door, long way home")

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

A→B and B→C where C sits next to A: a portal you can only travel one direction through, and a separate return leg you must find.

**How it works.** A three-portal directed chain closed by geography rather than by graph structure, and the cheapest genuinely one-way experience that still lets players get home.

Encoding. Three portals A, B, C all on one tag T. `A.SetConnection(Portal, B.m_uid)`, `B.SetConnection(Portal, C.m_uid)`, `C.SetConnection(Portal, A.m_uid)` — formally this is a 3-ring, so it is a vanilla fixed point for exactly the reasons given in the Directed Ring entry (every target non-null, tag-matched, non-None). The design content is in the PLACEMENT: A and C are put twenty metres apart at the home site, B is at the far site. So the travel graph reads home→far (via A), far→home-ish (via B), and home→home (via C, the twenty-metre hop that closes the ring and which nobody uses on purpose).

Better variant with two portals and an anchor: A (home) → B (far), B → anchor placed two metres behind B. Then B is a dead end and the far site genuinely has no return. Use when you want a true expedition.

Best variant, three portals, no useless hop: A (home) → B (far); B → C where C is at the home site; C → anchor at the home site. Now A is the outbound door, B is the return door, C is an arrival pad that goes nowhere useful, and no edge is wasted. All on tag T. Pass 1 accepts it: A→B ok (B.connection = C ≠ None), B→C ok (C.connection = anchor ≠ None), C→anchor ok (anchor.tag = T, anchor.connection = anchor ≠ None). Stable.

Why bother instead of a plain pair: it makes the two directions independently controllable. The mod can null or repoint the return leg (B→C) for an event without touching the outbound leg, which a symmetric pair cannot express at all.

**Player experience.** At the base, two portals stand side by side under one roof: the left one signed with a runic arrow pointing out, the right one with an arrow pointing in. Stepping into the left portal takes the player to the Mistlands camp. There is exactly one portal at the camp; stepping into it brings them back — to the RIGHT portal at the base, not the left one. Stepping into the right portal again does nothing useful (an eight-second black screen and they are back on the same flagstones). During a server event the jarl closes the return leg: the camp portal goes dark and hovers `[$piece_portal_unconnected]`, so everyone at the camp has to walk out, while the outbound door stays lit and people can still be sent in.

**Failure modes.**
- Same unravelling risk as any chain if the terminator is lost: if the anchor dies, C is nulled, then B is nulled on the next tick, then A. Anchor persistence is load-bearing.
- All three portals share one tag so they all hover with the same name — signage or the Displaced Routing option is needed to make the in/out distinction legible.
- World reload recovers at most one pair out of the three-edge structure; mandatory re-assert.

**Prerequisites.** Directed Ring; Anchor-Terminated One-Way / Dead Drop

## 22. Per-Player Destination Arbitration on a Shared Hub — RULED OUT as true per-player routing

`RULED-OUT` · `NOT-ENFORCEABLE` · effort: medium

A hub cannot send different players to different places at the same time; the connection is one global ZDOID, and the server cannot see who is about to walk in.

**How it works.** Two independent walls.

Wall 1, storage: one ZDOConnection per ZDO (:75524-75534). The hub's destination is a single global value visible to every client simultaneously. There is no per-viewer ZDO state anywhere in the protocol; ZDOMan.SendZDOs serialises one blob per ZDO and sends the same bytes to every peer (:77053-77062).

Wall 2, timing: the server has no moment-of-transit hook. TeleportWorld.Teleport is called only from TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter, which requires `colliderIn.GetComponent<Player>() != null` AND `Player.m_localPlayer == component` (:143672-143681) — and on a dedicated server no portal GameObject, no trigger collider and no Player component ever exists, because Game.FixedUpdate pins `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick (:100458-100466, a line absent from the client build) so ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects only ever instantiates in a sector 1e6 m from the world (:82268-82276). The server therefore cannot know that player X is the one about to transit, and cannot set the destination "for them" in time.

The closest legitimate approximations, all of which are different features:
- **Proximity latch**: poll connected characters' ZDO positions (ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS :81024-81044, position refreshed every physics tick by the owner's ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync :87527-87534) and set the hub to a player's pre-selected destination while they are the only person within ~10 m, releasing it when they leave or after a timeout. Works perfectly with one player near the hub and degrades to first-come-first-served with two. Announce the lock with PlayerNotify.Toast.
- **A bank instead of a hub** — N portals, no arbitration needed. Always the right answer if you can afford the portals.
- **Forced teleport instead of a portal** — detect the player's intent from an emote or map ping and move them with the routed RPC `RPC_TeleportPlayer` (registered in Chat.Awake on every vanilla client, :41627; body `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport)`, :41962-41968). This IS genuinely per-player, but it bypasses every vanilla portal rule including the ore check, and it is not a portal topology.

**Player experience.** What players would want: two people standing at the same gate, each stepping in and arriving at their own chosen destination. What actually happens with a naive implementation: player A selects the Mountains, player B selects the Swamp a second later and overwrites the hub, player A walks in and lands in the Swamp. With the proximity latch: player B gets a toast reading `Gate reserved by Astrid — 11s` and has to wait, which is honest but visibly worse than a bank.

**Failure modes.**
- Any implementation that writes the hub per-request without a lock produces silent mis-routing, which players will experience as the server teleporting them to random places.
- A forced teleport silently no-ops if the target teleported within the last 2 s or is mid-teleport (Player.TeleportTo :15308-15316), returns false, and the return value is discarded by both RPC handlers — the server never learns it failed.
- A forced teleport also skips the boss gate, the NoPortals gate and the inventory check entirely; the server cannot reproduce the inventory check because a player's inventory is never mirrored into any ZDO.

**Prerequisites.** Switchboard

## 23. Pairing Authority Takeover

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Harmony-prefix Game.ConnectPortals to return false and reimplement all pairing in the mod — the prerequisite for every dynamic-routing feature.

**How it works.** Vanilla's 5s reconciler is actively hostile to every dynamic topology. `Game.ConnectPortals` pass 1 (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100594-100606) nulls any portal's connection when the partner ZDO is missing, the partner's `ZDOVars.s_tag` string differs by ordinal comparison, OR the partner's own connection is `ZDOID.None`. Pass 2 (:100607-100622) then re-pairs every unconnected portal with a uniformly random same-tag partner via `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (:100664-100679). Any custom destination, any per-portal display tag, any parked portal, is destroyed within 5 seconds.

The clean architecture is a Harmony prefix on the public `Game.ConnectPortals` (:100589) returning false, plus a mod reimplementation that (a) runs vanilla's exact two passes over only the UNMANAGED subset of `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (:77648), and (b) applies mod policy to managed portals. Reproduce vanilla's `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` guard (`IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal` :100700) in the unmanaged path or portals owned by online peers double-pair, because their deferred `RPC_SetConnection` write leaves the server's local copy reading None.

The write primitive for managed portals is the three lines vanilla itself uses in `Game.SetConnection` (:100637-100651), taken unconditionally rather than conditionally: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` (:74627/:77362); `zdo.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, targetId)` (:73656, which internally bumps DataRevision and calls `SetDirtyPortals`); `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706).

Membership is decided by a mod-side registry keyed by rounded world position or by `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) — NEVER by ZDOID, which `ZDO.Load` renumbers on every world load (`m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`, :74552). The prefix must not be applied until OnWorldReady; the load-time call from `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` (:76523) should be allowed through so save-hash relinking completes first.

No-patch alternative ("tag cloaking"): give a managed hub and its current destination the SAME unique tag and a reciprocal link, satisfying pass 1 and making pass 2 skip both. It works, but every ex-destination must be parked with its own unique tag or two ex-destinations sharing a tag will pair to each other.

**Player experience.** Invisible. A player sees no difference in how ordinary portals behave — same-tag portals still auto-pair, orphaned portals still read "$piece_portal_unconnected" on hover. The only observable change is that server log lines stop reading "Connected portals X <-> Y" (:100619) unless the mod re-emits them. Existing bases keep working across the mod install because the mod's unmanaged path is a byte-for-byte behavioural copy.

**Failure modes.**
- Prefix applied before world load lets ZDOMan's own hash-based relink (:77850) run without vanilla's follow-up tag pass, leaving imported worlds with unpaired portals
- Forgetting the IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal guard double-pairs portals owned by online clients, because a deferred RPC_SetConnection leaves the server's copy reading None within the same tick
- Returning false but failing to reimplement pass 1 leaves dangling connections that ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461) then silently drops at the next save
- A second mod patching Game.ConnectPortals stacks unpredictably; Harmony prefix ordering is undefined without explicit priority
- Caching ZDO object references between ticks: ZDOPool.Release/Get (:78286-78311) recycles objects and ZDO.Reset sets m_uid = ZDOID.None (:73536)

## 24. Phantom Anchor Fabrication

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Server-fabricated portal ZDOs at arbitrary coordinates, used as invisible destination endpoints so a hub can point anywhere without a player having built a portal there.

**How it works.** `TeleportWorld.Teleport` (:143517-143549) performs zero prefab validation on the destination: it resolves `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connectionZDOID)`, reads `GetPosition()` and `GetRotation()`, and computes `pos = position + (rotation * Vector3.forward) * m_exitDistance + Vector3.up` (:143542-143545). Any ZDO with a position and rotation is therefore a legal arrival point for a 100% vanilla client.

Create one with `ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, prefabHash)` (:76674). CreateNewZDO does NOT set the prefab on the ZDO and does NOT set Persistent — replicate `ZNetView.Awake`'s fabrication block (:82613-82620): `zdo.Persistent = true; zdo.Type = ZDO.ObjectType.Default; zdo.Distant = false; zdo.SetPrefab(hash); zdo.SetRotation(rot);`. Pass a REAL portal prefab hash from `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` to CreateNewZDO, because `AddIfPortal` (:77732-77752) fires on the hash argument, files the ZDO in `m_portalObjects`, removes it from the sector array, and sets `DirtyPortalObjects` — which is the only thing that causes the ChunkPortal save file to be written (`GetSaveClonePerChunk` :77621-77635). A ZDO created with hash 0 and then `SetPrefab`ed to a portal hash is excluded from normal chunk saves by `AddObjectsPerChunk`'s filter (:77572) AND never entered the portal chunk — it exists in RAM and vanishes on restart with no error.

Two anchor flavours. A PORTAL-prefab anchor is always resident server-side, saved, and enumerated by GetPortalList — but it instantiates a visible portal mesh on any client who comes within ~96m (`ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea`, Chebyshev ≤ 1.5×64m, :82298-82319). Place these where players are meant to arrive. A NON-portal-prefab anchor (any harmless prefab hash) is invisible to vanilla's pairer entirely but must set `Persistent = true` explicitly or it is never saved, and must be resolvable by the traveller's client.

Delivery: the traveller's `TargetFound` (:143640-143656) requires the client to actually HOLD the target ZDO; if absent it fires `RequestZDO` and returns false with no message. The server answers via `RPC_RequestZDO` → `ForceSendZDO` (:77689-77692), so the second walk-through works. Pre-warm with `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerUid, anchorId)` (:77714) when a player approaches.

**Player experience.** A player walks into a hub portal and arrives standing one metre in front of an anchor, facing the direction the server chose. If the anchor uses a portal prefab they see a real portal there and can walk back through it. If it uses a non-portal prefab they arrive at what looks like empty ground — no structure at all, which reads as a genuine teleport-to-coordinates. The first attempt after a fresh server-side re-point to a never-visited region can silently do nothing: the player walks in, the screen does not fade, no message appears (gate 1 of Teleport returns without calling player.Message, :143519-143522). They step out, step back in, and it works.

**Failure modes.**
- CreateNewZDO with the wrong prefab hash produces a ZDO that exists in RAM and is silently lost at world save
- Anchor in an unvisited region: first transit is a completely silent no-op (no fade, no message) while RequestZDO round-trips — the single worst UX bug in this whole design space
- Portal-prefab anchors are visible structures; players will try to demolish them, and WearNTear RPC_Damage/RPC_Remove are client-executed and unobservable to the server (:150332/:150419)
- ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461) only persists a connection when BOTH endpoints resolve in m_objectsByID — a deleted anchor silently loses the link across a restart
- Never call zdo.SetPosition() on a portal-prefab anchor: ZDO.SetSector early-returns for portals (:73752-73757) so it stays filed under its creation sector forever, and HandleDestroyedZDO (:76980) then looks it up by the new index and leaks it

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover

## 25. Rotating Hub

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small-medium

A hub portal whose Portal connection cycles through an ordered ring of destinations on a fixed schedule, rewritten server-side.

**How it works.** A mod subsystem holds `{hubPositionKey, ZDOID[] destinations, int index, double nextRotateAt}`. On each `OnUpdate(dt)` tick (recommended 0.2s; cost is one dictionary lookup plus a comparison against `ZNet.instance.GetTimeSeconds()` :81546) it checks whether `nextRotateAt` has passed. If so it resolves the hub ZDO fresh via `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(hubId)` — never a cached ZDO object, because ZDOPool recycles them (:78286-78311) — advances the index, and performs the write triad: `SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, `SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, destinations[index])`, `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(hubId)`.

Propagation is fast and deterministic. `ForceSendZDO(ZDOID)` adds the id to every `ZDOPeer.m_forceSend` (:77706-77712); `AddForceSendZdos` inserts it at index 0 of that peer's sync list (:77275), ahead of everything else; `SendZDOToPeers2` services one peer per Update frame behind a 0.05s gate (:76837-76862). So the new connection reaches a standing player in roughly 50-100ms plus RTT, not seconds.

THE RACE, QUANTIFIED. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` re-reads `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` at the instant of transit (:143539) — nothing is cached. So a player who enters the trigger during the propagation window (~50-200ms) goes to the OLD destination; a player who enters after it goes to the new one. There is no in-between state and no torn read: the connection is a single ZDOID field written atomically inside one `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` call (:74951-74961) and serialized as one byte + one ZDOID (`ZDO.Serialize` :74169-74173). The change IS atomic from the client's point of view.

What is NOT within that window: the 0.5s `UpdatePortal` poll (`InvokeRepeating("UpdatePortal", 0.5f, 0.5f)`, :143450) is purely cosmetic — it spawns the `m_connected` EffectList on the rising edge of `HaveTarget()` and drives `m_target_found.SetActive(...)` (:143491-143509). It does not gate teleporting. The 5s vanilla reconciler is irrelevant once pairing is taken over.

If the new destination ZDO is not held by the traveller's client, `TargetFound` returns false and the walk-through silently does nothing (:143646-143654). Pre-warm the whole ring with `ForceSendZDO(peerUid, destId)` for every peer within ~200m of the hub on rotation, or simply once per peer join.

**Player experience.** A player standing at the hub sees the portal glowing and connected. At the rotation instant: within ~0.1s the destination has changed under them with no visual cue at all (the emission colour only changes when HaveTarget flips, and it never flipped). They walk in and arrive somewhere new. If the server blacked out the link first (see Blackout Swap), they instead see the glow die within 0.5s and the emission fade to m_colorUnconnected over ~1 second (Update lerps m_colorAlpha at 1.0/sec, :143513), hover text flips to "$piece_portal_unconnected", then the connected VFX/SFX puff fires when the new link lands. A player ALREADY STANDING inside the trigger volume when the swap lands does not re-trigger — OnTriggerEnter fires on ENTER only (:143673) — so they must step out and back in, which is an invisible, confusing dead portal until they move.

**Failure modes.**
- Silent no-op on the first transit to a cold destination (TargetFound → RequestZDO → return false, no player.Message) — the player reports 'the portal is broken'
- Player standing inside the trigger volume never re-triggers after a swap (OnTriggerEnter only, :143673)
- Without Pairing Authority Takeover, Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 tears the link down within 5s because the destination's s_tag differs from the hub's (:100601)
- A mid-transit rotation is harmless — Player.UpdateTeleport pins m_teleportTargetPos as a snapshot the moment TeleportTo is accepted (:15343) — but the traveller's arrival is the OLD target and the hub now points elsewhere, so their return walk lands somewhere else
- Rotating faster than ~10s makes the hub effectively unusable: the ~8s hard floor on a distantTeleport (Player.UpdateTeleport :15349) means a player can depart and the hub has already moved on by the time they land
- No delta encoding: ZDOMan.SendZDOs re-serializes the entire ZDO per peer per send (:77056-77064), ~80-120 bytes per rotation per in-range peer

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover; Phantom Anchor Fabrication (only if destinations are not real player-built portals)

## 26. Blackout Swap Protocol

`FEASIBLE` · `CLIENT-HONOURED` · effort: small-medium

A three-phase rotation (announce → disconnect → re-point) that turns an invisible destination change into a legible, signposted event on a vanilla client.

**How it works.** A bare connection rewrite is atomic but INVISIBLE — the player has no way to know the destination changed. This protocol spends time to buy legibility, using the only three vanilla-client-visible portal channels the server controls: the tag string, the connected/unconnected state, and the connected EffectList.

Phase 1, T-30s (announce). Write `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, "Swamp 30s")` (:73721, key at :78617) then `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702) — a tag-only write does NOT set DirtyPortalObjects and is silently lost at the next world save otherwise (only SetConnection/AddIfPortal/HandleDestroyedZDO set it, :73661/:77750/:76986). `GetHoverText` renders it live as `$piece_portal $piece_portal_tag:"Swamp 30s"` every frame the player hovers (:143453-143463). There is NO server-side length cap — the 10-character limit lives only in the client's `TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` (:143482). Rich text is stripped by `RemoveRichTextTags()` (:143459), so no colour.

Phase 2, T-0 (blackout). `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` + ForceSendZDO. Within ~0.1s the client's next `UpdatePortal` (≤0.5s) sets `m_hadTarget=false`, `m_target_found` glow goes dark, and `Update` lerps the emission from `m_colorTargetfound` to `m_colorUnconnected` at 1.0/sec (:143513). Hover flips to `$piece_portal_unconnected` (:143461). Crucially, a walk-through during blackout hits gate 1 of Teleport and returns silently with no message (:143519-143522) — the portal is safely inert, not mis-routed. Hold for a configured dwell (recommended 2-4s: long enough that the client's 0.5s poll definitely saw the flip and the colour visibly moved).

Phase 3 (re-point). Write the new connection + new tag. The client's next UpdatePortal sees `HaveTarget()` newly true and fires `m_connected.Create(transform.position, transform.rotation)` (:143499) — the vanilla portal-activation VFX and sound, at the portal, for free. Total legible swap: ~3-5s, of which ~2-4s is unusable.

Tick budget: one timer per hub, evaluated at 0.2s. Trivial.

**Player experience.** A player hovering the hub reads `$piece_portal_tag:"Swamp 30s"`. Thirty seconds later the portal's blue glow visibly fades to its unlit colour over about a second and the hover line changes to "$piece_portal_unconnected". They walk through and nothing happens — no fade, no message — which reads as 'it's off right now' rather than 'it's broken'. Two seconds later the portal audibly and visually snaps back on (the same effect a portal plays when it first finds a partner), and hovering now reads `$piece_portal_tag:"Swamp"`. It reads like a scheduled train, not a glitch.

**Failure modes.**
- A player who opens the tag dialog during announce sees the server's long tag pre-filled into a field whose characterLimit is 10 (TextInput.Show :61515-61522) and can save back a truncated string — keep announce tags ≤10 chars or accept the corruption
- Tag writes are silently lost at the next world save unless ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() is called explicitly (:76702)
- Under Pairing Authority Takeover this is safe; WITHOUT it, changing the tag instantly breaks the vanilla pair (tag equality at :100601) and pass 2 re-pairs the portal randomly
- No colour or size markup is possible — RemoveRichTextTags (:143459) strips it from the hover string, and Chat.OnNewChatMessage replaces '<' and '>' with spaces on the other text channels
- The blackout window is a real outage: a player who arrives mid-blackout and does not hover has no idea why walking in does nothing

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover; Rotating Hub

**Citations.** TeleportWorld.GetHoverText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143463 · TeleportWorld.Interact (10-char TextInput cap) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143482 · TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag (no length check, no filter) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143587-143602 · TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal (m_connected on rising edge) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143496-143507 · TeleportWorld.Update (emission lerp) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143511-143515 · TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1 (silent return) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143519-143522 · ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702-76705 · ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision / SetDirtySector — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73832-73840 · StringExtensionMethods.RemoveRichTextTags — assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703

## 27. One-Way Ring Rotation

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Exploit vanilla's missing reciprocity check to build a stable A→B→C→A ring, then rotate the whole network by rewriting a single edge.

**How it works.** `Game.ConnectPortals` pass 1's teardown predicate is exactly `zDO == null || zDO.GetString(s_tag) != tag || zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None` (:100600-100604). It never checks that the partner points BACK. So a ring, a chain, a fan-in hub and even a self-loop all survive vanilla's own reconciler indefinitely, provided every member shares one byte-identical tag string and no member's connection is None.

That makes a one-way ring the cheapest possible rotating network: N portals all tagged `"ring"`, with A→B, B→C, C→A. To "rotate", you do not rewrite N connections — you rewrite one edge and the topology shifts. To advance every member by one step you do rewrite N, but each write is the same three-line triad and the whole batch commits within one tick.

The killer caveat is persistence. The on-disk format collapses each ZDO to a single `ZDOConnectionHashData{type, int hash}` slot: `RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461-75478) gives the source `{Portal, h}` and the target `{Portal|Target, h}`. One slot per ZDO means the disk format can only express a pairwise perfect matching. Processing C overwrites A's source slot with a Target slot, so after a save/reload only one pair relinks and the rest are unconnected. Worse, `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (the load-time hash relinker, :77850-77893) writes RECIPROCAL connections on both ends — so a surviving one-way link comes back two-way. A self-loop A→A is erased outright (:75472-75475 writes then immediately overwrites the same key).

Mitigation is mandatory and simple: the mod re-asserts the entire ring from its own config in `OnWorldReady`, before any peer connects. At that moment `m_peers` is empty, `ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner)` is always null, every write takes the immediate local path, and the server owns both ends of everything (ZDO.Load resets OwnerRevision/DataRevision to 0 and Owned to false, :74550-74556). That pre-peer window is the cheapest time in the whole server lifecycle to write a topology.

Also re-assert on a slow heartbeat (30-60s) because `ZDO.SetConnection` is a no-op when the value is unchanged (`ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` early-returns on identical type+target, :74954-74957), so idempotent re-assertion costs zero DataRevision bumps and zero network traffic.

**Player experience.** A player learns that the Meadows gate always leads to the Black Forest gate, which always leads to the Swamp gate, which leads back to Meadows — a genuine one-way circuit rather than a pair. Hover text on every gate reads `$piece_portal_connected` and they all share the tag "ring", so nothing looks unusual. After a rotation the same physical door now opens onto the next stop in the circuit, with the swap either invisible (~0.1s) or signposted via the Blackout Swap Protocol. Crucially, walking back through the arrival portal does NOT return them to where they came from — it advances them another step around the ring, which is the whole point and must be taught.

**Failure modes.**
- Rings do not survive a save/load: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461) has one hash slot per ZDO and can only express a pairwise matching — the mod MUST re-assert at OnWorldReady or the ring silently degrades to one pair plus orphans
- One-way links come back BIDIRECTIONAL after a restart because ZDOMan.ConnectPortals writes both ends (:77879-77885)
- Self-loops (A→A) are erased at save time — do not use one as a 'parked' state
- If any single member's connection goes None, pass 1 tears down its neighbours' links too (the q.GetConnectionZDOID == None clause, :100601), cascading
- Players find one-way navigation disorienting; without tag signposting they will report portals as 'randomly moving'

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover

**Citations.** Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 (no reciprocity check) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100598-100605 · ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75461-75478 · ZDOExtraData.PrepareSave — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75480-75491 · ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (load-time reciprocal relink) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77850-77893 · ZDOExtraData.SetConnection (idempotent early-return) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74951-74961 · ZDO.Load (revisions reset, unowned) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74550-74556 · ZDOMan.LoadChunks — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76474-76531

## 28. Scheduled Routing (In-Game and Real-World Clocks)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small-medium

Destinations chosen by in-game day fraction, in-game day counter, or wall-clock time — including portals that only resolve during a window.

**How it works.** Three independent clocks, all readable on a dedicated server.

(1) IN-GAME TIME OF DAY. `EnvMan.instance.GetDayFraction()` returns `m_smoothDayFraction` (:96290-96293), and the statics `EnvMan.IsDay()`, `IsNight()`, `IsAfternoon()` (:96363-96376) are recomputed in `EnvMan.FixedUpdate` (:95736-95743) from `ZNet.instance.GetTimeSeconds()` (:95697) on EVERY machine including headless — only `UpdateTriggers` early-returns on a null local player (:95753). Proof that EnvMan.instance is live on a dedicated server: `Game.UpdateSleeping` sits behind `if (!ZNet.instance.IsServer()) return;` and then dereferences `EnvMan.instance.IsTimeSkipping()`, `EnvMan.IsAfternoon()`, `EnvMan.IsNight()` and `EnvMan.instance.SkipToMorning()` unguarded (:100714-100731). Night is `dayFraction <= 0.25 || >= 0.75` (:96457-96465).

(2) IN-GAME DAY COUNTER. `EnvMan.instance.GetDay()` = `(int)(ZNet.GetTimeSeconds() / m_dayLengthSec)` with `m_dayLengthSec = 1200` (:96295-96303, :95406). Lets a portal open on every 5th day, or change destination as the world ages.

(3) REAL-WORLD CLOCK. Plain `DateTime.UtcNow` in the mod. Independent of world time and immune to sleep-skipping.

Implementation: one subsystem evaluates a per-portal schedule expression at 1Hz (cheaper than the 0.2s hub tick — clock granularity does not need 5 ticks/sec). It computes the target destination index, compares to the last-written index, and only writes on change (`ZDO.SetConnection` is a no-op if unchanged, :74954-74957, so a blind re-write every tick is also safe but produces no traffic). Window portals write `ZDOID.None` outside the window — the portal then reads `$piece_portal_unconnected` (:143461), the glow dies within 0.5s, and a walk-through silently does nothing (:143519-143522), which is a legible 'closed' affordance for free.

THE SLEEP-SKIP GOTCHA: in-game time is not monotonic at a steady rate. `Game.UpdateSleeping` calls `EnvMan.SkipToMorning()` when every connected character has `ZDOVars.s_inBed` set (:100727-100729, `EverybodyIsTryingToSleep` :100735-100750), which ramps `ZNet.SetNetTime` forward over ~12 seconds (`UpdateTimeSkip`, :96310-96323; `m_timeSkipSpeed = delta / 12.0`, :96339). A schedule keyed on day fraction can jump an entire evening in 12 real seconds. Guard every transition with 'did the index change' rather than 'did we cross a boundary this tick', or an edge-triggered schedule silently skips.

**Player experience.** The player learns a routine. The stone circle gate reads `$piece_portal_unconnected` and its runes are dark through the whole day; at dusk the glow comes up with the vanilla connect sound and the hover line flips to connected, and it now leads to the Swamp outpost. A hover-time tag reading "Dusk only" (written once, permanently) teaches this without any documentation. On a server running a real-world raid night, the raid gate is dead all week and lights up at 20:00 local. If someone sleeps through the night, the gate can flick closed and open again inside 12 real seconds — visible as the glow dying and coming straight back.

**Failure modes.**
- Sleep-skip warps in-game time forward ~12 real seconds across a whole night (EnvMan.UpdateTimeSkip :96310-96323) — edge-triggered schedules skip their transition entirely; use level-triggered 'compute target, compare, write'
- EnvMan.instance null on some headless configuration would NRE the scheduler; guard it even though vanilla's own server code does not
- GetDayFraction is m_smoothDayFraction, which is LerpAngle-smoothed at 0.01 per FixedUpdate (:95704-95705) — it lags true fraction slightly and is not exactly 0 at midnight; do not test for equality
- A window that closes while a player is mid-transit is harmless (the destination was snapshotted at TeleportTo, Player.UpdateTeleport :15343) but their return leg is now dead
- Real-world schedules and in-game schedules on the same portal will contradict each other; pick one authority per portal

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover

**Citations.** EnvMan.GetDayFraction — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:96290-96293 · EnvMan.GetDay / GetDay(double) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:96295-96303 · EnvMan.IsDay/IsNight/IsAfternoon statics — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:96363-96376 · EnvMan.FixedUpdate (statics recomputed headless) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:95685-95744 · EnvMan.m_dayLengthSec = 1200 — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:95406 · Game.UpdateSleeping (server-only, dereferences EnvMan.instance) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100712-100733 · EnvMan.SkipToMorning / UpdateTimeSkip — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:96310-96341 · ZNet.GetTimeSeconds — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81546-81549 · TeleportWorld.GetHoverText (connected/unconnected) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143461

## 29. Progression-Gated Sealed Gate

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

A portal that resolves to nothing until the world has a given global key (boss defeated, quest flag), then permanently or conditionally opens.

**How it works.** The gate condition is a world global key. Reading is a plain dictionary lookup: `ZoneSystem.instance.GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.defeated_bonemass)` (:115948) or the string overload `GetGlobalKey("my_mod_flag")` (:115968) against `m_globalKeysEnums` / `m_globalKeysValues` (:113305-113309). Custom string keys are free — anything that does not parse as a `GlobalKeys` member is classified `NonServerOption` by `GetKeyValue` (:113560-113581) and persists in the world .db rather than the .fwl.

The subsystem evaluates each sealed gate at 1Hz: if the key is absent, hold `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)`; if present, write the real destination. Because `ZDO.SetConnection` early-returns on an unchanged value (:74954-74957) the steady state costs literally zero — no DataRevision bump, no packet. That makes 'blindly re-assert every tick' the correct implementation, and it also means the gate self-heals against anyone who tampers with the connection: `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653-100662) is an unauthenticated global routed RPC any client can invoke to rewire any portal, and a 1Hz re-assert reverts it within a second.

For an event-driven (rather than polled) version, postfix the private `ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd(string)` (:113483-113513), which is the single funnel for every key write. CRITICAL TRAP, already paid for by Wonderland's BossDefeatWatch: `ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys` re-adds EVERY persisted server-option key on every boot (:115904-115931), so a naive postfix re-fires the 'boss just died' handler for historical kills at every restart. Snapshot the existing key set in OnWorldReady and diff against it.

Hardening: `RPC_SetGlobalKey` and `RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` perform ZERO sender validation (:116022-116037) — any connected vanilla client can set or clear any key on the server. If a gate is meant to be earned, Harmony-prefix both RPCs to drop packets whose true sender (resolved by matching `p.m_rpc == rpc` over `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()`) is not an admin.

**Player experience.** A player finds a large stone portal in a ruin. Its runes are dark; hovering reads `$piece_portal $piece_portal_tag:"Sealed" [$piece_portal_unconnected]`. Walking into it does nothing at all — no message, no fade. Weeks later the server kills Bonemass; within one second the gate's runes light up with the vanilla portal-connect sound and hover now reads `$piece_portal_tag:"The Deep Road" [$piece_portal_connected]`. Everyone online near it sees it happen simultaneously. Walking in now takes them to the Mistlands outpost.

**Failure modes.**
- Any client can set or clear the gating key: RPC_SetGlobalKey has no sender check (:116022-116029). Without a prefix hardening it, a gate is one packet away from being opened
- Server-option keys (ordinals 0-40) are mirrored into ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys and baked into the .fwl permanently (GlobalKeyAdd :113511) — use a custom NonServerOption string key for mod gates so uninstalling the mod leaves nothing behind
- A GlobalKeyAdd postfix re-fires for every historical key at every boot via SetStartingGlobalKeys (:115904-115931)
- The 'sealed' state is indistinguishable from 'broken' to a player who does not hover — always carry an explanatory tag string
- GlobalKeyAdd unconditionally dereferences Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile() (:113506) and its UpdateWorldRates tail dereferences Minimap.instance (:101203); calling it too early in startup NREs before SendGlobalKeys

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover

## 30. Event-Driven Retarget

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Destinations that change in response to live world events — a raid starting, a boss being alerted, a global key write — rather than a clock.

**How it works.** Three server-readable event sources, in descending order of reliability.

(1) GLOBAL KEY WRITES. Postfix `ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd(string)` (:113483) — the single funnel for every key mutation, including the server's own and any client's forged one. Diff against an OnWorldReady snapshot to suppress boot replay. This covers boss defeats (`defeated_*`), world modifiers, and any custom mod key. Latency: synchronous, zero.

(2) RANDOM EVENTS / RAIDS. `RandEventSystem` genuinely runs server-side: its update path is gated on `ZNet.instance.IsServer()` (:106793-106798) and `UpdateRandomEvent(dt)` (:106838) selects events. The mod can read the private `m_randomEvent` (:106749) by reflection or publicizer for name/position/time, and `SetRandomEventByName(string name, Vector3 pos)` (:107067) is PUBLIC — so the mod can even force an event and retarget portals in the same tick. `SendCurrentRandomEvent` broadcasts `"SetEvent"` to all peers (:106952-106961), so client and server agree.

(3) BOSS ACTIVITY. `GlobalKeys.activeBosses` is a float key incremented by `BaseAI.SetAlerted` on whichever CLIENT owns the boss (:27258-27259) and decremented on death (:3163-3164). The server can read it with `GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, out float v)` (:115958). Use it to blackout a network during a boss fight, or to open a 'boss arena' gate.

Implementation: a 1Hz evaluator computes each managed portal's target from a small rule table `(condition → destination)` and writes on change. Rules are level-triggered, not edge-triggered, so a missed tick is self-correcting.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK SERVER-SIDE: `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent()` (:106939-106950) reads `EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss()`, and EnemyHud's `m_huds` dictionary is filled in `LateUpdate` relative to `Player.m_localPlayer.transform.position` — permanently empty headless, so the server's own GetBossEvent always returns null. That matters because it is one half of the client-side `NoBossPortals` condition in `TeleportWorld.Teleport` (:143528): the client evaluates it locally and the server cannot predict the result. `activeBosses` is the only half the server can observe.

Also note `activeBosses` can leak above zero if the boss-owning client crashes mid-fight, permanently blocking every portal on the server if NoBossPortals is set; a server mod should watch for and zero it with `SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, 0f)` (:115933).

**Player experience.** A raid siren goes up over the player's base. They run to their portal hall and find that every gate has gone dark except one, whose tag now reads "Muster" and which leads to the fortified keep — the server retargeted the whole network the instant the event fired. When the raid ends, the gates relight one by one on their normal destinations. Separately: the moment someone on the server drops Moder, a previously sealed mountain gate lights up for everyone simultaneously, with the vanilla connect sound playing at every instance of it.

**Failure modes.**
- RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() always returns null server-side (EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss, :106941-106944) — the server cannot predict the client-side NoBossPortals gate
- GlobalKeys.activeBosses is maintained by the boss-owning CLIENT (BaseAI.SetAlerted :27258) and leaks above zero if that client crashes mid-fight
- Any client can forge a global key write (RPC_SetGlobalKey has no sender validation, :116022), so an event-driven retarget is trivially triggerable by a hostile client unless the RPC is hardened
- m_randomEvent is private — a publicizer or reflection dependency that can break across patches
- A GlobalKeyAdd postfix fires during SetStartingGlobalKeys at boot for every historical key (:115904-115931)
- Retargeting many portals at once floods every peer: ZDOMan.SendZDOs has no delta encoding (:77056-77064) and the send queue caps at 10240 bytes (:77011). Budget writes per sweep (Wonderland's StructureUpkeep uses 256)

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover

## 31. Deterministic Assignment Replacement

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

Replace vanilla's uniformly-random same-tag pairing with nearest / oldest / round-robin / least-recently-used selection, via a one-method Harmony postfix.

**How it works.** The lowest-risk, highest-value intervention in the whole space. `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(List<ZDO> portals, ZDO skip, string tag)` (:100664-100679) is private, builds a candidate list filtered on reference inequality with `skip`, exact `s_tag` string equality, `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == None`, and `!IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal`, then returns `list[UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, list.Count)]` from the shared unseeded global RNG.

A Harmony POSTFIX on `AccessTools.Method(typeof(Game), "FindRandomUnconnectedPortal")` that overwrites `__result` replaces the selection policy while leaving every other vanilla behaviour — the two-phase commit through `m_currentlyConnectingPortals`, the ownership handling in `SetConnection`, the logging — completely intact. The postfix receives the same candidate universe via `__args` and can rebuild the filtered list itself (the filter is four cheap predicates) then pick by policy:

• NEAREST: minimise `Vector3.Distance(skip.GetPosition(), c.GetPosition())`. Makes a large same-tag group behave like a sensible local network instead of a lottery.
• OLDEST / STABLE: sort candidates by `m_uid.UserID` then `m_uid.ID` and take the first. Deterministic across ticks; note it is NOT stable across restarts because ZDOIDs are renumbered (`ZDO.Load` :74552) — sort by rounded position for true restart stability.
• ROUND-ROBIN: a mod-side per-tag cursor advanced on each successful pair.
• LEAST-RECENTLY-USED: a mod-side per-portal 'last transit' timestamp fed by the position-straddle transit detector; pick the candidate with the oldest timestamp to spread traffic.
• LOAD-BALANCED: count how many portals currently point at each candidate and pick the minimum.

This also fixes vanilla's permanent-orphan behaviour. With N≥3 same-tag portals, the first iterated portal picks randomly from the rest, the second finds every remaining candidate excluded, and exactly one member is stranded forever (subsequent ticks re-confirm the surviving pair). Iteration order is `Dictionary<SectorIndex, List<ZDO>>` bucket order — arbitrary and not stable across restarts — so which portal is orphaned changes on reboot. A deterministic replacement picker makes that predictable, and a mod-side detector can flag the orphan in a Heartbeat line or a Discord report.

Tick budget: runs only inside the existing 5s vanilla pass, over a candidate list that is almost always 1-3 entries. Free.

**Player experience.** A player with five portals all tagged "home" stops seeing them shuffle partners at random every time one is rebuilt. The nearest-pairing policy means the two gates in the same building always link to each other, and the distant one links to its own neighbour. With LRU, a busy hub distributes arrivals across several outposts instead of hammering one. The permanently-stranded fifth portal, which vanilla leaves dead forever with no explanation, now either pairs predictably or shows up in a server report as 'orphaned: tag "home" has an odd member'.

**Failure modes.**
- A private method target — AccessTools.Method by string name; a Valheim rename breaks it silently unless wrapped in SafePatch with a logged warning
- Sorting by ZDOID is not stable across restarts (ZDO.Load renumbers, :74552); use rounded position for restart-stable ordering
- Must not drop the IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal filter (:100671) or portals owned by online peers double-pair within a tick
- UnityEngine.Random.Range is the int overload and max-exclusive (:100678) — a replacement that uses the float overload off-by-ones the last candidate
- Nearest-pairing over a very large same-tag group is O(n) per call inside an O(n) loop; cap candidate scanning or pre-bucket by tag

**Citations.** Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100664-100679 · Game.ConnectPortals pass 2 — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100607-100622 · Game.IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100700-100710 · ZDO.Load (ZDOID renumbering) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74552 · ZDOMan.GetPortalList (bucket-order iteration) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77648-77656 · ZDOID.ToString / ZDO.ToString — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73514-73517

## 32. Approach-Triggered Just-In-Time Routing

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium-large

Detect a player closing on a portal from their character ZDO position and write THEIR destination into the portal before they reach the trigger collider — the closest a shared portal can get to per-player routing.

**How it works.** The transit decision is unhookable, but the APPROACH is fully observable. The owning client's `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` writes `zdo.SetPosition(GetPosition())` into the character ZDO every physics tick (:87527-87540), and client→server ZDO delivery is distance-independent via `m_clientChangeQueue` drained by `CreateSyncList`'s non-server branch (:77241-77258) on the same 0.05s round-robin (:76843-76852). So server-side character positions are fresh to roughly 50-150ms including RTT.

The loop: every 0.1s, for each `(ZNetPeer peer, ZDO characterZdo)` pair from `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` + `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID)` (Wonderland's ConnectedCharacters wraps exactly this), compute distance to each managed JIT portal. On crossing an outer radius R_arm (recommend 12m), the mod: (a) looks up that player's selected destination from its own registry keyed on `ZDOVars.s_playerID` (:78539); (b) calls `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, destinationId)` (:77714) to guarantee the client HOLDS the destination ZDO, because `TargetFound` requires it (:143646-143654); (c) writes the connection with the standard triad and `ForceSendZDO(portalId)`.

TIMING BUDGET. A sprinting player moves ~5-6 m/s. From 12m the lead time is ~2.0-2.4s. Detection costs up to 0.1s (poll) + ~0.15s (position staleness); the write reaches the client in ~0.05-0.2s. Total ~0.45s worst case, leaving ~1.5s of margin. At R_arm = 20m the margin doubles. The trigger collider itself is small (`m_activationRange = 5f` is only the glow radius, :143411; the collider is a separate child object of unknown size, :143664-143682).

CONTENTION is the fatal flaw and must be designed around explicitly. Two players inside R_arm at once share one ZDOID field. Policies: (1) FIRST-CLAIM LOCK — the first arriver locks the portal for T seconds; a second arriver gets a `PlayerNotify.Toast` ('gate busy') and the destination is not changed under the first. The second player can still physically walk in and be sent to the first player's destination — unavoidable. (2) BLACKOUT-ON-CONTENTION — write None while two claimants are present; both are safely blocked (silently, gate 1 at :143519) rather than mis-routed. (3) Accept it and use per-player terminals instead.

A second failure: a player who reverses direction after arming leaves the portal pointing at their destination for the lock duration. Disarm on leaving R_arm + hysteresis.

**Player experience.** A player walks toward the hub gate. At about 12 metres out — before they can see any change, because the portal's glow does not encode the destination — the server has already pointed the gate at the outpost they selected earlier at the terminal. They walk straight in and arrive where they chose, with no pause, no menu, and no extra step. It genuinely feels like the portal knows who they are. Then a second player runs up behind them: that player gets a HUD toast reading 'Gate is claimed — wait 6s', and if they push through anyway they land at the first player's destination, which is the moment the illusion breaks.

**Failure modes.**
- CONTENTION: two players inside the arming radius share one connection field. Someone will be mis-routed, or blocked, with no good third option
- A player who arms and then turns away leaves the portal mis-set for the lock duration unless disarmed with hysteresis
- Position staleness spikes on a laggy client: peer.m_refPos is only refreshed every 2s (ZNet.SendPeriodicData :80337) — you MUST use the character ZDO position, not peer.GetRefPos()
- A dead or teleporting player's ZDO position is stale/garbage; skip on zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead) (:78403)
- If the destination ZDO has not reached the client, the first walk-through is a silent no-op — the ForceSendZDO pre-warm is mandatory, not optional
- A player arriving by portal lands at ~5m/s with no approach phase; the arming radius may never fire before they step back in

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover; Phantom Anchor Fabrication

## 33. Per-Player Private Portal Terminals

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: large

Give every player their own physical portal; because only they ever use it, its pre-written destination IS a per-player destination. The honest answer to 'can routing be per-player'.

**How it works.** Per-player routing is impossible at the protocol layer (see the ruled-out Per-Peer Divergent ZDO Routing option). The workaround is physical, not technical: one portal per player.

IDENTITY. A player-built portal already carries its builder: `Piece.SetCreator` writes `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) — the builder's PlayerProfile UID, identical to `ZDOVars.s_playerID` on their character ZDO (:78539, `Player.SetPlayerID` :10129-10136) — plus `s_creatorIndex` (:78395) indexing `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` (:112396), which the server persists in the .fwl from socket-verified PlatformUserIDs. So the mod can enumerate `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (:77648), read `s_creator`, and know whose terminal each portal is with zero extra bookkeeping. Note `SetCreator` only writes when `GetCreator() == 0 && m_nview.IsOwner()` (:136417), so world-gen and pre-mod portals read 0.

SELECTION. The player chooses a destination by an observable gesture at their own terminal: an emote (`ZDOVars.s_emote` / `s_emoteID` polled at 0.25s, Wonderland's EmoteSignals), a map ping (`Chat.SendPing` broadcasts "ChatMessage" at targetPeerID 0 with the clicked world position — always reaches the server, :42058-42068), or an item placed on an adjacent ItemStand (`ZDOVars.s_item`, :78465). The mod stores `playerID → destinationId` in a position-keyed or playerID-keyed file — NEVER a ZDOID-keyed one (`ZDO.Load` renumbers, :74552).

WRITING. On selection change, the standard triad against that player's terminal only. No contention: only one player's selection ever touches that ZDO.

OUTBOUND IS FULLY SOLVED. INBOUND IS NOT, and this is the honest limit. A terminal T_p can point one-way at a shared public portal D_i (non-reciprocity is stable under vanilla's pass 1, :100598-100605 — but only if both carry the same tag, which pairing takeover makes free). The RETURN leg from D_i is shared: D_i has exactly one connection field, so it cannot send different players home. Three options: (a) one anchor per (player × destination) — N×M portal ZDOs, e.g. 20 players × 10 destinations = 200 extra ZDOs, which is fine for the server (portals are always resident and saved wholesale into ChunkPortal, :77621) but visually absurd unless the anchors use a non-portal prefab; (b) JIT approach-routing on the return portal, inheriting its contention; (c) a server-issued forced teleport home via `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, true)` (:41957-41968) triggered by an emote at the arrival point — which bypasses the ore check and every global key.

ACCESS CONTROL IS NOT POSSIBLE. Wards do not gate walking through a portal, and `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` (:137547) iterates `m_allAreas`, permanently empty server-side, so it returns true vacuously. The only enforcement is architectural: put the terminal behind a door inside a warded base.

SCALE. 2 ZDOs per player minimum. `GetPortalList()` allocates a fresh List per call — cache it on a 1-5s tick; vanilla already allocates one every 5s.

**Player experience.** Each player has a personal gate in their own base, distinguishable by a tag the server writes for them ("Rohan → Swamp"). They walk up to it, do the /point emote, and a HUD toast lists the next destination in their personal rotation; emoting again cycles it, and the gate's runes flicker off and back on as each new destination is written. When they walk through, they arrive exactly where their own gate said — every time, regardless of what anyone else is doing. The illusion is complete as long as nobody else walks into THEIR gate, at which point that person is sent to the owner's destination. Coming back is the rough edge: the public arrival portal leads to one fixed place, so the trip home either uses a second personal anchor they built at that destination, or a 'go home' emote that the server honours with a forced teleport.

**Failure modes.**
- No access control exists: any player who reaches another player's terminal uses that player's destination. PrivateArea.CheckAccess returns true vacuously server-side (empty m_allAreas, :137173/:137547)
- The return leg is fundamentally shared unless one anchor per (player × destination) is fabricated
- ZDOVars.s_creator is 0 for any portal placed before the mod or by an admin (Piece.SetCreator only writes once when creator == 0, :136417)
- A player who rebuilds their terminal gets a new ZDOID; the registry must key on s_creator + rounded position, not ZDOID
- Player count scaling: every terminal is a persistent portal ZDO resident in RAM forever (portals are never unloaded, ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS only reassigns ownership :76872-76885)
- Server-issued forced teleport as a return leg bypasses the ore/metal check entirely — Player inventories are never in any ZDO so the server cannot reproduce it (ZdoInventoryIO documents this)
- A forced teleport silently no-ops if the target teleported in the last 2s (Player.TeleportTo :15309-15316) and latches forever on a dead player (UpdateTeleport runs only in the !IsDead branch, :10213/:10226)

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover; Phantom Anchor Fabrication; Player-Requested Routing

## 34. Queue Dispatch

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

"The next player to arrive gets the next target" — achievable only as arrival-detection plus a lock, not as a true queue, because the server cannot observe the moment of transit before it happens.

**How it works.** Honest assessment first: a true queue is NOT observable. The only call site of `TeleportWorld.Teleport` is `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter`, gated on `Player.m_localPlayer == component` (:143664-143682), so the server never learns that a transit is about to happen and never learns it happened as an event. There is no RPC, no ZDO write, no ownership handshake at the moment of transit.

What IS observable is (a) arrival near the portal, and (b) the transit AFTER the fact. (a) is the approach detector described in Approach-Triggered JIT Routing. (b) is Wonderland's `PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit(fromPos, toPos, radius=40f)`, which walks `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals()` (:77643, the live dictionary, zero-alloc) and flags a transit when both endpoints of a position sample sit within 40m of some portal, additionally following one endpoint's `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` to check the linked target is within 60m of the other endpoint. It was built to suppress a false positive — a 3s sample across a portal reads as ~110 m/s against a 40 m/s ceiling — and is already production-tested.

So the implementable feature is: maintain an ordered destination list and a per-portal cursor. When a player crosses the arming radius, atomically (a) claim the portal for that playerID, (b) write `destinations[cursor]`, (c) advance the cursor, (d) start a T-second lock. The NEXT player to arm after the lock expires gets the next destination. That satisfies the intent of 'next arrival gets the next target' with a visible, explainable rule.

Detection resolution: the position poll can run at 0.1s (far tighter than PositionWatch's 3s default) because character ZDO positions are fresh to ~50-150ms. Cost per tick is |peers| × |managed portals| squared-distance tests — trivial below a few thousand.

CONFIRMATION after the fact: to know a dispatch actually consumed, sample positions at 0.1s and detect a >40m jump whose origin is within ~8m of the portal and whose landing is within ~8m of the written destination. That is a strong, near-unambiguous signal. Suppress on `ZDOVars.s_dead` (respawn), on `Character.InInterior` boundary crossings and |Δy|>1000m (dungeon doors, interiors sit at locationY+5000, `Location.Awake` :133512, `InInterior` = y>3000 :4538-4541), and for admins (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName())`, :81811).

**Player experience.** Three players queue at the dispatch gate. The first walks up, the gate's tag flicks to "→ Crypt 3" and they go. The tag then reads "LOCKED 4s" and walking in does nothing. Four seconds later the second player steps up, the tag becomes "→ Crypt 4", and they go. It reads as a working dispatcher — but only because the lock is enforcing turn-taking; a player who sprints in during someone else's window is silently blocked (if the mod blacks out on contention) or follows the previous player (if it does not). Nobody sees a queue UI, and the server only learns that anyone actually left ~0.1-3s after the fact.

**Failure modes.**
- No pre-transit event exists anywhere: TeleportWorld.Teleport's only caller is the local-player-gated trigger (:143673-143681). A true queue cannot be built
- A player who arms and walks away consumes a queue slot unless the lock is released on leaving the arming radius
- Transit confirmation is a heuristic, not a signal — a 40m position straddle near two portals produces false positives for anyone sprinting past a portal pair
- Dungeon doors (class Teleport) have NO ZDO at all (:143316-143390) and produce large position jumps that must be suppressed via the y>3000 interior test
- Contention inside the lock window mis-routes or silently blocks; there is no third option
- peer.m_refPos is 2s stale (:80337-80345) — using it instead of the character ZDO position blows the timing budget entirely

**Prerequisites.** Approach-Triggered Just-In-Time Routing; Pairing Authority Takeover

## 35. Self-Disconnecting Portals (One-Shot and Cooldown)

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

A portal that severs its own link after a single use, or after any use for N seconds, driven by after-the-fact transit detection.

**How it works.** Two variants on one mechanism.

COOLDOWN GATE. Cheapest and most reliable. On detecting a transit through portal P (position-straddle detector at 0.1s, see Queue Dispatch), write `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` + ForceSendZDO, record `reconnectAt = ZNet.GetTimeSeconds() + cooldown`, and restore the connection when the timer expires. The player who just left is unaffected — `Player.UpdateTeleport` snapshotted `m_teleportTargetPos` when TeleportTo was accepted (:15337-15348) and completes regardless. Anyone else arriving in the window finds the portal reading `$piece_portal_unconnected`, dark, and inert (gate 1 silent return, :143519-143522).

ONE-SHOT / CONSUMABLE. Same detection, but instead of restoring, the mod either leaves the connection None permanently, or destroys the portal ZDO outright: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` then `ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)` (:76929-76935, which is a silent no-op unless you own it) — `SendDestroyed` (:76937) then broadcasts the `DestroyZDO` routed RPC to every peer and the structure vanishes from every client's world. `HandleDestroyedZDO` removes it from `m_portalObjects` and sets `DirtyPortalObjects` (:76963-76999).

THE DETECTION LATENCY IS THE FEATURE'S WEAKNESS, and it is quantifiable. The detector needs two position samples: one near the portal, one near the destination. `Player.UpdateTeleport` does not move the transform until `m_teleportTimer > 2f` (:15337) and a distantTeleport (which portals always pass, :143546) does not COMPLETE until t>8s AND `ZNetScene.IsAreaReady` (:15349), with a 15s force-land fallback (:15360-15366). The character ZDO's position therefore changes ~2s after the transit and the player is locked in place until ~8s. So the earliest the server can confirm a transit is ~2.0-2.2s after the fact — during which a second player CAN walk through the still-live portal. The one-shot is therefore one-shot-per-2-seconds, not strictly one-shot.

MITIGATION: pair it with approach detection. Arm the portal when the first claimant enters the arming radius; the instant they cross an inner radius (~3m, i.e. committed), start a speculative cooldown and blacken the link. False positives (they turned away) cost a few seconds of outage; false negatives are eliminated. This converts a 2s hole into a <0.3s hole.

**Player experience.** An adventurer finds a shimmering gate in a crypt tagged "One Way". They step through and arrive at the surface. Looking back, the gate they came from is dark — and if it was a consumable, the portal at the crypt end has simply vanished from the world with the standard destroy behaviour. Their companion, two seconds behind them, walks into the same gate and nothing happens: no fade, no message, just a dark frame. On a cooldown gate the tag reads "Recharging 18s" and the runes relight audibly when the timer expires.

**Failure modes.**
- ~2.0-2.2s blind window between the transit and the earliest possible detection, because Player.UpdateTeleport does not move the transform until m_teleportTimer > 2f (:15337). A second player can slip through
- Position-straddle detection is heuristic: a player sprinting past two nearby portals can false-positive and consume a one-shot nobody used
- ZDOMan.DestroyZDO is a silent no-op unless the server owns the ZDO (:76929-76931) — SetOwner first or nothing happens at all
- A destroyed portal's ZDOID enters m_deadZDOs (:76043/:76997) and any client replaying old ZDO data for it is force-destroyed; never recreate a portal under a reused ZDOID
- The partner portal keeps a dangling connection until the next reconcile pass — under Pairing Authority Takeover the mod must clear it itself
- Speculative blackout on inner-radius crossing produces visible flicker for players who walk near the portal without using it

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover; Queue Dispatch (shares the transit detector)

## 36. Player-Requested Routing (Ping / Emote / Item Stand)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

The player names the destination through a vanilla input channel and the server pre-writes it — turning dynamic routing from a server decision into a player decision.

**How it works.** Three vanilla client→server channels carry player intent with zero client install.

(1) MAP PING — the best one. `Chat.SendPing(Vector3 position)` invokes the routed RPC `"ChatMessage"` at `targetPeerID = 0` (ZRoutedRpc.Everybody) carrying the clicked world position, type 3 (Talker.Type.Ping), the sender's UserInfo and empty text (:42058-42068). Because it targets peer 0, `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` always calls `RouteRPC` (:83577-83595) and the dedicated server always receives it — with ONE player online, unlike chat text. A vanilla player triggers it by middle-clicking the large map, double-clicking with the Ping pin type selected, or gamepad JoyButtonX. The server captures it with a Harmony prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` matching `data.m_methodHash == "ChatMessage".GetStableHashCode()` (save and restore `m_parameters.GetPos()`), resolves the sender to a peer, finds the managed portal nearest that player, finds the destination nearest the pinged coordinate, and writes the connection. That is a complete destination picker on a stock client: open map, middle-click, walk through.

(2) EMOTE — 25 discrete values. `Player.StartEmote` writes `ZDOVars.s_emote` (string) and bumps `s_emoteID` (:15585-15598). Poll every connected character's `s_emoteID` at 0.25s (Wonderland's EmoteSignals does exactly this) and dispatch on the new `s_emote`. Ideal for 'cycle this gate' / 'confirm' / 'go home'.

(3) ITEM STAND — a physical radio button. `ZDOVars.s_item` on an ItemStand ZDO holds the mounted item's prefab stable hash (:78465). A row of stands beside a portal is a self-documenting, in-world destination menu the server reads with one ZDO poll.

FEEDBACK: `PlayerNotify.Toast` via `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "Message", (int)MessageType, text, 0)` (`Player.RPC_Message` :14820-14825) puts a HUD line in front of the player. `"RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"` (registered on every client at `Game.Start` :100068, handler :100823) drops a NAMED, SAVED map pin at the destination — but it is save:true with no removal RPC, so use it once per new destination, never as a live-synced pin set.

CHAT TEXT IS NOT A CHANNEL: `Chat.SendText`/`Talker.Say` target each OTHER listed player individually (:41975-42043), so a solo player generates zero packets; slash commands run locally and print 'not a recognized command'.

**Player experience.** The player opens their map, middle-clicks the Swamp outpost, and gets a HUD line: "Gate set → Bonemire (412m)". The ping marker everyone can see doubles as a public announcement of where they are about to go. They walk into the gate and arrive. Alternative flow: they stand at the gate and do /wave; a toast reads "1/4 Meadows", /wave again gives "2/4 Black Forest", and the portal's runes visibly blink off and back on with each cycle as the server rewrites the connection. Or they drop a Copper Ore on the stand labelled 'Mine' and the gate re-points within a second.

**Failure modes.**
- Map pings are PUBLIC — broadcast to peer 0, so every online player sees the ping marker and its 5s map pin. A destination picker built on pings has no privacy and is trivially spammable; debounce hard
- Registering a routed RPC name the server already has throws (ZRoutedRpc.Register uses Dictionary.Add) — probe m_functions or patch HandleRoutedRPC instead of registering
- Chat text and slash commands are dead channels: SendText targets other players individually (:41996-42043) and unknown slash commands never leave the client
- RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse pins are save:true with no removal RPC — repeated pushes create duplicates unless name+type+position match within 1m (HaveSimilarPin)
- EmoteSignals' 0.25s poll means a rapid double-emote can be coalesced; StopEmote bumps the counter with an empty name and must be ignored
- The ping's y is forced to the pinging player's own y (:42058-42068), so the pinged coordinate is only meaningful in x/z

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover
