## 37. Randomised Roguelike Re-Roll

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium-large

A portal whose destination is re-rolled to a fresh procedurally-validated world coordinate on an interval or after each use.

**How it works.** Destination candidates must be validated without colliders, because every ZoneSystem raycast helper is dead on a dedicated server: `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f,0f,1000000f))` every physics tick in the SERVER build only (:100458-100466), so `GetGroundHeight`, `GetSolidHeight`, `IsBlocked`, `FindFloor` and `IsLava(Vector3)` all silently return their no-hit fallback rather than throwing.

Valid server-side validation stack, all pure math:
• `WorldGenerator.GetHeight(x, z)` (:151944) — sea level is 30 (`ZoneSystem.m_waterLevel`, :113218). Reject `< 30 + margin`.
• `WorldGenerator.GetBiome(x, z)` (:151725) — biome filter.
• `WorldGenerator.GetNormal(point, radius)` (:151925) / `GetTerrainDelta(center, radius, out delta, out slopeDir)` (:152364) — slope/roughness; vanilla's own location placement accepts delta ≤ 2f.
• `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap(pos, 0.6f)` (:115637) — STATIC, WorldGenerator-only, the only lava test that works headless.
• Reject `x*x + z*z > 110250000` (waterEdgeSqr, :151118-151122) and any y > 3000 (interiors, `Character.InInterior` :4538).
• Fast pre-filter: `ZNet.World.m_biomeData.PointHeights[WorldSpaceToMapSpace(x), WorldSpaceToMapSpace(z)]` (:92332/:92424) is an O(1) 12m-resolution cached grid; use it to reject candidates before spending a noise evaluation. `GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel(biomeMask)` (:92683) hands you a pre-validated land point in one call.

The roll: pick a candidate, validate, then either move an existing anchor (DO NOT — see Roaming Portal) or destroy the old anchor and fabricate a fresh one at the new coordinate via Phantom Anchor Fabrication, then re-point the hub. Destroy requires `SetOwner(GetSessionID())` first (:76929-76931). Fabricate BEFORE destroying so the connection never dangles.

Re-roll cadence: per real interval (a 1Hz check against `ZNet.GetTimeSeconds()`), per in-game day, or on transit-detected use (one-shot semantics). Pre-warm mandatory: a fresh far anchor is not held by any client, so the first walk-through is a silent no-op until `RequestZDO` round-trips (:143646-143654). Call `ForceSendZDO(peerUid, anchorId)` for every peer within ~200m of the hub immediately after the roll.

DANGER: `WorldGenerator` is blind to player terraforming and to a location's own flattening (`ZoneSystem.PlaceLocations` re-resolves with a raycast and forces y=30 for m_snapToWater locations, :114957-114968). Treat heights as ±2m and always add clearance; `Player.UpdateTeleport`'s 15s fallback drops the player to `GetSolidHeight + 0.5` anyway (:15360-15366), and because portals pass distantTeleport:true the teleport can never fail outright.

**Player experience.** A cracked obsidian gate in the hub hall is tagged "Unknown". Each dawn its runes flicker and the tag updates to "Unknown — Plains". A player steps through, takes the 8-second black screen, and lands on a random windswept ridge in the Plains they have never seen, next to nothing at all — no structure, no way back except the way they came, which is not there. Tomorrow it goes somewhere else. If the roll landed badly the player arrives a couple of metres above or below true ground and either drops a short distance or is force-landed on solid ground at the 15-second mark.

**Failure modes.**
- Every ZoneSystem raycast helper silently returns its fallback on a dedicated server (reference position pinned to 1e6, :100463-100466) — a GetGroundHeight that returns p.y unchanged looks like a valid answer
- WorldGenerator is blind to terraforming and location flattening; heights are ±2m
- A fresh far anchor is never held by any client: first walk-through is a totally silent no-op
- mask.a means lava only in the Ashlands (GetAshlandsHeight :152224); elsewhere the same channel carries an unrelated mask. Use IsLavaPreHeightmap, which biome-gates first
- BiomeSector.Center is a perimeter centroid and can land outside its own biome; BiomeSector.MinZone/MaxZone are computed wrongly (:92577-92578) and must never be used
- Churning anchors creates and destroys portal ZDOs repeatedly; each destroy enters m_deadZDOs (:76997) and each create dirties the portal chunk
- One-way roguelike gates strand players with no return — either fabricate a return anchor at the destination or accept it as the design

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover; Phantom Anchor Fabrication

**Citations.** Game.FixedUpdate (server reference position pin) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100458-100466 · WorldGenerator.GetHeight — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:151944 · WorldGenerator.GetBiome — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:151725 · WorldGenerator.GetTerrainDelta — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:152364-152390 · ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap (static) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115637-115646 · ZoneSystem.m_waterLevel = 30f — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113218 · AltBiomeWorldData.GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:92683 · AltBiomeWorldData.WorldSpaceToMapSpace — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:92424 · Player.UpdateTeleport (15s force-land) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15360-15366 · ZoneSystem.PlaceLocations (raycast re-resolve) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:114957-114968

**Open questions.**
- Does a vanilla client complete a forced distantTeleport into a never-generated zone within the 15s fallback on low-end hardware, and does it take fall damage? Player.UpdateTeleport resets m_maxAirAltitude every tick during teleport (:15345) which suggests no — verify with an 8km jump into unexplored Ashlands.
- Are AllPoints / AllPointsAboveSeaLevel retained in memory after GenerateSectors, and at what RSS cost across 2048×2048 cells? Log Biomes[b].AllPoints.Count per biome at server start before leaning on GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel.

## 38. Seasonal / Event Network Swap

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Swap an entire portal network's topology and naming at once — a Halloween layout, a raid-week layout, a wipe-eve layout — as a single batched, budgeted operation.

**How it works.** A 'network' is a named config set of `{portalPositionKey → (tag, destinationPositionKey)}`. Swapping means, for every member: write `ZDOVars.s_tag` (:78617), write the Portal connection, ForceSendZDO, and call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` once at the end (a tag-only write does not set DirtyPortalObjects and is silently lost at the next world save — only SetConnection/AddIfPortal/HandleDestroyedZDO set it, :73661/:77750/:76986).

BATCHING IS MANDATORY. `ZDOMan.SendZDOs` performs no delta encoding — it re-serializes the ENTIRE ZDO (every float/vec3/quat/int/long/string/byte[]) per peer per send (:77056-77064) — and `AddForceSendZdos` inserts each force-sent ZDO at index 0 of the sync list (:77275), so a hundred simultaneous force-sends monopolise every peer's next several send slots under the 10240-byte queue cap (:77011-77019). Wonderland's StructureUpkeep learned this the hard way and caps at 256 routed broadcasts per sweep. Apply the same discipline: rewrite at most K portals per tick (K=16 at a 0.2s tick gives ~80 portals/sec), and prefer ordering by distance from the nearest peer so visible portals change first.

CHEAPER PATH — do it at world load. `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` (:76474-76531) loads the entire portal chunk into `m_portalObjects` before any peer connects, `ZDO.Load` leaves every ZDO unowned with revisions at 0 (:74550-74556), and `Game.ConnectPortals` runs synchronously from :76523 with `m_peers` empty so every write takes the immediate local path. A seasonal swap applied in an OnWorldReady hook costs zero network traffic and zero contention. Schedule swaps to coincide with a restart where possible.

REVERSION: keep the previous network in the mod's own state file so a swap is undoable. Do NOT rely on the world save to remember the old layout — rings, one-way links and self-loops do not survive `RegenerateConnectionHashData`'s single-hash-slot-per-ZDO format (:75461-75478).

ANNOUNCEMENT: the tag string is the free in-world signage channel (`GetHoverText` :143453-143463, no server-side length cap). For an out-of-world announcement, `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "ShowMessage", (int)MessageHud.MessageType.Center, text)` (MessageHud registration :55808, handler :55848) puts a centre-screen line on every vanilla client, Localize'd client-side so `$token` strings resolve in each player's language.

**Player experience.** On the night of the event, every player online gets a centre-screen line: "The ways have shifted." Over the next couple of seconds the portals nearest them visibly blink — runes dying and relighting with the vanilla connect sound — and their hover tags change from "Home"/"Mine"/"Swamp" to "Hollow I"/"Hollow II"/"Hollow III". The gate that led to their base yesterday now opens onto a crypt. When the event ends the whole thing reverts on the next restart, and their old tags come back exactly as they were.

**Failure modes.**
- Un-budgeted mass force-sends monopolise every peer's sync queue (no delta encoding, :77056-77064; 10240-byte cap, :77011) and can visibly stall world streaming for everyone
- Tag-only writes are silently lost at the next world save without ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702)
- A player mid-transit when the swap lands arrives at the OLD destination (snapshotted at TeleportTo, :15343) and their return leg now goes somewhere else entirely
- Players who opened the tag dialog before the swap can save back a stale 10-char-truncated tag afterwards (TextInput cap, :143482 / :61515-61522)
- Reverting from the world save is impossible for non-pairwise topologies (RegenerateConnectionHashData, :75461) — the mod must keep its own before-state
- With Pairing Authority Takeover disabled, every retag instantly re-pairs portals randomly within 5s (:100601)

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover

**Citations.** ZDOMan.SendZDOs (full re-serialize, no delta) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77008-77074 · ZDOMan.AddForceSendZdos (Insert at 0) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77263-77280 · ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702-76705 · ZDOMan.LoadChunks — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76474-76531 · ZDO.Load (unowned, revisions 0) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74550-74556 · ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75461-75478 · MessageHud.RPC_ShowMessage — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:55848-55851 · TeleportWorld.GetHoverText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143463 · StructureUpkeep broadcast budget — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/StructureUpkeep.cs:29-40

**Open questions.**

Vanilla's ZNet.LowDiskLeftInformer calls MessageHud.instance.MessageAll unguarded under IsDedicated() (:80258), implying yes — but the send side does not need it, only a duplicate Register would break.

## 39. World-State Conditional Routing (Population, Load, Weather)

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Destinations that respond to ambient server state — how many players are online, which are where, and (with heavy caveats) the weather.

**How it works.** POPULATION (fully feasible). `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` (:81630) returns the live peer list; `GetNrOfPlayers()` (:81516) and `GetConnectedPeers()` (:80516) give counts. Per-peer character ZDOs come from `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID)` (:78794) and carry live position, `ZDOVars.s_dead` (:78403), `s_inBed` (:78457), health/stamina, and the full VisEquipment slot set as prefab hashes (:20569-20708). Rules that work: route the arrival gate to whichever outpost currently has the most players within 100m (a 'where is everyone' gate); open an overflow destination above N online; blackout a raid gate when fewer than 3 players are online; point a 'muster' portal at the centroid of the living player positions (fabricate/refresh an anchor there on a 5s tick).

DISTRIBUTION-AWARE LOAD BALANCING. Count players near each candidate destination and route new arrivals to the least crowded — the LRU/load-balanced policy of Deterministic Assignment Replacement, but driven by live occupancy rather than transit history.

WEATHER — LARGELY RULED OUT, and this is the important negative. `EnvMan.FixedUpdate` calls `UpdateEnvironment(num, GetBiome())` (:95719-95721), and `GetBiome()` on a dedicated server resolves against the pinned reference position at (1e6, 0, 1e6) (`Game.FixedUpdate` :100463-100466). The server's own `GetCurrentEnvironment()` therefore describes weather at a coordinate no player will ever stand on. Worse, weather is BIOME-LOCAL: each client computes its own current environment for its own biome, so there is no single 'server weather' to condition on even in principle. `EnvMan.IsWet()`/`IsCold()`/`IsFreezing()` (:96343-96356) read that same wrong environment. The only weather-adjacent state that IS globally coherent is the day fraction and the wind seed, both derived from `ZNet.GetTimeSeconds()` and identical on every machine. So: time-of-day routing yes (see Scheduled Routing); weather-conditional routing no, unless the mod recomputes the environment itself from the destination's biome and the shared time seed, which duplicates `UpdateEnvironment`'s selection logic and is fragile.

Tick budget: 1Hz is ample for all of this. `GetPeers()` returns the LIVE list (do not mutate while iterating); a peer's `m_characterID` is `ZDOID.None` between connect and spawn and between death and respawn (`Game.SpawnPlayer` :100270, `Game._RequestRespawn` :100413) so guard every lookup.

**Player experience.** A player logs in at 3am to a quiet server and finds the hub's 'Muster' gate dark and tagged "Too few awake". At peak hours the same gate lights up and leads to whichever outpost currently has the most people standing around it — hover reads "Muster → Bonemire (4)". A player who steps through the overflow gate during a busy evening is routed to the emptiest of three identical arrival pads rather than piling onto the first one. Weather never affects anything, and honestly telling players that up front is better than a feature that behaves differently on every client.

**Failure modes.**
- Weather is not server-coherent: EnvMan.GetBiome resolves at the pinned (1e6,0,1e6) reference position (:95719 + :100463) and weather is per-biome per-client anyway
- peer.m_characterID is ZDOID.None during two normal windows (connect→spawn, death→respawn) — guard every GetZDO
- ZNet.GetPeers() returns the live backing list; disconnecting someone mid-iteration corrupts it. Use GetConnectedPeers() (a copy) when mutating
- ZNet.GetPlayerList()[i].m_position is zero for any player with public position disabled (:81256-81259) — use the character ZDO position instead
- A population rule with hysteresis omitted flaps the portal on and off as one player logs in and out
- Centroid-following anchors require repositioning, which is forbidden for portal-prefab ZDOs (ZDO.SetSector early-return, :73752) — destroy and recreate, or use a non-portal anchor prefab

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover; Phantom Anchor Fabrication

**Citations.** ZNet.GetPeers / GetConnectedPeers / GetNrOfPlayers — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81630, :80516, :81516 · ZNetPeer.m_characterID — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78794 · Game.SpawnPlayer / Game._RequestRespawn (characterID windows) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100270, :100413 · EnvMan.FixedUpdate UpdateEnvironment(GetBiome()) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:95719-95721 · Game.FixedUpdate (reference position pin) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100458-100466 · EnvMan.IsWet/IsCold/IsFreezing — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:96343-96356 · ZNet.UpdatePlayerList (position blanked for privacy) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81245-81300 · ZDOVars.s_dead / s_inBed — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78403, :78457

## 40. Moving Destination Anchor (Follow a Ship or Player)

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Keep the portal fixed but point it at a ZDO that itself moves — a ship, a player — so the arrival point tracks a target in real time.

**How it works.** `TeleportWorld.Teleport` reads the destination ZDO's `GetPosition()` and `GetRotation()` at the instant of transit with no prefab validation (:143539-143545). So pointing a portal's `ConnectionType.Portal` at a Ship's ZDO, or at a player's character ZDO, genuinely resolves to that object's live coordinates on a vanilla client.

THREE HARD LIMITS, in ascending severity.

(1) Vanilla's reconciler kills it. `Game.ConnectPortals` pass 1 nulls the link within 5s unless the target ZDO carries the same `s_tag` AND a non-None Portal connection (:100598-100605). Fix: Pairing Authority Takeover. But note a ZDO holds exactly ONE connection (`s_connections` is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` with a single readonly target, :74794/:75524-75534) — writing a Portal connection onto a player's ZDO would DESTROY their `SyncTransform` parentage (the ship-attachment record written by `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` :87542-87562). Ships never have a parent so they are safe; player ZDOs are not. Point at ships, not at players.

(2) Staleness. `TeleportWorld.TargetFound` requests a missing destination ZDO exactly ONCE via `RequestZDO` (:143646-143654), which `SendZDOs` consumes by removing it from `m_forceSend` after one send (:77051). After that the client never re-requests, so a distant moving target goes stale immediately. Keeping it fresh requires the server to call `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(shipUid)` every send cycle (~20Hz) for every peer — an expensive permanent broadcast, since SendZDOs re-serializes the whole ZDO each time (:77056-77064).

(3) THE KILLER. Arriving 'on' a moving ship is impossible in vanilla. `Player.UpdateTeleport` snapshots `m_teleportTargetPos` once and force-assigns `transform.position = m_teleportTargetPos` every FixedUpdate from t>2s (:15343), and for `distantTeleport` — which portals always pass (:143546) — completion is blocked until t>8s AND `ZNetScene.IsAreaReady` (:15349). The traveller is nailed to an 8-second-old coordinate. Worse, `ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask` omits the 'vehicle' layer that `BaseAI` explicitly adds (:113424 vs :25909), so `FindFloor`/`GetSolidHeight` do not see a ship hull and the 15s fallback drops the player to seabed height (:15360-15366).

WHAT DOES WORK: pointing at a STATIONARY ship (a moored base-boat), or at a ship whose helmsman the server can identify via `ZDOVars.s_user` on the Ship ZDO (:78637, written by `ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl` :141326-141342) to blackout the portal while the ship is under way. That is a genuinely nice feature: 'the gate to the longship only opens while she's at anchor'.

**Player experience.** The harbour gate is tagged "Sea Serpent — moored" and glows. A player steps through and lands on the longship's deck at the dock. Once the crew casts off, the gate goes dark within a second and the tag reads "Sea Serpent — under way"; walking in does nothing. If the server instead left it live, a player stepping through while the ship sails would spend 8 seconds on a black screen and splash into open water somewhere behind the wake, then be force-landed on the seabed at the 15-second mark.

**Failure modes.**
- Arriving on a moving ship is structurally impossible: the destination is snapshotted and the player is pinned to it for ≥8s (Player.UpdateTeleport :15343-15349)
- ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask omits the vehicle layer (:113424) so a ship hull is invisible to FindFloor — the traveller is dropped to seabed height by the 15s fallback
- Writing a Portal connection onto a player's ZDO destroys their SyncTransform parentage — a ZDO holds exactly one connection (:74794, :75524-75534)
- Keeping a moving target fresh on every client requires ForceSendZDO every send cycle; TargetFound requests it only once (:143650) and SendZDOs consumes the request (:77051)
- Without Pairing Authority Takeover the link dies within 5s because the ship has no matching s_tag and no reciprocal Portal connection
- Ship top speeds are Inspector data, so the exact miss distance during the 8s hold cannot be computed from the decompile

**Prerequisites.** Pairing Authority Takeover

**Citations.** TeleportWorld.Teleport (live target pos/rot, no prefab check) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143539-143546 · Player.UpdateTeleport (snapshot pin, 8s distant gate, 15s fallback) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15337-15378 · ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask (no vehicle layer) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113424; BaseAI mask — :25909 · ZDOExtraData.s_connections (one connection per ZDO) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74794, :75524-75534 · ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync (SyncTransform parent write) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87542-87562 · TeleportWorld.TargetFound (RequestZDO once) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143640-143656 · ZDOMan.SendZDOs (m_forceSend consumed) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77051 · ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl (ZDOVars.s_user) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:141326-141342 · Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100598-100605

**Open questions.**
- What Unity layer are Ship hull/deck colliders on? Force-teleport a player 1m above a stationary deck and observe whether UpdateTeleport completes at deck height (FindFloor hit the hull) or they fall through into the water.
- Measure a longship's real ZDO position delta over 8 seconds under full sail — that number is the minimum miss distance for any moving-ship destination.

## 41. Roaming Portal (Moving the Portal Itself)

`RULED-OUT` · `NOT-ENFORCEABLE` · effort: medium

RULED OUT — a portal whose own position the server moves. Vanilla clients never re-read a portal's position, and the move permanently corrupts the portal registry.

**How it works.** Four independent mechanisms each independently kill this.

(1) THE CLIENT NEVER MOVES THE MESH. `ZNetScene.CreateObject` applies `zdo.GetPosition()` only at the `Object.Instantiate` call (:82011-82013), and `ZNetView.Awake` never touches `transform.position` — it applies scale only, and only when `m_syncInitialScale` is set (:82566-82626). Unless the portal prefab carries a `ZSyncTransform` with `m_syncPosition` (Inspector data, almost certainly absent on a static building piece), the portal mesh AND its `TeleportWorldTrigger` collider stay frozen at the build site no matter what the server writes. It does not rubber-band and does not re-instantiate — it ignores the write entirely until the instance is destroyed and recreated by `ZNetScene.RemoveObjects`/`CreateObjects` (:82196-82226), at which point it POPS to the new coordinate.

(2) THE SECTOR KEY IS FROZEN. `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for any prefab in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:73752-73757). A portal ZDO stays filed in `m_portalObjects` under whatever sector index `AddIfPortal` gave it. `CreateSyncList` → `FindSectorObjects` → `FindObjects` (:77367-77382) therefore keeps delivering a moved portal to peers near its ORIGINAL location and never to peers at its new one. Only a permanent per-tick `ForceSendZDO` gets it anywhere.

(3) PERMANENT REGISTRY CORRUPTION. `HandleDestroyedZDO` removes a portal from `m_portalObjects` using `zDO.GetSectorIndex()` recomputed from the CURRENT position (:76976-76987), which no longer matches the dictionary key set at creation. A moved-then-destroyed portal leaks in `m_portalObjects` forever, and `GetPortalList()` / `Game.ConnectPortals()` keep processing a dead object. On the CLIENT side it is worse: every sector boundary crossing makes `AddIfPortal` append the ZDO under a second key without removing the old one (:77738), producing unbounded duplicate growth in each client's portal registry over a long session.

(4) IT IS NOT SAVED. `AddObjectsPerChunk` excludes portal prefabs from normal chunk files (:77572) and the ChunkPortal file is only written when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set (:77621-77635) — which `ZDO.InternalSetPosition`/`IncreaseDataRevision` never do (:73734-73745, :73832). Every relocation reverts on restart. And a position write on a ZDO the server does not own does not even bump DataRevision (`IsOwner()` gate at :73740), while `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` revokes server ownership of anything within ~96m of a player every 2 seconds (:76901-76927).

USE THIS INSTEAD: destroy the portal ZDO and fabricate a fresh one at the new coordinate (Phantom Anchor Fabrication). That is correct, saved, and delivered properly.

**Player experience.** Nothing. A player standing beside a 'roaming' portal sees it sit perfectly still while the server believes it has moved 500 metres. Walking into it still teleports them (the trigger is where the mesh is). Then they log out and back in, or walk 120m away and return, and the portal has silently teleported itself across the map with no animation — and everyone else in the old zone still sees it there until they too reload.

**Failure modes.**
- Client never re-reads position: ZNetScene.CreateObject applies it only at Instantiate (:82011), ZNetView.Awake never does (:82566-82626)
- Sector key frozen for portals (ZDO.SetSector early-return, :73752) — normal sector sync stops reaching the new location
- HandleDestroyedZDO leaks the ZDO permanently if it was moved across a zone boundary (:76976-76987)
- Clients accumulate duplicate m_portalObjects entries on every boundary crossing (AddIfPortal, :77738)
- Position writes are not saved for portals (:77572 / :77621) and revert on restart
- A position write on a non-owned ZDO does not bump DataRevision at all (:73740); ownership is revoked within 2s near any player (:76901)

## 42. Per-Peer Divergent ZDO Routing

`RULED-OUT` · `NOT-ENFORCEABLE` · effort: small

RULED OUT — writing a different destination per player into the same portal. There is one ZDO object and the normal sync sweep reconverges every peer within ~50-100ms.

**How it works.** The idea: write connection X, force-send only to peer A; write connection Y, force-send only to peer B; each holds their own destination. `ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID id)` (:77714) does exist and does target one peer.

It cannot work, for a structural reason. There is exactly ONE `ZDO` object per portal in `m_objectsByID`, holding one `ZDOConnection{m_type, m_target}` entry in the static `ZDOExtraData.s_connections` dictionary (:74794, :75524-75534). Per-peer state is only a REVISION CACHE: `ZDOPeer.m_zdos` maps ZDOID → `PeerZDOInfo(dataRevision, ownerRevision, syncTime)` (:75963-75981), and `ZDOPeer.ShouldSend(zdo)` returns true whenever `zdo.DataRevision > value.m_dataRevision` (:76003-76014).

So the second write (revision R2) makes `ShouldSend` true for peer A as well as B. `CreateSyncList` on the server gathers `FindSectorObjects(zone(peer.GetRefPos()), ...)` (:77212-77241), and `FindObjects` explicitly merges `m_portalObjects[sectorIndex]` back into the result (:77376-77379) — so any peer standing at the portal is, by definition, in the sector query and receives R2 on their next send slot. `SendZDOToPeers2` services one peer per Update frame behind a 0.05s gate (:76837-76862), so reconvergence is ~50-100ms. The divergence window is shorter than a single human reaction, and the LAST write wins for everyone.

There is also no field-level merge on receive: `RPC_ZDOData` discards a packet whose DataRevision is ≤ the local one and otherwise calls `zDO.Deserialize(pkg2)` on the whole blob (:77103-77132). Nothing per-peer survives.

The only two things that genuinely differ per peer are (a) WHETHER a peer holds a ZDO at all — controllable via distance and `ForceSendZDO` — and (b) the revision cache. Neither carries divergent VALUES.

CONSEQUENCE: every 'per-player destination' feature must be physical (Per-Player Private Portal Terminals) or temporal (Approach-Triggered Just-In-Time Routing). There is no third route, and any design document claiming otherwise is wrong at the protocol level.

**Player experience.** Nothing coherent. Two players standing at the same portal would each briefly see a different destination for under a tenth of a second, then both converge on whichever the server wrote last, and both go to the same place. In practice it is indistinguishable from a portal that flickers between destinations at 20Hz.

**Failure modes.**
- One ZDO object, one connection field — ZDOExtraData.s_connections is Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection> with a single readonly target (:74794, :75524-75534)
- ZDOPeer state is a revision cache only (:75963-75981); ShouldSend re-pushes the latest value to every peer whose sector query covers the portal (:76003-76014)
- FindObjects merges m_portalObjects into every sector query (:77376-77379) so a peer at the portal always re-receives it
- RPC_ZDOData replaces the whole blob with no field-level merge (:77103-77132)
- Reconvergence is ~50-100ms (SendZDOToPeers2, :76837-76862) — far too fast to exploit

**Citations.** ZDOExtraData.s_connections / class ZDOConnection — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74794, :75524-75534 · ZDOMan.ZDOPeer / PeerZDOInfo / ShouldSend — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75961-76014 · ZDOMan.CreateSyncList — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77212-77241 · ZDOMan.FindObjects (portal merge) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77367-77382 · ZDOMan.SendZDOToPeers2 — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76837-76862 · ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (whole-blob replace) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77076-77140 · ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(long, ZDOID) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77714-77719

## 43. Transit-Instant Decision Hook

`RULED-OUT` · `NOT-ENFORCEABLE` · effort: small

RULED OUT — evaluating the destination at the moment a player steps in. Three independent gates make it unreachable on a dedicated server.

**How it works.** This is the request every dynamic-routing feature actually wants, and it is impossible. Confirmed by direct inspection, not inference.

`TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player)` has exactly ONE call site in the entire assembly: `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter(Collider colliderIn)` (:143673-143681), which requires `colliderIn.GetComponent<Player>() != null` AND `Player.m_localPlayer == component`.

Gate 1 — no GameObject. The SERVER build's `Game.FixedUpdate` unconditionally calls `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick (:100458-100466); the CLIENT build's `Game.FixedUpdate` has no such line. `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` computes its zone from `GetReferencePosition()` (:82268-82276) and `CreateObjectsSorted` returns immediately unless `ZoneSystem.IsActiveAreaLoaded()` (:82105-82112). No portal GameObject, no `TeleportWorld` component, no trigger collider ever exists server-side.

Gate 2 — no Player. `Player.Awake` is what adds a Player to `s_players` (:10032-10035); the list is permanently empty headless, so `Player.GetClosestPlayer` always returns null (:14840-14854) and no collider ever enters anything.

Gate 3 — `Player.m_localPlayer` is never populated on a dedicated server.

Corollaries. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` is `public` and appears in any reflection dump, which makes it look callable — it is not usefully callable: `m_nview` would be null, `player.Message` needs `MessageHud.instance`, and `IncrementPlayerStat` writes the server's own throwaway profile. A Harmony patch on `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`, `Teleport`, `UpdatePortal` or `TargetFound` compiles and applies on a dedicated server and never fires once. Even for a routed RPC that DID cross the wire, `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` dispatches ZDO-targeted RPCs through `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zdo)` (:83646-83663, :82229), whose `m_instances` dictionary is permanently empty server-side — and a client that OWNS the ZDO never puts the RPC on the wire at all, because `InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally and skips `RouteRPC` when `targetPeerID == m_id` (:83588-83594).

The closest achievable substitutes, in descending fidelity: Approach-Triggered JIT Routing (~0.45s before the trigger), Per-Player Private Terminals (physical separation), and after-the-fact transit detection (~2.0-2.2s late, because the character ZDO position does not move until `m_teleportTimer > 2f`, :15337).

**Player experience.** N/A — the mechanism does not exist. What a player experiences instead is whatever the server pre-wrote. The practical consequence is that no server-side feature can react to WHO is walking through at the moment they walk through, cannot reproduce vanilla's ore/metal check (inventories are never in any ZDO), and cannot refuse a specific player's transit.

**Failure modes.**
- TeleportWorld.Teleport's only caller is the local-player-gated TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143673-143681)
- No portal GameObject exists server-side: Game.FixedUpdate pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) (:100463-100466)
- Player.s_players is permanently empty (Player.Awake :10032), so GetClosestPlayer always returns null
- ZNetScene.m_instances is empty, so ZDO-targeted routed RPCs are never dispatched server-side (:83656, :82229)
- A ZDO-owning client's RPC never reaches the wire at all (InvokeRoutedRPC self-dispatch, :83588-83594)
- Patches on TeleportWorld members apply cleanly and silently never fire — the most expensive possible failure mode, because it looks like it works

**Citations.** TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (sole call site) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143664-143682 · TeleportWorld.Teleport — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143517-143549 · Game.FixedUpdate (SERVER-only reference position pin) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100458-100466 · ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects / CreateObjectsSorted — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82268-82276, :82105-82112 · Player.Awake (s_players) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:10032-10035 · Player.GetClosestPlayer — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:14840-14854 · ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC / ZNetScene.FindInstance — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83645-83663, :82229 · ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC (self-dispatch skip) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83577-83595 · Player.UpdateTeleport (2s position hold) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15337-15348

- Confirm ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances() (:82334) really is 0 on a running dedicated server with players online. It is the single empirical check that validates this entire ruled-out verdict.

## 44. Authentic Sender Context

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

A thread-static ambient record of the socket-verified ZNetPeer for the duration of every routed-RPC and ZDOData dispatch — the prerequisite that turns every spoofable `sender`/`playerID`/`authorId` argument into something checkable.

**How it works.** Two Harmony prefix/postfix pairs, both on methods that receive the real `ZRpc` and then discard it.

(1) `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (:83632). The whole chain RPC_RoutedRPC → HandleRoutedRPC (:83646) → `m_functions[hash].Invoke(data.m_senderPeerID, data.m_parameters)` (:83652) is one synchronous call stack on the main thread. A prefix resolves `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)` (GetPeers is public, :81630; ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc) is private) and assigns it to a `[ThreadStatic] static ZNetPeer s_current`; a `finally`-shaped postfix clears it. Every routed-RPC handler that runs during that window — including `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO` (:76953), `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653), `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey` (:116022), `ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject` (:82355), `ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO` (:77689) — can now ask "who really sent this?" and get `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`, the only platform-verified identity on the box (Steam session ticket / PlayFab auth, ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo :79843-79870).

(2) `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (:77076). Vanilla itself resolves the peer here (`FindPeer(rpc)`, :77078/:76800) and then throws the identity away before applying data. Same prefix/postfix pattern. Crucially, `ZDO.Deserialize` (:74206) is called *inside* this loop at :77131, so a postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize` — the SpawnGovernor pattern (Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:58) — can read `s_current` and know exactly which authenticated account pushed that ZDO field set.

Derived helpers: `AuthPeer` (the ZNetPeer), `AuthUserId` (`peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`), `AuthIsAdmin` (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(hostName)`, :81811 → `ListContainsId` :80159, which since 1.0.12 matches either ID form), and `AuthPlayerId` (`ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID)?.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_playerID)` — still a client self-report, but now *bound* to a verified account so a mismatch is detectable).

Cost: two dictionary-free linear scans of `m_peers` per packet. Cache per-ZRpc in a small map keyed by reference to avoid the scan on hot paths.

**Player experience.** Nothing. This is pure plumbing — no player-visible behaviour changes. Its whole value is that every option below can say "and we know for certain that this packet came from Steam ID 76561198…" instead of "the packet claimed to be from peer 12345".

**Failure modes.**
- `ZRpc` → peer resolution returns null during the handshake window (before `peer.m_uid` is assigned at ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo :79905) — treat null as untrusted and refuse, never as trusted.
- A future Valheim build that dispatches routed RPCs asynchronously or off the main thread would silently break the ambient-context assumption with no error. Guard with a depth counter and assert single-entry.
- It gives you identity, not authority: it does nothing about RPCs that never cross the wire (see Retag Interception at the Relay).
- `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` is private — bind with `AccessTools.Method(typeof(ZRoutedRpc), "RPC_RoutedRPC")` and wrap in SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch so a signature change degrades to a warning.

**Citations.** ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83632-83644 · ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83646-83665 · ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData.Deserialize (m_senderPeerID read straight off the wire) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83607-83615 · ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77076-77140 · ZDOMan.FindPeer(ZRpc) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76800-76810 · ZNet.GetPeers — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81630 · ZNet.IsAdmin / ListContainsId — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81811, :80159-80173 · ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo session-ticket verification — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79843-79870

## 45. Retag Interception at the Relay

`RULED-OUT` · `NOT-ENFORCEABLE` · effort: small

Dropping `RPC_SetTag` packets at the server's `RouteRPC`/`RPC_RoutedRPC` chokepoint — RULED OUT as a general lock, because the most common case never puts a packet on the wire at all.

**How it works.** The obvious design: prefix `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632), deserialize a *copy* of the package, match `m_methodHash == "RPC_SetTag".GetStableHashCode()`, resolve `m_targetZDO` via `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO()`, confirm it is a portal (`Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(zdo.GetPrefab())`, :100021), check the Authentic Sender Context against your ACL, and return false to drop both the local handling and the relay.

Why it fails. `TeleportWorld.SetText` calls `m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", text, platformUserId)` (:143583), and `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string, …)` is `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(m_zdo.GetOwner(), m_zdo.m_uid, method, parameters)` (:82855-82858). `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` (:83577) then does:
```
if (targetPeerID == m_id || targetPeerID == 0) HandleRoutedRPC(data);   // local
if (targetPeerID != m_id)                       RouteRPC(data);         // wire
```
In ordinary play the retagging player is standing next to the portal, so `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901-76926) has already handed that portal's ZDO to *that same client* within 2 seconds. `m_zdo.GetOwner() == m_id` for them, so the branch takes only the local path: the tag is written in-process, zero bytes are sent, the server's relay never sees it, and the change arrives at the server later, laundered, as an ordinary `RPC_ZDOData` field push with a bumped DataRevision (:77076-77132) that is indistinguishable from any other legitimate edit.

The complementary idea — Harmony-patching `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` itself (:143587) — is equally dead. `HandleRoutedRPC` dispatches a ZDO-targeted RPC only through `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zDO)` (:83659), and a dedicated server has no instances at all because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition((1e6,0,1e6))` every physics tick (:100458-100466), so `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` (:82268) never instantiates a world ZDO. The patch compiles, applies, and never fires once.

The relay hook is still worth building — as *telemetry*, not as a lock. It catches the minority of retags where a different client (or the server) owns the portal, which is exactly the case where a stranger is retagging a portal in someone else's base while its owner is offline. That is the grief case you most want logged.

**Player experience.** If you shipped this as a lock: a player retagging their own portal while standing at it succeeds normally (packet never reached the server); a player retagging a portal whose owner is a different online player is silently refused with the text box appearing to accept the new name and the hover text never changing. Inconsistent and confusing — which is precisely why this cannot be the mechanism.

**Failure modes.**
- The common case (owner retags own portal) is invisible to the server. Fatal for use as a lock.
- `ZPackage` read position advances as you inspect it — a prefix must deserialize a copy (`new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray())`) or vanilla routing reads garbage.
- Returning false from the prefix also suppresses the relay of a *legitimate* retag, producing a permanently desynced portal between two clients.
- `m_senderPeerID` in the packet is self-reported (:83609) — useless without the Authentic Sender Context.

**Prerequisites.** Authentic Sender Context

## 46. Creator Attestation

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Validate a newly-placed portal's `s_creator`/`s_creatorIndex` against the socket-verified account that actually sent the ZDO, at the instant of arrival — turning build ownership from a client self-report into a server-notarised fact.

**How it works.** `Piece.SetCreator(long uid, PlatformUserID platformUserID)` runs on the *placing client* and writes two fields into the piece's ZDO: `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) = that client's local `PlayerProfile.m_playerID`, and `ZDOVars.s_creatorIndex` (:78395) = `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory.FindIndex(a => a.m_id == platformUserID)` (Piece.SetCreator :136415-136424). Both are client-authored and both are forgeable in isolation.

But `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` is a **server-maintained** table. `ZNet.UpdatePlayerHistory` (:81436-81461) appends entries built by `ZNet.UpdatePlayerList` (:81245-81299), which derives each `m_userInfo.m_id` from `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()` per backend (:81270-81281) — the platform-verified identity. The list is append-only (FindIndex-then-Add), persisted into the .fwl (`World.SaveWorldFWLData`, :112587-112591) and read back in order, so indices are stable across restarts. The server pushes its copy to clients via the `HistoricalPlayerList` RPC (:81317-81341), which is why the client's index is meaningful to the server at all.

The attestation, in the Deserialize postfix pair (SpawnGovernor pattern): a postfix on the private `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int)` (:76684) records the new ZDOID when `prefabHash == 0` (the network-receive path — the prefab is not known yet); a postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` (:74206) — reached at :77131, inside `RPC_ZDOData` — fires the moment the prefab IS known. There, for a ZDO in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash`:
1. Read `idx = zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_creatorIndex, -1)` and `claimed = zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator, 0)`.
2. Resolve the Authentic Sender Context's `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()` to a `PlatformUserID` and find its true index in `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory`.
3. If `idx` does not match, the claim is a forgery: overwrite both fields with the truth (`zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_creator, trueProfileId); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_creatorIndex, trueIdx)`), `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706), and raise an audit flag.
4. If `idx == -1` (the placer had not yet entered the history when they placed — a real case, see failure modes), stamp the true index rather than trusting the zero.
5. Record the notarised `(position-key → PlatformUserID, profileId, firstSeenTicks)` into the Portal Record Store.

From that point on, every other option in this document can say "the owner of this portal is this Steam account" and mean it. Note the field is a per-piece stamp: the identity is captured at birth, when the server still has the sending socket in hand, and is never trusted again from the wire.

**Player experience.** Invisible when honest. A player places a portal and it is theirs; every later ownership decision (who may retag it, whose cap it counts against, whose network it joins) attributes correctly even after they log out, change display name, or the world restarts. A player running a modified client that forges `s_creator` to steal credit for someone else's structure gets their forgery silently corrected on arrival and an audit line appears in the server log and Discord.

**Failure modes.**
- `Piece.SetCreator` only writes when `GetCreator() == 0L && m_nview.IsOwner()` (:136417). World-gen portals and anything placed before the field existed have `s_creator == 0` — treat 0 as "unowned", never as "owned by player 0".
- `FindIndex` returns -1 if the placer is not yet in `m_playerHistory` when they place, which happens on a brand-new account's first minutes because the history is only refreshed by `SendPeriodicData` (~2s). The server must stamp the correct index rather than reject.
- A client can forge `s_creator` (the profile-UID long) independently of `s_creatorIndex`; validating only the index leaves the long wrong. Overwrite both.
- The attestation only fires on the *network-receive* path. A portal placed while the world is loading, or one the server itself fabricates, never passes through RPC_ZDOData — handle those separately.
- If `m_playerHistory` ever gains a removal path in a future build, every stored index silently reattributes. Store the resolved `PlatformUserID` string in the mod's own record, not just the index.

**Prerequisites.** Authentic Sender Context; Portal Record Store

## 47. Tag Author Rewrite

`FEASIBLE` · `REACTIVE-ONLY` · effort: small-medium

Stop treating `s_tagauthor` as evidence and start treating it as a server-owned output field: overwrite it with the verified account of whoever actually caused the change.

**How it works.** As shipped, `ZDOVars.s_tagauthor` (:78619) is worthless as identity. `TeleportWorld.SetText` fills it from `PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.LocalUser.PlatformUserID.ToString()` on the *client* (:143583), and `RPC_SetTag(long sender, string tag, string authorId)` writes `authorId` verbatim (:143599) without ever comparing it to `sender`, and `sender` itself is the self-reported `m_senderPeerID` off the wire (:83609). A modified client can name any account as the author of any tag. It is also cosmetic in vanilla: the only consumer is `TeleportWorld.GetTagSignature` (:143571) feeding `GetTagInfo`'s `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` call (:143566), and `FilterUGC` is literally `return text;` in the server build (:94588-94591) and early-returns on non-PlayFab backends in the client build.

So the field is free real estate. The Tag Watchdog (below) already re-reads every portal's `s_tag`/`s_tagauthor` on its tick and holds the previous known-good snapshot. When it observes a tag change it must attribute it. Attribution sources, in descending confidence:
1. A relay-observed `RPC_SetTag` in the last tick with a matching target ZDOID, whose true sender came from the Authentic Sender Context. Certain, but only covers the minority of retags (see Retag Interception at the Relay).
2. The `RPC_ZDOData` packet that carried the change: a prefix on `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` stamps the current authenticated peer, and the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix fires per-ZDO inside that loop (:77131) — so for *every* laundered retag the server knows exactly which account's socket delivered it. This is the load-bearing path and it covers the common case the relay cannot.
3. Nothing else. Proximity heuristics ("who was standing nearest") are guesses and should never be logged as identity.

On attribution the mod writes the truth back: `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tagauthor, verifiedPlatformUserId)`, plus its own richer record in the Portal Record Store. Because the field is cosmetic and unfiltered on Steam, you can go further and make it human-readable — but note `ZDO.Set(string,…)` overloads exist (:73716) so mod-private keys such as `"tp_lastRetagBy"` / `"tp_lastRetagAt"` are cleaner than overloading a vanilla field, and `ZDODataHelper.ReadData` only *adds* the keys present in an incoming packet (:74718-74730) — it never clears — so a mod-private key the client does not know about survives a client's ZDO push intact.

This is reactive-detection-only for the *change*: the retag has already happened by the time you attribute it. It becomes enforcement only when paired with Tag Watchdog's revert.

**Player experience.** A player retags a portal `MINE` and the hover text reads `MINE` as usual. Server-side, the admin's `/portals` report and the Discord audit line now say `"Elin's Gate" → "MINE" by Steam:76561198… (Elin) at 19:42`, which is true even if the player was running a client that claimed to be someone else. A player who forges the author field sees it corrected within one watchdog tick and appears in the audit trail as an attempted forgery.

**Failure modes.**
- Reactive by construction: the tag was already wrong for up to one watchdog tick before you know who did it.
- If a retag arrives inside a packet carrying many ZDOs, the per-ZDO Deserialize postfix still attributes correctly — but a *batched* packet from a proxying client would attribute all of them to that proxy. No such vanilla path exists; flag it if one appears.
- Rewriting `s_tagauthor` bumps DataRevision and resends the ZDO to every peer (`ZDO.Set` → `IncreaseDataRevision` :73832; `ZDOPeer.ShouldSend` :76003). Doing it on every tick for every portal is a broadcast storm — only write on actual change.
- Vanilla's own `RPC_SetTag` rewrites the field on the next legitimate retag; your value is not sticky against an honest client. Keep the authoritative copy in the mod's record store and treat the ZDO field as a mirror.

**Prerequisites.** Authentic Sender Context; Tag Watchdog; Portal Record Store

## 48. Ownership Pin

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Permanently hold managed portals' ZDO ownership on the server so `RPC_SetTag`, `RPC_Remove` and `RPC_Damage` all route to a machine with no component to receive them — the only genuinely unbypassable portal lock available server-side.

**How it works.** Every mutating operation a client performs on a portal goes through `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string, …)`, which targets `m_zdo.GetOwner()` (:82855-82858). If the owner is the dedicated server, the packet is sent to the server, `RPC_RoutedRPC` sees `m_targetPeerID == m_id` and calls `HandleRoutedRPC` (:83636-83639), which for a ZDO-targeted RPC requires `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zDO)` (:83659) — permanently null on a dedicated server, because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) every tick (:100465) and `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` only instantiates around it (:82268-82276). The RPC is dropped on the floor. This is not a check that can be bypassed; it is an absence of the receiving code path.

What that kills, for a server-owned portal:
- **Retag.** `TeleportWorld.SetText` → `InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", …)` (:143583) → dropped. The player types a name, confirms, and nothing changes anywhere. `RPC_SetTag` also no-ops on any other machine because it is gated on `m_nview.IsOwner()` (:143589).
- **Demolition.** The hammer's remove path calls `WearNTear.Remove()` for any WearNTear-bearing piece (Player.RemovePiece :12405-12408) → `InvokeRPC("RPC_Remove", blockDrop)` (:150411-150416) → dropped. Note the hammer only calls `ClaimOwnership()` on the *non*-WearNTear fallback branch (:12419), so it never tries to steal the portal first.
- **Damage destruction.** `WearNTear.Damage` → `InvokeRPC("RPC_Damage", hit)` (:150315-150320) → dropped. `RPC_Damage` is `IsOwner()`-gated anyway (:150332).
- **Client-side ZDO destruction.** `ZDOMan.DestroyZDO(zdo)` is gated on `zdo.IsOwner()` (:76929-76935), so a non-owning client cannot even queue the destroy broadcast.

Holding the pin requires beating two independent ownership thieves:
(a) `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901-76926) runs every 2s per peer and reassigns any persistent ZDO in that peer's active area whose owner is not itself in an active area — and the server never is, because of the 1e6 pin (`IsInPeerActiveArea` :76887-76892). Block with a Harmony **prefix on `ZDO.SetOwner(long uid)`** (:74627) that returns false when the ZDO's prefab is in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash`, the portal is in the managed set, and `uid != 0L && uid != ZDOMan.GetSessionID()`. This is the Wonderland `ZdoSetOwnerPatch` pattern (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313). The predicate must fail fast on prefab hash — `SetOwner` is a global hot path.
(b) **The correction the existing research misses:** ownership also arrives over the wire *without* going through `SetOwner`. `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` calls `zDO.SetOwnerInternal(ownerInternal)` directly at :77114 and :77128, bypassing the public setter entirely — and the :77112-77117 branch applies an owner change even when the incoming DataRevision is *not* newer, as long as `OwnerRevision` is higher. A `SetOwner` prefix therefore does **not** stop a client from claiming a managed portal. You must also prefix the public `ZDO.SetOwnerInternal(long uid)` (:74636) with the same predicate, or re-assert ownership in the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix on every arriving portal packet.

After claiming: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` (:77362 for the session id), then `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706) so every peer learns the new owner immediately. A slow reconcile tick (2-5s) re-asserts the pin for anything that slipped through.

Scope this to *managed* portals only (admin networks, ward-protected gates, reserved-namespace hubs). Pinning every portal in the world would make the whole build system feel broken.

**Player experience.** A player walks up to an admin hub portal tagged `⌁HUB-CENTRAL`, presses E, types a new name, presses OK — and the hover text still reads `⌁HUB-CENTRAL`. They try again. Nothing. They swing a hammer at it: the removal animation plays, resources are not refunded, the portal is still standing. They hit it with a maul: no damage number, no health loss. The portal is, from their side, part of the terrain. Pair it with a PlayerNotify toast (`"This gate is held by the server."`) triggered from the relay-observed RPC or the watchdog so the wall has an explanation rather than feeling like a bug.

**Failure modes.**
- **The legitimate owner also cannot demolish or rename it.** This is total, not selective. Any managed portal needs a server-side unpin path (an emote command, an admin console command, or a ward/ACL check that releases the pin) or players will file bug reports.
- `ZDO.SetOwner` is called constantly by `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` for every persistent ZDO near every peer. A slow predicate here is a server-wide framerate problem. Check `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(prefab)` first and keep the managed set in a `HashSet<ZDOID>`.
- Blocking `uid == 0L` would break `ReleaseNearbyZDOS`'s release path and vanilla's own `Game.SetConnection` (:100637-100651). Always let 0 and the session id through.
- `ZDOID`s are regenerated on every world load (`ZDO.Load` does `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`, :74552; `ZDOID.SetID` :75878) — the managed set must be rebuilt from the Portal Record Store by position on every boot, not persisted as ZDOIDs.
- A pinned portal never receives a client's own connection writes, so `Game.SetConnection` (:100637) always takes the immediate local-write path for it — which is actually a benefit, but it means vanilla's deferred `RPC_SetConnection` path is never exercised for managed portals and will be untested code in your mod.
- Does not stop `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO` (:76953), which is a ZDO-*less* routed RPC that runs on the server and calls `HandleDestroyedZDO` with no ownership check at all. See Destroy Veto — the pin and the veto are both required.

**Prerequisites.** Portal Record Store; Authentic Sender Context

## 49. Tag Watchdog (detect and revert)

`FEASIBLE` · `REACTIVE-ONLY` · effort: medium

A slow server tick that snapshots every portal's `s_tag`, `s_tagauthor` and Portal connection, compares against the policy-approved state, and rewrites anything that drifted — the honest default mechanism for everything the Ownership Pin is too blunt for.

**How it works.** This is **detect and revert**, not prevention. Say so plainly in the mod's own documentation: for a window of up to one tick, the griefer's tag is real and other players will see it.

Tick body, on a 1-2s timer from a subsystem's `OnUpdate` (the Wonderland Heartbeat/SubsystemRegistry shape):
1. `var portals = ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (:77648) — a freshly flattened list of **every** portal in the world, always resident, no spatial query and no player needed, because portals live in `m_portalObjects` (:76039) and are never released (`ReleaseZDOS` only reassigns ownership, :76872-76883). Use the live `GetPortals()` dictionary (:77643) instead if you need zero allocation, but never mutate it.
2. For each portal: key it by rounded world position (`ZDO.GetPosition()`, :73822 → `(Mathf.RoundToInt(x), RoundToInt(y), RoundToInt(z))`) — **not** by ZDOID, which is regenerated on every world load (`ZDO.Load` :74552, `ZDOID.SetID` :75878). This is exactly the migration TortalPortal's Favorites.cs was forced to make (Favorites.cs:109-124).
3. Read `tag = zdo.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` (:73967 / :78617), `author = zdo.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tagauthor)`, `conn = zdo.GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal)` (:74002).
4. Diff against the Portal Record Store's approved state. On a mismatch, consult the policy chain: reserved namespace → ward gate → ACL → rate limit → claim registry (each is its own option below). The chain answers ALLOW (adopt the new value as the new approved state) or DENY.
5. On DENY: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, approvedTag)`, `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tagauthor, approvedAuthor)`, `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702 — **mandatory**: a tag-only write does not dirty the portal chunk, and `GetSaveClonePerChunk` only writes the ChunkPortal file when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set, :77621-77635, so an un-dirtied revert is silently lost at the next world save), then `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706), then `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` (:100589) once at the end of the tick to re-pair immediately rather than waiting up to 5s.
6. Attribute the change via the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix record (see Tag Author Rewrite) and emit an audit line.

Ordering matters. Vanilla's own `Game.ConnectPortals` runs every 5s (:100580-100587) and its phase-1 reconcile tears down any connection whose partner's `s_tag` differs (:100601). If your revert restores a tag but you do not also restore the connection, vanilla will have already broken the pair. Always revert tag and connection together, then call `ConnectPortals()`.

Budget the sweep. Wonderland's StructureUpkeep caps routed broadcasts at 256 per sweep because the first pass over a long-lived world produced thousands of dirty ZDOs in one frame; the same applies to a mass revert or a lockdown that nulls every connection.

**Player experience.** A griefer walks into an unclaimed corner of your base, retags your `farm` portal to `farm ` (trailing space — a different network under vanilla's ordinal string comparison, :100601) and walks away. Within a second or two the tag snaps back to `farm`, the pair re-forms, and the griefer's own portal is left unconnected. Meanwhile the server log and the Discord channel carry `[SECURITY:PortalRetag] Steam:7656… (Bjorn) tried "farm" → "farm " at (412, 31, -1180); reverted.` A legitimate owner renaming their own portal sees the new name stick, because the policy chain said ALLOW and the store adopted it.

**Failure modes.**
- **There is a real window.** Between the malicious write landing and the revert, up to one tick, the wrong tag is live and a fast attacker can walk through a mis-paired portal. Shortening the tick costs CPU and broadcast bandwidth linearly.
- An attacker in a tight loop (a scripted client pushing `RPC_ZDOData` faster than your tick) makes the portal flap. Detect flapping (N reverts in M seconds on one portal) and escalate to the Ownership Pin for that portal plus a kick (`ZNet.instance.Kick`, :81658).
- Forgetting `SetDirtyPortals()` makes every revert vanish at the next world save with no error anywhere — the single most likely shipped bug in this design.
- `GetPortalList()` allocates a fresh `List<ZDO>` every call (:77648-77656). At 1s on a world with thousands of portals that is real GC churn; cache and refresh on a slower cadence, or iterate `GetPortals()`.
- A moved portal appears twice in `GetPortalList()` because `AddIfPortal` keys on the *current* sector and never removes the old entry (:77732-77752), and `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portals (:73752). Deduplicate by ZDOID. Never move a portal ZDO.
- Rewriting a tag on a portal a client owns loses a DataRevision race if the client re-pushes; pair the revert with a temporary Ownership Pin on that portal for a few seconds.

**Prerequisites.** Portal Record Store; Authentic Sender Context

**Citations.** ZDOMan.GetPortalList — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77648-77656 · ZDOMan.GetPortals (live dictionary) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77643-77646 · ZDOMan.m_portalObjects — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76039; portals never released, ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS :76872-76883 · ZDO.GetString / ZDO.Set(int,string) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73967, :73721 · ZDO.GetConnectionZDOID — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74002 · ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702; ChunkPortal write gated on DirtyPortalObjects — :77621-77635 · ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77706 · Game.ConnectPortals phase-1 tag-mismatch teardown — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589-100606 (teardown :100601) · Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine 5s cadence — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100580-100587 · ZDOID regenerated on load — ZDO.Load :74552, ZDOID.SetID :75878 · ZDO.SetSector early-return for portals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73752-73768 · TortalPortal Favorites ZDOID→position migration — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/Favorites.cs:109-124 · Wonderland StructureUpkeep broadcast budget — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/StructureUpkeep.cs:29-40

## 50. Portal Record Store

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Where per-portal ownership, ACLs, network membership and approved-tag state actually live: a position-keyed mod file as the authority, mirrored into mod-private ZDO keys for locality — with a precise account of what survives what.

**How it works.** Three candidate stores, and only one combination works.

**(a) Vanilla ZDO fields.** `s_creator` (:78393) is the right *semantic* home for build ownership and, once notarised by Creator Attestation, is trustworthy. But it is a single long with no room for an ACL, a network name, a lock flag or a claim timestamp. `s_tagauthor` (:78619) is a free string but is overwritten by every legitimate `RPC_SetTag` (:143599).

**(b) Mod-private ZDO keys.** `ZDO.Set(string name, T value)` overloads exist for every type (:73559-73727) and hash the name internally, exactly as `PrivateArea` does with its runtime-concatenated `"pu_id"+i` / `"pu_name"+i` keys (:137338-137347). So `zdo.Set("tp_owner", platformUserIdString)`, `zdo.Set("tp_net", networkName)`, `zdo.Set("tp_lock", 1)`, `zdo.Set("tp_claimed", ticks)` all work and cost nothing.
  - They **persist**: portal ZDOs are saved wholesale into the dedicated `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal` file (:113180) by `GetSaveClonePerChunk` (:77621-77635) with no `Persistent` filter — but **only when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set**, which a plain `ZDO.Set` does not do. Always follow with `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702).
  - They **survive a client's ZDO push**: `ZDO.Deserialize` → `ZDODataHelper.ReadData` (:74718-74730) calls `ZDOExtraData.Add` per key present in the packet and never clears the dictionaries, so a key the client's copy lacks is not removed. A client that *does* hold the key echoes it back verbatim from `ZDO.Serialize` (:74112). Either way the key survives an honest client. A *malicious* client can rewrite it (there is no ownership check on any ZDO setter — `ZDO.Set(int,int,bool okForNotOwner)` ignores its own parameter, :73648-73654), which is why this is a mirror, not the authority.
  - They must not collide with `ZDOExtraData.s_sessionOnly` (seeded from the 16 `ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes`, :74814-74825 / :78689-78693) or they are stripped from every save in the world. A `tp_` prefix is safe.
  - Keep the count small: `ZPackage.WriteNumItems` caps a per-type field count at 32767 (:83237-83246) and `ZDODataHelper.WriteToDisk` warns above 100 (:74662-74675). Put anything list-shaped in one string or byte[].

**(c) A mod-side file.** `BepInEx.Paths.ConfigPath/TortalPortalLite.Portals.<worldName>.json`, written temp-then-move, the SupplySwitch pattern (SupplySwitch.cs:100-165). **Keyed by rounded world position, never by ZDOID** — `ZDO.Load` renumbers every ZDOID on world load (`m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`, :74552) and `ZDOID.SetID` forces `UserKey = UnknownFormerUserKey`, so a ZDOID-keyed file points at nothing after a restart. This is the exact bug TortalPortal's Favorites hit and fixed (Favorites.cs:109-124) and the one Wonderland's SupplySwitch still masks by pruning dead ids on save.

**The working combination:** the file is the authority; the ZDO keys are a mirror the watchdog re-asserts. On boot, rebuild the in-memory `Dictionary<PosKey, PortalRecord>` from the file, then reconcile against `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()`: portals in the world but not the file are new (attest and adopt); records in the file with no portal within ~0.5m are demolished (retain for a grace period, then prune). Because portals are all resident from world load (`ZDOMan.LoadChunks` :76474-76531, and the load-time `Game.ConnectPortals()` at :76523 runs before any peer connects), this reconcile can happen in the pre-peer window where every portal ZDO is server-owned and uncontested (`ZDO.Load` leaves `Owned = false`, :74550-74556) — the cheapest possible moment to claim and stamp.

A fourth store exists and should be used for *per-player* one-shot facts rather than per-portal ones: world global keys (`ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey("tplite_...")`, :115943), which persist in the world save and travel with its backups — the FirstSpawnGrant pattern.

**Player experience.** Invisible directly. What players notice is that ownership, network membership and lock state survive server restarts, world backups being restored, and the portal being unloaded for months — and that an admin running `/portals` gets a report with real names attached to portals built by players who have not logged in since spring.

**Failure modes.**
- Position keys break if a portal is ever moved. Never call `ZDO.SetPosition` on a portal: `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752), so it stays filed under its old sector in `m_portalObjects` forever, `FindObjects` stops delivering it to the new zone (:77367-77381), and `HandleDestroyedZDO` looks it up under the *new* index and leaks it (:76976-76986).
- Two portals stacked within the rounding tolerance collide in the key space. Use a 0.1m-resolution key or include the prefab hash.
- A restored world backup and a current mod file disagree — the file will claim ownership of portals that no longer exist and miss ones that do. Reconcile at boot, log the delta, never auto-delete on the first pass.
- The mirrored ZDO keys can be forged by a modified client; treat a mismatch between file and ZDO as an intrusion signal, and always resolve in favour of the file.
- Forgetting `SetDirtyPortals()` after writing mod keys means they are never written to the ChunkPortal file and quietly vanish on restart.

## 51. Reserved Tag Namespace

`FEASIBLE` · `REACTIVE-ONLY` · effort: small

Declare a prefix (e.g. a leading `⌁` or `#`) that only the server and admins may write, and enforce it by reverting any player-written tag that uses it — plus the honest admission that vanilla's 10-character limit and rich-text stripping shape what is possible.

**How it works.** A configured list of reserved prefixes and exact reserved names. The Tag Watchdog's policy chain rejects any tag change into the reserved space unless the attributed account is in `ZNet.instance.m_adminList` (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(hostName)`, :81811) or the portal's Portal Record Store entry says it is server-managed.

The server side is unconstrained. `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` applies no length cap and no filter (:143587-143602), and `ZDO.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, …)` (:73721) writes any string. `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is `return text;` in the server build (:94588-94591), and on a Steam backend the client computes the censored flag in `GetTagInfo` (:143566-143569) and then discards it because `GetHoverText` only surfaces the warning when `ZNet.m_onlineBackend == OnlineBackendType.PlayFab` (:143462). So a server-written reserved tag can be as long and as decorated as you like — it will display in full on the hover label.

The **client** side is where the limits bite:
- The player-facing text box is hard-capped at 10 characters: `TeleportWorld.Interact` calls `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` (:143482) and `TextInput.Show` assigns `m_inputField.characterLimit = charLimit` (:61515-61522). So a player *cannot type* a long reserved tag even if they wanted to — a long prefix is self-enforcing against honest clients, and the watchdog covers modified ones.
- Rich text is stripped from the displayed label: `GetHoverText` runs the tag through `RemoveRichTextTags()` (:143459 → assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703, `Regex.Replace(text, "<[\\/a-zA-Z0-9= \"''#;:()$_-]*?>", "")`). Do not plan on coloured reserved tags.
- `GetHoverName()` returns the hard-coded literal `"Teleport"` (:143466-143469), so the reserved marking can only appear in the hover *text*, never the hover *name*.
- Tag matching is bare C# `string !=` on `GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` with `""` default (Game.ConnectPortals :100601, FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100669) — **ordinal, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant**. `Hub` / `hub` / `Hub ` are three different networks. A reserved-namespace check must therefore be case- and whitespace-exact, and you should additionally normalise/reject trailing-whitespace tags as a griefing vector in their own right (see Anti-Grief Tag Integrity).

A reserved name is also a *lock*: combine with the Ownership Pin for reserved portals and the namespace becomes genuinely unwritable rather than merely reverted.

**Player experience.** A player opens a portal's rename box and types `⌁HUB`. They get 10 characters to play with, hit OK, and within a second the name reverts to whatever it was, with a centre-screen toast: `Tags starting with ⌁ are reserved for server gates.` The admin hub network's portals all read `⌁HUB-CENTRAL`, `⌁HUB-SWAMP` — names no player can produce through the vanilla text box at all, because they are longer than 10 characters.

**Failure modes.**
- Reactive unless combined with the Ownership Pin. A reserved tag written by a modified client is live until the next watchdog tick.
- Unicode in a reserved prefix may render as a missing-glyph box in some clients' fonts. Test the exact glyph against the shipped UI font before committing to it.
- A reserved tag written by the server *onto a portal a player owns* can be clobbered by that client's next ZDO push if you do not also pin ownership.
- If the reserved prefix is short enough to type (≤10 chars total), an honest player can create a colliding tag by accident and be confusingly refused.

**Prerequisites.** Tag Watchdog; Portal Record Store

**Citations.** TeleportWorld.Interact 10-char TextInput — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143482; TextInput.RequestText/Show :61509-61522 · TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag: no length cap, no filter — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143587-143602 · CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC is `return text;` server-side — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:94588-94591 · TeleportWorld.GetHoverText RemoveRichTextTags — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143459; StringExtensionMethods.RemoveRichTextTags — assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703 · TeleportWorld.GetHoverName returns "Teleport" — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143466-143469 · Game.ConnectPortals ordinal tag comparison — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100601; FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100669 · ZNet.IsAdmin — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81811 · ZDO.Set(int,string) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73721

**Open questions.**

If it clamps, a player opening the rename dialog on a server-written 13-character reserved tag and pressing OK would save back a truncated version. IN-GAME CHECK: server-write a 20-char tag, open and confirm the dialog on a vanilla client, and re-read `s_tag`.
