## 66. Admin command channel: server-registered ConsoleCommand + RPC_RemoteCommand

`FEASIBLE` · `ADMIN-ONLY` · effort: small

Register onlyServer/remoteCommand console commands from a Terminal.InitTerminal postfix; an admin types them in their own vanilla F5 console and the server executes them, replying into that admin's console.

**How it works.** Harmony-postfix `Terminal.InitTerminal` and construct commands:

`new Terminal.ConsoleCommand("tplite.list", "[tag] — list portals", handler, isCheat:false, isNetwork:false, onlyServer:true, isSecret:false, allowInDevBuild:false, hideBehindDevCommands:false, optionsFetcher:null, alwaysRefreshTabOptions:false, remoteCommand:true)` — exact 13-parameter ctor at :43094/:43112.

The delivery path, all verified: the admin's client runs `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (:45734); `ConsoleCommand.IsValid` (:43203) fails because `OnlyServer` requires `ZNet.instance.IsServer()`; control falls to the `value.RemoteCommand && !ZNet.instance.IsServer()` branch (:45743) → `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text)` (:81869) → server `RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879), which is admin-gated by `ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())` — the same authenticated PlatformUserID vanilla uses for kick/ban (:81670) → `InternalCommand(rpc, command)` (:81891) → `Console.instance.TryRunCommand(command)`.

`Console.instance` **is** non-null on a dedicated server: `Game.Awake` instantiates `m_consolePrefab` when absent (:100038-100041).

Reply to the requesting admin with `ZNet.instance.RemotePrint(peer.m_rpc, line)` (:81635) → client `RPC_RemotePrint` → `Console.instance.Print`. Resolve the peer from the ZRpc by reproducing the private `ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` (:80504) as `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)`. Also call `args.Context.AddString(line)`, which additionally writes `ZLog.Log("Console: " + line)` (:45983-45985) so every admin action is in the server log.

Command set: `tplite.list [tag]`, `tplite.show <x,z>`, `tplite.dump <x,z>` (full ZDO key dump via `ZDOExtraData.GetData` :75108), `tplite.health`, `tplite.repair [--dry-run]`, `tplite.reload`, `tplite.export`, `tplite.snapshot <name>`, `tplite.restore <name>`, `tplite.tag <x,z> <tag>`, `tplite.link <a> <b>`, `tplite.unlink <a>`, `tplite.lockdown on|off`, `tplite.uninstall --clean-keys`.

Namespace every command `tplite.` — `ConsoleCommand`'s ctor does `commands[command.ToLower()] = this` (an indexer assignment, :43096/:43114), so a name collision with another mod **silently overwrites** rather than throwing.

**Player experience.** An operator joins the server with a vanilla client, is on adminlist.txt, presses F5, types `tplite.health` and presses Enter. Two seconds later their console fills with `[tplite] 214 portals / 61 tags / 2 stranded / 1 dangling / 0 cross-tag`. A non-admin typing the same command gets `You are not admin` printed back by ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand (:81883). Ordinary players never see anything.

**Failure modes.**
- Calling `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(cmd)` from server-side mod code: the IsServer() branch passes a null rpc (:81873) into `InternalCommand`, which dereferences `rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName()` unconditionally at :81893 → NullReferenceException. Call `Console.instance.TryRunCommand(cmd)` directly instead.
- Registering a command name another mod already took: the indexer assignment (:43096) clobbers silently, with no log, and the loser's command simply stops working.
- Setting `isCheat:true` — `Terminal.IsCheatsEnabled()` requires the static `m_cheat` flag (:45721-45732), so a cheat command may refuse on the server; keep ops commands non-cheat and rely on the adminlist gate.
- Assuming `onlyAdmin:true` adds a check — `ConsoleCommand.IsValid` (:43203-43217) never reads `OnlyAdmin`; the ConsoleEvent overload does not even fold it into OnlyServer (:43120), unlike the ConsoleEventFailable overload (:43100). The real gate is RPC_RemoteCommand's adminlist test.
- Long reports: one RemotePrint per line is one ZRpc.Invoke each. Chunk to ~40 lines per response and paginate.

**Prerequisites.** PortalCensus — the single-source-of-truth index engine

No `Console.ReadLine`/stdin reader appears in the assembly; `Console.Update` only drains `Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog` (:42923) and reads ZInput. ## 67. File-queue command channel (scriptable, no in-game presence)

`FEASIBLE` · `ADMIN-ONLY` · effort: small

A watched text file the operator appends command lines to from ssh/cron; the mod polls its mtime, executes each line on the main thread, and writes the result to a sibling response file.

**How it works.** Extend Wonderland's existing config-poll pattern (WonderlandPlugin.PollConfigFile, Plugin.cs:97) to a second file. Every 1 s (configurable) compare `File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc(<config>/TortalPortalLite.cmd)` against a cached stamp. On change, read all lines, execute each through the same handler table the console commands use, append `<timestamp> <command> -> <result>` to `TortalPortalLite.cmd.out`, then truncate the input file (write-temp-then-File.Replace, the atomic pattern SupplySwitch.Save and TortalPortal/PortalExport.Write:75 both use).

Everything runs on the main thread inside `Update()`, so ZDOMan access is safe — ZDOMan has no locking anywhere and vanilla's only background thread (`ZNet.SaveWorldThread`, :80583) deliberately operates on a clone built on the main thread by `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` (:76197-76205).

This is the only command channel that works with zero players connected, zero admin clients, and (if the stdin question resolves negative) zero interactive console. It makes every ops action cron-able: a nightly `echo tplite.export >> …/TortalPortalLite.cmd` produces a fresh JSON dump; a monitoring script tails `.cmd.out`.

Security model: the file lives inside `BepInEx/config`, so filesystem permission on the server box *is* the authorization. Explicitly refuse to accept a command file outside `BepInEx.Paths.ConfigPath`, and never make the handler table reachable from any network path without the adminlist check.

If a background thread ever needs to emit text (an HTTP handler, a webhook callback), do not touch Terminal directly — enqueue into the public `Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog` `ConcurrentQueue<string>` (:43245), which `Console.Update` drains one line per frame into `AddString` → `ZLog.Log` (:42923-42925). Vanilla's own save thread uses exactly this to report save errors (:80675, :80710).

**Player experience.** Invisible to players. An operator on a phone over ssh runs `echo 'tplite.repair --dry-run' >> ~/valheim/BepInEx/config/TortalPortalLite.cmd; sleep 2; tail -20 ~/valheim/BepInEx/config/TortalPortalLite.cmd.out` and reads `would relink 'merchant-ring' member #3 (4420,95,2180): connection None -> #1; would retag 2 portals 'trade' -> 'TRADE'`.

**Failure modes.**
- Executing the file's contents off the main thread — ZDOMan is not thread-safe and a concurrent GetPortalList during a SendZDOs sweep will throw or corrupt.
- Not truncating after execution: the same commands re-run on the next unrelated mtime bump.
- Leaving the file world-writable on a shared host — this channel has no authentication beyond filesystem permissions.
- Editor tools that write via rename rather than in-place can make mtime jump backwards; compare for inequality, not greater-than (the same reason Wonderland's PollConfigFile compares `stamp == _configStamp`, Plugin.cs:109).

**Prerequisites.** Admin command channel: server-registered ConsoleCommand + RPC_RemoteCommand

**Citations.** WonderlandPlugin.PollConfigFile — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Plugin.cs:97-131 · SupplySwitch.Save atomic write — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/ItemFlow/SupplySwitch.cs:100-165 · PortalExport.Write atomic write — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PortalExport.cs:75 · ZDOMan.PrepareSave main-thread clone — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76197-76205 · ZNet.SaveWorldThread — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:80583 · Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:43245; drained Console.Update :42923-42925; vanilla producer :80675

- How fast does the operator expect a response? A 1 s poll costs one File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc per second; measure that on the target filesystem (network/overlayfs mounts can make stat expensive).

## 68. Network definition as a hot-reloaded JSON file (with worked example)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

A separate, position-keyed JSON document next to the .cfg that declares admin-defined portal networks (ring / hub / pairs / one-way chain) and is re-parsed and re-applied on save without a restart.

**How it works.** BepInEx's flat `key=value` `.cfg` cannot express a list of networks each with a list of members, so put the topology in its own file and keep the `.cfg` for scalars. Poll `File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc` on a 5 s timer exactly as `WonderlandPlugin.PollConfigFile` does (Plugin.cs:97), parse into an immutable model, validate, and only then swap the live model (never mutate in place mid-tick).

**Members are resolved by position, never by ZDOID** — ZDOIDs are renumbered every world load (`ZDO.Load` :74552). Resolution: for each declared `at`, scan the census for the nearest portal ZDO within `radius` (default 6 m); ambiguity (two portals inside the radius) is a validation error, not a coin flip.

```jsonc
// BepInEx/config/TortalPortalLite.networks.json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "world": "Wubarrk",          // advisory; warn if != ZNet.instance.GetWorldName() (:80876)
  "defaults": { "reassertSeconds": 2.0, "onMissingMember": "warn", "tagCase": "exact" },
  "networks": [
    { "id": "merchant-ring", "enabled": true, "topology": "ring", "tag": "TRADE",
      "members": [
        { "name": "Haldor",   "at": [1240.5, 31.2, -3310.0], "radius": 6.0 },
        { "name": "Docks",    "at": [-210.0, 33.9, 180.0],   "radius": 6.0 },
        { "name": "Mistvale", "at": [4420.0, 95.4, 2180.0],  "radius": 6.0 }
      ] },
    { "id": "spawn-hub", "enabled": true, "topology": "hub", "tag": "HUB",
      "hub":   { "name": "Spawn Gate", "at": [0.0, 32.0, 4.0], "radius": 8.0 },
      "rotation": { "mode": "cycle", "dwellSeconds": 120 },
      "spokes": [
        { "name": "Swamp",  "at": [-980.0, 30.5, 1420.0] },
        { "name": "Plains", "at": [2600.0, 41.0, -700.0] }
      ] },
    { "id": "lore-gate", "enabled": false, "topology": "oneway-chain", "tag": "DEEP",
      "members": [ {"name":"A","at":[10,30,10]}, {"name":"B","at":[20,30,20]} ] }
  ]
}
```

**`tag` is load-bearing, not cosmetic.** `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 clears any connection whose partner's `s_tag` string differs (:100601) using bare ordinal `string !=`. Every member of a network must carry one byte-identical tag or vanilla tears the network down within 5 s. The validator must therefore reject two networks sharing a tag, and reject a tag that collides with an unmanaged portal's tag.

Validation before swap: unique `id`; unique `tag`; ≥2 members for ring/pairs; hub has ≥1 spoke; no member appears twice; no `at` beyond ±16320 m (`ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex` clamps out-of-range zones to sector 0, :115755-115774); no `at` with y>3000 unless explicitly allowed (`Character.InInterior` :4538). On any error, keep the previous model, log every error, and write them to the `.cmd.out` file.

**Player experience.** An operator edits `TortalPortalLite.networks.json` in nano, saves, and within 5 s the server log prints `[Networks] reloaded: 3 networks, 8 members, 0 errors`. Within a further 2 s a player standing at the Docks portal sees its hover text change from `Teleport — 'docks'` to `Teleport — 'TRADE'` and the gate's blue connected-glow snap on (TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal re-evaluates every 0.5 s, :143491-143509). Walking through now lands them at Haldor rather than at whatever random same-tag gate vanilla had picked.

**Failure modes.**
- Two networks declaring the same `tag`: vanilla's random same-tag pairing (Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664-100679) will cross-link them the instant the reassert loop is late, and phase 1 will not tear it down because the tags match.
- Declaring a per-member display tag: impossible without patching. Phase 1's `zDO.GetString(s_tag) != @string` test (:100601) transitively forces every linked portal in a network onto one literal string.
- A member coordinate that no longer has a portal (player demolished it): with `onMissingMember: "warn"` the ring silently degrades to a chain; the health scanner must surface it loudly.
- Whitespace or case drift in `tag` ('Base ' vs 'Base') producing two invisible networks — the comparison is ordinal and whitespace-significant.
- Hot-swapping the model mid-tick while the reassert engine is iterating it.

**Prerequisites.** PortalCensus — the single-source-of-truth index engine

**Citations.** Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 tag-equality teardown — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100594-100606 (tag test :100601) · Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100664-100679 · ZDO.Load ZDOID renumber — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74552 · ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex out-of-range clamp — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115755-115774 · Character.InInterior — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:4538-4541 · ZNet.GetWorldName — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:80876 · WonderlandPlugin.PollConfigFile — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Plugin.cs:97

**Open questions.**
- Which JSON parser? BepInEx 5.4.23.5 ships no JSON library and TortalPortal vendors none; Wonderland's DiscordWebhook hand-rolls only an escaper (DiscordWebhook.cs). Either vendor a ~400-line reader or use `UnityEngine.JsonUtility` — but JsonUtility cannot deserialize top-level arrays or Dictionary and needs [Serializable] mirror classes. Decide before writing the schema.

## 69. NetworkReassertEngine — the only writer, and the race with vanilla's 5 s pass

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

A 2 Hz loop that force-writes each managed portal's intended tag and connection using ownership-claim + ForceSendZDO, designed so vanilla's own reconciler never tears the topology down.

**How it works.** Exactly one engine in the mod writes `s_tag` or `ConnectionType.Portal`. Every tick (default 2.0 s; must be < 5 s) it walks the resolved network model and, per member, compares the census's current tag/connection against the intended values. If they differ it performs vanilla's own immediate-write recipe verbatim (`Game.SetConnection` :100637-100646):

```
zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID());                       // :74627 / :77362
zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, intendedTag);                       // :73721
zdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, intendedTarget);  // :73656
ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);                   // :77706
ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals();                         // :76702 (SetConnection already does this, :73661; a tag-only write does NOT)
```

Use `SetConnection`, never `UpdateConnection` — `ZDOExtraData.UpdateConnection` returns false and writes nothing when no connection entry exists (:74962-74976).

**Why this survives vanilla.** `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 (:100596-100605) only clears a connection when the partner ZDO is missing, the partner's tag differs, or the partner's own connection is `None`. It never checks reciprocity. So a ring A→B→C→A, a fan-in hub, and even a self-loop are all indefinitely stable *at runtime* as long as every member shares one literal tag and no member's connection is `None`. Phase 2 (:100607-100622) only touches portals already reading `None`. Therefore a correctly-asserted network is invisible to vanilla and the 2 s loop is a repair mechanism, not a race.

**Idempotence is free.** `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` early-returns when type and target are unchanged (:74951-74961) and `BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false on an equal value (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345), so `ZDO.Set` skips `IncreaseDataRevision`. An unchanged re-assert generates zero DataRevision bumps, zero network traffic and zero disk dirtying. Budget `ForceSendZDO` calls per tick (cap 256, mirroring StructureUpkeep.MaxHealthBroadcastsPerSweep) so a first-boot mass repair does not spike every peer in one frame.

**Ownership contention.** `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` runs every 2 s and hands any persistent ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer (:76872-76885, :76901-76927). Our claim will be stolen back — that is fine, the *value* already went out via ForceSendZDO. Only add the `ZDO.SetOwner` Harmony prefix guard (the WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313 pattern) if measurement shows write-back contention; keep the predicate a single `PortalPrefabHash.Contains` test and never block `uid == 0` or `uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()`.

**Player experience.** A player demolishes one gate of a three-gate ring. Within ≤5 s vanilla's reconciler notices the dangling partner and nulls the neighbours' links; within ≤2 s of that the reassert engine re-closes the ring between the two survivors and their hover text goes from `unconnected` back to `connected`. A player retagging a managed gate through the vanilla 10-character box sees their new tag persist for at most 2 s and then snap back to `TRADE`, with a toast: `This gate belongs to the TRADE network.`

**Failure modes.**
- Setting reassertSeconds ≥ 5 s: vanilla's phase 2 wins a window and randomly re-pairs a briefly-orphaned member (`UnityEngine.Random.Range` :100678).
- Writing a tag without calling `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702): `ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision` (:73832) only routes to `SetDirtySector`, and portals are explicitly excluded from the ordinary chunk save (`AddObjectsPerChunk` filter :77572). The rename is live but silently absent from the next world save.
- Racing vanilla's deferred branch: `Game.SetConnection` only defers to an online owner (:100647-100650). Our direct claim-and-write bypasses that, which is correct — but it means a client that currently owns the portal may push a conflicting higher-DataRevision blob back via `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77103-77133), which replaces the whole ZDO with no field-level merge. The 2 s loop re-corrects it; instantaneous consistency is not achievable.
- Caching ZDO object references between ticks — vanilla itself does this in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` and can force-write through a pooled, recycled reference (Game.ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698 vs ZDOPool.Release in HandleDestroyedZDO :76990). Do not copy that.

**Prerequisites.** Network definition as a hot-reloaded JSON file (with worked example); PortalCensus — the single-source-of-truth index engine

## 70. HealthScanEngine — orphan, strand and corruption detection

`FEASIBLE` · `ADMIN-ONLY` · effort: small-medium

A 30 s pure-read pass over the census that classifies every pathology vanilla's pairing algorithm can produce, including the permanent one-member strand that 3+ same-tag portals always create.

**How it works.** Runs on the census snapshot, writes nothing. Each finding carries severity, portal id(s) and a suggested repair.

1. **Odd-count strand (the big one).** Group portals by exact `s_tag`. For any group of size N ≥ 3, vanilla's strictly-pairwise phase 2 leaves exactly ⌊N/2⌋ pairs and `N mod 2` permanently orphaned members: the surviving pair re-confirms itself every tick, so the orphan never rotates in. Report every unmanaged tag group with N ≥ 3, naming the currently-orphaned member and warning that *which* member is orphaned is dictionary-bucket order and changes across restarts (iteration order comes from `m_portalObjects` enumeration in `GetPortalList` :77648-77656).
2. **Dangling connection.** `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` non-None but `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id)` returns null. Vanilla clears this within 5 s (:100600-100603); report only if it persists across two scans, which indicates something is re-writing it.
3. **Non-reciprocal link.** A→B while B→C or B→None. Legal and stable in vanilla (phase 1 has no reciprocity check) — informational for unmanaged portals, an error for a network declared `pairs`.
4. **Self-loop.** A→A. Stable at runtime, but **erased at save**: `RegenerateConnectionHashData` writes the source slot then immediately overwrites it with the Target slot because target != None (:75461-75478). Flag as 'will not survive restart'.
5. **Cross-tag link.** Partner tag != own tag; vanilla will tear it down within 5 s.
6. **Duplicate / near-duplicate tags.** Ordinal comparison means `Base`, `base` and `Base ` are three networks. Report groups that differ only by case or trailing whitespace.
7. **Out-of-world.** |pos.xz| beyond ~16320 m falls into `ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex`'s clamp-to-sector-0 bucket (:115755-115774) — the same bucket the server's own pinned reference position maps to.
8. **Interior portal.** `pos.y > 3000f` (:4538) — built inside a dungeon; shares the surface XZ zone, worth flagging for operators who forbid it.
9. **Unknown prefab.** `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(zdo.GetPrefab())` null — a portal from an uninstalled mod.
10. **Sector duplication.** The same ZDOID appearing twice in `GetPortalList()` — `AddIfPortal` adds under the current sector without removing the old entry (:77732-77752), so any repositioned portal duplicates and `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76980-76986) can only clean one bucket, leaking the other permanently.

Note there is **no** 'portal in an unloaded zone' pathology: portals live in `m_portalObjects`, are loaded wholesale from the dedicated `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal` file at world load (:76474-76482), are never released (`ReleaseZDOS` only reassigns ownership, :76872-76885), and `FlushClientObjects` is client-only (:76180-76183). The census is always complete.

**Player experience.** No player-visible effect. The operator's 30 s log line reads `[Health] OK` most of the time, and on a problem: `[Health] tag 'home' has 5 portals — 2 pairs + 1 permanently stranded at (410,33,-88); tag 'Base ' (trailing space) is a separate 1-portal network, probably a typo for 'Base'`. A player who tagged three gates `home` and wondered why one never connects finally gets an answer an admin can give them.

**Failure modes.**
- Reporting a dangling connection during the normal 5 s window after someone demolishes a gate — require two consecutive scans before flagging.
- Reporting every untagged portal as one giant broken group: `ZDO.GetString` defaults to `""` (ZDOExtraData.GetString :75079-75082), so every untagged portal in the world is a single tag group and freshly placed untagged gates genuinely do auto-pair at random. Treat tag `""` as a special case with its own message.
- Treating the orphan as a stable identity — it is bucket-order-dependent and can differ after a restart.
- Missing a duplicated portal because the diff is keyed by rounded position, which collapses the two entries; key the duplicate check on ZDOID reference count within the raw list.

**Prerequisites.** PortalCensus — the single-source-of-truth index engine

## 71. Automatic repair pass (with dry-run and blast-radius cap)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Turn each health finding into a bounded, logged, reversible corrective ZDO write — normalising tags, splitting odd groups, clearing dangling links — gated behind an explicit config opt-in and a --dry-run default.

**How it works.** A repair is a (finding → action) table executed on demand (`tplite.repair`) or on a slow timer if `AutoRepair` is enabled. Default is **dry-run**: compute and print every action, write nothing.

Actions, each using the reassert engine's write primitive (claim owner → write → ForceSendZDO → SetDirtyPortals):
- **Tag normalisation.** Trim trailing/leading whitespace and optionally case-fold, when and only when it merges a 1-member group into an existing group. Writing `s_tag` alone requires `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` explicitly (:76702) — `ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision` (:73832) routes to `SetDirtySector`, which the portal chunk ignores (`AddObjectsPerChunk` filter :77572).
- **Odd-group resolution.** For an N≥3 unmanaged group, either (a) suffix the orphan's tag (`home` → `home-2`) so it stops competing, or (b) promote the whole group into a managed ring in the network file. Never silently retag a player's gate without `AllowTagRewrite=true` and an audit entry naming the original tag.
- **Dangling clear.** `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` — identical to what vanilla does 5 s later, useful only when combined with an immediate `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` call (public, :100589) to re-pair in the same frame instead of waiting.
- **Self-loop removal.** Break it before the next save silently does.
- **Duplicate-bucket cleanup.** Not repairable through any public API: the duplicate lives inside the private `m_portalObjects` dictionary. `GetPortals()` (:77643) returns the live dictionary and *can* be mutated to remove the stale entry — powerful and dangerous; gate behind a separate `AllowRegistrySurgery` flag and log loudly.

Every repair emits an audit line and is preceded by an automatic state snapshot (see the snapshot/rollback option), so `tplite.restore pre-repair` undoes the whole batch.

Cap actions per invocation (default 64) and per tick (default 16). Vanilla's own cost model makes this cheap — idempotent re-writes are free — but a first repair on a neglected 400-portal world can otherwise issue hundreds of `ForceSendZDO` calls in one frame, each of which re-serialises the entire ZDO to every peer with no delta encoding (`ZDOMan.SendZDOs` :77053-77062).

**Player experience.** An operator types `tplite.repair` and gets a printed plan: `DRY RUN — 4 actions: retag (410,33,-88) 'home' -> 'home-2' [orphan of 5]; trim 'Base ' -> 'Base' at (12,30,80); clear dangling link at (2600,41,-700); break self-loop at (0,32,4). Re-run with --apply.` They run `tplite.repair --apply`; the log shows `[Repair] applied 4/4, snapshot 'pre-repair-2026-09-12T14:02Z' saved`. A player who had two gates tagged `Base ` and `Base` walks into one and now arrives at the other for the first time.

**Failure modes.**
- Auto-repair on by default: silently retagging player-built gates is the single fastest way to make an operator uninstall the mod. Default off, default dry-run.
- Repairing during the 5 s window in which vanilla is itself mid-repair — the two writes fight and produce audit noise. Skip any portal whose connection changed within the last 6 s.
- Mutating the live `m_portalObjects` dictionary returned by `GetPortals()` (:77643) while `Game.ConnectPortals` is iterating a `GetPortalList()` snapshot of it — the snapshot is a copy so it will not throw, but `AddIfPortal`/`HandleDestroyedZDO` bookkeeping desynchronises.
- Assuming a repair persists: without `SetDirtyPortals()` a tag-only repair is live in memory and absent from the world file.

**Prerequisites.** HealthScanEngine — orphan, strand and corruption detection; NetworkReassertEngine — the only writer, and the race with vanilla's 5 s pass; Network state snapshot, rollback and migration

## 72. AuditEngine — attributed change log for every tag and link write

`CAVEATS` · `REACTIVE-ONLY` · effort: medium

Census-diff as the complete channel, an RPC_RoutedRPC prefix for authenticated attribution, and m_onZDODestroyed for deletions — with 'probable' vs 'confirmed' actor never conflated.

**How it works.** Three complementary sources, only one of which is complete:

**(1) Census diff — the only complete source.** Every tick, diff (tag, tagauthor, connection, position, owner) per portal. This catches changes that never touch the wire: `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally and skips `RouteRPC` entirely when `targetPeerID == m_id` (:83577-83595), and `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string,…)` targets `m_zdo.GetOwner()` (:82855-82858), so a client that already owns a portal retags it in-process with zero packets. The resulting ZDO change still reaches the server, because `ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision` queues `ZDOMan.ClientChanged` on a client (:73832-73849, :77727-77730) and `CreateSyncList`'s non-server branch drains that queue to the server peer regardless of distance (:77241-77258). Detection latency = the census tick.

**(2) `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` Harmony prefix — authenticated attribution when available.** `RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (:83632) is the one and only place where the authentic socket and the payload coexist; `m_senderPeerID` is deserialised straight off the wire (`RoutedRPCData.Deserialize` :83487-83495) and is a client self-report everywhere downstream. In the prefix: save `pkg.GetPos()`, deserialise a **copy** (`new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray())`), match `m_methodHash` against `"RPC_SetTag".GetStableHashCode()`, resolve the true sender as `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)`, and take `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()` — the PlatformUserID the Steam session ticket / PlayFab auth actually verified at connect (ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo :79843-79870; the same identity vanilla's own admin check uses, ZNet.RPC_Kick :81670). Restore `pkg.SetPos()` and return true.

**(3) `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed`** (:76033, invoked :76975) — a public `Action<ZDO>` field fired before removal, so the portal is still readable. Filter with `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(zdo.GetPrefab())`. **Combine, never assign**: `ZNetScene.Awake` already attaches its own handler (:81953).

Record shape: `{utc, portalId, field, from, to, actor, actorConfidence}`. `actorConfidence` is `confirmed` only for source (2); for a census-detected change with no matching RPC it is `probable`, resolved to the nearest connected character within 40 m at detection time (`ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS` :81024-81044), or `unknown`. Follow `AuditLog.Flag`'s discipline of writing `Unknown` rather than guessing (AuditLog.cs:15). Suppress the mod's own writes by having the reassert engine register each intended change in an 'expected' set the audit subtracts.

Store as a bounded ring buffer (2000 entries, the `ItemLedger` pattern) plus an append-only `portal-audit.log`.

**Player experience.** No player-visible effect unless the operator enables the optional toast. The log reads `[AUDIT] tag (1240,31,-3310) 'trade' -> 'TRADE' by 76561198…/Rohan (confirmed) at 14:02:11Z` for a retag that crossed the wire, and `[AUDIT] link (0,32,4) #A -> #B by (probable) Rohan @ 6m` for one that did not. A player who demolishes someone else's gate shows up as `[AUDIT] destroyed (410,33,-88) tag 'home' builder Sigrid`.

**Failure modes.**
- Reading the live `ZPackage` in the RPC prefix without saving/restoring `GetPos()` — the real handler then reads garbage and every routed RPC on the server breaks.
- Assigning to `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` instead of `Delegate.Combine` — this wipes ZNetScene's own handler (:81953) and breaks client-side object destruction for the whole server.
- Trusting `m_senderPeerID` or `s_tagauthor`: both are unverified client input (:83489, :143587-143602).
- Presenting a 'probable' actor as fact in a Discord channel where players read it — this is how a mod gets someone falsely accused of griefing.
- Missing changes made while the mod was down: the audit is a live diff, not a reconstruction. Snapshot at shutdown and diff at boot to catch the gap.

**Prerequisites.** PortalCensus — the single-source-of-truth index engine

## 73. MetricsEngine — portal counts, transit counts and most-used routes

`CAVEATS` · `REACTIVE-ONLY` · effort: medium

Inventory metrics for free from the census; transit metrics only from Wonderland's position-straddle heuristic, because vanilla's own PortalsUsed stat never leaves the client.

**How it works.** **Free, exact metrics** (census-derived, zero extra cost): total portals; portals per tag; per biome (`WorldGenerator.GetBiome` :151692); per builder (`s_creator`); connected vs unconnected; managed vs unmanaged; new/destroyed per hour (from the audit stream). Plus server-wide context vanilla already exposes: `ZDOMan.instance.NrOfObjects()` (:77658), `GetSentZDOs()`/`GetRecvZDOs()` (:77663-:77671), `ZDOPool.GetPoolActive/Size/Total` (used by vanilla at :42773) — all public and all useful for the 'is my ZDO count exploding' question that portal mods get blamed for.

**Transit counts are heuristic only.** Vanilla increments `PlayerStatType.PortalsUsed` (ordinal 15, :106516) via `Game.IncrementPlayerStat` → `PlayerProfile.IncrementStat` (:100569-100572, :106287-106300), which writes an in-memory dictionary saved only into that client's own `.fch`. `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles` (:79653-79670) merely tells each client to save its own file and returns nothing. So the server can never read it.

The usable signal is the straddle test Wonderland already ships and has already tuned against a live false-positive: `PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit(fromPos, toPos, radius=40f)` (PositionWatch.cs:148) walks `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals()` (zero-alloc, :77643) and fires when both ends of a position sample sit within 40 m of some portal, with a secondary check that one end's `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` target is within 60 m of the other end. Sample every 3 s from `ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` (:81024). Invert its sense (count the transit instead of suppressing the speed alarm) and additionally record the two nearest portal ids → a (from,to) route counter, which yields 'most-used routes'.

Exclusions, all cheap and exact: skip when `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)` (respawn); skip when `Character.InInterior(pos)` (:4538) changes across the sample or |Δy| > 1000 (a dungeon door — `class Teleport` has no ZDO at all, :143316-143390, so it must never be counted as a portal transit); skip admins (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName())` :81811) whose `tplite` teleports would otherwise inflate the numbers.

Aggregate on a 60 s timer into a rolling window; emit into the heartbeat line, the JSON export and Discord.

**Player experience.** Players see nothing. The operator's heartbeat line becomes `[Heartbeat] 'Wubarrk' up 3h12m | 4 online: Rohan, Sigrid, … | 214 portals / 61 tags | 37 transits/hr | top route Spawn->Swamp (11)`. A community Discord gets a weekly `#portal-report` embed showing the busiest gates.

**Failure modes.**
- Presenting heuristic transits as exact. A 3 s sample can miss a player who walks through and back, and two portals within 40 m of each other produce false positives.
- Counting dungeon-door transits as portal transits — `Teleport.Interact` (:143345-143370) never touches `NoPortals` and has no ZDO, but produces a huge position jump.
- Counting server-issued teleports (RPC_TeleportPlayer, :41957-41968) as portal use.
- Trying to read `PortalsUsed` from anywhere server-side — it is not networked at all.
- Sampling faster than 3 s on a large server: the cost is O(players) ZDO reads plus a `GetPortals()` walk per player per sample.

**Prerequisites.** PortalCensus — the single-source-of-truth index engine

## 74. Output surface: atomic JSON/CSV file export

`FEASIBLE` · `ADMIN-ONLY` · effort: small

A periodic and on-demand write of the full census, health findings and metrics to a JSON (and CSV) file under BepInEx/config, written temp-then-replace so a reader never sees a torn file.

**How it works.** Serialise the immutable census DTO plus the current health findings and the metrics window. Write to `<name>.tmp`, then `File.Replace`/`File.Move` — the exact atomic pattern `TortalPortal/PortalExport.Write` (PortalExport.cs:75) and Wonderland's `SupplySwitch.Save` (SupplySwitch.cs:100-165) already use, so an external tool tailing the file never reads a half-written document.

Cadence: on a timer (default 300 s), on every network-file reload, on `tplite.export`, and once from the `ZNet.WorldSaveStarted` hook (`public static Action`, :78989, invoked at :80524 on the main thread before `PrepareSave`) so the export is always consistent with the world file on disk.

Two files: `portals.json` (full, nested, machine-readable) and `portals.csv` (flat, one row per portal, for spreadsheets and `awk`). CSV columns: `id,tag,x,y,z,biome,zone,prefab,connected,partnerId,partnerTag,distance,reciprocal,network,ownerPeer,builder,tagAuthor,firstSeen,lastChanged`.

Prior art is already server-side and directly liftable: `PortalExport` is an `IsServer()`-gated coroutine that waits for ZDOMan/Game, counts portals per `s_creator` from `PlacementPatch.GetAllPortals()` (which wraps `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` with a prefab-iterative fallback, PlacementPatch.cs:195) and joins names from `PlayerNames` — the only two files of full TortalPortal that already run exclusively on the server.

Build the DTO on the main thread; serialisation itself can be done on a thread-pool task from the already-copied DTO, never from live ZDOs.

**Player experience.** Invisible to players. A community website cron-rsyncs `portals.json` every 5 minutes and renders a public gate directory. An operator runs `jq '.portals[] | select(.connected==false) | .tag' portals.json | sort | uniq -c` to find every broken network in one line.

**Failure modes.**
- Writing directly over the live file — a reader mid-read gets a truncated document. Always temp-then-replace.
- Serialising live ZDO objects from a background thread; they are pooled and can be recycled mid-serialise (ZDOPool.Release → ZDO.Reset :73536-73545).
- Exporting `sessionZdoId` as the primary key and letting an external tool build state on it — it changes every restart.
- Exporting on a very short timer with a large world: JSON for 1000 portals is ~400 KB and rewriting it every 10 s is pointless disk churn.

**Prerequisites.** Full-realm portal enumeration report (the canonical data model)

## 75. Output surface: Discord webhook reporting

`FEASIBLE` · `ADMIN-ONLY` · effort: small

Fire-and-forget posts of health findings, audit events and a periodic portal summary through Wonderland's already-shipped DiscordWebhook helper.

**How it works.** Lift `DiscordWebhook` verbatim (DiscordWebhook.cs): one shared static `HttpClient` with a 10 s timeout, `Send()` fire-and-forget, `SendBlocking(msg, timeoutMs)` for the shutdown message only — the process can exit before a fire-and-forget task runs — and a hand-rolled JSON escaper so no JSON library is needed. It requires a `System.Net.Http` reference resolved from the net472 reference assemblies (Wonderland.csproj:72).

Event classes, each independently toggleable in config:
- **Health digest** (default: only when findings change) — 'tag `home` now has 5 portals; one is permanently stranded'.
- **Audit stream** (default off, high volume) — retags and relinks with attribution and a confidence marker.
- **Destruction notices** — from `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` (:76033), filtered to `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:100021).
- **Network reload** — 'networks.json reloaded: 3 networks, 0 errors' / the full error list on a failed parse.
- **Periodic summary** — shares the Heartbeat timer rather than running a second one, exactly as Wonderland's `Heartbeat.OnUpdate` shares between the log and Discord heartbeats (Heartbeat.cs:21-56).
- **Server lifecycle** — 'portal engine online / offline', the offline one via `SendBlocking` from `OnDestroy`.

Rate-limit and coalesce in the mod, not in Discord: batch findings into one message per interval, and hard-cap messages per minute. Delivery is best-effort by design — a failed post is logged and dropped, never retried, because nothing else depends on it landing.

Everything posted is derived from the main-thread DTO; the HTTP call itself happens on a thread-pool task and must never touch ZDOMan.

**Player experience.** Players see nothing in-game. The server's Discord gets, in `#server-ops`: `🌀 **Portal health** — 214 portals / 61 tags. ⚠️ tag `home` (5 portals) permanently strands one gate at (410, 33, -88). ⚠️ tag `Base ` looks like a typo for `Base`.` Community members who built the gates learn why one never connects, without an admin having to log in.

**Failure modes.**
- Posting the audit stream by default: a busy server generates dozens of retag events an hour and the channel becomes unreadable.
- Posting 'probable' attribution to a channel players read — a false griefing accusation.
- Using `Send()` from `OnDestroy` — the process exits first and the offline message never arrives; that is exactly why `SendBlocking` exists.
- Creating a new HttpClient per post: socket exhaustion under Mono.
- Leaking the webhook URL into the exported JSON or a log line.

**Prerequisites.** HealthScanEngine — orphan, strand and corruption detection

## 76. Output surface: in-process HTTP endpoint

`CAVEATS` · `ADMIN-ONLY` · effort: medium

An HttpListener on a configurable loopback port serving the census/health/metrics snapshot as JSON and Prometheus text, answered entirely from a main-thread-built immutable DTO.

**How it works.** `System.Net.HttpListener` lives in `System.dll` and the dedicated server ships a full Mono runtime, so no new dependency beyond what the csproj already resolves for `System.Net.Http`.

Architecture is forced by thread-safety: ZDOMan has no locking anywhere, and vanilla's only background thread (`ZNet.SaveWorldThread` :80583) deliberately operates on a clone built on the main thread by `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` (:76197-76205). So the listener thread must **never** touch ZDOMan, ZNet, ZoneSystem or WorldGenerator. Instead: the census engine publishes `volatile Snapshot _latest` (fully immutable, pre-serialised to a `byte[]` on a thread-pool task) each tick; the listener thread only hands out `_latest`.

Routes: `GET /portals.json`, `GET /portals.csv`, `GET /health` (200 with `{ok:true}` or 503 with findings — directly usable as a container health probe), `GET /metrics` (Prometheus text: `tplite_portals_total`, `tplite_portals_unconnected`, `tplite_tag_groups`, `tplite_transits_total`, `tplite_repairs_total`, plus `valheim_zdos_total` from `ZDOMan.NrOfObjects()` :77658 sampled on the main thread).

Security: bind `127.0.0.1` by default and require an explicit `Bind` config change plus a bearer token to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Refuse to start without a token when bound non-loopback. No write routes at all in v1 — writes go through the file-queue or the admin console, both of which already have an authorization story.

Any text the listener thread wants in the server log must go through `Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog.Enqueue(...)` (`public static ConcurrentQueue<string>`, :43245), drained one line per frame by `Console.Update` into `AddString` → `ZLog.Log` (:42923-42925) — vanilla's own save thread reports errors exactly this way (:80675, :80710).

**Player experience.** Invisible in-game. An operator points Grafana at `http://server:9101/metrics` and gets a graph of portal count and transits per hour; their Docker healthcheck hits `/health` and restarts the container if the portal engine stops ticking.

**Failure modes.**
- Touching any Valheim singleton from the listener thread — ZDOMan, ZNetScene and ZDOExtraData are all unsynchronised static state; this will produce intermittent, unreproducible crashes.
- HttpListener requiring elevated privileges or an http.sys URL ACL on Windows hosts — Linux/Mono is fine, Windows dedicated servers may need `netsh http add urlacl`.
- Binding 0.0.0.0 with no token and exposing the full builder/PlatformUserID list to the internet.
- Not disposing the listener in `Shutdown()`/`OnDestroy` — the port stays bound across a BepInEx hot reload.
- Serialising on the listener thread from live objects instead of from the pre-built byte[].

**Prerequisites.** Output surface: atomic JSON/CSV file export

**Citations.** ZNet.SaveWorldThread (vanilla's only background thread) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:80583 · ZDOMan.PrepareSave main-thread clone — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76197-76205 · ZDOMan.NrOfObjects — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77658 · Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:43245; drained Console.Update :42923-42925; vanilla producer :80675 · System.Net.Http csproj reference precedent — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Wonderland.csproj:72

- Does BepInEx's Mono resolve `System.dll` for the plugin without an explicit reference? Confirm at build and at load.

## 77. Output surface: generated realm map (SVG first, PNG as a stretch)

`CAVEATS` · `ADMIN-ONLY` · effort: medium

A server-rendered top-down map of every portal, coloured by biome and linked by its connection, emitted as plain-text SVG — with a hand-rolled PNG encoder only if a raster is truly required.

**How it works.** **SVG (recommended, feasible today).** Pure string building, zero image libraries, zero graphics device. World XZ maps to SVG coordinates with `sx = (x + 10500) * scale`, `sy = (10500 - z) * scale` (world radius constants: `WorldGenerator.worldSize = 10000f`, `waterEdge = 10500f`, :151118-151122). Draw, in order: a background disc for the ocean; optional biome tinting by sampling `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome(x, z)` (:151725) on a coarse grid (a 256×256 sample grid = 65 536 closed-form noise evaluations — run it once at OnWorldReady on a time-sliced coroutine, never per export, and cache); a `<line>` per portal connection; a `<circle>` per portal coloured by network; a `<text>` label per tag. Output ~50–200 KB, opens in any browser, zooms losslessly, and is trivially diffable in git.

For an even cheaper variant, use `ZNet.World.m_biomeData` (`AltBiomeWorldData`, assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:92332) — a precomputed 2048×2048 grid at 12 m/cell with `PointBiomes[x,y]` and `PointHeights[x,y]`, populated by `ZNet.ServerLoadWorld` before any peer connects (:79273-79285), indexed via `AltBiomeWorldData.WorldSpaceToMapSpace(float)` (:92424). That is an O(1) lookup per cell with no noise evaluation at all.

**PNG (stretch, needs an in-game check).** `Texture2D` + `EncodeToPNG` requires the ImageConversion module and a graphics device; a dedicated server reports `SystemInfo.graphicsDeviceType == GraphicsDeviceType.Null` (vanilla itself branches on exactly that in `ZNet.UpdatePlayerList` :81245-81299). `System.Drawing` is unreliable under Mono without libgdiplus. The safe route is a ~120-line hand-rolled PNG writer (IHDR + zlib *stored* blocks + Adler-32 + CRC-32 + IEND) over a raw RGB byte buffer — no compression, larger files, but no dependency and no GPU.

Either renderer runs off the main thread from the census DTO, writing temp-then-replace.

**Player experience.** No in-game effect. The operator opens `portals.svg` in a browser and sees the whole realm: 214 dots on a biome-tinted disc, coloured lines showing every link, the `TRADE` ring drawn as a closed triangle, and three grey dots with no line at all — the stranded gates. They post it in Discord and players immediately understand the network layout without any client mod.

**Failure modes.**
- Calling `Texture2D`/`EncodeToPNG` headless and getting a null graphics device exception at runtime, or worse a silently black image.
- Sampling `WorldGenerator.GetBiome` per export instead of once — 65 536 noise evaluations on every 5-minute export is pure waste.
- Using any `ZoneSystem` raycast helper for terrain shading; they all return the no-hit fallback server-side (Game.FixedUpdate reference pin :100465).
- Labelling every portal at full zoom — 200 overlapping `<text>` nodes is unreadable; label per tag group, not per portal.
- Drawing interior portals (y > 3000, :4538) at their XZ position on top of the surface gate above them without a distinct marker.

**Prerequisites.** Full-realm portal enumeration report (the canonical data model)

## 78. Network state snapshot, rollback and migration

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Capture the live portal topology (positions, tags, links) to a versioned file that can be diffed, restored onto a running server, or replayed onto a different world.

**How it works.** A snapshot is the census DTO plus a schema version and a world fingerprint (`ZNet.instance.GetWorldName()` :80876, `GetWorldUID()` :80871, `ZNet.World.m_seedName` :112376). Written temp-then-replace to `<config>/snapshots/<name>.json`. Taken automatically before every `--apply` repair, on every network-file reload, and on `ZNet.WorldSaveStarted` (:78989/:80524) so the newest snapshot always matches the world file on disk.

**Restore** re-resolves every snapshot entry by rounded position (never ZDOID — `ZDO.Load` renumbers, :74552), then issues the reassert engine's write primitive for each tag and connection that differs. Portals present in the snapshot but absent from the world are reported, not recreated, unless `--recreate` is passed; recreation uses `ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, portalPrefabHash)` (:76674-76692) followed by the mandatory five lines `ZNetView.Awake` normally performs (:82613-82620): `Persistent = true; Type = ObjectType.Default; Distant = false; SetPrefab(hash); SetRotation(rot);` — `CreateNewZDO` sets none of them, and a prefab-less ZDO will not survive a save. Pass the real portal hash to `CreateNewZDO` so `AddIfPortal` (:77732-77752) files it in `m_portalObjects` and sets `DirtyPortalObjects`; setting the prefab afterwards on a hash-0 ZDO leaves it in the sector array, where `AddObjectsPerChunk` (:77572) then skips it as a portal and it is written to no chunk file at all.

**Migration to another world** rewrites the network file's `at` coordinates but cannot move the portals themselves — never call `zdo.SetPosition()` on a portal: `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752-73756) so the `m_portalObjects` key goes stale, clients in the new zone never receive it through sector sync, and `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76980-76986) later fails to remove it, leaking the entry permanently. Destroy and recreate instead: claim ownership (`DestroyZDO` is a silent no-op unless `IsOwner()`, :76929-76935) then `ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)`. Note the recreated portal must use a **fresh** ZDOID — `m_deadZDOs` (:76043) causes the server to immediately re-destroy any ZDO recreated under a previously-destroyed id (`RPC_ZDOData` :77133-77137).

Complement this with vanilla's own safety net: `ConsiderAutoBackup` runs inside `SaveWorldThread` (:80601-80604), so a bad mass repair is also recoverable from the world backup.

**Player experience.** No player-visible effect during a snapshot. During a restore, players near affected gates see hover text change and the connected-glow flicker once as links are rewritten. The operator types `tplite.restore pre-repair-2026-09-12T14:02Z` and gets `restored 4 portals, 0 missing, 0 recreated`.

**Failure modes.**
- Restoring a snapshot taken on a different world — the position keys resolve to unrelated portals. Refuse on a world-UID mismatch unless `--force`.
- Recreating a portal without the five ZNetView.Awake lines: the ZDO is non-persistent and prefab-less, vanishes at the next save, and clients log a CreateObject failure.
- Recreating under an old ZDOID: `m_deadZDOs` makes the server destroy it again immediately.
- Repositioning a portal instead of destroy-and-recreate: permanent `m_portalObjects` corruption.
- Snapshotting during a save: take it from `WorldSaveStarted` (before `PrepareSave`), never from `WorldSaveFinished`, which is reached through `PrintWorldSaveMessage` (:80566-80581) — a method that dereferences `MessageHud.instance` unguarded at :80574/:80578.

**Prerequisites.** Full-realm portal enumeration report (the canonical data model); NetworkReassertEngine — the only writer, and the race with vanilla's 5 s pass

## 79. World-save footprint of mod-created ZDOs, and how to clean them up

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Quantify exactly what the mod adds to the world file — one portal chunk rewrite plus per-portal key bytes — and ship an explicit garbage-collection command for mod-created anchors and keys.

**How it works.** **Where portals live on disk.** Every portal in the world is written to one dedicated chunk, `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal = new ChunkIndex(1, 0)` (:113180). `GetSaveClonePerChunk` clones *every* entry of `m_portalObjects` into it (:77621-77632, via `ZDO.Clone` :73552) — but only when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set (:77621). There is no `Persistent` filter on that path, unlike ordinary chunks (:77572). Consequences:
- Adding a mod key to every portal grows exactly one file. At ~16 bytes per int key, 500 portals × 3 keys ≈ 24 KB. Negligible.
- Any single portal change dirties the flag and rewrites the **whole** portal file at the next autosave (default `Game.m_saveInterval = 1800f`, :99914; overridable by `-savinterval`, :97477).
- Idempotent re-assertion costs nothing: `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` early-returns on an unchanged value (:74951-74961) and `BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false on equality (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345), so no DataRevision bump, no dirty flag, no rewrite.
- After a world load `LoadChunks` ends with `DirtyPortalObjects = false` (:76474-76531), so a freshly loaded world will not rewrite the portal file until something actually changes.

**Non-portal anchor ZDOs** (used for computed-coordinate destinations) go into ordinary chunks and are only written when `Persistent == true` (:77572). `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` does **not** set Persistent (:76674-76692).

**Cleanup.** Tag every mod-created ZDO with a mod-private int key (e.g. `"tplite_owned"` = a schema version). GC pass: enumerate `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Int, hash)` (:75390-75407 — Float/Long/Int/String only; an unindexed nested scan, so one-shot at boot, never per tick), and for each result not referenced by the current network model, claim ownership and `ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)` (:76929). For keys written onto *player-built* portals (which must survive), remove the key instead with the public statics `ZDOExtraData.RemoveInt/RemoveString/RemoveFloat` (:75122+) and then `SetDirtyPortals()`.

Expose the footprint in the report: mod-created portal count, mod-created anchor count, total mod keys, and the estimated added bytes.

**Player experience.** No player-visible effect. The operator runs `tplite.footprint` and sees `mod-created portals: 4 (hub anchors); mod-created anchors: 2; mod keys on 214 portals: 642; est. added save bytes: ~11 KB; portal chunk rewritten on 3 of the last 10 autosaves`. On uninstall they run `tplite.uninstall --clean-keys --destroy-anchors` and the footprint drops to zero.

**Failure modes.**
- Creating an anchor without `Persistent = true` — it vanishes on the next restart with no error and the portal it served becomes permanently dangling.
- Creating an anchor with a fabricated prefab hash: `FilterZDO` only drops prefabs in `s_brokenPrefabsToFilterOut` (two entries, :76109/:76350); an unknown hash merely logs a warning and the ZDO is **kept forever** (:76346-76361), so every boot prints 'ZDOs with prefabs not supported' and clients attempt to create an object for it. Always use a real, harmless prefab hash.
- Running `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` or `GetAllZDOsWithHash` on a tick — the former walks a 512×512 = 262 144-slot array ~400 non-empty sectors per call (:77442-77494), the latter is an unindexed nested walk over every ZDO's field dictionary (:75390-75407).
- Calling `DestroyZDO` without claiming ownership: it is a silent no-op (:76929-76935).
- Assuming a tag write persists without `SetDirtyPortals()`.

**Prerequisites.** PortalCensus — the single-source-of-truth index engine

**Citations.** ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113180 · ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk portal branch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77621-77636 · ZDO.Clone — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73552 · ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk persistence filter — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77572 · ZDOMan.LoadChunks clears DirtyPortalObjects — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76474-76531 · ZDOMan.DirtyPortalObjects — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76139-76149 · Game.m_saveInterval / -savinterval — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:99914, :97477 · ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76674-76692 · ZDOMan.FilterZDO / s_brokenPrefabsToFilterOut — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76346-76361, :76109 · ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75390-75407 · ZDOExtraData.RemoveInt/RemoveFloat — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75120-75130 · ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77442-77494 · ZDOMan.DestroyZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76929-76935 · BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue — assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345

## 80. What happens when the mod is removed (graceful-uninstall design)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small-medium

Nothing corrupts and no phantom portals appear — but managed topologies degrade to random same-tag pairs after one restart, so ship an explicit uninstall command that lands the world in a clean, vanilla-stable state.

**How it works.** Traced end to end through the decompile:

**Mod-created portal-prefab ZDOs survive and behave like normal portals.** They are written into the portal chunk unconditionally when dirty (:77621-77632) and `LoadChunks`'s portal branch loads them straight into `m_portalObjects` and `m_objectsByID` with **no** `FilterZDO` call at all (:76474-76482). Vanilla then pairs them by tag like any other gate. No phantoms, no orphan files.

**Mod keys on portal ZDOs become dead bytes.** Nothing reads them; they cost a few bytes each in the portal chunk forever. Harmless, but removable — hence `tplite.uninstall --clean-keys`.

**Non-portal anchor ZDOs** persist if `Persistent` was set and the prefab is real. With an unknown prefab hash they are *kept* and merely warned about (:76346-76361) — a permanent log-spam legacy. Destroy them on uninstall.

**Topologies unravel, in two stages.** At runtime, a ring A→B→C→A survives indefinitely because `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 never checks reciprocity (:100600-100604). At the **next world load**, it does not: the on-disk format gives each ZDO exactly one `ZDOConnectionHashData` slot (`RegenerateConnectionHashData` :75461-75478 writes the source slot then overwrites it with the Target slot), which can only express a pairwise perfect matching. So `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (:77850-77893) restores at most one pair per ring and vanilla randomly re-pairs the leftovers. One-way links come back **bidirectional** (ConnectPortals writes both sides, :77879-77885). Self-loops are erased entirely.

**Therefore the honest answer is: no corruption, but any non-pairwise topology is lost at the first restart after removal, silently and without warning.**

`tplite.uninstall` should: (1) snapshot; (2) collapse every managed network into plain vanilla pairs, or split tags so that each group has an even count (eliminating the permanent strand); (3) remove mod keys; (4) destroy mod anchors; (5) write a final report naming every gate whose tag was changed so the operator can tell players. Also expose `tplite.export --for-uninstall` producing a human-readable 'here is what your networks were' document.

**Player experience.** If the operator just deletes the DLL: for the rest of that session every gate keeps working exactly as it did. After the next server restart, players find the three-gate `TRADE` ring has become one working pair plus one gate that says `unconnected` forever, and nobody can tell them why. If the operator runs `tplite.uninstall` first, every network has already been split into clean pairs with distinct tags (`TRADE-1`, `TRADE-2`) and a Discord post lists the new tag for each gate, so nothing changes at the restart.

**Failure modes.**
- Removing the mod without running uninstall and only discovering the topology loss days later, after a restart.
- Leaving anchors with unknown prefab hashes behind — every boot logs 'ZDOs with prefabs not supported' and clients fail to create the object.
- Leaving an odd-sized managed tag group behind: vanilla permanently strands one member (Game.ConnectPortals phase 2, :100607-100622).
- Assuming `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (load-time, hash-based, :77850) is the same thing as `Game.ConnectPortals` (runtime, tag-based, :100589) — patching or reasoning about the wrong one gives the wrong uninstall model.

**Prerequisites.** Network state snapshot, rollback and migration

**Citations.** ZDOMan.LoadChunks portal branch (no FilterZDO) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76474-76482 · ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk portal branch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77621-77632 · ZDOMan.FilterZDO keeps unknown prefabs — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76346-76361 · ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75461-75478 · ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (load-time, hash-matched, writes both sides) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77850-77893 · Game.ConnectPortals (runtime, tag-based) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589-100627 · ZDO.Save connection as hash — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74315-74317

**Open questions.**

## 81. Version migration — mod schema, world version and Valheim build fingerprinting

`FEASIBLE` · `ADMIN-ONLY` · effort: small

Version every persisted artifact, fingerprint the game build at boot, and refuse to run destructive passes when the fingerprint is unrecognised.

**How it works.** Three independent versions, all recorded in every persisted file and in the boot log:

1. **Mod schema version** — an int in `networks.json`, every snapshot and the audit file. Migrations are forward-only, run on load, write the upgraded file back after taking a `.bak`, and log every field they changed. Refuse to load a schema newer than the running mod.
2. **Valheim build** — `Version.GetVersionString()` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:112112) plus the network version literal (40u as seen at :42875/:97033) logged at Awake. Keep a config'd allowlist of verified builds; outside it, run in read-only mode (census/health/export still work, reassert and repair refuse) until the operator sets `AcceptUnverifiedBuild=true`. Precedent: TortalPortal's MIGRATE-1.0.md re-verified the mod unmodified against 1.0.12 (build 25253764, network version 40) with 37 types / 55 method bodies changed and all 48 Harmony targets still resolving — so the 1.0.7 decompile is a valid authority through at least 1.0.12 for everything this mod touches.
3. **World version** — `ZNet.World.m_worldVersion`/the `Version.World` enum used by `ZDOMan.LoadChunks(…, Version.World version)` (:76486). Record it so a snapshot taken on an older save format is flagged on restore.

Structural self-checks at Awake, all cheap and all failing *soft*: confirm `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` is non-empty (:100021); confirm `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` returns without throwing; confirm the Harmony targets resolve via `AccessTools.Method` before patching and wrap each patch set in `SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch` (SubsystemRegistry.cs:99), which degrades a signature change to a logged warning rather than killing Awake.

Honour the Mono JIT rule GameShape.cs encodes: a compile-time binding to a member the loaded assembly lacks throws at JIT of the *calling* method, so an internal try/catch does not save it. Any version-sensitive call must live in its own method reached only after a reflection-based probe confirms the shape (GameShape.Detect, Core/Compat/GameShape.cs:72). Never use the single-result `Type.GetMethod` overload — a compatibility patcher can inject a same-name/same-parameter overload and make it throw `AmbiguousMatchException` (GameShape.cs:155 comment, learned live).

**Player experience.** Nothing player-facing. On a game update the operator sees `[tplite] Valheim 1.0.14 is not in the verified list (last verified 1.0.12). Running READ-ONLY: census/health/export active, reassert and repair disabled. Set AcceptUnverifiedBuild=true to override.` Their gates keep working exactly as vanilla does; the mod simply stops writing until a human says it is safe.

**Failure modes.**
- Silently continuing to write ZDOs after a game update that changed a signature — the worst possible failure for a mod that rewrites persistent world data.
- Binding at compile time to a member that may not exist and taking down the whole Awake at JIT time.
- Migrating a file in place without a `.bak` — a bad migration is unrecoverable.
- Using the game version string as a Harmony-target guarantee; verify the targets directly with AccessTools.

**Citations.** Version.GetVersionString — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:112112 · network version literal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:42875, :97033 · ZDOMan.LoadChunks(Version.World) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76486 · Game.PortalPrefabHash — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100021 · SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/SubsystemRegistry.cs:99 · GameShape.Detect (Mono JIT rule, AmbiguousMatchException) — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Compat/GameShape.cs:72, :155 · TortalPortal 1.0.12 re-verification — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/MIGRATE-1.0.md:1-60

## 82. Compatibility with other server mods that touch ZDOs

`FEASIBLE` · `ADMIN-ONLY` · effort: small-medium

Enumerate the exact shared mutable surfaces — m_onZDODestroyed, ZDO.SetOwner prefixes, Game.ConnectPortals patches, Terminal.commands, ZRoutedRpc.Register — and adopt a defensive convention for each.

**How it works.** Each contention point, with the safe convention:

1. **`ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed`** (:76033) is a single public `Action<ZDO>` field, and `ZNetScene.Awake` already attaches its own handler (:81953). Always `Delegate.Combine`; never assign. An assignment silently disables ZNetScene's destruction handling for the entire server.
2. **`ZDO.SetOwner` prefixes.** Wonderland's `WaterBuoyancyEngine.ZdoSetOwnerPatch` (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313) already prefixes this global hot path (`ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` calls it for every peer every 2 s, :76901-76927). Two mods both vetoing is a real hazard. Convention: only add the guard if measured contention demands it; fail fast on `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(prefab)` as the very first test; never block `uid == 0` or `uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()`; log once per minute when a veto fires so contention is visible.
3. **`Game.ConnectPortals` patches.** A prefix returning false disables *all* vanilla pairing, including for portals we do not manage. Do not do it. If our cooperative model is being defeated because another mod prefixed it, detect that (managed links stop being torn down when we deliberately mistag a probe portal) and log a compatibility warning rather than fighting.
4. **`Terminal.commands`.** The ConsoleCommand ctor does `commands[command.ToLower()] = this` (:43096/:43114) — an indexer assignment, so a duplicate name silently clobbers with no exception and no log. Namespace every command `tplite.` and, at registration, check whether the key already exists and log if so.
5. **`ZRoutedRpc.Register`.** Per the digest it uses `Dictionary.Add`, so re-registering an existing name throws `ArgumentException`. Never register a vanilla name (`ChatMessage`, `ShowMessage`, `RPC_SetConnection`); for a mod-private RPC use a GUID-prefixed name and probe the private `m_functions` dictionary via `AccessTools` before registering.
6. **Sender identity.** `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653-100662) is registered on every peer with **no** sender check and will rewire any ZDO's Portal connection to any target. Any mod (or malicious client) can undo our topology instantly. Our reassert loop restores it within 2 s; do not claim 'unbypassable'. The same applies to `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey`/`RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` (:116022-116037), which also have no sender validation.
7. **Other mods writing `s_tag`.** Detect: if the census sees a managed portal's tag change to a value we did not write, and no `RPC_SetTag` crossed the wire, log a 'foreign writer' warning naming the portal rather than silently fighting forever.

Ship a `tplite.compat` command that lists every Harmony patch currently applied to the methods we care about, via `Harmony.GetPatchInfo(MethodBase)` — this turns a support ticket into one line of output.

**Player experience.** No player-visible effect. The operator running two ZDO-touching mods sees `[tplite] compat: ZDO.SetOwner has 2 prefixes (wubarrk.wonderland, wubarrk.tortalportal-lite) — ownership guards may interact; Game.ConnectPortals has 1 prefix (other.mod) — cooperative pairing may be disabled` instead of a mysterious, intermittent 'my portals keep unpairing'.

**Failure modes.**
- Assigning to `m_onZDODestroyed` and breaking ZNetScene's own destruction path server-wide.
- Two SetOwner prefixes each vetoing the other's claims, producing a portal nobody can own and writes that never propagate.
- Registering a routed RPC name another mod took and throwing at Awake, taking the whole plugin down.
- Claiming a lockdown is unbypassable when `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653) is an unauthenticated global routed RPC any client can invoke.

**Prerequisites.** NetworkReassertEngine — the only writer, and the race with vanilla's 5 s pass

## 83. Performance budget and cache-invalidation policy

`FEASIBLE` · `ADMIN-ONLY` · effort: small

Portal ops cost is independent of world ZDO count because portals live in their own always-resident dictionary — everything expensive is a non-portal query, and this option defines the budgets for each.

**How it works.** **The headline fact:** portals are not in `m_objectsBySector` at all. `AddIfPortal` files them in `m_portalObjects` and explicitly calls `RemoveFromSector` (:77732-77752); they are loaded wholesale from the dedicated portal chunk at world load (:76474-76482) and never released (`ReleaseZDOS` only reassigns ownership :76872-76885; `FlushClientObjects` is client-only :76180-76183). So `GetPortalList()`/`GetPortals()` is O(P) in portal count and completely independent of whether the world holds 10 000 or 300 000 ZDOs.

**Budgets:**
- `GetPortalList()` — one `List<ZDO>` alloc of P refs (:77648-77656). At P = 500 and 1 Hz that is ~4 KB/s of gen-0 garbage. Acceptable. `GetPortals()` (:77643) is zero-alloc for read-only walks; `PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit` already uses it.
- Census tick 1.0 s; health 30 s; reassert 2.0 s; metrics sample 3.0 s; metrics aggregate 60 s; export 300 s; file-queue poll 1.0 s; config poll 5.0 s; heartbeat 15 min.
- **Non-portal queries are the expensive ones.** `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` (:77442-77494) walks a 512×512 = 262 144-slot array (`new ZDOMan(512)` :79163, `ResetSectorArray` :76163) at ~400 *non-empty* sectors per call, re-hashing the prefab name each call — one full pass is ⌈nonEmpty/400⌉+1 calls. `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash` (:75390-75407) is an unindexed nested walk over every ZDO's field dictionary. Both are one-shot/boot-only. Use Wonderland's `PrefabSetSweeper` with an explicit `sectorBudget` (ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:135, :153) when several prefab families are needed in one walk; its header records the name-based scanner taking *hours* for ~800 prefabs.
- Spatial 'nearest altar/bed/ship' lookups use `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear` (ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25) over `ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects` (:77142) — note that method reuses a shared `m_visitedSectorIndices` HashSet and is **not reentrant**.
- Broadcast budget: cap `ForceSendZDO` at 256 per sweep (StructureUpkeep.cs:29-40 precedent); `ZDOMan.SendZDOs` re-serialises the entire ZDO with no delta encoding (:77053-77062) and a 10 240-byte per-peer send-queue cap (:77010-77016).

**Cache policy:** cache the biome grid (immutable for the life of the world), the prefab-hash→name map (immutable after OnWorldReady), and the `s_creator`→name map (append-only). Invalidate the census every tick — there is no dirty flag to key off, and `GetPortalList` has no cache of its own. Never cache ZDO object references across ticks (ZDOPool recycling, :73536-73545). Cache ZDOIDs and re-resolve.

**Player experience.** No player-visible effect, which is the point: the operator's `ServerLog` line (vanilla's own 10-minute `InvokeRepeating("ServerLog", 600f, 600f)`, :100048/:100089-100096) showing `Connections N ZDOS:M sent:X recv:Y` should be indistinguishable with and without the mod. `tplite.perf` prints each engine's last and 95th-percentile tick cost in microseconds so a regression is visible immediately.

**Failure modes.**
- Running any prefab-iterative or hash scan on a tick instead of at boot.
- Calling `FindSectorObjects` from inside a loop already iterating its results — the shared visited-set makes it non-reentrant.
- Mass `ForceSendZDO` in one frame on first boot after enabling networks.
- Assuming `GetPortalList()` is cached and calling it several times per tick from different engines instead of once into a shared snapshot.
- Scaling worry to world ZDO count — the relevant number is portal count, and it is the one to alarm on.

**Prerequisites.** PortalCensus — the single-source-of-truth index engine

## 84. Subsystem architecture — registry, engines, tick rates, data ownership, config surface

`FEASIBLE` · `ADMIN-ONLY` · effort: medium

One BepInEx plugin, one ops subsystem, nine engines with disjoint write ownership and a fixed intra-tick ordering, mirroring Wonderland's registry/heartbeat shape so the two mods are maintainable side by side.

**How it works.** **Plugin shell** (copy `WonderlandPlugin`, Plugin.cs:35-143 and `SubsystemRegistry`, SubsystemRegistry.cs, renamed). `Awake()`: init logger → `GameShape.Detect()` (only if `FindNear` is used) → build `ConfigSync` → `TpLiteConfig.Bind` → `RegisterSubsystems()` → `Subsystems.InitializeAll(Config, ConfigSync, harmony)` → `SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch(harmony, typeof(WorldReadyHook))`. `WorldReadyHook` is a postfix on `ZNetScene.Awake` — the first point prefab lists are populated. `Update()`: `PollConfigFile()` (5 s) → `PollNetworkFile()` (5 s) → `PollCommandFile()` (1 s) → `Heartbeat.OnUpdate(dt)` → `Subsystems.OnUpdate()`. `OnDestroy()`: `Subsystems.ShutdownAll()` → `_harmony.UnpatchSelf()` → `DiscordWebhook.SendBlocking("portal engine offline")`.

**One subsystem, `PortalOpsSubsystem`**, owning nine engines. Fixed intra-tick order, because ordering is semantics not taste:

1. `PortalCensus` — 1.0 s. **Owns** the snapshot + the change stream. Writes nothing.
2. `NetworkModel` — event-driven on file change. **Owns** the parsed networks and their position→ZDOID resolution.
3. `AuditEngine` — consumes the change stream *before* any write this tick, subtracting the reassert engine's declared 'expected changes' set. **Owns** the ring buffer and `portal-audit.log`.
4. `NetworkReassertEngine` — 2.0 s. **The only writer of `s_tag` and `ConnectionType.Portal`.** Declares its intended writes to the audit engine before issuing them.
5. `HealthScanEngine` — 30 s. **Owns** findings. Pure read.
6. `RepairEngine` — on demand / slow timer, opt-in, dry-run by default. Writes only through the reassert engine's primitive; never writes directly.
7. `MetricsEngine` — 3 s sample, 60 s aggregate. **Owns** counters + route table.
8. `ExportEngine` — 300 s + on-change + on `ZNet.WorldSaveStarted`. Pure read; serialises off-thread from the DTO. **Owns** `portals.json`, `portals.csv`, `portals.svg`.
9. `CommandEngine` — registers ConsoleCommands from a `Terminal.InitTerminal` postfix; drives the file queue; dispatches to the others. **Owns** nothing.

Plus a mod-wide `Heartbeat` ticked directly from `Update()` (not through the registry), exactly as Wonderland does (Heartbeat.cs:21) — it is a mod-wide concern, not any one engine's.

**Ownership rule, enforced by convention and by code review:** exactly one engine may write any given ZDO field, and the census may never write at all. Everything else reads the census snapshot, never live ZDOs.

**Config surface** (BepInEx `.cfg`, scalars only; topology lives in `networks.json`): `[General]` Enabled, VerboseLogging, AcceptUnverifiedBuild. `[Census]` IntervalSeconds. `[Networks]` File, ReassertSeconds, AllowTagRewrite, MaxWritesPerTick. `[Health]` IntervalSeconds, ReportUnmanagedOddGroups, ReportInteriorPortals. `[Repair]` AutoRepair (default false), DryRunDefault (true), MaxActionsPerRun. `[Audit]` Enabled, LogFile, RingSize, ToastOnBlockedRetag. `[Metrics]` TransitDetection, SampleSeconds, StraddleRadius. `[Export]` Json, Csv, Svg, IntervalSeconds, Directory. `[Discord]` WebhookUrl, Health, Audit, Destructions, Heartbeat. `[Http]` Enabled, Bind, Port, Token. `[Commands]` FileQueueEnabled, ConsolePrefix.

Every scalar is bound through the `BindSynced*` helpers (WonderlandConfig.cs:406-442) and registered with `ConfigSync` — pointless for a zero-client mod but free, and it gains the locking/version behaviour if a companion client ever appears.

**Player experience.** Ordinary players experience the mod only as: gates that stay correctly connected, occasionally a tag that snaps back to the network's tag with a toast (`This gate belongs to the TRADE network.`), and nothing else. The operator experiences it as one `.cfg` of scalars, one `networks.json` of topology, a set of `tplite.*` console commands, a JSON/CSV/SVG export directory, a Discord channel and a heartbeat line every 15 minutes.

**Failure modes.**
- Two engines writing the same ZDO field — the classic way a self-healing mod oscillates forever.
- Running the audit after the reassert without an 'expected changes' set, so the mod attributes its own writes to players.
- Putting topology in the BepInEx `.cfg` — flat key=value cannot express nested lists, and the resulting stringly-typed format is unvalidatable.
- Doing ObjectDB/ZNetScene prefab reads in `Initialize()` instead of `OnWorldReady()`; worse, assuming `ObjectDB.instance` is non-null even at `OnWorldReady` — it frequently is not (BuffRosterEngine.cs:83-96 retries once per tick until it resolves).
- Letting an engine throw and take down the whole plugin — every call must go through the registry's try/catch (SubsystemRegistry.cs:29-79) and every patch through `SafePatch` (:99).

**Citations.** WonderlandPlugin.Awake / Update / OnDestroy — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Plugin.cs:35, :71, :78 · WorldReadyHook on ZNetScene.Awake — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Plugin.cs:151-159 · SubsystemRegistry.InitializeAll / OnUpdate / SafePatch — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/SubsystemRegistry.cs:24, :63, :99 · IWonderlandSubsystem contract — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/IWonderlandSubsystem.cs:7 · Heartbeat ticked from Update — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Heartbeat.cs:21 · WonderlandConfig Bind helpers — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/WonderlandConfig.cs:150, :406-442 · BuffRosterEngine ObjectDB retry — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/StatusEffects/BuffRosterEngine.cs:83-96 · ZNet.WorldSaveStarted — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78989, invoked :80524 · Wonderland.csproj (net472, server assemblies, publicizer) — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Wonderland.csproj:1-31, :19-27
