## 100. Server Treasury, Tax Skim and Collective Unlocks

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Route a slice of every toll into a real chest somewhere in the world, and let the server spend it on world-scale effects that nobody could buy individually.

**How it works.** **The treasury.** Fabricate a server-owned Container ZDO at an admin-chosen position: `var z = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, chestPrefabHash); z.Persistent = true; z.SetPrefab(chestPrefabHash); z.SetRotation(rot);` (mirroring `ZNetView.Awake` :82613 — `CreateNewZDO` :76674 sets neither prefab nor persistence). Write into it with `ZdoInventoryIO.Save` (Wonderland `Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs:52`), which does `zdo.SetOwner(ZNet.GetUID()); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_items, pkg.GetArray())`. A vanilla client standing near it sees a perfectly ordinary chest whose contents change; `Container.CheckForChanges` (`InvokeRepeating` 1f, :121920) reloads it within a second.

**The skim.** Every debit in Prepaid Toll Escrow or Charge Cells names a beneficiary. Split it: `ownerShare` back to the gate owner's payout chest, `treasuryShare` moved into the treasury. Use `ZdoInventoryIO.MoveMatchingItem` (`Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs:68`) which commits the destination add before the source removal, so a crash lands on "nothing moved" rather than "vanished".

**What the treasury buys — the interesting part.** The server-side spend targets are world-scale global keys, which is exactly the class of thing no individual can purchase:
- `GlobalKeys.TeleportAll` (ordinal 35, :101307) — an ORE HOLIDAY. Set it and every portal on the server carries metal for the duration; `Inventory.IsTeleportable` honours it (:68869). Price it at a level the whole server has to co-fund, run it for one in-game week, then `RemoveGlobalKey`. Caveat: items with `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` are rejected before the key is even consulted (:68862).
- `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` (:101304) inverted — a paid "portal amnesty" that lifts an admin-imposed blackout early.
- `GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild` (:101306) — buy the right to build inside crypts server-wide.
- Custom `mod_route_*` keys — collectively fund a new trunk route into existence (see Progression-Gated Route Tiers).
- The 17 numeric world-rate keys consumed by `Game.UpdateWorldRates` (:101128-101198) — a funded `ResourceRate` or `CarryWeightRate` week, written exactly as Wonderland's `WorldRatesEngine` does (`Subsystems/WorldGovernor/WorldRatesEngine.cs:33`: `GlobalKeyAdd("key value", true)` then `SendGlobalKeys(0L)`).

The world-modifier keys are client-HONOURED, not server-enforced (they are read by client code at the point of use), but they are honoured exactly the way vanilla honours its own modifiers, and the PURCHASE is fully server-enforced because the balance check is a server-side read.

Critically: use the publicized `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` + `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` for a temporary purchase, or the key is mirrored into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113511) and baked into the .fwl permanently.

**Player experience.** There is a stone vault at the hub with a chest in it that nobody can open — it is just visibly full, and a sign beside it reads what it is for. Every toll anyone pays anywhere on the map puts a tenth of it in there. A Discord bot posts the balance each day. At 20,000 coins the server buys an Ore Holiday: a broadcast toast goes out (`The Vaults open: metal flows through every gate for seven days`), and for a week every portal on the map carries iron. Everyone stops what they are doing and moves their stockpiles. Then it ends, the vault is empty, and the grind to the next holiday begins. It is the only economic sink in the game that the whole server plays toward together, and no single rich player can buy it alone.

**Failure modes.**
- A treasury chest players can reach is a treasury chest players will empty. Put it inside a ward AND at a position no gate routes to, or accept it as a heist target (which is arguably better content).
- `GlobalKeyAdd` mirrors keys with ordinal < `NonServerOption` (41) into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113511), which is written to the .fwl on the next autosave — so a naive `SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.TeleportAll)` permanently bakes the holiday into the world and it survives even uninstalling the mod. Use `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` + `SendGlobalKeys(0L)`.
- `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.X)` stringifies PascalCase (:115938) while the store holds lowercase, so `RPC_SetGlobalKey`'s dedupe guard (`!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)`, :116024) never trips and every call re-broadcasts the entire key list to every peer. In a polling loop that is a broadcast storm. Pass the lowercase literal and pre-check with `GetGlobalKey`.
- `ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys` (:115904) wipes ordinals 0..40 on every world load — a holiday in progress evaporates across a restart unless you re-apply it in a POSTFIX on that method.
- Any client can set or clear these keys itself (`RPC_SetGlobalKey` has no sender check, :116022), so an unhardened server lets one player grant themselves the Ore Holiday for free.
- The Steam browser "modifiers" badge is snapshotted in `ZNet.OpenServer` (:79454) and refreshed only on the registration-retry path, so a live holiday leaves the public listing stale and confuses operators comparing it to `listkeys`.

**Prerequisites.** Prepaid Toll Escrow; Progression-Gated Route Tiers (for the custom-key spends)

## 101. One-Way Trade Routes

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

A→B with no return leg — runtime-stable in vanilla because the pairing reconciler never checks reciprocity, but silently repaired into a two-way link by every world save, so it must be re-asserted at load.

**How it works.** A ZDO holds exactly one connection — `ZDOExtraData.s_connections` is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` with a single readonly target (:74794, :75524) — and `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` writes only that ZDO's own entry (:74951). So writing A→B without writing B→A is genuinely representable.

The reason it survives is a quirk of vanilla's own reconciler. `Game.ConnectPortals` pass 1 clears A's link only when the partner ZDO is missing, the partner's `s_tag` differs, or the partner's own connection is `ZDOID.None` (:100600-100604). It never checks that B points back at A. So A→B while B→C is stable indefinitely, as are rings and self-loops, provided every participant shares one byte-identical tag string and no participant's connection is None.

That gives you three shipping topologies with no Harmony at all:
- **One-way spoke:** A→B, B→C, C→A (a ring that reads as one-way from any node).
- **Funnel:** A→H, B→H, C→H with H→A. Everyone can reach the hub; only one route leaves it.
- **Dead-drop:** A→Sink where Sink is a Customs House anchor carrying the same tag and a self-loop back.

The part that breaks is persistence, and it is unambiguous. `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461-75478) collapses `s_connections` into `s_connectionsHashData`, giving the SOURCE `{type, h}` and the TARGET `{type|Target, h}` for a fresh hash. Each ZDO has exactly one hash slot. Then `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (:77850, called at load from `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` :76515 and `ZDOMan.Load` :76653) matches hash pairs and writes BOTH directions: `zDO.SetConnection(Portal, item2); zDO2.SetConnection(Portal, item);` (:77882-77883). So a one-way link comes back bidirectional, a 3-ring loses a link, and a self-loop is erased outright.

The fix is a load-time re-assert: in `OnWorldReady`, before or immediately after the first `Game.ConnectPortals()` call, walk your persisted topology table (position-keyed, since `ZDO.Load` renumbers every ZDOID at :74552) and force every edge with `SetOwner` + `SetConnection` + `ForceSendZDO`. That window is the cheapest possible time to do it: `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` has just set the server as owner of both ends of every pair (:77880-77881), and `m_peers` is empty so every write takes the immediate local path.

Economically this is what makes trade real. A one-way route means goods move but people do not commute; a funnel means the frontier feeds the capital and the return trip is a boat.

**Player experience.** The mining outpost has a gate tagged `"→ CAPITAL"`. You step through with a full pack and arrive in the market square. You turn around and the gate you just came out of is tagged `"→ NORTHWATCH"` and does not go back to the mine — it goes somewhere else entirely. To get back to the mine you take the road, or the boat, or the long southern chain. Suddenly there are caravans, there are wagons, there is a reason for the coastal route to exist, and the gate network stops being a teleport grid and starts being a one-way freight system. New players work this out the first time they try to nip home for a forgotten pickaxe.

**Failure modes.**
- THE failure mode: a one-way link is silently converted to two-way by the next world save/reload (`ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` :77879-77885). Without the load-time re-assert, your whole trade economy quietly becomes a normal portal network overnight and nobody notices the mod stopped working.
- Rings >2 lose a link across a save because each ZDO has one hash slot (`RegenerateConnectionHashData` :75471-75475 overwrites the source entry with a Target entry). The re-assert must rebuild the whole ring, not patch one edge.
- The topology only survives at runtime while every member shares one literal tag string. The moment a player renames one gate, pass 1 tears its links down (tag mismatch, :100601) — which means one-way routes REQUIRE the Routing Kernel to own tags, or a single rename collapses the network.
- `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653) lets any client rewire any portal with no sender check, so an unhardened server lets one player reverse your trade route. Harden at `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632).
- A player who arrives via a one-way route and immediately logs out reappears there; there is no server-side way to send them back except a forced teleport (`RPC_TeleportPlayer` :41962), which bypasses every rule you built and should be admin-only.

**Prerequisites.** The Routing Kernel; Park and Release

## 102. Distance and Biome Pricing

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small-medium

Charge by how far the route reaches and what it reaches into — computed entirely from procedural world data the server already has, with no colliders and no players nearby.

**How it works.** Both endpoints of every managed route are ZDOs whose `GetPosition()` (:73822) the server holds permanently — portals are never unloaded, because `ZDOMan.AddIfPortal` files them in `m_portalObjects` and `RemoveFromSector`s them (:77732-77752), and nothing ever releases them (`ReleaseNearbyZDOS` only reassigns ownership, :76901). So `Vector3.Distance(a.GetPosition(), b.GetPosition())` is always available for every portal on the map, for free, with zero bookkeeping and no player online.

Biome is equally free and equally collider-independent. `WorldGenerator.GetBiome(float wx, float wy)` (:151725) is closed-form; `WorldGenerator.GetHeight` (:151944) gives terrain height with sea level 30 (`ZoneSystem.m_waterLevel` :113218). For an O(1) cached alternative, `ZNet.World.m_biomeData` is an `AltBiomeWorldData` holding `PointBiomes[x,y]` and `PointHeights[x,y]` on a 2048×2048 grid at 12m per cell, indexed by `AltBiomeWorldData.WorldSpaceToMapSpace(x)` (:92424) — populated by `ZNet.ServerLoadWorld` → `VerifyBiomeData` before any peer connects (:79283).

Price function, all server-side:
```
price = base
      + distanceRate * Vector3.Distance(a,b)
      + biomeSurcharge[GetBiome(b.x,b.z)]
      + crossBiomePenalty(GetBiome(a), GetBiome(b))
      - tierDiscount(tierOf(a), tierOf(b))
```

The enforcement is the same park/release primitive: a route whose escrow or fuel does not cover its computed price is simply not in the topology this tick.

**Range caps are the stronger form.** Rather than pricing a long hop, forbid it: a tier-1 gate may pair only within 400m, tier-2 within 2000m, tier-3 unlimited. This is pure topology — the Routing Kernel just never emits the edge — so it needs no economy at all and is completely unexploitable. It also produces the single most interesting map-level consequence available here: a network of short hops means relay stations, which means a *physical* infrastructure map that people build along, rather than a fully-connected teleport mesh.

**Ashlands / Deep North surcharges** come out of the same data: `WorldGenerator.ashlandsMinDistance = 12000f` (:151114), `IsDeepnorth` (:151719), `worldSize = 10000f` / `waterEdge = 10500f` (:151118-151122). And `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap(pos)` (:115637) is the one lava test that works on a dedicated server — it is static and uses only `WorldGenerator`, unlike `ZoneSystem.instance.IsLava` (:115647) which raycasts and is therefore always-false server-side.

**Player experience.** You build a portal pair 6km apart and tag them, and instead of connecting they both read `"MINE — out of range (tier 1: 400m)"`. So you build a relay: a hut at the 400m mark with two gates in it, then another, then another, and after an afternoon you have a chain of eight stations marching north across the Black Forest, each one a real little structure with a fire and a bed. Your gate hops cost 3 coins each in the Meadows and 11 each crossing the Plains, and the tag on every station tells you the fare before you step in. The map you end up with looks like a railway, because it is one — and when a troll wrecks station four the whole line goes dark until somebody rebuilds it.

**Failure modes.**
- Every `ZoneSystem` collider helper — `GetGroundHeight`, `GetSolidHeight`, `IsBlocked`, `FindFloor`, `GetGroundData`, `IsLava(Vector3)` — COMPILES and RUNS on a dedicated server and always returns the no-hit fallback, because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) (:100465) so no terrain collider exists near real coordinates. They do not throw and do not log. Use `WorldGenerator` only.
- `WorldGenerator` is blind to player terraforming and to a location's own flattening, so a computed height can be metres off. Only matters if you price on terrain rather than distance.
- `BiomeSector.Center` is the centroid of the region's PERIMETER cells (`AltBiomeWorldData.GenerateSectors` :92531-92535), not its area centroid, so for a crescent-shaped region it can land in a different biome. Always re-check `WorldGenerator.GetBiome` at the chosen point. `BiomeSector.MinZone`/`MaxZone` are outright broken (both computed from `sector.Min` with z=0, :92577-92578) — never use them.
- A range cap that changes when a player's tier changes will silently break existing routes. Grandfather, or warn in the tag for an in-game day before enforcing.
- Distance-priced routes create an arbitrage: a chain of cheap short hops undercuts one expensive long hop. That is usually the desired behaviour (it drives infrastructure), but if you want long hops to be genuinely premium you must price per-transit, not per-metre, and then a relay chain costs more.

**Prerequisites.** The Routing Kernel; Prepaid Toll Escrow or Charge Cells (if pricing rather than capping)

## 103. Leases, Rent, Repossession and Caps

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium-large

Portals as rented infrastructure with an expiry timestamp the server owns — plus a hard build cap enforced at the only moment a server can actually see a new portal appear.

**How it works.** **The lease clock.** Store `tpl_leaseUntil` as a long of `ZNet.instance.GetTime().Ticks` (:81535) on the portal ZDO; `ZNet.GetTimeSeconds()` (:81546) is the monotonic world clock persisted in the save (:80624/:80763). Each tick: `open = now < leaseUntil`. Expiry parks the route; paying from the bound escrow chest extends it. Call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702) after writing the field, because a non-connection write does not set `DirtyPortalObjects` and the lease would otherwise vanish at the next world save.

Grace period, then repossession: after `leaseUntil + graceTicks`, `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo);` — note `DestroyZDO` (:76929) is a silent no-op unless you own the ZDO first, and it works by queueing into `m_destroySendList` which `SendDestroyed` (:76937) broadcasts as the `DestroyZDO` routed RPC.

**The build cap — the one place a server-only mod is STRONGER than a client mod.** A dedicated server cannot hook `Player.PlacePiece` (no `Player` instance exists) or `ZNetScene.Instantiate` (the client instantiates; only the ZDO arrives over the wire) — the PAUSED PortalLock project shipped exactly those hooks behind an `IsServer()` guard and could never fire once. The working hook is the pair Wonderland's `SpawnGovernor` uses (`Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43`, :58):
1. Postfix `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int)` (:76684) — `prefabHash == 0` identifies the network-receive path; record the ZDOID only. A postfix here always sees `GetPrefab() == 0`; the prefab is not known yet.
2. Postfix `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` (:74225) — first moment the prefab hash exists. If it is in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:100021), read `ZDOVars.s_creator`, count that player's existing portals from `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (:77648), and if over cap: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo);` plus a `PlayerNotify.Toast` explaining why.

This is genuine server-side enforcement of a per-player rule — and it works because the rule is evaluated at CREATION, not at USE. The moment of creation is server-visible; the moment of transit is not. That asymmetry is the whole shape of this domain.

Cap and lease compose: a player's first N gates are free and permanent, gates N+1..M are leased, and beyond M the ZDO is destroyed on arrival.

**Player experience.** **Lease:** the market district has six numbered portal bays for rent. Yours reads `"BAY 3 — 4d left"` and the number ticks down as the days pass. Two days out it starts reading in orange and you get a login toast. At zero the gate goes dark and the tag reads `"BAY 3 — LAPSED"`; a week later, if nobody pays, the whole arch is simply gone one morning and the bay is free for someone else. The district turns over. Prime bays near the trader get bid up.

**Cap:** you have five portals and you try to place a sixth. It places normally on your screen — the build cost is deducted, the arch appears — and then about a second later it pops out of existence and a toast reads `Portal limit reached (5/5). Dismantle one first.` Slightly jarring the first time, permanently clear thereafter, and no amount of client modding gets you a sixth.

**Failure modes.**
- The cap's destroy-on-arrival is visible to the placing client as an object that appeared and then vanished, and the build materials are consumed client-side before the server ever sees the ZDO. There is no refund mechanism — the server cannot touch a player's inventory. Either accept the loss, or drop a compensating `ItemDrop` at their feet (`ItemDrop.DropItem` :70674, the pattern in Wonderland `Subsystems/WorldGovernor/FirstSpawnGrant.cs:218`), which requires knowing the build cost.
- A postfix on `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` ALONE always sees `GetPrefab() == 0` on the network-receive path and can never act — this is documented as a shipped bug in SpawnGovernor's own first version (`SpawnGovernor.cs:16-24`).
- `s_creator` is 0 for world-generated and pre-field structures (`Piece.SetCreator` only writes when it is 0 and the client owns the ZDO, :136417). A cap that counts creator-0 portals against somebody destroys admin infrastructure.
- A repossessed portal cannot be undone. `ZDOMan.m_deadZDOs` (:76043) additionally makes the server destroy any ZDO re-created under the same ZDOID (`RPC_ZDOData` :77133), so there is no restore-from-backup at the ZDO level.
- Lease expiry that lands while the owner is mid-transit strands them. Park at the far end with a grace window rather than instantly.
- A mass expiry sweep that parks or destroys hundreds of gates in one frame spikes every peer — Wonderland's `StructureUpkeep` caps routed broadcasts at 256 per sweep for exactly this reason (`Subsystems/WorldGovernor/StructureUpkeep.cs:29`). Budget your sweep.

**Prerequisites.** Park and Release; Prepaid Toll Escrow; Debtor's Lien and Personal Gates

## 104. Naming Rights and Prestige

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small-medium

Sell the one piece of text a server can put in front of a vanilla player's eyes in the world — the portal tag — plus a saved map pin to go with it.

**How it works.** Once the Routing Kernel owns pairing, `ZDOVars.s_tag` (:78617) is decoupled from routing and becomes a pure display string the server fully controls. Three facts make it a sellable asset:

1. **No length cap on the write side.** The 10-character limit lives only in the client's text widget (`TeleportWorld.Interact` → `TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` :143482, applied at `TextInput.Show` :61519). `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` (:143587) performs no length check at all, and a direct server ZDO write performs none either. A server can write a 60-character name and every vanilla client displays it in the hover panel.
2. **No profanity filter on a Steam backend.** `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is literally `return text;` in the dedicated-server assembly (:94588), and `TeleportWorld.GetTagInfo` only surfaces the censored warning when `ZNet.m_onlineBackend == OnlineBackendType.PlayFab` (:143462). So a server that wants filtering must do it itself — `CensorShittyWords.Filter(input, out output)` (:94295) IS fully implemented server-side and returns a masked string.
3. **Rich text is stripped.** `GetHoverText` applies `RemoveRichTextTags()` (:143459, `Regex.Replace(text, "<[\\/a-zA-Z0-9= \"''#;:()$_-]*?>", "")` in assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700). No colour, no size. Unicode glyphs (★ ▮ ⚑ ✦) pass through untouched and are the only decoration available.

Product design:
- **Reserved names.** The server maintains a namespace; `"THE BIFRÖST"` is sold once and thereafter refused to everyone else. Enforcement is trivial because the server rewrites the tag on the next tick regardless of what any client wrote.
- **Prestige glyphs.** A tier-3 gate gets `★`; a treasury patron gets `✦`; a lapsed lease gets nothing. Purely cosmetic, purely server-controlled, entirely visible.
- **Map presence.** `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse", pinName, (int)Minimap.PinType.Icon3, pos, false)` pushes a real SAVED pin onto a vanilla client's map with an arbitrary name at an arbitrary coordinate. `Game.RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` is registered on every client unconditionally in `Game.Start` (:100068) and its body calls `Minimap.DiscoverLocation(pos, type, name, showMap)` → `AddPin(..., save: true)`. Sell a named gate and every player on the server gets it pinned on their map on next login. This is the only way a vanilla client ever gets portal names on its map.
- **Announcement.** A fabricated `"ChatMessage"` of type Shout from a server-chosen speaker name gives a chat line plus a 5s labelled world pin (`Chat.OnNewChatMessage` :41775, `Chat.AddInworldText` :41873).

**Player experience.** Most gates on the server are tagged with whatever their owner typed — `home`, `mine2`, `xxx`. The big ones are different. The central arch reads `Teleport tag:"★ THE BIFRÖST — Hall of the Raven" [Connected]` in full, un-truncated, and it has been that since the guild paid for it; nobody else can ever take that name, because a rival who renames their own gate to it gets it wiped back five seconds later with a toast reading `Name reserved.` And the first time you log in after the sale, a pin appears on your map at the Bifröst's coordinates with that exact name on it, saved permanently in your own map file. Names become a real status economy because they are scarce, visible, permanent and server-adjudicated — the first thing a new player sees is somebody else's name on their own map.

**Failure modes.**
- `TextInput.Show` assigns `m_inputField.text` to the existing tag AFTER setting `characterLimit = 10` (:61519-61520). If `GuiInputField` clamps, any player who opens and confirms the rename dialog on a long server-written name saves back a 10-character truncation. The kernel rewrites it on the next tick, so the damage is transient — but if you were using the tag as routing state (no kernel) it would be catastrophic.
- `ZDOVars.s_tagauthor` (:78619) is an unverified client self-report — `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`'s `authorId` parameter is whatever the client sent and is never cross-checked against the sending peer (:143587-143602). Never adjudicate a naming dispute on tagauthor; use `ZDOVars.s_creator` and the `s_creatorIndex` → `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` cross-check.
- Tag writes do not set `DirtyPortalObjects`. Every rename needs `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702) or it is silently lost at the next world save.
- `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` pins are `save: true` and there is NO removal RPC. A pin for a gate that is later demolished is permanently stuck on every player's map. Push pins only for genuinely permanent landmarks, and note `HaveSimilarPin` (same name + type within 1m) suppresses duplicates so a rename creates a SECOND pin rather than editing the first.
- A hostile client can write an arbitrarily long or abusive tag directly via `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77076) with no RPC involved at all. The kernel's next-tick rewrite is the defence; make sure it runs on a timer, not only on detected RPC traffic.
- Rewriting the tag every tick bumps DataRevision and re-sends the whole ZDO to every peer (`ZDOMan.SendZDOs` has no delta encoding, :77053). Write only on change — `ZDO.Set` is already a no-op for an unchanged value (`BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue`, assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321), so a straight compare-and-set is enough.

**Prerequisites.** The Routing Kernel

## 105. Event Topologies — Rotating Gates, Treasure Chains and the World Tour

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium-large

Scheduled, server-authored route graphs that change on a clock: a weekly dungeon gate, a chain that opens one link at a time, and a ring that tours the map — all pure topology, all unexploitable.

**How it works.** Three campaign shapes, all built out of the same primitives, all sitting squarely in the enforceable bucket because they express "which routes exist right now".

**Rotating Dungeon Gate.** A public hub portal whose far end is a Customs House anchor placed at a rotating world destination. Destinations come from `ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances` (:113295), a public `Dictionary<Vector2s, LocationInstance>` holding every location in the world, persisted in the save and fully populated before any peer connects (`ZNet.ServerLoadWorld` → `GenerateLocationsIfNeeded` :79273-79285). Each `LocationInstance` carries `m_position` whose y is already `WorldGenerator.GetHeight` (`ZoneSystem.GenerateLocationsTimeSliced` :114735) and `m_location` (a `ZoneLocation` exposing `m_prefabName`, `m_biome`, `m_exteriorRadius`, `m_iconAlways`/`m_iconPlaced` — :112885+). `ZoneSystem.FindLocations(name, ref list)` (:115728) and `GetLocationIcons(dict)` (:115450) give you named sets. Each in-game week, pick the next crypt, destroy the old anchor, fabricate a new one at `instance.m_position + Vector3.up * 2f`, re-point the hub, `ForceSendZDO` to every peer, rewrite the tag to the destination's name, and push a map pin.

**Treasure Chain.** N gates, edges enabled one at a time. Leg k opens only once a transit through leg k−1 has been detected (Reactive Transit Toll), or once a token appears on leg k's turnstile (Token Turnstile — better, because it needs no detection). Store progress as a world global key `mod_chain_leg <k>` so it survives restarts (`ZoneSystem.GetKeyValue` :113560 classifies any unrecognised name as `NonServerOption`, saved in the .db). Note the chain is SERVER-wide, not per-player — see the ruled-out option for why a per-player chain is impossible.

**World Tour Ring.** A ring topology A→B→C→…→A re-asserted every tick, rotating one position each in-game day so the ring's stop order changes. Vanilla's reconciler tolerates rings indefinitely because it never checks reciprocity (:100600-100604) — but `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461) collapses a ring across a save, so the kernel must rebuild it in `OnWorldReady`.

**Event dressing, all server-callable:**
- `RandEventSystem.instance.SetRandomEventByName(name, pos)` (:107067) is public and `SendCurrentRandomEvent` broadcasts `"SetEvent"` to every peer (:106956) — force a raid at the destination the moment the gate opens. Careful: if it is a boss event, `RandEventSystem.instance.GetBossEvent() != null` will blackout every portal on the server while `GlobalKeys.NoBossPortals` is set (`TeleportWorld.Teleport` :143528).
- `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "SpawnObject", pos, rot, prefabNameHash)` plays a vanilla VFX/SFX on one client (`ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject` :82355; working example Wonderland `Subsystems/ItemFlow/VacuumEngine.cs:199`).
- A fabricated Shout `"ChatMessage"` announces the opening with a labelled 5s map pin.

**Player experience.** **Rotating gate:** the hub has an eighth arch that has no fixed home. Every Sunday it changes: the tag reads `"THE WANDERING DOOR — Sunken Crypt (Swamp, 3.2km E)"`, a pin lands on everyone's map, and a shout goes out in chat. Step through and you are at the crypt mouth. Next Sunday it is a Mountain cave, the week after a Fuling village. People organise raids around it; the gate becomes a weekly appointment.

**Treasure chain:** five arches scattered across the map, all dark but one. The first, at the start temple, reads `"THE LONG ROAD I/V"` and is lit. Step through and you arrive at a mountain shelf where arch II stands with an item stand in front of it and a riddle on a sign. Mount the right trophy and II lights. Nobody can skip ahead — arch IV is genuinely not connected to anything until somebody solves III, and a cheater with a modified client finds exactly the same empty connection field everyone else has. When the last leg opens, the whole server knows, because the shout goes out.

**World tour:** a lit ring of eight gates. Step in anywhere and you come out at the next stop; step in there and you continue. Once a day the order shuffles, so the route you memorised on Tuesday goes somewhere else on Wednesday. It turns the map into a circuit you ride rather than a grid you address.

**Failure modes.**
- A location's OBJECT ZDOs (the crypt entrance, the altar, the chests) do not exist until that zone has been ghost-generated for some peer (`ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation` :115162, driven by `CreateGhostZones` :113934). The `LocationInstance` exists from world creation; the things inside it do not. Anchor to `m_position`, never to a scanned object ZDO.
- `LocationInstance.m_position.y` is the PRE-placement `WorldGenerator.GetHeight`; `ZoneSystem.PlaceLocations` re-resolves it with a raycast at spawn time and forces y = 30 for `m_snapToWater` locations (:114963-114968). Add ≥1-2m clearance or travellers arrive inside terrain — where `Player.UpdateTeleport`'s 15s fallback drops them at `GetSolidHeight + 0.5` anyway (:15360-15366), which is survivable but ugly.
- Ring and chain topologies do not survive a world save (`RegenerateConnectionHashData` :75461 gives each ZDO one hash slot). Without an `OnWorldReady` rebuild the event silently degrades into ordinary pairwise links.
- The first transit to a brand-new anchor in an unvisited region silently fails: `TeleportWorld.TargetFound` (:143640) needs the client to HOLD the destination ZDO and calls `RequestZDO` then returns false. `ForceSendZDO` the anchor to every peer at the moment of opening.
- Forcing a boss event via `SetRandomEventByName` while `NoBossPortals` is set blacks out EVERY portal on the server for every player (`TeleportWorld.Teleport` :143528 tests `GetBossEvent() != null` globally, not per-fight). Also `activeBosses` is maintained by whichever client has the boss loaded (`BaseAI.SetAlerted` :27258) and can leak above zero if that client crashes, permanently blocking portals until the server zeroes it.
- Anchor churn leaks ZDOs. Every rotation must destroy the previous anchor (claim ownership first, `DestroyZDO` :76929) or the save grows a dead anchor a week forever.

**Prerequisites.** The Routing Kernel; Park and Release; The Customs House; Token Turnstile (for the chain's gating) or Reactive Transit Toll

## 106. Route Auctions

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Scarce trunk slots awarded each cycle to whoever has the largest standing escrow balance — the cleanest possible use of the standing-balance primitive, with no debit and no race at all.

**How it works.** Declare a trunk endpoint — say a single arch in the capital that is the only gate reaching the Plains outpost — and make its partner a contested slot. Each cycle (an in-game day, tracked with `ZNet.instance.GetTimeSeconds()` :81546, or `GetDayFraction` :81542), the server ranks every candidate gate that has registered a bid and awards the edge to the top bidder.

The bid is not a payment, it is a standing balance in the bidder's bound escrow chest — read as in Prepaid Toll Escrow (`ZdoInventoryIO.Load` on `ZDOVars.s_items`, skipping `s_inUse`). This is the key simplification: **nothing is ever debited during bidding.** The server reads balances, sorts, writes the topology, and the losers' coins are untouched in their own chests. There is no clawback, no race with `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData`'s whole-blob conflict resolution (:77107), no refund path to get wrong, and a bidder who withdraws their coins simply drops out of the next ranking.

Settlement, if you want the winner to actually pay, is a single debit of the clearing price (second-highest bid, for a Vickrey auction) at the moment of award, via `ZdoInventoryIO.Save`. If that debit races and loses, the next cycle's balance check corrects it automatically.

Topology write is the ordinary kernel path: emit the edge `capitalTrunk ↔ winnerGate`, park every losing bidder's gate against the trunk (they keep their own local routes), `ForceSendZDO` both ends, and rewrite tags: winner gets `"TRUNK ★ — held by <name>"`, losers get `"TRUNK — outbid (1200c)"`.

Transparency is what makes it good play, and it is all free: the current high bid goes in every losing gate's tag, so a bidder can read the clearing price by walking to their own gate; the award goes out as a fabricated Shout `"ChatMessage"` (`Chat.OnNewChatMessage` :41775) with a 5s labelled map pin at the winner's gate; and a map pin push (`RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` :100823) marks the trunk's current terminus for everyone.

This generalises. Anything scarce and route-shaped can be auctioned: the Ore Gate flag (one on the server, held for a week), a Customs House bay, a slot in the World Tour ring, the right to name the trunk. Every one of them is "which route exists right now", so every one of them is enforced.

**Player experience.** There is one gate out of the capital that reaches the Plains, and it changes hands at dawn. Your gate at the southern farm reads `"PLAINS BID 800c — outbid (current 1200c)"`. You have until dawn. You top your chest up to 1300 and go to bed. At first light a shout goes across the server — `Auction: THE SOUTHERN ROAD holds the Plains trunk (clearing 1200c)` — a pin drops on everyone's map at your farm, and your gate lights with the tag `"PLAINS ★ — Southern Road"`. For one in-game day every trader who wants the Plains comes through your yard, and you charge them a toll of your own. Tomorrow you defend it or lose it. Nothing about this needs an admin, a web panel, or a client mod: it is chests, arches and a clock.

**Failure modes.**
- A bidder who leaves 1300 coins in an unwarded chest overnight is running an auction and a bank robbery simultaneously. Require the escrow chest to sit inside an enabled ward (Physical Tiers signal 2) or the whole mechanic collapses into theft.
- Reading every bidder's chest each cycle costs an `Inventory.Load` per chest, which does `Instantiate`/`Destroy` per stack (:68726). With 40 bidders that is one lumpy frame per cycle — spread it across ticks with a resumable cursor, never in one pass.
- Sniping: a bidder who tops up seconds before the cycle boundary wins on a stale read. Either read all balances in a single frame at the boundary (accepting the cost) or announce a sealed window and freeze reads for the last minute.
- Coin-lending collusion — one stack of coins passed between chests to inflate multiple bids — is undetectable, because coins are fungible and the server cannot see who moved them. Mitigate by debiting the winner (the coins are actually consumed) rather than running a pure standing-balance auction.
- A client can rewrite its own chest's `s_items` wholesale via `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77076) — no RPC, no validation, no ownership test. A modified client can claim any balance. This is the one place the auction is genuinely exploitable, and the only defence is anomaly detection (a balance that jumps by more than any legitimate transfer) plus a Discord audit line.

**Prerequisites.** The Routing Kernel; Park and Release; Prepaid Toll Escrow; Cooldowns and Throughput Quotas (for the cycle clock)

**Citations.** ZNet.GetTimeSeconds / GetDayFraction — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81546 and :81542 · ZDOVars.s_items / s_inUse — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78475 and :78673 · Container.Save / Load — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:122294 and :122303 · Inventory.AddItem(int prefabHash,…) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:68726 · ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (client can rewrite any ZDO) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77076 · Game.SetConnection (write primitive) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100637 · ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77706 · Chat.OnNewChatMessage (fabricated shout) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41775 · Game.RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100823 · ZdoInventoryIO.Load — Wonderland/Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs:31

## 107. RULED OUT — Point-of-Transit Enforcement and Traveller Inspection

`RULED-OUT` · `NOT-ENFORCEABLE` · effort: small

Everything of the form "should THIS PLAYER pass right now?": per-player tolls at the gate, cargo tariffs, PIN prompts, per-player progression locks, refunds, and reading a traveller's inventory. All impossible, for four independent reasons.

**How it works.** Four independent walls, any one of which is fatal.

**1. No transit hook exists.** `TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player)` has exactly one call site in the entire assembly: `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter(Collider)` (:143664-143682), gated on `colliderIn.GetComponent<Player>() != null && Player.m_localPlayer == component`. On a dedicated server no portal GameObject, no trigger collider and no `Player` component ever exists, because `Game.FixedUpdate` unconditionally pins `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick (:100458-100466 — a line present in NO form in the client assembly), so `ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted` (:82105) only instantiates in a sector 1e6 m from the world and `Player.s_players` (filled by `Player.Awake` :10032) is permanently empty. A Harmony patch on `TeleportWorld.Teleport`, `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` or `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` compiles, applies and never fires.

**2. Even a ZDO-targeted RPC would not reach a handler.** `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` (:83646-83663) dispatches a ZDO-targeted RPC only through `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zdo)` (:82229), which reads `m_instances` — permanently empty server-side. Worse, `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` (:83577-83595) skips `RouteRPC` entirely when `targetPeerID == m_id`, so a client that OWNS the portal ZDO executes `RPC_SetTag` in-process with no packet on the wire at all. The server cannot observe, let alone veto, the most common case.

**3. The inventory is never networked.** An exhaustive scan of every `Set(ZDOVars.s_*)` in `Character` (:178-6796), `Humanoid` (:6796-9414) and `Player` (:9414-16500) yields only vitals, identity, pose and emote fields — never items. `ZDOVars.s_items` (:78475) is written by exactly one live path, `Container.Save` (:122294). A player's inventory lives in `Player.Save`'s ZPackage inside their own local `.fch` (`Player.Save` :14091 → `PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData` :105706), and `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles` (:79653) merely invokes `"SavePlayerProfile"` on each client to write its OWN disk file and returns nothing. So vanilla's ore check (`Inventory.IsTeleportable` :68860) is unreproducible, no cargo tariff is possible, no debit from a living player's pack is possible, and no refund is possible.

**4. Detection is 2s late and cannot refuse anything.** See Reactive Transit Toll — the server learns a transit happened ≈2s after `Player.UpdateTeleport` begins assigning positions (:15337-15343), by which time the move is done and the player is invulnerable.

Also ruled out for related reasons: portal PIN prompts (`TextInput` is a client GUI singleton; `TeleportWorld.Interact` is local-player-only, :143471); per-player progression gates (skills/recipes/uniques are in the `.fch`, `Player.m_uniques` :9711); vanilla portal telemetry (`PlayerStatType.PortalsUsed` = 15, `PortalDungeonIn/Out` = 83/84 go to `PlayerProfile.IncrementStat` :106287, never networked); and dungeon/crypt doors entirely (`class Teleport` :143316 has no ZNetView, no ZDO, no RPC — its destination is the compiled Inspector reference `public Teleport m_targetPoint` :143322, so it cannot be re-routed, audited, priced or even observed).

**Player experience.** None — this is the set of features that must NOT be promised. The failure is silent and looks like a bug: a "pay 5 coins per trip" feature that actually charges after the fact lets the first trip through free every time; an "ore tariff" quietly charges nobody; a "members only" gate lets everybody through. What players CAN be given instead, and what every enforceable option above does, is a world where the route itself is the subject of the rule: the gate is dark, or lit, for everyone, for a reason they can read in its tag. That reads as a game rule. A per-player check that silently fails reads as a broken mod.

**Failure modes.**
- The seductive trap: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` is `public` and appears in any reflection dump, so it looks callable from a server plugin. It is not usefully callable — no instance exists, `m_nview` would be null, `player.Message` needs `MessageHud.instance`, and `Game.instance.IncrementPlayerStat` writes the server's own junk profile (`Game.Awake` creates a `new PlayerProfile()` named "Stranger" at :100047).
- Equally seductive: `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` (:137547) returns TRUE for every point on a dedicated server — not as a grant but because `m_allAreas` (:137173) is empty. Using it as an authorisation check is a silent allow-all.
- Same class: `Bed.IsMine`, `Bed.IsCurrent`, `Piece.IsCreator`, `TombStone.IsOwner`, `Container.CheckAccess` all compare against `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()` — a junk "Stranger" profile with a random UID on a dedicated server. They return garbage rather than throwing.
- The only genuine per-player levers the server has are all REACTIVE and post-hoc: forced teleport (`Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer` :41962 / `Character.RPC_TeleportTo` :4126, both ungated on the client and both silently no-op if `Player.m_teleportCooldown < 2f`, :15311), a status effect (`SEMan.RPC_AddStatusEffect` :28823, with no removal RPC anywhere), a toast, a map pin, a kick or a ban. None of them can prevent a transit; all of them can punish one.
- Any design that routes a per-player rule through property instead — see Debtor's Lien — moves it back into the enforceable bucket. That transformation is the only correct response to a per-player requirement.

## 108. NoPortals Global Key

`FEASIBLE` · `CLIENT-HONOURED` · effort: small

Flip vanilla's own world-modifier key so every unmodified client refuses portal transit with the stock $msg_blocked message.

**How it works.** `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey("noportals")` is a one-line call whose entire body is `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey", name)` (:115943-115946). The 1-arg InvokeRoutedRPC targets `GetServerPeerID()`, which on the server is its own id, so `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` dispatches synchronously through `HandleRoutedRPC` (:83588) and the key is readable before the call returns. `RPC_SetGlobalKey` (:116022-116029) checks `!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)`, calls `GlobalKeyAdd`, then `SendGlobalKeys(0L)`. `SendGlobalKeys` (:113466-113471) invokes the `GlobalKeys` routed RPC at peer 0 with `new List<string>(m_globalKeys)`; each client's `RPC_GlobalKeys` (:113473-113481) does `ClearGlobalKeys()` then re-adds every entry. Propagation is one routed-RPC hop inside the same call stack — `RouteRPC` (:83597-83629) calls `peer.m_rpc.Invoke` immediately, with no accumulation buffer. There is no polling interval and no relog requirement. Late joiners are covered by `ZoneSystem.OnNewPeer` (:113607-113616), hooked onto `ZRoutedRpc.m_onNewPeer` in `ZoneSystem.Start` (:113444), which calls `SendGlobalKeys(peerID)` for every peer that becomes ready. On the client, `TeleportWorld.Teleport` reads it live at :143523 and returns after `player.Message(Center, "$msg_blocked")`. CRITICAL CALLING DETAIL: use the lowercase string literal `"noportals"`, not `SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)`. The enum overload stringifies PascalCase (:115938-115941) and the store only ever holds lowercase (normalised in `GlobalKeyAdd` :113487), so `RPC_SetGlobalKey`'s `!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)` dedupe guard at :116024 never trips and every call re-adds and re-broadcasts the entire key list to every peer. In a polling loop that is a broadcast storm. Pre-check with `GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` (:115948, a `m_globalKeysEnums.Contains` lookup) and only write on an actual transition.

**Player experience.** Nothing visible changes until the player walks into a portal. The portal still glows, `GetHoverText` still reads `$piece_portal_connected` (:143461) because `HaveTarget()` only inspects the connection, and `UpdatePortal`'s 0.5s poll still lights `m_target_found` (:143507) — none of that reads the key. The player steps through the ring, nothing happens, and a centre-screen `$msg_blocked` appears. Every portal on the server behaves identically and instantly, including for players who were already standing next to one. Dungeon and crypt doors keep working normally, ore and all. When the key is cleared the very next step through the ring teleports — no relog, no zone reload.

**Failure modes.**
- 100% client-honoured. A modified client that deletes the `if` at :143523 teleports normally and the server observes nothing — not the attempt, not the transit.
- `RPC_SetGlobalKey` has zero sender validation (:116022-116029). Any connected vanilla client can clear `noportals` at will by invoking the routed RPC. Unusable as a lockdown without the hardening option.
- Setting the key at runtime permanently edits the world: `GlobalKeyAdd` mirrors any key with ordinal < 41 into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113511), written to the .fwl at the next autosave. Uninstalling the mod leaves `noportals` baked into the world forever.
- Zero player-facing warning before the block. The portal looks and sounds fully functional right up to the moment of refusal, which reads as a bug to players.
- Does not touch dungeon/crypt doors at all — `Teleport.Interact` (:143345-143370) never reads NoPortals. Advertising this as 'disable all teleportation' is factually wrong.
- `GlobalKeyAdd` unconditionally dereferences `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()` at :113506-113508 and its `UpdateWorldRates` tail reaches `Minimap.instance` via `Game.UpdateNoMap`. Calling it before those objects exist turns a key write into an NRE that aborts before `SendGlobalKeys`.

**Citations.** ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115943-115946 · ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:116022-116029 · ZoneSystem.SendGlobalKeys — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113466-113471 · ZoneSystem.RPC_GlobalKeys — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113473-113481 · ZoneSystem.OnNewPeer — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113607-113616 · ZoneSystem.Start RPC registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113444-113449 · TeleportWorld.Teleport NoPortals gate — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143523-143527 · GlobalKeys enum NoPortals=32 — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:101304 · ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd lowercase + .fwl mirror — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113483-113513 · ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC self-dispatch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83577-83595

Strong indirect evidence yes (Wonderland's WorldRatesEngine calls GlobalKeyAdd live on a dedicated server), but not provable from the decompile. ## 109. Global-Key RPC Hardening

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small-medium

Prefix RPC_SetGlobalKey and RPC_RemoveGlobalKey to drop any packet that did not originate from the server itself, closing the hole that lets any client lift a key lockdown.

**How it works.** `ZoneSystem.Start` registers `SetGlobalKey` and `RemoveGlobalKey` on `ZRoutedRpc.instance` only when `ZNet.instance.IsServer()` (:113445-113449), so both handlers genuinely execute on the dedicated server and are real Harmony targets (unlike ZDO-targeted handlers). Neither body inspects `sender` (:116022-116037). The mod adds `[HarmonyPatch(typeof(ZoneSystem), "RPC_SetGlobalKey")] static bool Prefix(long sender, string name)` and the matching one for `RPC_RemoveGlobalKey`, returning false unless `sender == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()` (:77362, the server's own id, which is what `ZRoutedRpc`'s self-dispatch path stamps into `m_senderPeerID` at :83580) OR the mod is itself the caller (set a `[ThreadStatic] bool s_selfWrite` flag around its own `SetGlobalKey` calls, which is more robust than an id compare because the id path depends on `GetServerPeerID`). Scope the veto to a configured allowlist of key NAMES — resolve with the public static `ZoneSystem.GetKeyValue(name, out value, out gk)` (:113560-113579) and veto only when `gk` is one of NoPortals/NoBossPortals/TeleportAll/DungeonBuild, so legitimate client-originated key traffic (boss `defeated_*` keys written by `Character.OnDeath` :3153-3156, `activeBosses` written by `BaseAI.SetAlerted` :27258-27259) still passes. A vetoed packet should be routed to `AuditLog.Flag("GlobalKeyTamper", playerName, key)`. Resolve the offending peer for the log by matching `sender` against `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` `m_uid` — but note `m_senderPeerID` is deserialized straight off the wire (`RoutedRPCData.Deserialize` :83487-83495) and is a client self-report, so for a *forensic* identity you must patch `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (:83632) instead, where the authentic socket is in scope, and map `rpc` to a peer via `GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)`. There the true identity is `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`, the same string vanilla's own `ZNet.RPC_Kick` uses against `m_adminList` (:81670).

**Player experience.** Invisible to honest players. A cheating client that fires `RemoveGlobalKey noportals` sees absolutely nothing happen — no error, no key change, no broadcast — because the veto drops the packet before `GlobalKeyRemove` runs, and the client's own key set is a read-only mirror that the next `SendGlobalKeys` overwrites anyway. The server log gets one `[SECURITY:GlobalKeyTamper]` line naming the SteamID64 that tried it.

**Failure modes.**
- Does nothing for the far larger hole: `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77076-77139) applies any incoming ZDO wholesale when the incoming DataRevision exceeds the local one, with no ownership, prefab or field validation. Global keys are not ZDO data so they are safe here, but a client can still rewrite portal tags and connections directly.
- Vetoing too broadly breaks vanilla progression: `Character.OnDeath` writes `m_defeatSetGlobalKey` from the client that killed the boss (:3153-3156), and `BaseAI.SetAlerted` writes `activeBosses` from whichever client owns the boss (:27258-27259). An allowlist keyed on `GetKeyValue`'s parsed `GlobalKeys` enum is mandatory.
- `m_senderPeerID` is spoofable, so an id-based allow test can be forged by a client claiming the server's own id. The `[ThreadStatic]` self-write flag plus a socket-derived check in `RPC_RoutedRPC` is the only sound version.
- A prefix on `RPC_SetGlobalKey` that returns false also suppresses `SendGlobalKeys(0L)`, so if the mod ever vetoes its own write by accident the key silently never propagates and the lockdown appears to work server-side while every client is unlocked. Always read back with `GetGlobalKey` after writing.

**Prerequisites.** NoPortals Global Key

## 110. Session-Only Key Writes

`FEASIBLE` · `CLIENT-HONOURED` · effort: small

Write NoPortals/TeleportAll through the publicized GlobalKeyAdd with canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false so a temporary lockdown never gets baked into the world's .fwl modifier list.

**How it works.** `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey` routes through the RPC and always ends in `GlobalKeyAdd(name)` with the default `canSaveToServerOptionKeys = true`, whose only effect is the `flag` computed at :113488 (`canSaveToServerOptionKeys && ZNet.World != null && gk < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption`) which drives `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys.Add(keyStr.ToLower())` at :113511. Bypassing that is a direct call to the private `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` followed by an explicit `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` — both require `<Publicize>true</Publicize>` on assembly_valheim, which the sibling Wonderland csproj already sets. The full session-only write is: `ZoneSystem.instance.GlobalKeyAdd("noportals", false); ZoneSystem.instance.SendGlobalKeys(0L);` and the matching clear is `ZoneSystem.instance.GlobalKeyRemove("noportals", false); ZoneSystem.instance.SendGlobalKeys(0L);` (:113516-113539). Because the key is absent from `m_startingGlobalKeys` it is also absent from the .fwl (`World.SaveWorldFWLData` :112581-112585) and absent from the .db (`ZoneSystem.Save` strips ordinals < 41 at :113751-113755), so a restart returns the world to whatever `SetStartingGlobalKeys` (:115904-115931) finds in the .fwl — i.e. the pre-mod state. The mod's own intent is then persisted in its own config/state file and re-applied after boot. Re-application must be a POSTFIX on `ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys`, never a prefix, because a `preset` key in the world causes `ServerOptionsGUI.m_instance.SetPreset(ZNet.World, text)` to reapply an entire slider key set at :115920-115926 and would clobber a prefix-applied key. Note the asymmetry in `GlobalKeyAdd`: the removal of a prior value at :113492-113496 uses the trimmed `keyValue + " " + value2` form while the add at :113511 uses the raw `keyStr.ToLower()`, so always pass the same canonical lowercase literal for both add and remove or the .fwl entry can be orphaned.

**Player experience.** Identical in-game to the plain key write — `$msg_blocked` on transit while engaged. The difference is invisible to players and entirely visible to the operator: after a restart the world is clean, the server-browser modifier badge does not permanently claim 'Portals: off', and removing the mod does not leave a locked world behind.

**Failure modes.**
- Requires the assembly publicizer for `GlobalKeyAdd`, `GlobalKeyRemove` and `SendGlobalKeys` (all private). A signature change in a future patch breaks it silently unless wrapped in Wonderland's `SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch` / a reflection probe.
- A session-only key vanishes on an unplanned restart. If the intent was a multi-day lockdown the mod must re-apply from its own state file at boot, and there is a window between `ZNet.WorldSetup` → `SetStartingGlobalKeys` and the mod's postfix where the key is absent — harmless because no peer is connected yet, but it must be verified the postfix runs before `ZNet.OpenServer`.
- `GlobalKeyAdd` with `canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false` still fires `Achievements.MarkAchievementDifficultyDirty()` (:113505) and `UpdateWorldRates()` (:113513) — the achievement-integrity side effects are unchanged.
- Does not solve tamper: a client can still `SetGlobalKey`/`RemoveGlobalKey` freely. Needs the hardening option.

**Prerequisites.** NoPortals Global Key

**Citations.** ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd canSaveToServerOptionKeys flag — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113483-113513 (flag :113488, .fwl write :113511) · ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyRemove — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113516-113539 · ZoneSystem.Save strips ordinals < NonServerOption — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113742-113760 · ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys (wipes 0..40, SetPreset at :115925) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115904-115931 · ZoneSystem.SendGlobalKeys — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113466-113471 · World.SaveWorldFWLData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:112570-112597 · Wonderland WorldRatesPatches re-assert pattern — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/WorldRatesPatches.cs:9-25

## 111. Force-Disconnect Lockdown

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium-large

Null every portal's Portal connection server-side and suppress vanilla's 5s re-pairing, leaving even a fully hacked client with no destination coordinate to travel to.

**How it works.** Enumerate with `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (:77648-77656, a freshly flattened list of every portal ZDO in the world, always resident because portals live in `m_portalObjects` and are never unloaded). For each portal: record `(rounded position, s_tag, current connection's rounded position)` into the Connection Vault, then `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` (:74627 / :77362), `zdo.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, ZDOID.None)` (:73656-73666 — bumps DataRevision and calls `SetDirtyPortals`), then `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706) to push it to every peer immediately rather than waiting for the ordinary sync sweep. This is exactly the shape of vanilla's own `Game.SetConnection` immediate-write branch (:100641-100646), so it is a supported access pattern, not a hack. THREE DEFENCES ARE MANDATORY OR THE LOCK UNDOES ITSELF. (1) Vanilla re-pairing: `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 2 (:100607-100622) pairs every `ZDOID.None` portal with a random same-tag partner within 5s (`ConnectPortalsCoroutine` :100580-100586). Add `[HarmonyPrefix]` on the public `Game.ConnectPortals` (:100589) returning false while locked. Note it must be a full suppression, not just phase 2, because phase 0's `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` (:100690-100698) force-commits the previous tick's proposals with `forceImmediateConnection: true` regardless of ownership. (2) Ownership theft: `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901-76926) runs every 2s from `ReleaseZDOS` (:76872-76883) and hands any persistent ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer; the server always fails `IsInPeerActiveArea` for real coordinates because its reference position is pinned at (1e6,0,1e6) (:100465). Guard with a `[HarmonyPrefix]` on `ZDO.SetOwner` returning false for portal-prefab ZDOs while locked, allowing through only `uid == 0` and `uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()` — the exact `ZdoSetOwnerPatch` shape in Wonderland's WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313. Fail fast on `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(zdo.GetPrefab())` because SetOwner is a global hot path. (3) Client write-back: `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653-100662) is a global routed RPC registered on every peer at `Game.Start` :100066 with zero sender validation — prefix it to drop any call whose portal ZDO is under lockdown. And `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77107-77132) replaces the whole ZDO blob on a higher DataRevision, so also run a 1s re-assert tick that re-nulls any locked portal whose connection has become non-None, bumping `DataRevision += 4096` to win the race (Wonderland's proven counter-measure).

**Player experience.** A player walking up to a locked portal sees it visibly dead: `HaveTarget()` returns false (:143631-143638) so `GetHoverText` reads `$piece_portal_unconnected` (:143461), `Update()` lerps `m_colorAlpha` toward 0 and the emission material fades from `m_colorTargetfound` to `m_colorUnconnected` (:143511-143515), and `UpdatePortal`'s 0.5s poll leaves `m_target_found` off (:143507). Walking through the ring does absolutely nothing — no message at all, because `Teleport()` returns at gate 1 (`if (!TargetFound()) return;` :143519-143522) before any `player.Message` call. That silence is a UX problem in its own right and is why the graceful-lockdown option pairs an explicit announcement with the disconnect. A hacked client that strips all four gates still cannot move: :143539 resolves the connection to `ZDOID.None`, `ZDOMan.GetZDO` returns null for None (:76756-76759), and the whole teleport body is inside `if (zDO != null)` at :143540. When lockdown lifts and the vault restores the wiring, the first walk-through may still fail silently once — `TargetFound()` requires the client to actually HOLD the destination ZDO and fires `RequestZDO` and returns false when it does not (:143646-143655) — so plan a one-transit warm-up, or pre-push destinations with `ForceSendZDO(peerUid, destId)`.

**Failure modes.**
- THE BIG ONE: `ZDO.SetConnection(Portal, ...)` sets `DirtyPortalObjects` (:73661-73664), and that flag is the sole trigger for writing the portal chunk (`GetSaveClonePerChunk` :77621-77632). An autosave during lockdown persists every connection as None; on reload `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` calls `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` (:76523) and phase 2 randomly re-pairs same-tag portals (:100678). The original network is not merely still-locked, it is SCRAMBLED. Mandatory mitigation: the Save-Boundary Transparency option, or the Connection Vault with load-time restore, or both.
- Suppressing `Game.ConnectPortals` wholesale also suppresses its self-heal pass (:100594-100606), so dangling connections to destroyed portals accumulate for the duration of the lockdown. A portal demolished mid-lockdown leaves its partner holding a dead ZDOID that is only cleaned when suppression lifts.
- Eventually consistent with a ~50-100ms tail. `ZDOMan.SendZDOToPeers2` services one peer per 0.05s (:76837-76861). A player who steps into a trigger in that window uses their client's stale connection and teleports. `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` fires on ENTER only (:143673), so a player already standing inside the volume never re-triggers either way.
- Cannot recall an in-flight traveller. Once `Player.TeleportTo` returns true the destination is snapshotted into `m_teleportTargetPos` (:15324) and `UpdateTeleport` force-assigns it every tick (:15343); a counter-teleport is refused because `m_teleportCooldown < 2f` (:15313) and is zeroed every tick while teleporting (:15336).
- A fully hacked client can call `Player.TeleportTo` locally with no portal at all. 'Unbypassable' means no portal-mediated travel, never no travel.
- Mass `ForceSendZDO` on hundreds of portals floods every peer's sync queue against the 10240-byte cap (:77010-77016) — see the spike-control option.
- The `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix is on a global hot path touched by `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` for every peer every 2s. A slow or throwing predicate degrades the whole server.

**Prerequisites.** Connection Vault and Crash Recovery; Save-Boundary Transparency; Mass-Rewrite Spike Control

## 112. Connection Vault and Crash Recovery

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

A position-keyed side-file recording the true wiring of every portal before any lockdown touches it, restored at world load so a crash mid-lockdown never scrambles the network.

**How it works.** A JSON or line-delimited file under `BepInEx.Paths.ConfigPath`, named per world UID, written atomically (write `.tmp`, then `File.Replace` / temp-then-move — the SupplySwitch pattern). Each record is `{ tagBefore, posA (x,y,z rounded to 0.1), posB (x,y,z rounded to 0.1), lockedAtUtc, reason }`. KEYED BY ROUNDED WORLD POSITION, NEVER BY ZDOID: `ZDO.Load` renumbers every ZDO on every world load (`m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`), so a ZDOID-keyed vault silently points at nothing after a restart — this is the exact bug TortalPortal's Favorites.cs hit and documented before switching to a position key. Position is safe for portals specifically because `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for any prefab in `Game.PortalPrefabHash` (:73752-73756), meaning portals are never repositioned by any vanilla path and a mod must never reposition one either. WRITE ORDER on engage: snapshot the whole vault and fsync it FIRST, then begin nulling connections. Never interleave. RESTORE runs at world load, which is the cheapest possible window: at `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` every ZDO comes back with `Owned=false, OwnerRevision=0, DataRevision=0`, `m_peers` is empty so `Game.SetConnection`'s `owner == 0L` branch (:100641) always takes the immediate local write, and no client can contend. Hook a postfix on `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` (or `Game.Start` before the `ConnectPortalsCoroutine` StartCoroutine at :100074) and for each vault record: find the live portal ZDO nearest `posA` within a 1.0m tolerance in `GetPortalList()`, find the one nearest `posB`, verify both still carry `tagBefore` (or at least both carry the same tag as each other), then `SetOwner(sessionID)` + `SetConnection(Portal, otherUid)` on both ends + `ForceSendZDO`. Discard any record whose endpoints no longer resolve — that portal was demolished while locked. Then delete the vault. EXPECTATION MANAGEMENT: exact restoration is only meaningful for tag groups of exactly 2. `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (:100664-100679) picks uniformly at random among same-tag unconnected portals, and for a group of 3+ vanilla itself strands exactly one member arbitrarily, with the stranded member determined by `m_portalObjects` dictionary bucket order which is not stable across restarts. For groups of 3+ the vault restores *a* valid pairing identical to the one that was live, which is strictly better than a random re-shuffle but is not a promise vanilla ever made.

**Player experience.** Operator-facing. After an unplanned restart during a lockdown the server log prints `[TortalPortal] Restored 47/49 portal links from vault (2 endpoints missing — portals demolished during lockdown)`, and players find their base-to-mine and base-to-swamp portals connected to exactly the same partners as before the crash, rather than discovering their swamp portal now leads to someone else's identically-tagged outpost.

**Failure modes.**
- Only protects what it recorded. A portal built during the lockdown has no vault entry and will be randomly paired by vanilla on restore — correct behaviour, but it must be logged rather than silently absorbed.
- A world rollback to an older backup makes the vault describe portals that no longer exist, or exist at those positions with different tags. Every record must be validated against live state before restore, and a record whose endpoints resolve but whose tags disagree must be discarded, not forced.
- Two portals within the 1.0m position tolerance (stacked or clipped builds) make the nearest-match ambiguous. Tie-break on tag, then refuse and log rather than guess.
- Restoring a 3+ member tag group reproduces the previous pairing, not a canonically 'correct' one — there is no canonical one. Do not advertise it as such.
- If the mod is uninstalled while a lockdown is active, the vault is never replayed and the world keeps nulled connections until vanilla re-pairs them randomly. The uninstall path must be documented: lift the lockdown before removing the plugin.
- Vault writes are disk I/O on the main thread. Batch them; a per-portal fsync on a 500-portal world will stall a frame.

**Prerequisites.** Force-Disconnect Lockdown

## 113. Save-Boundary Transparency

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Sandwich the world-save snapshot between a restore and a re-lock so that a lockdown is never written to disk at all, making crash recovery a non-event.

**How it works.** `ZNet.SaveWorld` (:80521-80546) runs entirely on the main thread up to the point it spawns the writer thread: it fires `WorldSaveStarted?.Invoke()` at :80524, then `m_zdoMan.PrepareSave()` at :80532, then `ZoneSystem/RandEventSystem/PersistentEventSystem.PrepareSave()`, then starts `m_saveThread`. `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` (:76197-76205) is public and does `m_saveData.m_objectsByChunk = GetSaveClonePerChunk()` — which deep-clones every portal ZDO into the ChunkPortal bucket when `DirtyPortalObjects` (:77621-77632) — followed by `ZDOExtraData.PrepareSave()` (:75480-75491) which calls `RegenerateConnectionHashData()` (:75461-75477) to turn live `s_connections` into the saveable `s_connectionsHashData`. Everything the writer thread later serialises is captured in those two calls. So: `[HarmonyPrefix]` on `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` writes the TRUE connections back from the vault into `s_connections` via `zdo.SetConnection(Portal, trueTarget)`; `[HarmonyPostfix]` on the same method immediately re-nulls them. Both halves run in the same frame with no `ZDOMan.Update` between them (the send sweep is gated on a 0.05s timer at :76843-76861 and is driven from Update, not from the save path), so no peer ever receives the unlocked state. Use `ZDO.SetConnection` rather than poking `ZDOExtraData` directly so `DirtyPortalObjects` stays set and the chunk is actually written. DO NOT close the sandwich with `ZNet.WorldSaveFinished` (:78991): it is invoked from `PrintWorldSaveMessage` (:80580), ~0.5s after the thread ends via `UpdateSave` (:80548-80564), and that method dereferences `MessageHud.instance.MessageAll` unguarded at :80574 and :80578 — if that singleton is ever null on a headless build the event never fires and the world is left unlocked in memory. `WorldSaveStarted` is a safe *notification* hook (public static Action, :78989) for logging and for forcing a vault flush, but the actual sandwich must be the PrepareSave prefix/postfix pair because only that is guaranteed to bracket the snapshot. Additionally guard against re-entrancy: `SaveWorld` joins a still-running previous save thread at :80525-80530, and a synchronous shutdown save (`ZNet.Shutdown(save:true)` → `Save(sync:true)` :79466-79472) goes through the same path — the sandwich covers both.

**Player experience.** Entirely invisible. The only observable difference is that a `kill -9` during a two-hour maintenance lockdown produces a world that comes back with every portal wired exactly as it was, with no vault replay needed and no log noise.

**Failure modes.**
- Relies on a Harmony patch on `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` running atomically around the snapshot. If another mod also patches it and returns false from a prefix, the postfix may not run and the world is left restored-and-unlocked in memory until the next re-assert tick catches it. Make the re-assert tick authoritative rather than trusting the postfix alone.
- `ZoneSystem.SkipSaving()` (:115874-115881) and `DungeonDB.SkipSaving()` can make `ZNet.Save` bail at :80183 BEFORE `SaveWorld` is ever called, so the sandwich never runs — harmless (nothing is written either) but the mod must not assume a paired prefix/postfix for every `Save()` call.
- If the mod's own re-assert tick fires between prefix and postfix (it cannot, same frame, but a coroutine or thread could), the lock state becomes indeterminate. Keep all lockdown mutation single-threaded on the main thread.
- `ConsiderAutoBackup` runs INSIDE `SaveWorldThread` at :80601, after the snapshot — so a backup taken during lockdown contains the sandwiched (restored) state, which is correct. But a manual file-level backup taken by an external cron while the server is running copies whatever is already on disk, which is also the restored state. Both are fine; a backup taken by copying live memory is not possible, so there is no third case.
- Doubles the number of `SetConnection` calls per save on a locked world — 2N revision bumps per save cycle. On a 500-portal world that is 1000 dictionary writes plus 1000 `IncreaseDataRevision` calls inside the save freeze. Measurable but small; still worth a budget.

**Prerequisites.** Force-Disconnect Lockdown; Connection Vault and Crash Recovery

## 114. Scheduled Blackout Windows

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

A cron-style schedule that engages and lifts portal restrictions at fixed real-world or in-game times, with announcements and an idempotent reconciler rather than edge-triggered toggles.

**How it works.** A config list of windows, each `{ days, startLocal, endLocal, mode }` where mode is one of `KeyOnly` (NoPortals), `Disconnect` (force-disconnect), or `TagQuarantine`. The engine ticks from the subsystem `OnUpdate(dt)` at 1Hz and computes the DESIRED state from wall-clock time, then reconciles: if desired != actual, apply the transition. Level-triggered, never edge-triggered — this is the single most important design choice, because an edge-triggered scheduler that misses its tick (server restart across the boundary, a long save freeze, a clock change) leaves the world in the wrong state forever. On every tick the reconciler also verifies the invariant (all locked portals still have `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal).IsNone()`) and repairs drift, which doubles as the anti-tamper re-assert. In-game-time scheduling is also available and is often what operators actually want ('portals closed at night'): the server's day fraction comes from `EnvMan` / `ZNet.GetTimeSeconds`, and `Game.m_dayTimeSpeed`-scaled day length means a real-time schedule and an in-game schedule drift apart — pick one per window and label it in the config. State (which windows are currently engaged, and the vault) persists to the mod's own file so a restart inside a window resumes correctly rather than re-announcing. Announcements fire at T-10min, T-5min, T-60s and at engage, through the channels in the graceful-lockdown option; each announcement is rate-limited per player so a reconciler that runs at 1Hz does not spam. Hot-reload of the schedule without a restart comes free from the Wonderland `PollConfigFile` pattern (5s mtime poll, `SaveOnConfigSet` parked false during `Config.Reload()` so re-applied values do not bump mtime and cause a reload loop).

**Player experience.** At 21:50 server time every online player gets a top-left message: 'Portal network closes in 10 minutes (nightly maintenance window).' At 21:55 and 21:59 the warning repeats, the last one centre-screen. At 22:00 every portal in the world visibly goes dark — hover text flips to `$piece_portal_unconnected`, the ring's emission fades — and walking through does nothing. At 06:00 the reconciler restores every link from the vault and a message reads 'Portal network is open.' A player who logs in at 03:00 sees dark portals and, on their first `OnNewPeer`, a toast explaining the window and when it ends. A player mid-transit at exactly 22:00:00 still arrives — `Player.UpdateTeleport` cannot be interrupted (:15343-15349).

**Failure modes.**
- Wall-clock schedules across a daylight-saving transition either fire twice or not at all. Compute in UTC and convert for display only.
- `WaitForSeconds` and `Time` are scaled; `Game.UpdateSleeping`'s time-skip path can advance in-game time in a jump, so an in-game-time window can be skipped entirely by a sleep. The level-triggered reconciler absorbs this correctly; an edge-triggered one does not.
- A restart inside a window must not re-run the engage transition (re-announcing, re-vaulting over an already-vaulted state). Persist 'currently engaged' and treat a matching persisted state as already-applied.
- Two overlapping windows with different modes need a defined precedence or they will fight each other on every tick. Define strictest-wins and log the resolution.
- A window that engages within the 30s pre-save warning (`Game.UpdateSaving` :100474 fires `$msg_worldsavewarning 30s`) piles two disruptive announcements on top of each other and puts the lock right next to a snapshot. Refuse to engage within 60s of `m_saveInterval` (default 1800f, :99914) elapsing, or force a clean save first.

**Prerequisites.** Force-Disconnect Lockdown; Graceful Lockdown and Announcement
