## 130. Crypt Ingress — Portals Into Dungeon Interiors

`CAVEATS` · `CLIENT-HONOURED` · effort: medium

Dungeon interiors sit at zone-centre XZ with y + 5000, which is the same 64 m sector as the surface, so a portal can drop a player directly into a specific crypt room.

**How it works.** Location.Awake (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133505-133515) instantiates a location's interior at `new Vector3(zoneCenter.x, transform.position.y + 5000f, zoneCenter.z)`. Character.InInterior(Vector3) is literally `position.y > 3000f` (:4538-4541). Zones and sectors are XZ-only — ZoneSystem.GetZone (:115741-115746) and GetSectorIndex (:115748-115753) ignore y entirely. So a dungeon interior occupies the SAME sector as the surface above it, and any ZDO placed at (zoneCentreX, ~5030, zoneCentreZ) syncs, saves and pairs exactly like a surface ZDO with no special handling anywhere.

Finding a specific room: DungeonGenerator.Save (:152970-152999) serialises every placed room into the generator's own ZDO as the byte array ZDOVars.s_roomData (:78573) with the layout `int count; { int roomHash; Vector3 worldPos; Quaternion worldRot; } * count`, read back verbatim by Load (:153002-153033). A server mod can BinaryReader that blob and get real, exact interior room coordinates. Resolving the room hash to a name needs DungeonDB.GetRoom (:152489), which is asset data.

Locating the DungeonGenerator ZDO itself is the hard part: ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash (:75390-75407) refuses ByteArray, so you cannot index on s_roomData. Two workable routes: (a) query Type.Int on ZDOVars.s_location (:78501) to enumerate every LocationProxy ZDO in the world with its location hash and position, then spatially query that zone's sector for a ZDO whose prefab carries a DungeonGenerator; or (b) simply place the anchor at the location's own zone centre + 5000 y and accept landing in whatever room the generator put there.

Critically, the dungeon room ZDOs only exist once that zone has been ghost-generated for some peer (ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation :115162, CreateGhostZones :113934-113938). On a fresh server the ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances entry exists from world creation but the s_roomData blob does not. So the mod must either wait for generation or fall back to the LocationInstance surface position.

Departure is free: the crypt door (class Teleport, :143316-143390) is untouched and still works normally. Note that building a portal inside a dungeon requires the client-honoured GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild key (read at Player piece validation :13353) — but a SERVER-created portal ZDO needs no such permission, because nothing validates placement server-side.

**Player experience.** A dungeon-delve server where clearing a crypt permanently unlocks a shortcut back into its deepest room. The player finishes a Sunken Crypt, and a stone portal appears at the surface entrance tagged 'Crypt VII - Deep'. Walking in gives the normal 8-second portal fade, and they materialise in the same torch-lit chamber they fought the boss in, with the crypt door behind them for the walk out. To a vanilla client this is completely ordinary — the interior geometry loads exactly as it does when you walk in through the front door, because the sector is the same one. The server-authored portal inside the crypt cannot be built by hand without the DungeonBuild key, which means it reads unmistakably as a reward rather than something anyone could place.

**Failure modes.**
- The dungeon interior is a Location prefab instantiated by the client's LocationProxy; if that expansion has not happened when the teleport completes, IsAreaReady (:82076) fails and the player waits out the full 15 s, then lands at GetSolidHeight — which may be the SURFACE terrain 5000 m below, dropping them outside the crypt entirely
- s_roomData only exists after that zone has been ghost-generated for some peer, so on a fresh world the room list is empty and the mod has nothing to aim at
- A portal ZDO physically inside dungeon geometry may intersect a wall; the TeleportWorldTrigger collider still fires but the model clips
- Character.InInterior gates several unrelated client behaviours (crypt door NoBossPortals at :143355, building rules); a player standing at y>3000 is 'in an interior' to all of them
- Interior room positions are stored in the generator ZDO, which is owned by whichever client generated it — reading it is safe, but it can be rewritten under you

**Prerequisites.** The Void Anchor (or a real portal ZDO placed at the interior coordinate)

**Citations.** Location.Awake interior at y+5000 — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133505-133515 · Character.InInterior(Vector3) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:4538-4541 · ZoneSystem.GetZone / GetSectorIndex are XZ-only — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115741-115753 · DungeonGenerator.Save — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:152970-152999 (s_roomData write at :152986) · DungeonGenerator.Load — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:153002-153033 · ZDOVars.s_roomData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78573 · ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash rejects ByteArray — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75390-75407 · ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113295 · class Teleport (crypt doors, no ZDO) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143316-143390

- What is the prefab name of the DungeonGenerator component's host object, so it can be found by GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative? IN-GAME: dump prefab names of all ZDOs in a crypt's sector and look for the one carrying s_roomData.

## 131. Ephemeral Event Gates

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Portals the server conjures for the duration of an event and destroys afterwards, with no player ever placing a piece.

**How it works.** Creation (the full five-line recipe, because ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO does not do it for you): `int h = <portal prefab hash>; var z = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, h); z.Persistent = true; z.Type = ZDO.ObjectType.Default; z.Distant = false; z.SetPrefab(h); z.SetRotation(rot); z.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, tag);` CreateNewZDO (:76674-76692) pools a ZDO, sets owner to the server session, and calls AddIfPortal(zdo, prefabHash) — which, because the hash is in Game.PortalPrefabHash, files it in m_portalObjects, removes it from the sector array, and sets DirtyPortalObjects (:77732-77752). It does NOT write the prefab onto the ZDO body and does NOT set Persistent; ZNetView.Awake (:82612-82620) is where vanilla does those, and a hand-built ZDO missing SetPrefab has m_prefab = -1 and will spam 'Missing prefab hash' on every client every frame (:82004-82008).

Portal ZDOs are saved by a special path: GetSaveClonePerChunk (:77621-77632) dumps the WHOLE of m_portalObjects into the ChunkPortal file whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set, with no Persistent filter at all — so a mod-created portal survives restart even if you forgot Persistent. Conversely, AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) explicitly excludes portal-hash ZDOs from normal chunks.

Deletion: ZDOMan.DestroyZDO (:76929-76935) is a silent no-op unless zdo.IsOwner(), so always `z.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` first. It queues into m_destroySendList and SendDestroyed broadcasts the routed DestroyZDO RPC to every peer; each client's HandleDestroyedZDO (:76963-77000) removes it from m_portalObjects, sets DirtyPortalObjects, and ZNetScene.OnZDODestroyed (:82186-82194) destroys the GameObject in front of the player. The ZDOID goes into m_deadZDOs (:76997) so it can never be resurrected by a replayed packet.

Lifecycle: trigger on anything the server can see — a boss key appearing (Harmony postfix on ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd, the BossDefeatWatch pattern), a RandEventSystem event starting, a clock, an admin command on the dedicated server's stdin. Pair the gate with Game.instance.ConnectPortals() called directly (:100589) instead of waiting up to 5 s.

To hide a temporary gate from vanilla's pairer entirely, ZDOMan.GetPortals() (:77643) returns the LIVE m_portalObjects dictionary — removing an entry makes Game.ConnectPortals blind to it while the ZDO stays fully alive for clients. That lets a server hold a hand-wired one-way link with no reconciliation race at all.

**Player experience.** Eikthyr dies. Within a second, a stone portal fades into existence in the middle of the sacrificial circle, already glowing 'connected', tagged 'Stag Road - 20m'. Everyone present sees it appear from nothing — no build effects, no materials, no one placed it. It links to a fixed hub the admins maintain. Twenty minutes later it winks out mid-conversation and the ground is empty again. Nobody can deconstruct it for materials while it exists, nobody can retag it into their own network, and it leaves no trace in the world save once the timer runs out.

**Failure modes.**
- Omitting SetPrefab leaves m_prefab at -1 and every client logs 'Missing prefab hash: -1' 30 times per second while standing near it
- Forgetting SetOwner before DestroyZDO makes the delete a completely silent no-op — the portal stays forever
- Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals (:99903) caches raw ZDO object references across a full 5 s tick; if an ephemeral gate is destroyed inside that window, ZDOPool.Release recycles the object and ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-writes a connection through a stale reference
- If the gate shares a tag with player portals, Game.ConnectPortals will happily pair a player's portal to it and then strand that player when it vanishes
- Creating a portal ZDO with a hash that is not in Game.PortalPrefabHash skips AddIfPortal entirely, so it lands in m_objectsBySector, is excluded from the chunk save by the portal filter (:77572), and disappears on restart with no error

**Prerequisites.** Runtime discovery of Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash / m_portalPrefabs (never hard-code portal_wood)

## 132. The Decoy Gate

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

A portal that reports itself connected and glows, but silently refuses to teleport forever, built by pointing its connection at a ZDOID that does not exist.

**How it works.** The client evaluates 'connected' and 'usable' with two DIFFERENT functions and only one of them is on the hover path.

TeleportWorld.HaveTarget (:143631-143638) returns `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != ZDOID.None` — a pure field test, no lookup. GetHoverText (:143461) picks between $piece_portal_connected and $piece_portal_unconnected from HaveTarget alone, and UpdatePortal (:143496-143501) fires the m_connected EffectList and drives m_hadTarget from it, which Update (:143511-143515) lerps into the model's _EmissionColor toward m_colorTargetfound.

TeleportWorld.TargetFound (:143640-143656) additionally requires `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connectionZDOID) != null`, and when the ZDO is absent it calls ZDOMan.instance.RequestZDO and returns false. Teleport() gate 1 (:143519-143522) is `if (!TargetFound()) return;` — a bare return with NO player.Message.

So: write `portal.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, new ZDOID(someSessionId, someNeverAllocatedId))`. HaveTarget is true (hover says connected, portal glows blue), TargetFound is permanently false (the ZDO never resolves), and walking through does absolutely nothing with zero feedback. The client's RequestZDO goes to the server's RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692), which calls peer.ForceSendZDO(id); AddForceSendZdos (:77263-77281) then finds GetZDO(id) == null and prunes the entry silently. No log, no packet, no cost.

Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 (:100600-100604) WILL tear this down within 5 s because `zDO == null`. Two ways to keep it: (a) re-assert the fake ZDOID every 2 s with SetOwner + SetConnection + ForceSendZDO, which costs one DataRevision bump per rewrite because ZDOExtraData.SetConnection (:74951-74960) no-ops on an unchanged value and phase 1 always changes it back; or (b) cleanly, remove the decoy from the live ZDOMan.GetPortals() dictionary (:77643) so vanilla's pairer never iterates it at all.

A softer decoy variant: point it at a real Void Anchor that the server deliberately never force-sends and that sits in a sector no peer visits. The link is then legitimate and survives reconciliation (given a matching tag and a self-loop), but every client's TargetFound fails until the server chooses to deliver the anchor — a switchable gate with no visible state change.

**Player experience.** A grand stone portal stands at the top of a ruined tower, humming and glowing exactly like a working one, hover text reading 'Portal, tag: THE DEEP ROAD [connected]'. Players walk in. Nothing. No message, no black screen, no bounce-back — they simply walk out the other side of the frame. They try again. They check their inventory for ore. They ask in chat. The portal is, as far as any vanilla client can tell, perfectly healthy and connected to something. Used deliberately this is the best puzzle primitive in the whole toolkit: the gate is 'sealed' in a way that gives the player no error to Google, and the server can make it real later by simply delivering the anchor — at which point the very same portal, unchanged, suddenly works.

**Failure modes.**
- Game.ConnectPortals nulls a dangling connection every 5 s (:100601, zDO == null branch), so the decoy needs either a re-assert loop or removal from the live portal dictionary
- A re-assert loop that fights vanilla generates a DataRevision bump and a ForceSendZDO per cycle to every peer — budget it like Wonderland's StructureUpkeep 256-broadcast cap
- The complete absence of feedback is genuinely indistinguishable from a mod bug; pair every decoy with a PlayerNotify toast or a DamageText Bonus string, or players will file it as broken
- A fabricated ZDOID could theoretically collide with a real future ZDOID from the same session; mint decoy targets from a real ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO that is then destroyed, so the id lands in m_deadZDOs (:76997) and can never be reused
- ZDOID.UserID values are renumbered on world load, so a hand-built fake id must be re-derived after every restart

**Citations.** TeleportWorld.HaveTarget — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143631-143638 · TeleportWorld.TargetFound — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143640-143656 · TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1 silent return — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143519-143522 · TeleportWorld.GetHoverText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143464 · TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal / Update — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143491-143515 · ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77689-77692 · ZDOMan.AddForceSendZdos prunes missing ZDOs — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77263-77281 · Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100594-100606

**Open questions.**
- How often does a vanilla client actually fire RequestZDO for an unresolvable target — every UpdatePortal tick (0.5 s) or only on transit? UpdatePortal calls TargetFound at :143507, so likely 2/s per nearby player. IN-GAME: count RequestZDO packets server-side with a player idling next to a decoy for 60 s.

## 133. The Tag As A Public Broadcast Surface

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

ZDOVars.s_tag is an uncapped, unfiltered, server-writable string that a vanilla client renders live through Localization.Localize — the only in-world text channel a server-only portal mod has.

**How it works.** The write side has no limits whatsoever. ZDO.Set(int, string) performs no ownership check and no validation (:73721). The 10-character cap lives only in TeleportWorld.Interact's call to TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, '$piece_portal_tag', 10) (:143482), which sets m_inputField.characterLimit on the CLIENT UI. CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC in the SERVER build is the single statement `return text;` (:94588-94591), and in the CLIENT build (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94901-94947) it early-returns unless ugcType is ServerName or RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering() — false on Steam. The censored flag from CensorShittyWords.Filter is computed in GetTagInfo (:143568) and then only surfaced when ZNet.m_onlineBackend == PlayFab (:143462). On a Steam dedicated server the raw string is what every player reads.

The render path is the interesting part. GetHoverText (:143453-143463) builds `Localization.instance.Localize('$piece_portal $piece_portal_tag:"' + text + '" [' + text2 + ']' + newline + text3 + ...)` — the tag is CONCATENATED INTO the string BEFORE Localize runs. Three exploitable consequences:
(1) A tag containing a localization token such as $piece_portal_connected or $KEY_Use is resolved by the client in the player's own language and their own keybinds.
(2) A newline character in the tag produces a genuine multi-line hover panel. The tag is a small text box, not a single line.
(3) Rich text: `text.RemoveRichTextTags()` is applied at :143459, and StringExtensionMethods.RemoveRichTextTags (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703) is `Regex.Replace(text, '<[/a-zA-Z0-9= "''#;:()$_-]*?>', '')`. The character class EXCLUDES the less-than sign. Regex.Replace makes a single forward pass and does not re-scan its own output. Therefore the input `<<color=red>color=red>` has no match starting at index 0 (the lazy class cannot consume the second less-than), matches `<color=red>` starting at index 1, and the surviving output is exactly `<color=red>` — which TextMeshPro then renders as real markup. Nested-tag smuggling gives coloured, sized and sprite-tagged portal hover text from a pure ZDO write.

Persistence trap: a tag-only write does NOT dirty the portal chunk. DirtyPortalObjects is set by ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection for ConnectionType.Portal (:73661-73676), by AddIfPortal (:77750) and by HandleDestroyedZDO (:76986) — and by nothing else. ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision goes to SetDirtySector (:73839), and SetDirtyChunks marks a normal chunk that portals are explicitly excluded from (:77572). So every server-side tag rewrite MUST be followed by ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702) or it silently vanishes at the next world save.

**Player experience.** Portals stop being labels and become signage. A hub gate reads, on hover, a three-line panel: 'THE CROSSROADS' in gold, then 'Next rotation in 04:12', then 'Currently open to: Ashlands Foothold'. A quest gate's tag counts down live as the server rewrites it. A contested gate turns red when another faction holds it. During a server event every portal in the world briefly reads the same line. And because the tag is also the pairing key for Game.ConnectPortals, the mod has to be careful: the visible text and the routing key are the same field, so a 'display' tag must either be shared byte-for-byte across a whole network or the mod must own pairing outright.

**Failure modes.**
- s_tag is BOTH the display string and Game.ConnectPortals's equality key (:100601, :100669) — any per-portal display text inside one network is torn down every 5 s unless the mod owns pairing
- A tag-only write is lost at the next save unless ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() is called explicitly
- If a player opens the vanilla tag dialog on a server-written long tag, TextInput.Show assigns the existing text after setting characterLimit = 10 (:61515-61522) — a vanilla client may clamp and save back a truncated tag, destroying the display AND the routing key
- RemoveRichTextTags strips plain markup; only the nested-smuggle form survives, and TMP's tolerance for it is unverified
- A very long tag is re-serialized in full on every ZDO send (ZDOMan.SendZDOs :77062 has no delta encoding), so a 500-character tag on 200 portals is real per-peer bandwidth
- Rewriting a distant portal's tag as a message does not reach a player until they are in that portal's sector (CreateSyncList :77212-77227) unless the mod calls ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerUid, id)

**Prerequisites.** Ownership of Game.ConnectPortals pairing if per-portal display text is wanted

**Citations.** TeleportWorld.GetHoverText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143464 (Localize concatenation at :143463, RemoveRichTextTags at :143459) · TeleportWorld.GetTagInfo — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143556-143570 · TeleportWorld.Interact 10-char cap — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143482; TextInput.RequestText/Show — :61509-61522 · CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC is `return text;` on the server — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:94588-94591; client version assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94901-94947 · StringExtensionMethods.RemoveRichTextTags regex — assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703 · ZDO.Set(int,string) no ownership check — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73721 · ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702-76705 · ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision / SetDirtySector — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73832-73840, 76694-76700 · ZDOVars.s_tag / s_tagauthor — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78617, 78619

## 134. The Adamant Gate — Server-Enforced Indestructible Portals

`CAVEATS` · `CLIENT-HONOURED` · effort: small

Writing a huge ZDOVars.s_health onto a portal makes it survive any vanilla-client damage, and Repair can never undo it.

**How it works.** WearNTear.ApplyDamage (:150387-150409) reads the CURRENT health straight from the ZDO every hit: `float f = m_nview.GetZDO().GetFloat(ZDOVars.s_health, m_health); if (f <= 0) return false; f -= damage; m_nview.GetZDO().Set(ZDOVars.s_health, f); if (f <= 0) Destroy(hitData);` The prefab field m_health (:149248) is only the DEFAULT when the ZDO key is absent. So a single server-side `portalZdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_health, 1e9f)` means a player must land a billion points of damage to break the portal.

The repair path cannot undo it. WearNTear.Repair (:149522-149539) returns false immediately when `GetFloat(s_health, m_health) >= m_health` — an inflated value always satisfies that, so RPC_Repair (:149541-149548), which would reset s_health to m_health, is never invoked. Cosmetics are also safe: WearNTear.Awake computes `m_healthPercentage = Mathf.Clamp01(num / m_health)` (:149439), which clamps to 1, so the piece renders as pristine rather than glitching.

ZDO.Set performs no ownership check at any type (the okForNotOwner parameter at :73648-73654 is accepted and ignored), so the write lands immediately and propagates by DataRevision. A nearby owning client can clobber it with a higher-revision push (ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77103-77132 replaces the whole blob), so re-assert on a slow tick — the write is idempotent and free when unchanged, because BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue returns false on an equal value and ZDO.Set then skips IncreaseDataRevision.

The complementary half is deconstruction, which ignores health entirely. Player.RemovePiece (:12364-12378) refuses outright when `!piece.m_canBeRemoved`, silently returning false with no message. m_canBeRemoved is a `public bool` on Piece (:136171) — exactly the shape ZNetView.LoadFields can override (see 'Field Injection'). Writing `HasFields`, `HasFieldsPiece` and `Piece.m_canBeRemoved = false` onto the portal ZDO means a vanilla client's hammer refuses to remove it.

Both halves together give a portal that cannot be smashed and cannot be deconstructed by an unmodified client, with no client install. It is still NOT tamper-proof against a modified client — a hostile client can write s_health directly through RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77139, zero validation) or broadcast a forged DestroyZDO (RPC_DestroyZDO :76953, ungated on receive). That is the honest ceiling: this stops griefing, not cheating.

**Player experience.** The public hub portals at spawn are simply unbreakable. A new player swings a hammer at one out of curiosity and the deconstruct prompt does nothing at all — no 'private zone' message, no refusal text, the hammer just declines. A raider who decides to cut the network drops a boulder on the gate and it takes a hit sound and a chip of effect and nothing else. Admins can still remove it with the mod's own command. Critically the portal still looks and behaves completely normally — full health bar, normal wear model, normal glow — so it reads as 'this is a server fixture', not as a bug.

**Failure modes.**
- A modded client can write s_health or forge a DestroyZDO packet; RPC_ZDOData (:77103-77132) and RPC_DestroyZDO (:76953) validate nothing
- LoadFields only runs inside ZNetView.Awake (:82631), so a m_canBeRemoved change reaches a player only after that portal is next created in their scene — they must leave and return to the area
- The field-injection half depends on the portal prefab actually carrying a Piece component; that is asset data
- Terrain destruction, fire spread and a fully destroyed supporting structure can still orphan a portal even if the portal itself is immortal
- A per-hit re-assert loop would fight the owning client's revision; use a slow idempotent re-assert (the write is free when unchanged, BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue at assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321)
- WearNTear.Destroy (:150427-150477) writes s_health = 0 directly, so an already-destroyed portal cannot be revived by re-inflating health

**Prerequisites.** Field Injection Through ZNetView.LoadFields (for the m_canBeRemoved half)

## 135. Field Injection Through ZNetView.LoadFields

`CAVEATS` · `CLIENT-HONOURED` · effort: medium

Vanilla reflects every public field of every component on an instantiated prefab out of the ZDO — which makes per-portal m_allowAllItems, m_exitDistance and m_activationRange genuinely achievable on a 100 percent vanilla client.

**How it works.** ZNetView.LoadFields (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82669-82739, byte-identical in the client at :82898) is called as the last step of ZNetView.Awake (:82631), immediately before AddInstance. It is a reflection override mechanism baked into vanilla for the modding-adjacent 'spawn a variant' use case, and it is entirely ZDO-driven:

1. `if (!zdo.GetBool('HasFields')) return;` — one gate key on the whole object.
2. `gameObject.GetComponentsInChildren(m_tempComponents)` over List<MonoBehaviour> (so self plus active children).
3. Per component, `if (!zdo.GetBool('HasFields' + typeName)) continue;`
4. For each `BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.Public` field, look up the ZDO key `typeName + '.' + fieldName` and, if present, SetValue. Supported types are exactly int, float, bool, Vector3, string, GameObject (resolved by prefab name) and ItemDrop (resolved by prefab name). Color, enum and arrays are NOT supported.

Applied to a portal, the reachable knobs are: TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems (bool, :143429) — a genuine PER-PORTAL ore policy, read by Teleport at :143533 and by UpdatePortal's glow at :143505; TeleportWorld.m_exitDistance (float, :143413) — per-portal arrival offset, used at :143545; TeleportWorld.m_activationRange (float, :143411); TeleportWorld.m_hoverOffset (float, :143431); Piece.m_canBeRemoved (bool, :136171); Piece.m_comfort (int, :136120 region); Piece.m_allowedInDungeons (bool); WearNTear.m_health (float, :149248); WearNTear.m_burnable, m_ashDamageImmune, m_noRoofWear, m_noSupportWear, m_supports, m_triggerPrivateArea (bools, :149201-149258 region).

Server-side write for an ore-permissive gate: `z.Set('HasFields'.GetStableHashCode(), true); z.Set('HasFieldsTeleportWorld'.GetStableHashCode(), true); z.Set('TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems'.GetStableHashCode(), true); ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals();` Booleans are stored as ints by ZDO.GetBool/Set (:73937-73940), which is what GetBool reads back, so this is a plain ZDO int write.

This directly REFUTES the common 'there are no per-portal knobs server-side' conclusion. The correct statement is: the fields are not RPC'd or ZDO-backed by TeleportWorld itself, but ZNetView has a generic override channel underneath them and the server owns the ZDO. It is client-honoured (a modified client can ignore it), on exactly the same footing as vanilla's own boss gating.

The one hard limitation is timing: LoadFields runs only at instantiation. Flipping the field on a portal a player is already standing next to does nothing until that object is destroyed and recreated in their scene — i.e. they walk about 100 m away (ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea, :82298-82320) and come back, or relog. Note also that TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems cannot lift the Inventory.IsTeleportable toolTier >= 1000 gate, which is checked BEFORE allowAllItems (:68862-68872).

**Player experience.** Two portals side by side at the mining outpost, both stone, both tagged. One is labelled 'ORE ROAD - heavy cargo' and the other 'PASSENGER'. A player loaded with iron walks into the ore gate and it works; the same player walking into the passenger gate gets the normal '$msg_noteleport'. Nothing about the ore gate looks unusual — its ready-glow correctly lights up for a player carrying metal, because UpdatePortal reads the same injected field. The catch a server operator has to explain: after an admin flips a gate's policy, players standing beside it will not see the change until they wander away and come back. In practice the mod flips policy on portals nobody is near, or accepts one relog of latency.

**Failure modes.**
- LoadFields fires only in ZNetView.Awake (:82631) — a live change never reaches an already-instantiated portal until the client destroys and recreates it (~100 m away and back, or a relog)
- Client-honoured only: a modified client simply does not apply the override
- Color fields (m_colorUnconnected, m_colorTargetfound) are NOT supported by LoadFields (:82693-82736) — per-portal colour is ruled out through this route
- GlobalKeys.TeleportAll and m_allowAllItems both sit AFTER the m_toolTier >= 1000 rejection in Inventory.IsTeleportable (:68862-68868); some items can never be carried through
- A wrong key spelling silently does nothing — there is no error path in LoadFields
- HasFields keys are plain ZDO ints and count against the per-ZDO per-type item budget; ZPackage.WriteNumItems corrupts above 32767 (:83237-83246) and ZDODataHelper warns above 100 (:74662-74676)
- A stale HasFieldsTeleportWorld key applies to every TeleportWorld component found in children if a modded prefab has more than one

**Citations.** ZNetView.LoadFields — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82669-82739; call site ZNetView.Awake :82631 · TeleportWorld public fields — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143411-143431 · TeleportWorld.Teleport reads m_allowAllItems — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143533; m_exitDistance at :143545 · TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal reads m_allowAllItems — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143505 · Inventory.IsTeleportable toolTier gate before allowAllItems — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:68860-68881 · Piece.m_canBeRemoved — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:136171 · WearNTear public fields — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:149201-149258 · ZDO.GetBool via GetInt — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73937-73940 · ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82298-82320

## 136. Portal As Trigger, RPC As Transport

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium-large

Abandon the connection field entirely: poll character ZDO positions near a portal and force-teleport with RPC_TeleportPlayer — which breaks the one-destination-per-ZDO ceiling and gives true multi-destination hubs.

**How it works.** A ZDO holds at most ONE connection — ZDOExtraData.s_connections is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` and ZDOConnection carries one readonly type and one readonly target (:74794, :75524-75534). Simultaneous multi-destination hubs are therefore structurally impossible through the vanilla mechanism. This option sidesteps it completely.

Leave the portal's Portal connection at ZDOID.None (or pointed anywhere). The portal never teleports anyone — TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1 returns silently (:143519). Instead, the server polls: `foreach (peer in ZNet.instance.GetPeers()) { var z = ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID); ... }` at 0.2-0.4 s, comparing z.GetPosition() against every entry of ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals() (:77643, the live zero-alloc dictionary) within about 3-4 m. Position freshness is good: the owning client's ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync writes zdo.SetPosition every physics tick (:87527-87540) and ZDOMan services one peer per Update on a 0.05 s timer (:76843-76861), so character positions are 50-100 ms stale regardless of distance.

On a hit, send `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, 'RPC_TeleportPlayer', pos, rot, true)`. The handler is registered on every vanilla client in Chat.Awake (:41627) and its entire body is `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport);` — no sender check, no admin check, no key check, no item check (:41962-41968). A second, ZDO-scoped path exists: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, 'RPC_TeleportTo', pos, rot, true)`, handled by Character.RPC_TeleportTo (:4126-4132), registered for every Character in Character.Awake (:886) and owner-gated so it cannot be misdirected.

What this buys: the DESTINATION is chosen by the server at the moment of transit, per player, per condition. A hub can route by player identity (character ZDO ZDOVars.s_playerID), by the emote they last performed (ZDOVars.s_emote / s_emoteID), by a map ping they sent (Chat.SendPing broadcasts 'ChatMessage' to peer 0 with the clicked world Vector3), by time of day, by a rotation counter, or round-robin. It also bypasses vanilla's ore check entirely, which is a design decision the operator must make consciously.

Mandatory pre-checks, all readable from the character ZDO: skip if GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead) (Player.UpdateTeleport runs only inside the !IsDead() branch of FixedUpdate at :10213/:10226, so a teleport sent to a dead player latches m_teleporting true and never executes); skip if GetBool(ZDOVars.s_inBed) (Player.UpdateAttach at :10217 runs BEFORE UpdateTeleport at :10226 and re-snaps to the attach point every tick, and AttachStop early-returns while sleeping at :15892). And rate-limit per player to at least 12 s: Player.TeleportTo refuses while IsTeleporting() or while m_teleportCooldown < 2f (:15309-15316), and m_teleportCooldown is zeroed every tick of a teleport (:15336), so the dead window is the whole 8+ s teleport plus 2 s.

**Player experience.** A single great archway at spawn labelled 'THE WAYGATE'. Walking into it does not take you to a fixed partner. Before stepping through you open your map and middle-click a location you have discovered; that ping goes to the server. You walk into the arch, and after the usual black screen you are standing at the spot you marked. If you did not ping anything, it takes you to the destination you used last. One archway, unlimited destinations, on a completely unmodified client, with the standard portal fade and no visual tell that anything unusual happened. The failure mode players will notice: if you step in twice within about twelve seconds, the second attempt does nothing at all and gives no message.

**Failure modes.**
- Every failure is silent and one-directional: TeleportTo returns false (:15309, :15313), both RPC handlers discard the return (:41966, :4130), and no reply is ever sent — the server's only confirmation is watching the character ZDO position change roughly 2 s later
- The real cooldown is not 2 s after the RPC; m_teleportCooldown is zeroed every tick WHILE teleporting (:15336), so the refusal window spans the entire teleport plus 2 s, at least 10-12 s for distantTeleport
- A dead player latches: the teleport is accepted, m_teleporting goes true, and UpdateTeleport never runs (:10213/:10226). Check ZDOVars.s_dead first
- An attached or sleeping player ping-pongs between the attach point and the target every tick because UpdateAttach runs first (:10217, :15818-15836); check ZDOVars.s_inBed first
- Position polling at 0.2-0.4 s can miss a fast player; a 4 m radius at 5 m/s and 0.5 s sampling is about the floor
- This bypasses NoPortals, NoBossPortals, PrivateArea and the ore check completely — every rule the operator wants must be re-implemented in the mod
- RPC_TeleportPlayer is not a privileged channel: vanilla's own client-side `recall` command sends it peer-to-peer (:44548-44556) and RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID is a self-report (:83487-83495), so shipping this feature obliges the mod to also harden ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC
- With distantTeleport true the player is invulnerable and input-locked for ~8 s (Player.CanMove at :14423-14428, damage suppression at :2425/:2429/:2582) — abusable as a stun if triggered by another player

**Prerequisites.** A per-player destination selector (emote signal, map ping, item stand, or chest content)

## 137. Portals As A Data Store

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

Portal ZDOs are the only always-resident, always-saved, distance-independent ZDO collection in the game — and they take arbitrary mod-private keys for free.

**How it works.** Portals have four properties no other ZDO family has. (1) They live in their own dictionary ZDOMan.m_portalObjects (:76039) and are removed from the sector array by AddIfPortal (:77750), so they are never unloaded and never released — ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS only reassigns ownership (:76872-76924) and FlushClientObjects is client-only. (2) They are enumerable world-wide for free with ZDOMan.GetPortalList() (:77648) with zero bookkeeping and no prefab-name guess. (3) They save to a dedicated ChunkPortal file (ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal, :113180), written wholesale with NO Persistent filter whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set (:77621-77632). (4) They are loaded straight into m_portalObjects at world load, bypassing FilterZDO entirely (:76474-76483).

A ZDO's extra data is seven independent int-keyed dictionaries — float, Vector3, Quaternion, int, long, string, byte[] (ZDOExtraData s_floats ... s_byteArrays, :74757-74771). Keys are arbitrary ints; vanilla just uses name.GetStableHashCode(). So a mod can hang whatever it likes on a portal: a network id, a rotation index, a cooldown timestamp, an owning faction, a toll price, a puzzle state, an ordered route list serialized into one byte array. It round-trips through both the network (ZDO.Serialize :74112-74174) and the save with no work.

The correct write discipline: ZDO.Set has no ownership check on any overload (:73601-73727), so write freely; but ALWAYS follow with ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702), because only ConnectionType.Portal SetConnection, AddIfPortal and HandleDestroyedZDO set DirtyPortalObjects — a plain field write goes through IncreaseDataRevision to SetDirtySector (:73839), which dirties a normal chunk that portals are explicitly excluded from (:77572). Without SetDirtyPortals the whole portal file is skipped and every portal reverts to its last-dirtied state.

Two hard budgets. ZPackage.WriteNumItems (:83237-83246) encodes a per-ZDO per-type item count in one byte below 128 and two bytes up to 32767 — above that the stream corrupts; ZDODataHelper.WriteToDisk logs a warning above 100 items of a single type (:74662-74676). And ZDOMan.SendZDOs (:77053-77062) re-serializes the ENTIRE ZDO on every send with no delta encoding, under a 10240-byte per-peer queue cap (:77010-77016). So: a handful of scalar keys plus one byte array, never two hundred int keys.

One global landmine: ZDOExtraData.s_sessionOnly is a GLOBAL hash set (:74776) seeded from the 16 entries of ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes (:78689-78693) and from anything ever passed to AddSessionHash. Any key in it is stripped from the save for EVERY ZDO in the world. Never reuse s_support, s_inUse, s_alert, s_velHash and friends for portal metadata.

**Player experience.** Invisible to players — this is infrastructure. What they see downstream is that the network remembers: the hub they set to 'Ashlands' is still pointed at Ashlands after a server restart, a gate they unlocked stays unlocked, a toll they paid stays paid, and the rotation schedule picks up exactly where it left off rather than resetting. Nothing in the world save is a separate mod file that can drift out of sync with the world; the state travels with the portals, which means it also travels with world backups and world copies.

**Failure modes.**
- A field write without ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() is silently lost at the next world save — the single most likely bug in the whole mod
- ZDOIDs are renumbered on every world load (ZDO.Load sets m_uid via ZDOID.SetID), so a portal's identity must be derived from position, tag, or a mod-written key — never from its ZDOID
- Reusing any of the 16 ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes strips that key from the save for every ZDO in the world, not just portals
- More than 100 keys of one type on one ZDO logs a warning; more than 32767 corrupts the wire stream
- Every extra byte is re-sent in full on every ZDO sync to every nearby peer (no delta encoding), so a large byte array on a hub portal is real recurring bandwidth
- A nearby owning client can clobber the whole ZDO with a higher-revision push (RPC_ZDOData :77103-77132) — conflict resolution is whole-ZDO, not per-field

**Citations.** ZDOMan.m_portalObjects — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76039; AddIfPortal :77732-77752 · ZDOMan.GetPortalList — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77648-77656 · ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk portal branch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77621-77632 · ZDOMan.LoadChunks portal branch bypasses FilterZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76474-76483 · ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113180 · ZDOExtraData seven type dictionaries — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74757-74771 · ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702-76705 · ZDOMan.SetDirtySector — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76694-76700; AddObjectsPerChunk portal exclusion :77572 · ZPackage.WriteNumItems — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83237-83246; ZDODataHelper.WriteToDisk warning :74662-74676 · ZDOMan.SendZDOs full re-serialize and queue cap — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77008-77074 · ZDOExtraData.s_sessionOnly — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74776, seeded at :74814-74825; ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes :78689-78693

## 138. Non-Portals As Portals — Extending Game.PortalPrefabHash At Runtime

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

PortalPrefabHash is a mutable List<int> behind a private setter, so an arbitrary prefab can be enrolled into the portal registry, the portal save chunk and vanilla's own pairing.

**How it works.** Game.PortalPrefabHash is declared `public List<int> PortalPrefabHash { get; private set; }` (:100021) and populated in Game.Awake from the Inspector list m_portalPrefabs (:100027-100032). The SETTER is private but the LIST OBJECT is not — `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Add(someHash)` is a legal, no-reflection mutation of live game state.

Everything portal-specific keys off membership in that list, in four places: ZDOMan.AddIfPortal (:77734) decides whether a new ZDO is filed in m_portalObjects and removed from the sector array; ZDO.SetSector (:73754) early-returns, freezing the sector key; ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) excludes it from normal chunk saves; and GetSaveClonePerChunk (:77621) includes it in ChunkPortal.

Adding a hash makes any FUTURE ZDO of that prefab a portal for all four purposes, and makes it appear in ZDOMan.GetPortalList() and therefore in Game.ConnectPortals's tag-pairing loop (:100592-100622). It does NOT retroactively re-file existing ZDOs — AddIfPortal only runs from CreateNewZDO (:76689) and from the RPC_ZDOData deserialize loop (:77132), so already-loaded instances of that prefab stay in the sector array until they are destroyed and recreated. Conversely, `.Remove(hash)` does not un-register already-tracked ZDOs from m_portalObjects.

The DANGEROUS half is the mirror image: removing a portal hash, or adding a hash for a prefab that already has thousands of instances in the world, changes where those ZDOs are saved. Adding a common prefab hash means every new instance goes into the single global ChunkPortal file, which is written in full whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set — a pathological save-size and save-time regression.

The genuinely useful applications are narrow and deliberate: (a) enrolling a modded portal piece from another server mod so vanilla's own pairing handles it for free; (b) enrolling a rare marker prefab so that mod-created network anchors get the always-resident, always-saved, distance-independent treatment portals get; (c) in reverse, NOT enrolling an anchor so it is invisible to vanilla's pairer while still being a legal teleport destination (see The Void Anchor).

The converse question — can a portal be made into a non-portal — is effectively no: removing the hash after ZDOs exist leaves them stranded in m_portalObjects with a frozen sector key and no path back into the sector array, because ZDO.SetSector for a ZDO whose current prefab is no longer in the list would then try to AddToSector but the ZDO was already RemoveFromSector'd, and nothing re-triggers it.

**Player experience.** Nothing directly visible. What players notice is that a modded portal piece from a different mod suddenly behaves exactly like a vanilla one — it pairs by tag, it survives restarts, it shows up in the server's portal census and its Discord reports — with no per-mod integration code. And, in the other direction, that admin waypoints the server maintains never show up in anyone's portal list and cannot be accidentally paired to by a player who happens to pick the same tag.

**Failure modes.**
- Adding a hash does not retroactively move existing ZDOs into m_portalObjects — only ZDOs created or received afterwards (AddIfPortal call sites :76689 and :77132)
- Removing a hash strands already-tracked ZDOs in m_portalObjects permanently and they are never reachable from the sector array again
- Enrolling a common prefab dumps every new instance into the one global ChunkPortal file, which is rewritten in full on every dirty save — a real save-size and save-time regression
- Portal-hash ZDOs are exempt from ZDO.SetSector (:73752), so an enrolled prefab that MOVES (anything with a Rigidbody) silently stops syncing to clients at its new location
- Load order matters: PortalPrefabHash is filled in Game.Awake (:100027), so the mutation must happen after that and before any relevant ZDO is created or received
- Another mod doing the same thing will collide; the list has no ownership model

**Prerequisites.** Runtime enumeration of Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash

**Citations.** Game.PortalPrefabHash property — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100021; populated in Game.Awake :100027-100032; m_portalPrefabs field :99828 · ZDOMan.AddIfPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77732-77752 (membership test :77734) · ZDO.SetSector portal early-return — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73752-73757 · ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk portal exclusion — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77572 · ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77621-77632 · ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO AddIfPortal call — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76689 · Game.ConnectPortals iterates GetPortalList — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100592

## 139. The Connection Field Beyond Portals

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

An honest map of the other ConnectionType values, what abusing them buys and costs, including the one-connection-per-ZDO ceiling and a latent creature-spawner suppression trick.

**How it works.** ConnectionType is a [Flags] byte enum with None=0, Portal=1, SyncTransform=2, Spawned=3, Target=0x10 (:74747-74754). Note Portal, SyncTransform and Spawned are NOT independent bits — 1, 2 and 3 overlap, so Spawned is bitwise Portal|SyncTransform. Only Target is a real flag. ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID (:75094-75102) requires EXACT type equality, which is what keeps these from cross-matching.

A ZDO holds exactly one connection (s_connections is Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>, one readonly type and one readonly target, :74794, :75524-75534). Consequences:
- Writing Portal onto a player's character ZDO destroys their SyncTransform ship-parent link (ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync at :87548 writes it).
- Writing Portal onto a CreatureSpawner's ZDO destroys its Spawned link.
- A portal can never simultaneously be a Portal endpoint and a SyncTransform child, so a portal physically parented to a moving ship is structurally impossible.
- Writing Portal|Target (0x10 | 1 = 0x11) onto a live portal makes GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) return None, so vanilla treats it as unconnected and re-pairs it. The Target bit belongs only to the save-hash representation.

SyncTransform (:87542-87571) is written by the RIDER's client when standing on a Rigidbody with a ZNetView, alongside ZDOVars.s_relPosHash, s_relRotHash and s_attachJointHash. It is a latch, written only when the parent changes (:87546). Reading it server-side is the documented way to know a player is on a ship — though ShipAttachment's ZDOVars.s_user read on the Ship's own ZDO (written by ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl :141332) is stronger because it has no Inspector dependency. There is also a genuine vanilla bug worth not building on: OwnerSync writes relative velocity to ZDOVars.s_velHash while SyncPosition reads s_velRelHash (:87561 vs :87647), so velRel is never written by anything.

Spawned (:5649-5656, :5820) is CreatureSpawner's link to the creature it made. `SpawnedCreatureStillExists(connectionZDOID)` plus `m_respawnTimeMinuts <= 0f` means a spawner whose Spawned connection points at ANY still-resident ZDO never spawns again. Writing `spawnerZdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Spawned, somePermanentPortalZdoId)` therefore permanently silences a fixed creature spawner from the server — an off-label but real world-governance primitive, and a reason a portal mod must be careful never to write a Portal connection onto a non-portal ZDO it did not create.

The save-time collapse is the hard ceiling on all of it: ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) gives the source ZDO {type, h} and then OVERWRITES the target's slot with {type|Target, h}. With one slot per ZDO, the disk format can express only a pairwise perfect matching. Rings lose links, one-way links come back bidirectional via ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77879-77885), and self-loops are erased outright (:75472-75475, target != None so the source slot is immediately overwritten).

**Player experience.** Indirectly visible as topology that vanilla could not produce: a one-way drop gate that only works in one direction, a ring of six portals where each leads to the next rather than to a random partner, a fan-in where four remote outposts all exit at one hub. All of it holds at runtime because Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 never checks reciprocity (:100601 tests only that the partner resolves, shares the tag, and is itself non-None). All of it quietly degenerates after a server restart into ordinary random pairs unless the mod re-asserts it on world load — which players experience as 'the network scrambled overnight' if the mod forgets.

**Failure modes.**
- Non-pairwise topologies are runtime-only. Rings above 2, one-way links and self-loops do not survive RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) — they must be re-asserted after every world load
- Writing any connection type onto a ZDO that already has one destroys the old one silently; ZDOExtraData.SetConnection just replaces (:74951-74960)
- ZDO.UpdateConnection (:74962-74976) writes nothing at all when no entry exists — it can never CREATE a link, only overwrite one. TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag uses it (:143595), which is why retagging a never-connected portal is a no-op on the connection field
- Writing Portal|Target onto a live portal makes vanilla read it as unconnected and re-pair it
- Suppressing a CreatureSpawner via a Spawned connection is off-label and will confuse any other world-governance mod inspecting spawner state
- GetAllConnectionZDOIDs(ConnectionType) (:75414-75427) reads s_connectionsHashData — the SAVE-time table — not the live s_connections, so it is empty at steady state. Use the parameterless overload (:75409) or iterate GetPortalList()

**Prerequisites.** Ownership of Game.ConnectPortals, or a world-load re-assert pass

## 140. Self-Organising Networks From Player Behaviour

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium-large

Rewire the world's portal topology from what players actually do — transit counts, dwell time, build ownership — using data the server can already see for free.

**How it works.** Every input this needs is already server-readable with no client install.

Usage: PositionWatch-style sampling of character ZDO positions (Wonderland Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:31, IsPortalTransit at :148) already detects a portal transit by checking whether two consecutive position samples both sit within about 40 m of some entry in ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals(), and additionally follows one endpoint's GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal) to see whether its partner is near the other endpoint. It was built in Wonderland v0.6.4 precisely because portal transits were tripping a speed check at roughly 110 m/s over a 3 s window. Invert its sense and it is a transit counter.

Ownership: every player-placed piece carries ZDOVars.s_creator (:78393), a PlayerProfile UID written by Piece.SetCreator (:136415-136424) from Player.PlacePiece (:12514-12517), plus s_creatorIndex indexing ZNet.World.m_playerHistory (:112396), which the server persists in the .fwl and maintains from socket-verified PlatformUserIDs (ZNet.UpdatePlayerHistory :81436-81461). So 'who built this portal' is durable, offline-readable and account-level.

Dwell and adjacency: ConnectedCharacters.All() gives (peer, character ZDO) pairs; character positions are refreshed every physics tick by the owner's ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync (:87527-87540). Count time spent within a radius of each portal.

The rewiring step is then the standard write triad, applied on a slow tick (30-120 s, not per transit): `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, targetId); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);` — literally what Game.SetConnection does at :100643-100645. Because TeleportWorld.Teleport re-reads GetConnectionZDOID at the instant of transit (:143539) and never caches, a rewire takes effect on the very next walk-through with no client refresh.

The cleanest way to own the decision without owning the whole algorithm is a Harmony POSTFIX on the private `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(List<ZDO>, ZDO, string)` (:100664-100679) that overwrites __result — swapping UnityEngine.Random.Range for nearest / most-used / least-used / admin-designated, while leaving vanilla's two-phase commit, ownership handling and logging completely intact. For full control, prefix Game.ConnectPortals (:100589) and return false.

Three structural facts shape what topologies are worth aiming for. Phase 1 never checks reciprocity, so rings and fan-in are stable at runtime. Three or more portals on one tag PERMANENTLY strand exactly one member (the surviving pair keeps re-confirming itself), which is a free 'broken network' detector for an admin report. And which member gets stranded depends on dictionary bucket order and is not stable across restarts, so no admin-facing feature may assume a stable orphan identity.

**Player experience.** The network learns. A player builds a portal at a new outpost and tags it with the same name as their base gate — and instead of the usual coin-flip about which of their three same-named portals it links to, it links to the one they actually use most. Over a week the hub at spawn rotates its outbound link toward whichever frontier the server's population is currently pushing into, and the hover text says so: 'THE CROSSROADS - currently: Mistlands Camp (41 crossings this week)'. A long-abandoned outpost quietly falls out of the rotation. Nobody configured any of it, and nobody installed anything.

**Failure modes.**
- Transit detection is sampled, not eventful — a 3 s sample can miss a transit and a 0.25 s sample costs a per-player allocation and a full portal-dictionary walk each tick
- Three or more same-tag portals permanently strand one member and the victim changes across restarts (dictionary bucket order, ZDOMan.GetPortalList :77648)
- A rewire on a portal an online player currently owns is deferred by Game.SetConnection over RPC_SetConnection (:100649) and the server's local copy still reads the old value that tick — phase 2 then skips it, so a retag near a player takes 2+ ticks
- ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924) hands portal ownership to any peer within roughly 96-112 m every 2 s, so the mod's ownership claim is transient; guard with a ZDO.SetOwner Harmony prefix (the Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine ZdoSetOwnerPatch pattern)
- Never cache ZDO object references across ticks — ZDOPool.Release recycles them and Game's own m_currentlyConnectingPortals violates this; cache ZDOIDs and re-resolve
- A mass rewrite spikes every peer; budget routed broadcasts per sweep (Wonderland StructureUpkeep uses 256)
- Rewiring under a player standing inside a portal's trigger volume does not re-trigger — TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143673) fires on ENTER only; they must step out and back in

**Prerequisites.** Portals As A Data Store (to persist usage counters); The Tag As A Public Broadcast Surface (to surface the result)

**Citations.** Game.ConnectPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589-100627 · Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100664-100679 · Game.SetConnection write triad — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100637-100651 · TeleportWorld.Teleport re-reads the connection at transit — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143539 · TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter fires on enter only — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143673-143681 · Piece.SetCreator / ZDOVars.s_creator — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:136415-136424, 78393 · ZNet.UpdatePlayerHistory — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81436-81461; World.m_playerHistory :112396 · ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76901-76924 · ZDOMan.GetPortals / GetPortalList — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77643-77656 · Wonderland PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:148

## 141. Portal-Driven Map Surfaces

`CAVEATS` · `CLIENT-HONOURED` · effort: medium

Honest inventory of what a server can put on a vanilla client's map because of a portal — three real channels, none of them portal-specific, and one hard limitation.

**How it works.** Vanilla shows portal tags NOWHERE on the map; TeleportWorld exposes them only through GetHoverText (:143453-143463). So there is no portal pin to influence. What exists are three general server-to-client map channels, all usable in reaction to portal events.

(1) A NAMED, SAVED pin: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, 'RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse', pinName, (int)Minimap.PinType, pos, showMap)`. Game.Start registers this handler on EVERY peer, outside the IsServer block (:100068), and the client body (:100823-100831) calls Minimap.DiscoverLocation, which AddPin(..., save: true) and shows a '$msg_pin_added' toast, optionally centring the map. This is Wonderland's FirstSpawnGrant pattern (Subsystems/WorldGovernor/FirstSpawnGrant.cs:253-263). The hard catch: save:true means the pin lands PERMANENTLY in that player's own profile and there is NO removal RPC. Re-pushing after a rename creates a second pin; HaveSimilarPin only suppresses an identical name+type within 1 m. So this is a one-shot discovery push, not a live-synced pin set.

(2) An ICON-ONLY overlay the server fully owns: ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons (:113581-113593) packs a (Vector3, string) list into a ZPackage and sends the 'LocationIcons' routed RPC; the client's RPC_LocationIcons (:113595-113607) CLEARS and replaces its whole m_locationIcons dictionary, and Minimap.UpdateLocationPins rebuilds pins from it every 5 s. The server therefore controls the entire location-icon pin set on every vanilla client, and can add or remove entries at will. Limits: no label text at all, and only names that resolve to a sprite in the client's compiled Minimap.m_locationIcons render — an invented name is silently dropped. Also note this same channel is the authority for where a vanilla client respawns, via the Game.m_StartLocation ('StartTemple') entry read by Game.FindSpawnPoint.

(3) A TEMPORARY labelled pin plus in-world text plus a chat line, from one RPC: a fabricated 'ChatMessage' (Chat.Awake registration :41626; Chat.RPC_ChatMessage :41970-41973; OnNewChatMessage :41775-41816). Type 2 (Shout) renders a chat line, yellow uppercase floating world text, and an animated map pin labelled '<UserInfo.Name>: <TEXT>' for m_worldTextTTL = 5 s. Type 3 (Ping) gives no chat line and forces the world text to 'PING'. UserInfo.Name is entirely server-chosen, so 'The Waygate' can be the speaker. Less-than and greater-than are replaced with spaces in OnNewChatMessage (:41795-41796), so no markup.

Combined, a portal event can: permanently pin a newly discovered destination (once), keep a live icon-only overlay of every active gate, and flash a 5-second labelled pin plus a floating caption at the moment a hub rotates.

**Player experience.** A player uses a hub gate for the first time this week. As the black screen clears, a toast reads 'Pin added: Ashlands Foothold' and a marker is now permanently on their map at the place they just arrived. Meanwhile a set of small icons has appeared across the map wherever the server currently maintains an open public gate — no names, just markers, updating every five seconds as gates open and close. And at the moment the hub rotates, everyone within range sees 'THE WAYGATE: NOW OPEN TO MISTLANDS CAMP' briefly appear in chat, in the air above the arch, and as a labelled pin on the map for five seconds. None of it required a client install; all of it is vanilla's own discovery and shout machinery.

**Failure modes.**
- RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse pins are save:true and there is NO removal RPC — a demolished portal's pin stays on the player's map forever
- A renamed destination produces a SECOND permanent pin; HaveSimilarPin matches on name AND type AND within 1 m
- LocationIcons pins carry no name and render only for names present in the client's compiled Minimap.m_locationIcons sprite list — invented names are dropped with no error
- LocationIcons is a full replace, not a delta, and it is also what tells a vanilla client where StartTemple is (Game.FindSpawnPoint) — overwriting the set carelessly can move where players respawn
- A fabricated Shout or Ping renders its map pin only if Chat.AddInworldText runs, which is skipped when Minimap.m_mode is None AND the position is beyond m_nomapPingDistance (50 m) — i.e. in nomap worlds or with the HUD hidden
- Minimap.AddPin forces any PinType outside the visible range to Icon3, so exotic types silently collapse
- Map pings are public: Chat.SendPing broadcasts to peer 0 (:42058-42068), so a ping-driven feature is a visible, shared, spammable gesture

**Prerequisites.** Portal As Trigger, RPC As Transport (for arrival-time pin pushes)

**Citations.** TeleportWorld.GetHoverText is the only tag surface — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143464 · Game.Start RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse registration (all peers) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100068; handler :100823-100831 · Minimap.DiscoverLocation / AddPin(save:true) / HaveSimilarPin — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:58394-58421, 58375-58406, 58363-58374 · ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons / RPC_LocationIcons — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113581-113607 · ZoneSystem.OnNewPeer pushes icons on join — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113607-113616 · Chat.Awake ChatMessage registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41626; Chat.OnNewChatMessage / AddInworldText :41775-41913 · Chat.SendPing — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:42058-42068 · Wonderland FirstSpawnGrant map pin — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/FirstSpawnGrant.cs:253-263

## 142. The Tag Is Also The Lock — Puzzle And Progression Gates

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium-large

A composite: use the tag, the connection, global keys and the Void Anchor together to build gates that open and close on server-side conditions with no client install.

**How it works.** Four independent levers compose into real puzzle mechanics.

HARD LOCK (server-enforced): null the connection. `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, ZDOID.None); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);` TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1 (:143519) is the ONLY genuinely server-enforced gate of the four, because it reads the ZDO connection the server owns. Vanilla's pairer will re-pair it within 5 s if another same-tag unconnected portal exists, so a locked gate must either be alone on its tag or the mod must own pairing.

SOFT LOCK (silent): the Decoy Gate — connection pointed at an unresolvable ZDOID. Hover still reads connected, glow still lights, transit silently does nothing. This is the better puzzle primitive because it gives the player no error to search for.

GLOBAL LOCK (client-honoured, world-wide): `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey('noportals')` reaches every connected vanilla client within one network frame — SetGlobalKey (:115943-115946) routes to the server's own handler synchronously, RPC_SetGlobalKey (:116022-116029) adds and then SendGlobalKeys(0L) (:113466-113471) broadcasts the whole key list, and each client's RPC_GlobalKeys clears and rebuilds. TeleportWorld.Teleport reads it live at gate 2 (:143523) and shows '$msg_blocked'. Two operational cautions: this is world-wide, not per-portal; and GlobalKeyAdd mirrors any key below GlobalKeys.NonServerOption (41) into ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys (:113511), permanently baking it into the .fwl — use the publicized `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` plus SendGlobalKeys(0L) for a session-only lock.

STATE: per-portal puzzle state lives in mod-private ZDO keys on the portal itself (see Portals As A Data Store), plus per-player once-only flags as world global keys following the Wonderland FirstSpawnGrant convention `<mod>_<feature>_<playerID>` — persisted in the .db, readable synchronously after SetGlobalKey returns.

INPUT: the only reliable vanilla-client-to-server channels are emotes (ZDOVars.s_emote / s_emoteID polled on the character ZDO at 0.25 s, the Wonderland EmoteSignals pattern), map pings (Chat.SendPing broadcasts to peer 0 with a world Vector3), equipped item hashes on the character ZDO (VisEquipment writes s_rightItem etc.), item stands (ZDOVars.s_item is the mounted prefab hash), signs (ZDOVars.s_text, written directly by the client with no RPC), and chest contents (ZDOVars.s_items). Chat text is NOT usable — a solo player's chat produces zero packets.

FEEDBACK: PlayerNotify toasts via the character-ZDO 'Message' RPC, DamageText.TextType.Bonus floating text within 30 m, a granted status effect, a vanilla vfx/sfx through the 'SpawnObject' routed RPC, and the portal's own tag rewritten live.

**Player experience.** A ring of five ancient portals in a stone circle, all tagged with runes, all glowing 'connected', none of them working. Beside each is an item stand. Mount the right offering on the right stand — the server reads ZDOVars.s_item on each stand's ZDO — and when the combination is correct, all five tags change in the same instant from runes to 'THE ROAD OPENS', a vfx flares at each one, everyone present gets a centre-screen toast, and the ring becomes a real fan-in network to a sixth, hidden gate. The puzzle state persists across server restarts because it lives on the portal ZDOs themselves. A player who solves it gets a permanent map pin to the destination. Nobody installed anything; every element is either vanilla's own hover text, vanilla's own effects, or vanilla's own map.

**Failure modes.**
- Nulling a connection is undone by Game.ConnectPortals within 5 s if another same-tag unconnected portal exists (:100607-100621)
- GlobalKeys.NoPortals is world-wide and client-honoured, and RPC_SetGlobalKey has ZERO sender validation (:116022-116029) — any client can lift it unless the mod Harmony-prefixes that RPC
- Setting a portal key at runtime permanently edits the world's .fwl modifier list via GlobalKeyAdd (:113511) unless canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false is passed
- ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys wipes enum ordinals 0..40 on every world load (:115904-115931) and re-adds only what is in the .fwl — mod-owned world-modifier keys must be re-applied in a POSTFIX on it
- Emote polling has a 0.25 s resolution and a first-sighting seed; a player can emote faster than the poll
- Map pings are broadcast to every player, so a ping-based puzzle input is public
- All puzzle logic runs server-side against sampled state; there is no atomic transaction and two players can race a combination

**Prerequisites.** The Decoy Gate; Portals As A Data Store; The Tag As A Public Broadcast Surface

**Citations.** TeleportWorld.Teleport four gates — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143517-143537 · ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey / RPC_SetGlobalKey / SendGlobalKeys — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115943-115946, 116022-116029, 113466-113471 · ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd mirrors to m_startingGlobalKeys — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113483-113513 (:113511) · ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115904-115931 · ZDOVars.s_emote / s_emoteID — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78417, 78419; Player.StartEmote :15585-15598 · ZDOVars.s_item (ItemStand) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78465; ItemStand ZDO write :131795 · Sign.SetText writes ZDOVars.s_text directly with no RPC — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:141913-141928 · Chat.SendPing — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:42058-42068 · ZNetScene SpawnObject routed RPC — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81954, 82355-82366 · Wonderland EmoteSignals — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/EmoteSignals.cs:46

## 143. Sector Zero — Portals Outside The World, And Server-Side Instantiation

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

Any ZDO beyond roughly plus or minus 16.4 km clamps into the same sector bucket the dedicated server's own pinned reference position maps to, which makes the server instantiate it.

**How it works.** This is the mechanism nobody documents and it cuts both ways.

ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex (:115760-115773) computes `uint num = (uint)(sectorX + 256)` and clamps ANY sector outside 0..511 to `result.Sector = 0`. Zones are 64 m, so the legal range is roughly x/z in [-16416, +16352]; a normal world is plus or minus 10500, comfortably inside. Sector 0 is therefore shared by zone (-256,-256) and by EVERY out-of-range coordinate.

Game.FixedUpdate in the SERVER build pins `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick (:100458-100466) — a line that exists in no form in the client build. Zone (15625, 15625) maps through SectorToIndex to Sector 0.

Crucially, the server does NOT simply idle there. ZoneSystem.PokeLocalZone (:114021-114037) chooses `SpawnMode.Full` when `ZNet.instance.IsServer() && !IsZoneGenerated(zoneID)`, and SpawnZone (:114071-114107) succeeds and registers the zone in m_zones. So the server's own local zones around (1e6, 0, 1e6) ARE created, and ZoneSystem.IsActiveAreaLoaded() (:114054-114069) becomes true for them. ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects runs every 1/30 s (:82257-82276) and calls FindSectorObjects for zone (15625,15625) — which, via the clamp, returns m_objectsBySector[0] plus m_portalObjects[SectorIndex 0].

Two real consequences:
(a) A ZDO created at an out-of-range coordinate WILL be instantiated as a real GameObject on the dedicated server. For a portal that means a live TeleportWorld with a ZNetView, a running InvokeRepeating('UpdatePortal', 0.5f, 0.5f), and a TeleportWorldTrigger collider — harmless only because Player.m_localPlayer is null and Player.s_players is empty, so OnTriggerEnter (:143673-143681) can never fire. It is still a per-tick cost and a surprise in any object dump.
(b) The invalid-prefab reaper is SERVER-ONLY: CreateObjectsSorted's `else if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` branch (:82137-82143) takes ownership and destroys any ZDO whose CreateObject returns null. That branch is the ONLY thing in the game that reaps prefab-less ZDOs — and it only ever sees bucket 0. This is exactly why a Void Anchor placed at normal world coordinates survives indefinitely, and exactly why one placed out of bounds is deleted within a frame.

Practical rules: never create a portal or an anchor beyond about plus or minus 16000 m; if a mod wants a 'nowhere' anchor, put it at a legal but unvisited coordinate (deep ocean, or high above terrain) rather than out of bounds. And if any mod ever moved the server's reference position into the real world, the server would start instantiating real portal GameObjects with real colliders everywhere.

**Player experience.** Nothing intentional — this is a trap to be avoided rather than a feature to sell. The player-visible symptom of getting it wrong is an admin waypoint or an event gate that works for exactly one frame and then vanishes with a 'Destroyed invalid prefab ZDO' line in the server log, or a portal placed 'off the map' that quietly consumes server CPU forever while being reachable by nobody. The one legitimate use is diagnostic: a mod can deliberately park a marker ZDO in bucket 0 to confirm from the log whether the server's active area is loaded on a given build.

**Failure modes.**
- A Void Anchor placed out of bounds is destroyed by the server's own invalid-prefab reaper within a frame (:82137-82143)
- A valid portal prefab placed out of bounds is instantiated server-side as a live MonoBehaviour with a repeating invoke, permanently
- WorldGenerator.GetBiomeHeight returns -400 beyond 10500 m (:151978-151981), so out-of-bounds coordinates have no meaningful terrain at all
- Bucket 0 also holds legitimate zone (-256,-256) content, so anything a mod does there is mixed with real world data
- The whole behaviour hinges on IsActiveAreaLoaded being true for the pinned zone, which depends on HeightmapBuilder succeeding at (1e6, 0, 1e6) — plausible but unverified

**Citations.** ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex clamp to Sector 0 — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115755-115774 · Game.FixedUpdate pins reference position (SERVER build only) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100458-100466 · ZoneSystem.PokeLocalZone uses SpawnMode.Full on the server — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:114021-114037 · ZoneSystem.CreateLocalZones / IsActiveAreaLoaded — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113993-114012, 114054-114069 · ZNetScene.Update / CreateDestroyObjects — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82257-82276 · ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted server-only invalid-prefab destroy — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82105-82145 (:82137-82143) · ZDOMan.FindObjects merges m_portalObjects for the clamped sector — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77367-77382 · TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter requires Player.m_localPlayer — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143673-143681 · WorldGenerator edge constants — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:151118-151122, 151978-151981

**Open questions.**
