## 157. Animator SetTrigger as a real-time gesture channel (jump, dodge, forsaken power)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small-medium

Every jump, dodge-roll and forsaken-power activation is broadcast as a routed RPC that passes through the dedicated server carrying the player's character ZDOID — a zero-latency, zero-polling gesture input absent from the research digest.

**How it works.** NEW FINDING, verified. `ZSyncAnimation.SetTrigger(string name)` is `m_nview.InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, "SetTrigger", name)` (:87260-87263). `ZNetView.Everybody` is 0, and `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(long,…)` becomes `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, m_zdo.m_uid, "SetTrigger", name)` (:82850). `targetPeerID == 0` → the client handles locally AND calls `RouteRPC`, sending it to the server; the server's `RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632) sees `m_targetPeerID == 0`, calls `HandleRoutedRPC` (dropped — `ZNetScene.FindInstance` is null server-side, :83659) and relays to every other peer. A Harmony PREFIX on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage)` therefore sees every animation trigger from every player, one hop, no polling.

Payload: `(ZDOID m_targetZDO = the character's ZDO, string name)`. Map ZDOID → player via `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` → `peer.m_characterID`, then `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID).GetLong(ZDOVars.s_playerID)` (:78539) for stable identity and `GetPosition()` for where.

VERIFIED VOCABULARY: `"jump"` (`Character.ForceJump` :3483, every spacebar press) · `"dodge"` (Player roll :15196) · `"gpower"` (forsaken power :15717, cooldown-limited, unmistakable as a commit) · `"eat"` (:7705/:7766) · `"interact"` (:7659) · `"equip_hip"` (:8749/:8777) · `"attach"`/`"detach"`/`"attack_abort"`/`"stagger"`.

GRAMMAR: per-playerId ring of (trigger, time, position). JUMP×3 within 4 s while within 6 m of a portal and having moved <2 m between jumps = advance; JUMP×2 = back; `gpower` = commit. Combine with the crouch bit for a 2×N modal menu.

WHY IT BEATS EMOTES: `Player.StartEmote` requires `CanMove() && !InAttack() && !IsDrawingBow() && !IsAttached() && !IsAttachedToShip()` (:15585-15590) and is observed only by POLLING `s_emoteID` (:78419). `SetTrigger` is pushed, arrives in one hop, needs no emote wheel, and works while moving.

**Player experience.** You stand in front of your portal, tag `"Base"`. You jump — nothing. You jump twice more inside four seconds and a toast appears: `Base → next: Haldor (2/5)`. Three more jumps: `Base → next: Mine2 (3/5)`. You crouch to confirm and a toast reads `Locked in: Mine2`; the tag flips to `>Mine2` and the portal glows.

About eight seconds of hopping in place, which looks exactly like a player being impatient. No UI opened, no typing, works with a full load of ore, works on a controller.

The forsaken-power variant is one gesture: stand at the portal, hit your power key, toast reads `Committed → Mine2`. Unmistakable, un-accidental, naturally rate-limited — but it burns your Eikthyr/Elder power, which most players will resent.

Honest assessment: jumping-as-a-menu is the most embarrassing-looking mechanic in this document. It works, it is fast, it needs nothing — and a new player watching a veteran hop three times and vanish will have no idea what happened. Power-user shortcut layered over a legible primary input, never the primary.

**Failure modes.**
- Every jump on the server becomes a mod event; a player bunny-hopping near a portal trips the window constantly. Require proximity <6 m AND near-stationarity between jumps AND an armed state.
- Triggers fire on the OWNING client only; a dead, teleporting or attached player produces none (`Player.CanMove()` is false while `m_teleporting`, :14423).
- `"jump"` also fires from knockback and the grappling hook via `ForceJump`, so it is not purely voluntary.
- The prefix must not consume the ZPackage read position — deserialize a copy (`new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray())`) or vanilla's relay of the same packet reads garbage.
- `m_senderPeerID` is spoofable; resolve identity from `m_targetZDO` (the real character ZDOID) instead.
- This prefix runs on EVERY routed RPC on a busy server. Compare the int method hash first and return immediately.

**Prerequisites.** Per-player gesture ring buffer; Proximity binding to a portal

**Citations.** ZSyncAnimation.SetTrigger — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87260-87263 · ZSyncAnimation.Awake registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87157 · ZNetView.InvokeRPC(long,…) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82850-82853 · ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83632-83644 · Character.ForceJump ("jump") — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:3473-3490 · Player dodge ("dodge") — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15196 · Player guardian power ("gpower") — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15717 · Player.StartEmote preconditions — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15585-15599 · ZNetPeer.m_characterID — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78794

**Open questions.**
- Does the dedicated server ever hold a ZNetView for a character ZDO such that `HandleRoutedRPC` dispatches rather than dropping? It should not (`Game.FixedUpdate` pin :100465). IN-GAME: log `ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances()` (:82334) on a live server.
- How many `SetTrigger` packets per second does a busy 10-player server carry? Determines whether the hot-path hash compare is acceptable. IN-GAME: count for 60 s.

## 158. Posture bits — crouch and block as a silent modifier key

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

Crouching and raising a shield are each mirrored into the character ZDO as a live boolean the server can poll — a hands-free arming gate that costs one keypress.

**How it works.** NEW FINDING, verified. `Player.UpdateCrouch` calls `m_zanim.SetBool(s_crouching, …)` where `s_crouching = ZSyncAnimation.GetHash("crouching")` (:9984, :15667, :15671). `ZSyncAnimation.SetBool(int hash, bool)` does, when `m_nview.IsOwner()`, `zdo.AddSessionHash(438569 + hash); zdo.Set(438569 + hash, value ? 1 : 0)` (:87270-87281); the salt is the literal `c_ZDOSalt = 438569` (:87144). Server read:

  int key = 438569 + UnityEngine.Animator.StringToHash("crouching");
  bool crouching = characterZdo.GetInt(key) != 0;

`Animator.StringToHash` is a pure static in UnityEngine.AnimationModule, callable headless. The key is registered as a SESSION hash so `ZDOExtraData.GetSaveData` strips it from disk (:75507), but session hashes are NOT filtered from `ZDO.Serialize` — the value is live on the wire every tick.

Second bit, already a named constant: `ZDOVars.s_isBlockingHash` = `"IsBlocking"` (:78463), written on the character ZDO at :8690/:8708. Third, analogue: `ZDOVars.s_stealth` (:78613) written at :16372.

USE: poll `ZNet.instance.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` (:81024) at 0.2 s. Crouch alone as the ARMING gate for the ping and jump channels solves their biggest problem — accidental activation — at essentially zero cost. Crouch is a TOGGLE in Valheim (`m_crouchToggled`, `SetCrouch` :15675) so the armed state can be held indefinitely with no input strain; block is momentary (held mouse button) so it suits a transient 'show me detail' mode.

IMPORTANT: `UpdateCrouch` calls `SetCrouch(false)` when `IsBlocking()` (:15662), so the crouch+block combination is UNREACHABLE. Three modes exist, not four.

**Player experience.** You walk to your portal. Nothing happens — you are standing normally and the server is ignoring you. You press crouch (default Ctrl) and a toast appears instantly: `Portal armed — jump to cycle, crouch again to commit.` Your character is visibly crouching, which IS the feedback: anyone watching can see you are 'in the menu'.

You jump. `1/5 Base`. Jump. `2/5 Haldor`. You raise your shield and the toast expands to `2/5 Haldor · 1,140m · Black Forest · open`. You lower it, press crouch again, and the toast reads `Dialed → Haldor.` The portal glows.

Six seconds, no menu, no typing, one hand.

The honest problems: crouching is something players do constantly for sneaking, so ARMED fires whenever anyone sneaks past a portal — it needs a proximity gate and a 15 s auto-disarm. And crouch-as-a-modifier is invisible to a new player; nothing in the game hints that crouching near a portal means anything. This is a shortcut for people who already know.

**Failure modes.**
- Crouch is a common movement action; without tight proximity gating and auto-disarm, arming fires constantly.
- `IsBlocking()` forces crouch off (:15662) — crouch+block is unreachable, so only three of four states exist.
- `UpdateCrouch` also clears crouch on `!HaveStamina() || IsSwimming() || InBed() || InPlaceMode() || m_run || IsFlying()` (:15662), so the armed state silently drops when the player sprints or runs out of stamina.
- The write depends on `ZSyncAnimation.SetBool` running, which it does whenever the owner's `UpdateCrouch` runs — but never hard-code the resulting integer key; `Animator.StringToHash` is Unity-internal and only stable within one build.
- Session hashes are stripped from the save, so the armed state does not survive a relog — correct behaviour, but no persistent flag is possible here.

**Prerequisites.** Character ZDO polling loop

**Citations.** Player.s_crouching = ZSyncAnimation.GetHash("crouching") — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:9984 · Player.UpdateCrouch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15658-15673 · ZSyncAnimation.SetBool (ZDO write at 438569+hash) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87270-87281 · ZSyncAnimation c_ZDOSalt = 438569 — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87144 · ZSyncAnimation.SyncParameters read-back — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87210-87252 · ZDOVars.s_isBlockingHash — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78463; written :8690, :8708 · ZDOVars.s_stealth — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78613; written :16372 · ZDOExtraData.GetSaveData session filter — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75507-75513

**Open questions.**
- Is `"crouching"` in the Player prefab's `ZSyncAnimation.m_syncBools` list? Irrelevant to the server READ (SetBool writes whenever owner) but determines whether other players see the animation. IN-GAME: log `characterZdo.GetInt(438569 + Animator.StringToHash("crouching"))` while a player toggles crouch.
- What is the full contents of the Player prefab's m_syncBools/m_syncFloats/m_syncInts? Each entry is another free server-readable player-state bit. IN-GAME: dump from a client at world-ready.

## 159. Emote signalling near a portal

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

The player uses a vanilla emote while standing at a portal; the server polls the character ZDO's emote counter and treats each of 24 emotes as a command token.

**How it works.** `Player.StartEmote(string emote, bool oneshot)` writes three fields on the player's own character ZDO: `ZDOVars.s_emoteID` incremented (:78419), `ZDOVars.s_emote` = the lowercased enum name (:78417), `ZDOVars.s_emoteOneshot` (:78421) — see :15585-15599. `StopEmote` bumps the counter with an empty name (:15601-15609). No RPC; the change reaches the server as ZDO data within one 0.05 s client flush.

SERVER LOOP: reuse Wonderland's `EmoteSignals` verbatim (Core/Data/EmoteSignals.cs:38/:46/:125) — every 0.25 s, for each `ConnectedCharacters.All()` entry read `s_emoteID`; if it differs from cache, read `s_emote` and dispatch. Seed the counter on first sighting so a pre-existing emote does not fire a phantom command. Ignore empty names.

VOCABULARY: 24 usable emotes (`enum Emotes` :6216-6246). A sane portal mapping: Point → next destination · ThumbsUp → confirm · NoNoNo → cancel · Wave → list destinations as toasts · Challenge → lock/unlock · Shrug → status. Bind to the nearest managed portal within 6 m via `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` (:77643) and the character ZDO position.

WHY SECOND-CHOICE: `StartEmote` refuses when `!CanMove() || InAttack() || IsDrawingBow() || IsAttached() || IsAttachedToShip()` (:15587) — no emoting while seated, on a boat, mid-swing or mid-teleport. The emote wheel is a real UI the player must open; typing `/point` is faster but requires knowing the names, and an unknown name is silently swallowed by the client's own `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (:41947-41955). The 0.25 s poll adds a perceptible beat, and 24 tokens is far more than anyone will memorise — realistically 4-6 are usable.

It is nevertheless completely reliable, independent of player count, and the one channel Wonderland has already shipped and live-tested in production (`CacheClaimControl.cs`, `SupplySwitch.cs`).

**Player experience.** You stand at your portal, hold the emote key, and pick Wave. Your character waves. About a third of a second later five toasts stack up:

`1 Base      612m`
`2 Haldor  1,140m`
`3 Mine2     840m`
`4 Bog      3,010m`
`Point to cycle · ThumbsUp to confirm`

You emote Point: `▸ 1 Base (612m)`. Point again: `▸ 2 Haldor (1,140m)`. On the one you want you emote ThumbsUp: `Dialed → Haldor.` The portal glows, the tag flips to `>Haldor`.

Twelve to fifteen seconds, because opening the wheel and picking takes two to three seconds each time and every emote plays a full animation. Visibly slower than typing into the portal.

The upside: entirely mouse-driven, works on a controller, and your character is visibly doing something — a bystander sees you pointing at a portal and can guess what is happening, which is more than the jump or crouch channels offer.

**Failure modes.**
- `StartEmote` returns false and writes nothing while attached, on a ship, attacking, drawing a bow, or unable to move (:15587). The player gets no feedback that the command was swallowed.
- 0.25 s polling collapses two emotes in one tick into one observed event. Read the `s_emoteID` DELTA — a jump of 2 means a step was missed, and the mod should say so rather than silently mis-advance.
- Emotes are social: waving hello beside a portal fires a directory dump. Proximity gating plus an armed state is mandatory.
- `Sit`, `Rest`, `Relax`, `Vibe` are non-oneshot (`[Emote(OneShot=false)]`, :6219) and latch; the following `StopEmote` bumps the counter with an empty string that must be ignored.
- 24 tokens is beyond memorisation; only 4-6 are practical.
- Two players emoting at the same portal inside one tick are indistinguishable in ordering.

**Prerequisites.** ConnectedCharacters / character-ZDO poll; Proximity binding

**Citations.** Player.StartEmote — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15585-15599 · Player.StopEmote — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15601-15609 · enum Emotes (24 + Count) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6216-6246 · Emote.DoEmote — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6207-6214 · ZDOVars.s_emote / s_emoteID / s_emoteOneshot — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78417, :78419, :78421 · ZDOMan.GetPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77643-77646 · Chat.InputText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41947-41955 · Wonderland EmoteSignals — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/EmoteSignals.cs:38, :46, :125

**Open questions.**
- Does the emote WHEEL expose all 24 enum entries or a subset, with the rest reachable only by typing `/<emote>`? This decides the practical vocabulary size. IN-GAME: open the wheel and count.

## 160. Equipped item as a destination selector

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

Hold a specific item while touching the portal; its prefab hash is already in your character ZDO, so the server reads which one and dials the matching destination.

**How it works.** `VisEquipment` mirrors every VISIBLE equipped item into the character's own ZDO as a prefab stable hash: `s_rightItem` (+variant/quality), `s_leftItem`, `s_helmetItem`, `s_chestItem`, `s_legItem`, `s_shoulderItem`, `s_utilityItem`, `s_trinketItem`, `s_leftBackItem`, `s_rightBackItem` — written at :20569-20708 by the owning client. Server reads `characterZdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_rightItem)` and resolves via `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)?.name` (:82045).

SCHEME: a binding table `itemPrefabHash → destination` (server config or per-player). Torch = home, Cultivator = farm, a boss trophy = that boss's altar (resolvable server-side from `ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances` :113295 via `FindClosestLocation` :115707). Poll `ZNet.instance.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` (:81024) at 0.25 s; when an ARMED player within 6 m of a managed portal changes `s_rightItem`, dial.

WHY IT IS INTERESTING: it is the only channel that is simultaneously zero extra actions (players swap items constantly), physically legible (everyone can SEE what you hold), and thematically native (hold the key to the door). A row of stone portals where you show a Fine Wood for the Meadows and a Black Metal for the Plains reads as a game mechanic rather than a mod UI. The back slots (`s_leftBackItem`/`s_rightBackItem`) are also visible, doubling the vocabulary without the player holding anything awkward.

CRITICAL LIMIT: this reads EQUIPPED items only. A living player's inventory is never mirrored into any ZDO — `ZDOVars.s_items` (:78475) is written by exactly one live path, `Container.Save` (:122293-122300), and an exhaustive scan of Character/Humanoid/Player ZDO writes yields only vitals, identity, pose and equipment visuals. So 'carry a key item' cannot be a requirement, only 'hold' one, and nothing can be charged.

**Player experience.** You are at your base portal holding a Bronze Axe and you want the mine. You open your inventory, right-click your Antler Pickaxe to equip it, close the inventory, and step toward the portal.

As the pickaxe goes into your hand a toast reads `Pickaxe → Mine2 (840m). Step through.` The tag flips to `>Mine2` and the portal glows. You walk through.

At the mine you swap back to the axe and the return portal reads `Axe → Base`. You never opened a menu, never typed, and the thing in your hand is the thing that tells you where you are going. A friend watching sees you draw a pickaxe and walk into a portal, and understands the rule the first time they see it.

The failure is equally concrete: you arrive at the portal holding a Draugr Fang because you were fighting on the way, and the portal silently re-dials itself. Hence the arming gate — crouch, swap, un-crouch — or bind only to items nobody carries by accident.

Jank rating: low-to-medium. It feels like a game mechanic rather than a workaround, which is rare in this list.

**Failure modes.**
- Equipping happens constantly in normal play; without an arming gate a player re-dials portals by fighting near them.
- Only VISIBLE slots are in the ZDO — backpack contents are invisible, so no 'must be carrying X' requirement and no fee.
- `VisEquipment`'s read-back branches on `m_isPlayer` (:20857-20885), an Inspector bool; some slots may not be written for a Player specifically.
- The binding table has to be taught — nothing in the game indicates a Cultivator means anything to a portal.
- Two portals within 6 m are ambiguous; bind to the nearest and name it in the toast.
- Requires `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)` to be non-null on a dedicated server.

**Prerequisites.** Character ZDO polling; Arming gesture; Item→destination binding table

**Citations.** VisEquipment ZDO writes — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:20569-20571, :20590-20591, :20632, :20644, :20656, :20670-20672, :20684, :20696, :20708 · VisEquipment read-back (m_isPlayer branch) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:20857-20885 · ZNetScene.GetPrefab(int) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82045-82052 · ZDOVars.s_items written only by Container.Save — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78475; :122293-122300 · ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81024-81044 · ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances / FindClosestLocation — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113295, :115707-115727

**Open questions.**
- Is `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab("portal_wood")` (and item prefabs generally) non-null on a 1.0.7 dedicated server? IN-GAME: log it at the ZNetScene.Awake postfix.

## 161. Item stand token board

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small-medium

A row of vanilla item stands beside a portal; mounting an item on a stand selects that stand's destination, read from `ZDOVars.s_item` on the stand's own ZDO.

**How it works.** `ItemStand.UpdateAttach` (on the stand's owning client) does `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_item, m_queuedItem.m_dropPrefab.name.GetStableHashCode())` plus `ItemDrop.SaveToZDO(itemData, zdo)` and `m_nview.InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, "SetVisualItem", …)` (:131834-131854). Detach writes `Set(ZDOVars.s_item, 0)` (:131824). `HaveAttachment()` is `GetInt(s_item) != 0` (:132018).

SERVER: discover stands like signs — `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(portalPos, 8f)` filtered to prefabs carrying `ItemStand`. Order deterministically by bearing around the portal then y. Poll `GetInt(ZDOVars.s_item)` (:78465) at 0.5 s, or better catch it in the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix. Stand index N occupied → destination N.

TWO ENCODINGS: (a) POSITIONAL — the stand index is the address, item identity irrelevant; simple, teachable, and a sign under each stand becomes its label. (b) SEMANTIC — the item's prefab hash is the address; one stand, N destinations.

PUSH NOTIFICATION FOR FREE: `"SetVisualItem"` is `InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, …)` (:131849), targetPeerID 0, so it also passes through the server as a relayed routed RPC carrying `(itemHash, variant, quality, orientation)` and the stand's ZDOID — catchable with the same `RPC_RoutedRPC` prefix as the animation triggers, matching `"SetVisualItem".GetStableHashCode()`. No polling needed.

HARD LIMIT — NO STACK COUNT. The 'stack count = index' idea does not work here: `UpdateAttach` sets `itemData.m_stack = 1` unconditionally (:131843) and mounts exactly one item. Stack encoding requires a Container.

SERVER WRITE-BACK: the mod can clear a stand (`SetOwner(GetSessionID())`, `Set(s_item,0)`, `Set(s_type,0)`, `ForceSendZDO`) — but the item is then GONE, because spawning the drop needs a live GameObject (`DropItem` at :131820). Never auto-clear a player's item; that is item destruction.

**Player experience.** Beside your hub you have five item stands in a row, each with a sign under it: `1 Base`, `2 Haldor`, `3 Mine2`, `4 Bog`, `5 Swamp`. You are holding a Torch.

You walk to stand 3, press E, and the torch mounts with the usual vanilla animation. Within half a second a toast reads `Dialed → Mine2 (840m)` and the portal lights up. You step through.

The torch is still sitting on stand 3 across the map — so your base portal is still pointed at Mine2, which is what you want. The board is a physical, persistent, at-a-glance record of where every portal in your hub currently points. Anyone walking into your base reads the routing state off the wall without hovering anything or knowing any commands.

To re-route you take the torch off stand 3 (`Mine2 released`) and put it on stand 2 (`Dialed → Haldor`).

The most physically satisfying scheme in this list and arguably better than a UI — it is a patch panel. Its costs are build effort (five stands plus five signs is a real project) and that it scales only as far as you are willing to build.

**Failure modes.**
- An item on a stand is a persistent world object anyone can take; removing your torch silently un-dials your portal.
- `m_stack = 1` is forced (:131843) — no stack-count encoding.
- The server cannot return a mounted item; clearing `s_item` destroys it.
- Stand ordering must derive from world position (bearing around the portal), never ZDOID — `ZDO.Load` renumbers uids (:74552).
- Stands inside a ward the player cannot access refuse the interaction client-side with no server-visible signal.
- Two occupied stands need an explicit precedence rule (last-changed wins, via the Deserialize hook ordering).

**Prerequisites.** The Ledger (shared nearby-object discovery); Portal address book

## 162. Chest tokens — item type as destination, stack count as index

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Drop a specific item into a chest beside the portal; the server parses the chest's serialized inventory blob and reads item type AND stack size as a two-field command — the only channel that can also charge a fee.

**How it works.** A Container's whole inventory is one serialized byte blob on its ZDO: `Container.Save` does `m_inventory.Save(pkg); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_items, pkg.GetArray())` on every `OnContainerChanged` (:122286-122300); `ZDOVars.s_items` = `"items"` (:78475). Decode server-side with Wonderland's `ZdoInventoryIO.Load` (Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs), which builds a scratch `Inventory` over the blob — already shipped and tested.

Unlike an ItemStand, a Container DOES carry stack counts, so 'item type = destination, stack count = index' is available here and nowhere else: one Coal = network 'Mine', three Coal = slot 3 within it.

TIMING AND THE IN-USE GATE: `Container` runs `InvokeRepeating("CheckForChanges", 0f, 1f)` (:121922) and `Load()` early-returns while `m_inUse` (:122305). `UpdateUseVisual` writes `ZDOVars.s_inUse` (`"InUse"`, :78673) into the ZDO when the client owns it (:121990-122001), so the server can SEE that the chest is open and must not write `s_items` during that window (Wonderland's `ZdoInventoryIO.IsBusy`). The player's deposit reaches the server as soon as their `Save()` fires and the ZDO flushes (≤0.05 s + ½ RTT), but the server's REPLY does not repaint on their screen until they close the chest.

TOLL VARIANT: because the server can also WRITE `s_items`, this is the only channel that can charge for a teleport — consume 1 Coal per long-range dial via `ZdoInventoryIO.MoveMatchingItem`. Nothing else in the zero-client toolkit can take an item from a player.

WRITE PROCEDURE: `if (zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_inUse) == 1) defer;` then `SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, mutate the scratch inventory, `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_items, newBlob)`, `ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)`.

**Player experience.** There is a chest under your portal with a sign on it reading `DROP A TOKEN`. You open it — ordinary vanilla chest UI — drag two Coal in, and close it.

About a second later a toast reads `Coal x2 → Haldor (1,140m). Fee paid.` The portal glows. You look back at the chest: empty, the coal spent on the trip.

Drop in something unrecognised and the toast reads `Flint is not a token. Valid: Coal, Amber, Ruby.` and the flint is still there when you reopen. Drop Coal x7 with only five destinations: `Only 5 destinations. Coal x1-x5.` and the coal stays.

The unavoidable weirdness: if you keep the chest OPEN, nothing visibly changes inside it no matter what the server does, because vanilla refuses to reload a container's contents while its UI is up. You must close it to see the result. The toast fires immediately, so you are told what happened — you just cannot watch it happen.

Cost: open inventory, open chest, drag, close. Six or seven seconds, and it costs an item. High jank as routine navigation; excellent as an economy layer under a different primary input.

**Failure modes.**
- `Container.Load` refuses while `m_inUse` (:122305), so the server's reply is invisible until the player closes the chest.
- Writing `s_items` while the player has the chest open races their client's own Save and can destroy items. Always check `ZDOVars.s_inUse` first.
- Chests are public containers; anyone can drop a token into someone else's control chest unless the mod gates on ward permission or `s_creator`.
- The 1 s `CheckForChanges` cadence plus the flush means the observed deposit can lag a deposit-then-immediately-withdraw by enough to misread the state.
- Charging a fee is a destructive operation on player property — it must be opt-in, clearly signed, and never silent.

**Prerequisites.** ZdoInventoryIO (Wonderland Core/Data); Portal address book; Token→destination table

**Citations.** Container.Save / Load — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:122293-122322 · Container.OnContainerChanged — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:122286-122292 · Container InvokeRepeating("CheckForChanges", 0f, 1f) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:121922 · Container.UpdateUseVisual (s_inUse write) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:121990-122001 · ZDOVars.s_items / s_inUse — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78475, :78673 · Wonderland ZdoInventoryIO — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs

**Open questions.**
- Does a fresh chest write `s_items` promptly, or only after the owning client's first `OnContainerChanged` tick? Matters for a newly-built control chest. IN-GAME: build a chest, drop one item, and time how long until the server reads a non-null blob.

## 163. Debiting a living player's own inventory

`RULED-OUT` · `NOT-ENFORCEABLE` · effort: small

Taking an item directly from the player (rather than from a chest), or checking what they are carrying — the obvious design that is structurally impossible.

**How it works.** `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles()` does NOT collect anything — it invokes a `"SavePlayerProfile"` RPC on each peer whose handler calls `Game.instance.SavePlayerProfile` on that client, writing that client's own local `.fch` file; nothing returns to the server (:79653-79675). `Player.Save(ZPackage)` serialises inventory, known recipes, skills and uniques into `PlayerProfile.m_playerData`, stored only on that client's disk (:14091-14170, :105706-105711). An exhaustive read of every `Set(ZDOVars.s_*)` call inside Character (:178-6796), Humanoid (:6796-9414) and Player (:9414-16500) finds only vitals, identity, pose, emote and equipment-visual fields — never items.

The single exception is a DEAD player: `Player.CreateTombStone` moves the whole inventory into a tombstone Container whose ZDO carries `s_items` plus `s_owner`/`s_ownerName`/`s_timeOfDeath`/`s_spawnPoint` (:12702-12714, :19845-19853, :19732-19740). So the server can read and debit a corpse, and nothing else.

CONSEQUENCE FOR PORTAL UX: the server can never reproduce vanilla's ore/metal restriction for a server-issued teleport, because `Inventory.IsTeleportable` (:68860-68880) runs entirely client-side against data the server does not hold. Any forced-teleport feature silently allows ore through. Design around it — advertise it honestly, or never use forced teleport as the primary movement and let the vanilla portal (which DOES check) do the work.

**Player experience.** Not applicable — nothing can be built, so the player experiences nothing. Any documentation promising 'the server checks what you are carrying' or 'the portal charges you a coin' without a chest is a promise that cannot be kept.

**Failure modes.**
- Any design stating 'the server checks the player is carrying X' or 'the server takes X from the player' is impossible without a client mod.
- A server-issued teleport always bypasses the ore/metal restriction, which will be perceived as a cheat vector if not stated plainly.

**Citations.** ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles / RPC_SavePlayerProfile — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79653-79675 · Player.Save — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:14091-14170 · PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:105706-105711 · Container.Save (only live s_items writer) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:122293-122300 · Player.CreateTombStone / TombStone.Setup / TombStone.Awake — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:12702-12714, :19845-19853, :19732-19740 · Inventory.IsTeleportable — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:68860-68880

## 164. Positional input — plates, walk-sequences, approach vector

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

The server polls every connected character's ZDO position and treats named spots, dwell times, ordered sequences and the compass bearing of approach as commands.

**How it works.** POSITION IS THE CHEAPEST AND FRESHEST SIGNAL THE SERVER HAS. `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` writes `zDO.SetPosition(GetPosition())` every FixedUpdate on the owning client (:87527-87534), and client→server ZDO delivery is distance-independent (`ZDOMan.ClientChanged` :77727 → `CreateSyncList`'s non-server branch drains `m_clientChangeQueue` wholesale :77241-77258, flushed every 0.05 s :76843). So `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID).GetPosition()` is fresh to ~50-100 ms regardless of how far the player is from the server's pinned reference position (1e6,0,1e6, :100465).

PRIMITIVES:
(1) PLATE — a mod-side `(worldPos, radius, action)`. A player whose horizontal distance drops below radius and stays for a dwell time (default 1.5 s) triggers. Accumulate `dwell[playerId] += dt` while inside, reset on exit. Ignore y so a raised platform still counts.
(2) SEQUENCE — an ordered list of plates entered within a window. `A→B→A` inside 20 s is deliberate and essentially unspoofable. Bounded per-player ring of (plateId, time).
(3) APPROACH VECTOR — the bearing from which the player entered the portal's 6 m radius, quantised to 8 sectors. Walk in from the north for destination 1, from the east for 3. Zero construction, zero UI, the most invisible input available.
(4) LOOK DIRECTION — `CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation` writes `ZDOVars.s_lookTarget = eyePos + lookDir * 100f` into the character ZDO, at most every 0.2 s and only on change (:5041-5081). Disambiguates which of several adjacent portals/signs/stands the player means.

MARKING: the plates are ordinary player-built decoration (a stone tile, a rug, a torch ring); the mod needs only a coordinate list.

SAMPLING: 0.1-0.2 s is comfortable — a player at ~5 m/s covers 0.5-1 m per sample, so a 3 m plate is never missed. Far tighter than Wonderland's `PositionWatch` 3 s security sampling (Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:31), costing one `GetAllCharacterZDOS()` allocation plus N distance checks per tick.

**Player experience.** In front of your portal you have laid three stone tiles in a row, each with a torch, and a sign above reading `STAND TO CHOOSE`. The tiles are pure decoration you built with the hammer.

You walk onto the left tile and stop. About a second and a half later a toast reads `▸ Base (612m). Walk into the portal.` and the tag flips to `>Base`. You step off; nothing changes — the dial is set.

You walk onto the middle tile, wait, `▸ Haldor (1,140m)`. You step into the portal and you are in Haldor's meadow.

The approach-vector variant is quieter still: there are no tiles. You walk into the portal from the north and come out at your mine; from the east and you come out at the swamp. After the third time you stop thinking about it. A guest walks straight in from whichever side, gets destination 1, and is confused about nothing because they never knew there was a choice.

Cost: walking. Literally zero extra actions — that is its whole appeal. The problem is that it is undiscoverable and accident-prone; you will re-dial your hub by pathing across a tile on the way to a workbench.

**Failure modes.**
- Players path across their own base constantly; without an armed state and generous dwell times this fires by accident all day.
- Undiscoverable — nothing in the game hints that a floor tile means anything. Requires player-built visible marking plus a sign written by the server.
- Approach-vector input is invisible even after you know about it: a guest cannot tell there was a choice, and a player who circles a portal while fighting gets a random destination.
- Position is owner-authoritative; a player being knocked back or teleported crosses plates involuntarily.
- Dwell timers must be reset on death/respawn (`ZDOVars.s_dead`, :78403) and on large position jumps (dungeon transits cross y=3000, `Character.InInterior` :4538) or the tracker desyncs.

**Prerequisites.** Character ZDO polling at 0.1-0.2 s; Mod-side plate coordinate list; Arming gesture

**Citations.** ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87527-87540 · ZDOMan.ClientChanged / CreateSyncList non-server branch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77727-77730, :77241-77258 · ZDOMan.Update 0.05 s send cadence — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76843-76852 · CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation (s_lookTarget) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:5041-5081 · Game.FixedUpdate reference-position pin — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100465 · Character.InInterior — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:4538-4541 · Wonderland PositionWatch — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:31

**Open questions.**
- Does the Player prefab have `CharacterAnimEvent.m_headRotation` enabled and `m_head` assigned? Both are Inspector fields gating the `s_lookTarget` write (:5043). IN-GAME: poll `s_lookTarget` for 10 s while a player spins in place; a changing non-zero Vector3 confirms the channel.

## 165. Build-shape input — placing a piece as a latching switch

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: medium

Placing (or removing) a specific build piece in a specific socket near a portal is detected the moment the ZDO arrives and acts as a permanent, visible switch.

**How it works.** THE HOOK IS THE NON-OBVIOUS PART. A dedicated server never sees `Player.PlacePiece` (no Player instance) and never runs `ZNetScene.Instantiate` for a client-placed piece (the client instantiates locally and only the ZDO arrives). The PAUSED PortalLock project patched exactly those and could never fire once (`PAUSED/PortalLock/src/PortalLock/PlacementPatches.cs:14, :114`).

The correct hook is Wonderland's SpawnGovernor pair (`Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43, :58`): a postfix on the private `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int)` (:76684) that only REMEMBERS the ZDOID — on the network-receive path `prefabHash` is 0 and `GetPrefab()` returns 0, so nothing can be decided — plus a postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` (:74225), the first moment the prefab hash is known. There, read `GetPrefab()`, `GetPosition()` and `GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator)` (:78393 — the placer's stable PlayerProfile UID, written by `Piece.SetCreator` :136415-136424, the same value as that player's `ZDOVars.s_playerID`).

SWITCH DESIGN: per portal, a set of SOCKETS `(relativeOffset, acceptedPrefabSet, action)`. A Wood Beam in socket 1 → dial destination 1. A blue-burning torch in the lock socket → lock the portal. Because the ZDO persists, the switch is latching, survives restarts, and a visitor reads the routing state off the architecture.

DESTRUCTION is the other half: subscribe to the public `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` `Action<ZDO>` field (:76033), invoked from `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76975) BEFORE the ZDO leaves `m_objectsByID`, so it is still readable inside the callback. No Harmony needed.

SAME HOOK = THE SERVER-ENFORCED PORTAL CAP: on a new portal-prefab ZDO, read `s_creator`, count that player's portals in `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648), and if over the limit `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo);` (:76929 — owner-gated on send, so the SetOwner is mandatory) plus a toast. Strictly stronger than TortalPortal's client-side `Player.TryPlacePiece` cap, which any client can ignore.

**Player experience.** Your portal sits in a stone frame. On the left there are three empty 1×1 sockets where a wood beam obviously goes — you built the frame that way because the server-written sign beside it reads `PLUG A BEAM: 1 Base · 2 Haldor · 3 Mine`.

You take out your hammer, select Wood Beam, and place one in socket 2. It snaps in with the normal building sound. Within about a quarter second a toast reads `Haldor plugged. Portal → Haldor (1,140m).` The portal glows. The beam stays there forever.

A week later you come back and need to remember nothing: there is a beam in socket 2, so the portal goes to Haldor. Anyone standing in your base can read it. To change it you remove the beam (`Haldor unplugged`) and place one in socket 3.

Cost: equip hammer, select piece, place — about five seconds and one piece of wood. Slower than typing but permanent, visible, and it turns routing state into architecture, which is a genuinely Valheim-native idea.

Jank rating: medium. The mechanism is elegant; discoverability depends entirely on the server writing a sign that explains the sockets and on the sockets being visually obvious, which is on the player's building skill.

**Failure modes.**
- A `CreateNewZDO`-only postfix always sees `GetPrefab() == 0` on the network path and can never act — SpawnGovernor's header records this as a shipped bug in its own first version.
- Patching `Player.PlacePiece` / `Player.TryPlacePiece` / `ZNetScene.Instantiate` produces code that can never execute on a dedicated server (PortalLock's precedent).
- Socket matching must tolerate snap-grid offsets and rotation; a hard equality on position will miss almost every placement. Use a radius of ~0.75 m around the expected offset, in the portal's local frame.
- `Piece.SetCreator` only writes when `m_nview.IsOwner() && GetCreator() == 0` (:136417), so world-gen structures and some pieces have `s_creator == 0`. Do not treat a missing creator as 'unowned' without checking.
- Destroying a client-created ZDO inside the Deserialize postfix may leave an orphaned local instance on the placing client until the zone reloads; the build materials may or may not be refunded.
- Players rebuild and remodel constantly — a socket that overlaps a common building position will fire spuriously.

**Prerequisites.** SpawnGovernor-style CreateNewZDO + Deserialize hook pair; Portal address book; Per-portal socket definitions

**Citations.** Wonderland SpawnGovernor — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43, :58, :70 · ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID,Vector3,int) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76684-76692 · ZDO.Deserialize — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74225-74232 · Piece.SetCreator / Piece.Awake — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:136415-136424, :136246-136250 · ZDOVars.s_creator / s_creatorIndex — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78393, :78395 · ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed / HandleDestroyedZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76033, :76963-76999 · ZDOMan.DestroyZDO (owner-gated) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76929-76935 · PortalLock's dead hooks — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/PAUSED/PortalLock/src/PortalLock/PlacementPatches.cs:14, :114

**Open questions.**
- Can the server destroy a client-created portal/piece ZDO inside the Deserialize postfix without a visible desync on the placing client? SpawnGovernor does this for creatures and is shipped, but a Piece/WearNTear-bearing object may differ. IN-GAME: set a cap of 1, place a second portal on a vanilla client, and observe whether the ghost disappears cleanly and whether materials are refunded.

## 166. Chat commands (`/portal home`)

`RULED-OUT` · `NOT-ENFORCEABLE` · effort: small

Typing a command in chat — the obvious design, dead on a dedicated server for three independent reasons.

**How it works.** (1) SLASH COMMANDS NEVER LEAVE THE CLIENT. `Chat.InputText` does `text = ((text[0] != '/') ? ("say " + text) : text.Substring(1)); TryRunCommand(text, this);` (:41947-41955). `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (:45734-45758) looks the name up in the CLIENT's own compiled dictionary; `/portal` is not in it and the call uses silentFail, so the client does nothing and prints nothing. There is no network path for an unrecognised slash command.

(2) PLAIN CHAT IS INVISIBLE TO A SOLO PLAYER. Plain text becomes `say <text>` → `Chat.SendText`. Shout goes through `CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync` (:41996-42042), which — when a RelationsProvider exists, i.e. on Steam — sends one RPC to `ZNet.instance.LocalPlayerCharacterID.UserID` (the sender's OWN peer id) plus one per OTHER listed player's `m_characterID.UserID`. `InvokeRoutedRPC` calls `RouteRPC` only `if (targetPeerID != m_id)` (:83591). For a lone player every target IS their own id, so ZERO packets go on the wire. Normal/Whisper take `Talker.Say` → `m_nview.InvokeRPC(user, "Say", …)` (:18942-18950), same addressing, same result.

(3) WITH 2+ PLAYERS IT IS RELAY-ONLY. The packets pass through the server's `RPC_RoutedRPC` → `RouteRPC` (:83632-83643) but are never addressed to the server, so no registered handler fires. A prefix CAN sniff them — but a channel that works only when a second player is online is not a channel.

THE ADMIN EXCEPTION: `ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879-81889) is gated on `ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())` and runs the string through the SERVER's `Console.instance.TryRunCommand`; replies return via `ZNet.RemotePrint` → the client's console (:81635-81656). A mod-registered server-side `Terminal.ConsoleCommand` with `onlyServer: true, remoteCommand: true` gives ADMINS a genuine text console — invisible to ordinary players and landing in a window most people never open.

**Player experience.** The player types `/portal home` and presses Enter. Absolutely nothing happens — no error, no message, no log line on their machine or the server's. The chat box closes. They try `/tp home`, `!home`, `portal home`. The last one appears in chat as a shout nobody but they can see if they are alone. They conclude the mod is broken and file a bug.

**Failure modes.**
- Silent failure is the worst possible outcome for a discovery path — the player tries the obvious thing and gets zero signal.
- Any documentation saying 'type /portal …' generates support tickets forever.
- Sniffing shouts via a RouteRPC prefix works only with 2+ players online: untestable solo and unreliable in production.

**Citations.** Chat.InputText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41947-41955 · Terminal.TryRunCommand — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:45734-45758 · Chat.SendText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41975-41994 · Chat.CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41996-42042 · Talker.Say — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:18942-18950 · ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC (RouteRPC only when targetPeerID != m_id) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83587-83594 · ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81879-81889 · ZNet.RemotePrint / RPC_RemotePrint — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81635-81656

**Open questions.**
- Is `PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider` null on a Steam client? If yes, `SendText` shout collapses to a `targetPeerID 0` broadcast (:42002-42005) and shout-as-command becomes fully viable even solo — a total reversal of this ruling and by far the highest-value single test in this document, because it would give the mod a free-text command channel and make most of the janky schemes unnecessary. IN-GAME: prefix `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` on the server, have a SOLO player type a plain sentence and a `/s` shout, and see whether `"ChatMessage"` arrives.

## 167. Ward toggle as a switch (and ward data as the permission source)

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

Using a guard stone's Enable/Permit buttons as a portal command — dead as an RPC intercept, fine as a ZDO poll, and far more valuable as the source of portal permissions.

**How it works.** RPC PATH (ruled out): `PrivateArea` registers `"ToggleEnabled"` and `"TogglePermitted"` on its own ZNetView in `Awake` (:137200-137201); `Interact` sends them with `m_nview.InvokeRPC(...)` (:137370-137392), targeting the ward ZDO's OWNER — normally the interacting player, so the RPC is handled locally and never hits the wire (:83587-83594). Even when it crosses, the server's `HandleRoutedRPC` needs `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zdo)` non-null (:83659) and it never is (`Game.FixedUpdate` pin :100465). A patch on `RPC_ToggleEnabled`/`RPC_TogglePermitted` compiles and never fires. Worse, both handlers IGNORE the routed `uid` and act on the payload `playerID` (:137399-137421), so sender hardening buys nothing.

ZDO PATH (works): every field is plain ZDO data. `ZDOVars.s_enabled` (:78423) — the on/off state. `ZDOVars.s_permitted` (:78529) — the permitted COUNT; entries are raw runtime-concatenated string keys `"pu_id" + i` (long) and `"pu_name" + i` (string), with id==0 skipped on read (`SetPermittedPlayers` :137338-137347, `GetPermittedPlayers` :137349-137363). These have NO ZDOVars constant — hash the concatenated string. `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) and `s_creatorName` (:78397) give the builder.

SO: poll `s_enabled` at 0.5 s and treat a double-toggle within 5 s as a command — or, far more usefully, build the SERVER-SIDE WARD MODEL portal permissions actually need: 'may this player re-dial this portal?' answered from `s_creator` plus the pu_id list, entirely from ZDO reads with no `PrivateArea` instance.

NEVER call `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` (:137547-137593): it iterates the static `m_allAreas` list populated only in `Awake` (:137197), which is permanently EMPTY on a dedicated server, so it returns true for every point — a silent allow-all that looks like a working permission check.

RADIUS is the missing piece: `PrivateArea.m_radius` is a compiled Inspector field with a class default of 10f (:137132) and no ZDO backing.

**Player experience.** You press E on your guard stone to switch it off, then E again to switch it back on within a couple of seconds. A toast reads `Portal network unlocked for 60s.` You walk to any portal inside the ward and re-dial freely. After a minute it relocks: `Relocked.`

More useful and entirely invisible: you add your friend Bjorn to the ward's permitted list the normal vanilla way (he presses E while the stone is off). From then on, when Bjorn types `>Vault` on your portal it just works, and when a stranger types it they get `Vault is warded. Ask Bjorn or Astrid.` The server derived all of that from the ward's own list without anyone configuring anything mod-specific.

That second use — ward-derived permissions — is far more valuable than ward-as-a-button. The toggle gesture is clumsy, since it disables your base's protection to press a button, and should never be a routine input.

**Failure modes.**
- `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` returns TRUE for everything server-side because `m_allAreas` is always empty (:137173, :137197, :137547) — a silent allow-all masquerading as a permission check.
- `m_radius` is Inspector data (class default 10f, :137132); hardcoding 10 will mis-cover every real ward.
- Toggling a ward off to issue a command disables base protection for the duration — a bad trade.
- Any client can add itself to an un-enabled ward's permitted list, because `RPC_TogglePermitted` gates only on `m_nview.IsOwner() && !IsEnabled()` and trusts the payload playerID (:137399-137412). Ward-derived permissions inherit that vanilla weakness.
- `pu_id<i>`/`pu_name<i>` have no ZDOVars constant; writing `s_permitted` without the matching indexed keys produces phantom entries.

**Prerequisites.** Ward ZDO index (spatial scan for guard_stone prefabs)

## 168. Feedback: the tag echo (primary confirmation surface)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

The server rewrites the portal's own `s_tag` and the vanilla client redraws the hover text from the live ZDO every frame — the fastest, most in-context confirmation available.

**How it works.** `TeleportWorld.GetHoverText` (:143453-143464) calls `GetTagInfo()`, which reads `zdo.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` FRESH on every call — no cache, no timer, no DataRevision gate. The hover UI calls it each frame the player looks at the portal, so the instant a server-written ZDO update lands the text under the crosshair changes. Sub-frame repaint, no polling on either side.

The write: `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, reply)` + `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702, mandatory or the change is lost at save) + `ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706). No ownership claim is strictly required — no ZDO setter checks ownership (`okForNotOwner` is a dead parameter, :73648) and `IncreaseDataRevision` fires regardless — but claiming (`SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, :74627/:77362) guarantees the server wins a revision race with the nearby owning client. `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) hands ownership back within 2 s, which is fine and keeps vanilla retagging working.

HARD CONSTRAINTS ON THE ECHO:
• ≤10 characters, always (the `TextInput.Show` clamp, :61515-61521).
• No rich text — `GetHoverText` runs `RemoveRichTextTags()` (:143459), regex `<[\/a-zA-Z0-9= "\"''#;:()$_-]*?>` (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703). Colour is impossible here; it IS possible on a Sign face.
• ASCII only pending a glyph test.
• Both ends of a vanilla-paired link must carry BYTE-IDENTICAL tags or `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 tears the pair down within 5 s (:100601).
• Censoring is not a concern: `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is `return text;` server-side (:94588-94591) and the censored flag is surfaced only on PlayFab (:143462).

ECHO ALPHABET (char 0 = state glyph): `>NAME` dialed · `#NAME` this portal's own name · `?NAME` unknown/ambiguous · `!NAME` denied/locked · `-` unlinked · `.NAME` pending.

**Player experience.** You are hovering the portal; the text under your crosshair reads `Teleport  Portal tag:"#Base" [Connected]`. You press E, type `>Haldor`, hit Enter. The dialog closes, you are looking at the portal again — and the text now reads `Teleport  Portal tag:">Haldor" [Connected]`. It changed while you were watching it, with no perceptible gap.

A bad name reads `"?Haldr"` instead, and the `?` tells you at a glance something is wrong before you read the toast in the corner. A portal locked against you reads `"!Vault"`.

This is the single best feedback surface available: instant, exactly where the player is already looking, and persistent — you can walk away, come back tomorrow, hover the portal, and it still tells you where it points. A toast cannot do that.

**Failure modes.**
- An echo longer than 10 characters is truncated in the rename dialog and the truncation is submitted as a command on the player's next Enter.
- Rich text is stripped, so the echo cannot use colour to distinguish states — the leading glyph is the only channel.
- Distinct per-portal echoes are incompatible with vanilla pairing (`Game.ConnectPortals` tag-equality teardown, :100601) without prefixing it out.
- Without `SetDirtyPortals()` the echo is lost at the next world save.
- A player who opens the dialog and presses OK re-submits the echo as a command unless the parser is idempotent on its own canonical strings.

**Prerequisites.** The Dial (tag CLI); Pairing takeover

**Citations.** TeleportWorld.GetHoverText / GetTagInfo — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143470, :143556-143570 · ZDO.Set (no ownership check) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73648-73654, :73721 · ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals / ForceSendZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702, :77706 · ZDO.SetOwner / ZDOMan.GetSessionID — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74627, :77362 · ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76901-76927 · StringExtensionMethods.RemoveRichTextTags — assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703 · Game.ConnectPortals tag teardown — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100601 · CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC (server stub) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:94588-94591

**Open questions.**
- Does a client already standing at a portal pick up the tag change without a zone reload? `GetHoverText` reads live so it should be immediate, but confirm the ZDO update actually reaches a client that currently OWNS the portal. IN-GAME: stand at a gate, server-write a new tag, and watch the hover.

## 169. Feedback: MessageHud toasts (the detail channel)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

Server-pushed top-left or centre-screen HUD messages, addressed to one player, localized client-side, with no length limit and no truncation trap.

**How it works.** TWO INDEPENDENT PATHS, both proven in Wonderland.

(A) PER-CHARACTER, safer. `Player.Start` registers the routed RPC `"Message"(int type, string msg, int amount)` on the player's own ZNetView and ONLY when `m_nview.IsOwner()` (:10072); `Player.RPC_Message` re-checks IsOwner before calling `MessageHud.ShowMessage` (:14820-14825). Server: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "Message", (int)MessageHud.MessageType.TopLeft, text, 0)`. Because it is registered only on the owning client it can never be delivered to the wrong player. Wonderland ships this as `PlayerNotify.Toast` (Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs:15).

(B) GLOBAL. `MessageHud.Start` registers `"ShowMessage"(int type, string text)` on `ZRoutedRpc` (:55799-55809) and `RPC_ShowMessage` calls `ShowMessage` unconditionally (:55848-55851). Server: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "ShowMessage", (int)type, text)`, or `0L` to broadcast. No ZDOID needed, so it works in the window before `peer.m_characterID` is populated.

`MessageHud.MessageType` is `TopLeft = 1, Center = 2` (:55705-55709). TopLeft stacks and persists briefly; Center is the big single-line banner vanilla uses for `$msg_blocked`. Text is run through `Localization.Localize` on the RECEIVING client, so sending `"$piece_portal"` renders in that player's own language — a free i18n path for any string with a vanilla token.

NO LENGTH LIMIT and no truncation trap, because this is one-way output that never becomes input. Use it for everything the 10 characters cannot hold: distances, biome names, error explanations, directory listings, permission reasons. Sending 5 toasts in one frame produces 5 stacked TopLeft lines — that is how a directory is delivered. Keep it to ~6 lines before they scroll off.

**Player experience.** You type `>Haldor` on the portal. As the hover flips to `">Haldor"`, a line appears in the top-left: `Dialed → Haldor · 1,140m · Black Forest`. It fades after a few seconds.

You type `?`. Six lines stack up:

`— PORTALS —`
`1 Base      612m   yours`
`2 Haldor  1,140m   public`
`3 Mine2     840m   yours`
`4 Vault   2,300m   LOCKED`
`type >1 .. >4 or >name`

You try a locked one and get a Center banner across the middle of your screen, the same one vanilla uses when a portal is blocked: `Vault is locked by Bjorn.`

This is the workhorse. It carries everything the tag cannot, needs no construction, no proximity and no learning, and it looks identical to vanilla's own messages — a player will not perceive it as 'a mod talking to me'.

**Failure modes.**
- More than ~6 stacked TopLeft lines scroll off before they can be read.
- Center messages are intrusive; overusing them for routine confirmations trains players to ignore the banner that also carries vanilla's real warnings.
- Path (A) requires `peer.m_characterID` to be populated — it is `ZDOID.None` between connect and `Game.SpawnPlayer` and again between death and respawn (:100270, :100413). Guard with `!peer.m_characterID.IsNone()` and fall back to path (B).
- Path (B) depends on a `MessageHud` existing on the RECEIVING client (it always does) but the registration is global, so another mod registering `"ShowMessage"` server-side would collide.
- Toasts are transient — a player who alt-tabs misses the only record of what happened. Pair with the persistent tag echo.

**Prerequisites.** ConnectedCharacters (peer + character ZDO pairs)

**Citations.** Player.Start "Message" registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:10072 · Player.Message / RPC_Message — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:14800-14825 · MessageHud.Start "ShowMessage" registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:55799-55809 · MessageHud.RPC_ShowMessage / ShowMessage — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:55848-55860 · MessageHud.MessageType (TopLeft=1, Center=2) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:55705-55709 · ZNetPeer.m_characterID lifecycle — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78794, :100270, :100413 · Wonderland PlayerNotify — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs:15

**Open questions.**
- Is `MessageHud.instance` non-null on a dedicated server (which would mean `"ShowMessage"` is already registered in `ZRoutedRpc.m_functions` and a mod re-registering it would throw)? `ZNet.LowDiskLeftInformer` dereferences it unguarded under IsDedicated (:80258) while `Game.UpdateSaving` guards it (:100474). IN-GAME: dump `m_functions` keys at server start.

## 170. Feedback: server-pushed map pin

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

`RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` puts a named, permanently-saved pin on a vanilla client's map plus an iconed HUD toast — with no way ever to remove it again.

**How it works.** `Game.Start` registers `"RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"(string pinName, int pinType, Vector3 pos, bool showMap)` on EVERY peer, outside any IsServer branch (:100068). The handler calls `Minimap.instance.DiscoverLocation(pos, (PinType)pinType, pinName, showMap)` and, if map mode is None, also `Player.m_localPlayer.SetLookDir(pos - playerPos, 3.5f)` — physically turning the player's head toward the target (:100823-100830).

`Minimap.DiscoverLocation` (:58334-58361): if `HaveSimilarPin(pos, type, name, save:true)` it bails (showing `$msg_pin_exist` only when showMap); otherwise `AddPin(pos, type, name, save: true, isChecked: false, 0L)`. In BOTH branches it calls `Player.m_localPlayer.Message(MessageType.TopLeft, "$msg_pin_added: " + name, 0, sprite)` — so every pin push also yields an iconed HUD toast for free.

`HaveSimilarPin` matches name AND type AND save AND `Utils.DistanceXZ < 1f` (:58363-58373), so re-pushing the identical pin with showMap:false is idempotent and silent. `AddPin` clamps an out-of-range PinType to `Icon3` and force-enables that icon's filter if the player had turned it off (:58375-58405) — the server's pins cannot be filtered away.

`Minimap.PinType` verified: Icon0=0, Icon1, Icon2, Icon3, Death=4, Bed=5, Icon4=6, Shout=7, None=8, Boss=9, Player=10, RandomEvent=11, Ping=12, EventArea=13, Hildir1-3, Memorial=17 (:56079-56099).

THE FATAL CAVEAT: `save: true` is hard-coded. The pin goes permanently into that player's own PlayerProfile map data on their disk. There is NO removal RPC anywhere in the assembly. A demolished or renamed portal leaves its pin stuck on every player's map forever, and a re-push under a new name creates a SECOND pin. This is a one-shot discovery gift, NOT a live-synced set — TortalPortal's client-side PortalMapPins rebuilds every 2 s precisely because it can add AND remove.

SANE USE: push exactly once per (player, portal) when that player first NAMES a portal, storing the pairs in mod state so a restart does not re-push.

SECOND, NON-SAVING CHANNEL: `ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons` / the `"LocationIcons"` routed RPC (:113581-113607) replaces the client's whole `m_locationIcons` dictionary, which `Minimap.UpdateLocationPins` rebuilds from every 5 s as `save:false` pins — fully server-controlled and removable, but ICON-ONLY with no name, and rendering only for names present in the client's compiled sprite list.

**Player experience.** You name your first portal: press E, type `#Base`, Enter. The hover flips to `"#Base"` and simultaneously a toast with a small map-pin icon appears: `Pin added: Base`. You open your map and there it is, a named marker at your base, exactly like one you placed yourself — because it IS a pin you now own, saved into your character file, surviving logout.

Each new portal you name drops another pin. After a week your map has every portal labelled and you never placed a pin by hand.

The ugly part arrives when you tear down the mine portal. The `Mine2` pin stays on your map forever. You can delete it manually the vanilla way but the server cannot do it for you and will never try. Rename `Mine2` to `DeepMine` and you now have two pins a metre apart.

So the mod must be conservative: one pin per portal per player, pushed once at naming time, with a toast reading `Pin added: Base (delete it yourself if you move it)`. Anything more aggressive turns the player's map into litter.

**Failure modes.**
- `save: true` is hard-coded and there is no removal RPC — every pushed pin is permanent on that player's disk.
- Renaming a portal and re-pushing creates a duplicate pin one metre from the old one, because `HaveSimilarPin` matches on name.
- `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` calls `Minimap.instance.DiscoverLocation` unguarded (:100825); harmless on a client but it means the RPC must never be sent to the server's own peer id.
- `AddPin` force-enables the icon filter (:58400-58403), overriding a player's deliberate choice to hide that pin category.
- Repeated pushes with showMap:true spam `$msg_pin_exist` and re-centre the player's map, which is intensely annoying. Always send showMap:false for routine pushes.

**Prerequisites.** Portal address book; Per-(player, portal) pushed-pin ledger persisted in mod state

**Citations.** Game.Start registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100068 · Game.RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100823-100830 · Minimap.DiscoverLocation — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:58334-58361 · Minimap.HaveSimilarPin — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:58363-58373 · Minimap.AddPin — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:58375-58406 · Minimap.PinType enum — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:56079-56099 · ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons / RPC_LocationIcons — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113581-113607 · Wonderland FirstSpawnGrant.GrantBoat — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/FirstSpawnGrant.cs:253-263

**Open questions.**
- Does `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` render identically on a PlayFab/Xbox crossplay client? Wonderland ships it behind StarterBoatMapPin but carries no dated live-test note for it. IN-GAME: push a pin, confirm it appears, log out and back in to confirm save:true persisted, then re-send the identical payload and confirm HaveSimilarPin suppresses the duplicate.
- Which names does the client's compiled `Minimap.m_locationIcons` sprite list contain? That bounds what the non-saving LocationIcons overlay can render. IN-GAME: enumerate it on a client.

## 171. Feedback: the server as a speaking voice (fabricated ChatMessage)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

One forged `"ChatMessage"` RPC yields a chat line, floating world text and a labelled animated map pin from an arbitrary named speaker.

**How it works.** `Chat.Awake` registers `"ChatMessage"(Vector3 pos, int type, UserInfo user, string text)` on `ZRoutedRpc` (:41626); `Chat.RPC_ChatMessage` hands it to `OnNewChatMessage` (:41970-41973). The server forges one: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "ChatMessage", worldPos, (int)Talker.Type.Shout, userInfo, text)` with `userInfo.Name` set to anything — `"Portal Network"`, `"The Gate"`.

WHAT ONE PACKET PRODUCES (`OnNewChatMessage` :41775-41816): `type != Ping` → `AddString(sender.UserId, text, type)`, a real persistent scrollable chat line; `AddInworldText(go, senderID, pos, type, sender, text)`, floating text at `pos` with TTL `m_worldTextTTL` = 5 s, Shout uppercased and yellow; and `Minimap.UpdateShoutPins`/`UpdatePingPins` render a large animated map pin labelled `"<Name>: <TEXT>"` for Shout or `"<Name>: PING"` for Ping (:57591-57650).

GATE: `AddInworldText` is skipped only when `Minimap.instance.m_mode == MapMode.None` AND the position is farther than `m_nomapPingDistance` (50 m) (:41808). Normal play has the small minimap up, so it always runs.

PERMISSIONS: `OnNewChatMessage` routes through `RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync` unless the sender id equals the local character — and that is a one-line stub returning Granted synchronously in 1.0.7 (:88350-88353). No mute filter to defeat, no async delay.

SANITISATION: `text.Replace('<',' ').Replace('>',' ')` (:41795-41796). No rich text — and note this mangles a `>` sigil, so strip sigils before speaking a tag string.

PING TYPE (3) is the interesting one for portals: NO chat line, world text forced to the literal `"PING"`, and a labelled map pin at the given position. So the server can drop a transient, self-expiring beacon at a portal's DESTINATION — a 'this is where you are about to go' preview that costs nothing and leaves nothing behind, unlike the permanently-saved `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` pin.

**Player experience.** You dial your portal to Haldor. Along with the tag flip and the toast, a line appears in your chat log:

`Portal Network: → HALDOR, 1,140M NNE, BLACK FOREST`

and for five seconds a yellow shout-text hangs above the portal frame saying the same thing, and a labelled marker pulses on your minimap at Haldor's position so you can see where you are about to end up. Because it went into the chat log you can scroll back ten minutes later and find out where you sent yourself.

The beacon variant: you type `>Haldor` and a Ping-type message drops a pulsing marker at the destination with no chat spam at all. You check your map, see where it is, and decide whether to step through.

The risk is tone. A server that 'speaks' in the chat log reads as a bot, and if it speaks too often players tune it out. Reserve it for consequential events: a dial confirmed, a lock changed, a portal destroyed.

**Failure modes.**
- `<` and `>` are replaced with spaces (:41795-41796), mangling any echoed sigil and ruling out rich text.
- Shout-type messages clutter the chat log; over-use trains players to ignore the channel.
- The forged speaker name is arbitrary, which is also an impersonation vector if the mod ever lets player-supplied text set it.
- Ping type suppresses the chat line entirely and forces the world text to `"PING"` — you cannot say anything with it, only point.
- `AddInworldText` is skipped in nomap worlds beyond 50 m (:41808), so the world-text half silently vanishes on those servers.

**Prerequisites.** ConnectedCharacters (peer resolution)

**Citations.** Chat.Awake "ChatMessage" registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41626 · Chat.RPC_ChatMessage — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41970-41973 · Chat.OnNewChatMessage — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41775-41816 · Chat.m_worldTextTTL — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41594 · Minimap.UpdateShoutPins / UpdatePingPins — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:57591-57650 · RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync (stub) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:88350-88353 · Chat.SendPing (the Ping type reference) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:42058-42071

## 172. Feedback: floating world text over a portal (RPC_DamageText)

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

Arbitrary text hovering in 3D above any object within 30 m of the viewer, addressed to one player — the only surface that says WHICH portal changed.

**How it works.** `DamageText.Awake` registers the routed RPC `"RPC_DamageText"(ZPackage)` (:46352-46356). Payload is `{int TextType, Vector3 pos, string text, bool mySelf}`; `RPC_DamageText` localizes the string and hands it to `AddInworldText` (:46494-46510). Server side:

  var p = new ZPackage();
  p.Write((int)DamageText.TextType.Bonus);
  p.Write(portalPos + Vector3.up * 2.2f);
  p.Write("→ HALDOR");
  p.Write(false);
  ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_DamageText", p);

`TextType` is `Normal, Resistant, Weak, Immune, Heal, TooHard, Blocked, Bonus` (:46309-46319). `Bonus` is the attention-grabber — orange, 1.5× font, ~3 s. AVOID `TooHard` and `Blocked`: those branches overwrite or prefix the string with `$msg_toohard` / `$msg_blocked:`, mangling whatever you sent. `Heal` is green and reads as positive confirmation; `Immune`/`Weak` have distinct colours usable as a status palette.

CULLING: `m_maxTextDistance = 30f` (:46338) plus `Hud.IsUserHidden()`. Beyond 30 m nothing renders — strictly a 'label the thing in front of you' channel.

WHY USE IT over a toast: it is anchored in 3D to a specific object. With three portals side by side, a toast saying `Dialed → Haldor` does not tell you WHICH portal changed; a Bonus text over the middle one does. On entering a hub, push one DamageText per portal in range naming its current destination and the whole hub is annotated in-world for three seconds without hovering anything.

Strictly per-peer — send only to the player who acted, so a hub does not spam text for everyone standing there.

**Player experience.** You walk into your portal hall — six portals in a row in a stone building. You crouch (the arming gesture). For three seconds a line of orange text pops above each frame:

`→ BASE`   `→ HALDOR`   `→ MINE2`   `→ BOG`   `— UNLINKED —`   `LOCKED: VAULT`

Then it fades. You know instantly which door goes where without hovering six objects one at a time. You walk into the third one.

When you dial a portal, a green `→ HALDOR` floats up out of its frame — the same visual language as a heal number, which every player already reads as 'good thing happened here'.

The best surface in this list for disambiguating which object a command applied to, and it costs one small RPC.

**Failure modes.**
- 30 m culling (`m_maxTextDistance`, :46338) means nothing renders for a distant portal — useless for remote feedback.
- `TextType.TooHard` overwrites the string with `$msg_toohard` and `Blocked` prefixes `$msg_blocked:` — both mangle the payload.
- Text is localized on the client, so a raw string containing a `$` prefix that happens to match a token is substituted unexpectedly.
- Broadcasting instead of per-peer spams everyone standing at a hub.
- The payload is hand-packed into a ZPackage; a field-order mistake produces garbage with no error.

**Prerequisites.** ConnectedCharacters (peer resolution); Portal address book

**Citations.** DamageText.Awake registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46352-46356 · DamageText.ShowText / RPC_DamageText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46486-46510 · DamageText.AddInworldText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46395-46445 · DamageText.TextType enum — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46309-46319 · DamageText.m_maxTextDistance — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46338

**Open questions.**
- Does `Bonus` text render legibly against a lit portal at 2.2 m above the frame, or does it clip into the portal's own emissive glow? Purely visual. IN-GAME: push one and look.

## 173. Feedback: status effect as a persistent state indicator

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small-medium

The server grants a vanilla status effect so the player carries a buff icon representing portal state — the only indicator that survives walking away from the portal.

**How it works.** `SEMan` registers `"RPC_AddStatusEffect"(int nameHash, bool resetTime, int itemLevel, float skillLevel, int variant)` on the character's own ZNetView (SEMan shares `Character.m_nview`) (:28724-28729). Server: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "RPC_AddStatusEffect", nameHash, true, 0, 0f, -1)`. `Internal_AddStatusEffect` (:28831-28850) resolves the hash purely against the RECEIVING client's own `ObjectDB.m_StatusEffects`, so only effects every vanilla client already ships can be granted. Wonderland ships this as `StatusEffectRpc.Grant` (Core/Data/StatusEffectRpc.cs:27) with a `StatusEffectRegistry` keyed on `effect.name` (not `m_name`).

WHAT IT BUYS: a persistent, always-visible UI element where the player is already trained to look — the buff bar — with an icon and a countdown, that survives walking away. Nothing else in the zero-client toolkit gives persistent per-player UI state.

THE HARD LIMIT: there is NO RemoveStatusEffect RPC anywhere in the assembly. A granted effect can only be allowed to expire. So the vocabulary is restricted to short, self-expiring effects, and 'armed' must be a re-pinged short buff rather than a toggle. `BuffRosterEngine` is the reference re-ping loop: `RepingInterval = clamp(ttl*0.4, 0.2, ttl-0.2)`, decremented by real frame dt (Wonderland Subsystems/StatusEffects/BuffRosterEngine.cs:121).

The semantics are borrowed, not authored: granting `Rested` to mean 'armed' is a lie the game acts on (it actually gives regen). Pick effects whose mechanical side-effect is harmless or thematically apt — an asset question, not a code one.

**Player experience.** You crouch near a portal. A new icon appears in your buff bar with a short timer. You now know, without looking at the portal or reading anything, that the server is listening — and the timer tells you how long before it stops.

You pick a destination and stand up; the icon fades. You walk through the portal. On arrival a different icon appears for ten seconds — the server's way of saying 'this trip was logged'.

Honestly the weakest feedback channel here. The icon has a vanilla meaning players already know, and using `Rested` to mean 'portal armed' confuses people who then wonder why they are getting regen. Its one real strength is persistence — the only indicator that stays on screen after you stop looking at the portal — so it is worth exactly one slot, for the armed state, and nothing else.

**Failure modes.**
- No RemoveStatusEffect RPC exists — an effect can only expire, so every state must be modelled as a re-pinged short buff.
- Effect semantics are borrowed: any effect chosen carries its real gameplay side-effect (regen, resistance, movement) which the player will notice and misattribute.
- Only effects present in the client's `ObjectDB.m_StatusEffects` can be granted; no novel icon or name is possible.
- `ObjectDB.instance` is frequently still null at the ZNetScene.Awake 'world ready' hook (live-confirmed in Wonderland 2026-09-11) — any registry build must retry per tick until it resolves.
- A re-ping loop that stalls leaves the icon showing a stale state for up to the effect's full TTL.

**Prerequisites.** StatusEffectRpc + StatusEffectRegistry (Wonderland); A per-player re-ping loop
