## 174. Feedback: forced teleport as the delivery mechanism

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

Skip the portal entirely — the server moves the player with a routed RPC, visually indistinguishable from a portal transit, but bypassing every vanilla rule.

**How it works.** TWO INDEPENDENT PATHS against a 100% vanilla client.
(A) `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, true)` — `Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer` is `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport);` with no sender, admin, key or item check (:41962-41968), registered in `Chat.Awake` on every client (:41627). The server needs no `Chat.instance`: `Chat.TeleportPlayer` is a one-line wrapper (:41957-41960) and `InvokeRoutedRPC` with `targetPeerID != m_id` never touches a local handler.
(B) `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, true)` — `Character.RPC_TeleportTo` is registered on every Character in `Character.Awake` (:886) and gates on `m_nview.IsOwner()` (:4126-4132), so it can only move that character on its own owner.

WHY IT LOOKS LIKE A PORTAL: `Hud.UpdateBlackScreen` picks the teleport swirl purely from `ShowTeleportAnimation()` = `m_teleporting && m_distantTeleport` (:47872, :15386), and `TeleportWorld.Teleport` passes `distantTeleport: true` (:143546). A forced teleport with `true` is byte-for-byte the same experience — same black screen, same swirl, same ~8 s duration. Nothing to add, nothing missing.

ALWAYS PASS TRUE. With `false`, if `ZoneSystem.FindFloor` misses at the destination the client rubber-bands the player back to the origin and shows `$msg_portal_blocked` (:15369-15374) — a lie that will be reported as a mod bug. With `true` it cannot fail: the 15 s fallback force-lands on `GetSolidHeight + 0.5` (:15360-15366).

MANDATORY SERVER PRE-CHECKS, all off the character ZDO: `GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)` (:78403) — `UpdateTeleport` runs only inside the `!IsDead()` branch of `Player.FixedUpdate` (:10213, :10226), so a teleport to a dead player latches `m_teleporting` and never executes. `GetBool(ZDOVars.s_inBed)` (:78457) — `UpdateAttach` (:10217) runs BEFORE `UpdateTeleport` (:10226) and re-snaps to the attach point every tick, and `AttachStop` early-returns while `m_sleeping` (:15892), so a sleeping player is stuck outright. And your own cooldown table: `Player.TeleportTo` returns false with NO message if `IsTeleporting()` or `m_teleportCooldown < 2f` (:15309-15316), and the cooldown is zeroed every tick while teleporting (:15331-15336), so the real dead window is the whole ~8 s trip plus 2 s. `m_teleporting` is a private compiled bool never written to any ZDO (:9901) — the server can NEVER see it. Space forced teleports ≥12 s.

**Player experience.** You crouch at the portal, pick Haldor, and instead of walking through the frame the screen goes black with the same swirling teleport animation you have seen a thousand times. Eight seconds later you are standing outside Haldor's tent. If you did not know a mod was involved you would assume you had walked into a portal.

The difference you might notice: you did it carrying a full stack of iron and nothing stopped you.

Try again immediately and nothing at all happens — no message, no error, no swirl. That is vanilla's 2-second cooldown silently eating the request, and the server has no way to know. A good mod tracks its own send times and says `Wait 9s` instead of leaving you confused.

Best used NOT as the primary movement — walking into a portal is more satisfying and free — but as the escape hatch: 'send me home', the admin rescue, the 'you fell out of the world' recovery.

**Failure modes.**
- Bypasses `NoPortals`, `NoBossPortals`, ward checks and `Inventory.IsTeleportable` entirely; every rule must be re-implemented, and the ore check CANNOT be because the server never holds the player's inventory.
- Silent failure in both directions: `TeleportTo` returns false, both handlers discard it (:41966, :4130), and no reply is ever sent. The only after-the-fact signal is the character ZDO position changing ~2 s later.
- The cooldown window is the whole teleport plus 2 s (≥10 s), not 2 s after the RPC — anything retrying faster burns every retry.
- A dead player latches `m_teleporting` true and never advances; check `ZDOVars.s_dead` first.
- An attached player ping-pongs between attach point and target every tick; a sleeping one is stuck outright. Check `ZDOVars.s_inBed`.
- `distantTeleport: false` rubber-bands the player back with a misleading `$msg_portal_blocked`.

**Prerequisites.** ConnectedCharacters (peer + character ZDO); Mod-side per-player teleport cooldown table

**Citations.** Chat.TeleportPlayer / RPC_TeleportPlayer — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41957-41968, registration :41627 · Character.Awake "RPC_TeleportTo" registration / RPC_TeleportTo — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:886, :4126-4132 · Player.TeleportTo — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15302-15327 · Player.UpdateTeleport — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15329-15378 · Player.FixedUpdate (UpdateAttach before UpdateTeleport, !IsDead gate) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:10213-10226 · Player.ShowTeleportAnimation / Hud.UpdateBlackScreen — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15386-15393, :47855-47880 · TeleportWorld.Teleport distantTeleport:true — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143546 · ZDOVars.s_dead / s_inBed — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78403, :78457 · Player.AttachStop (m_sleeping early-return) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15890-15918

**Open questions.**
- Does a vanilla client complete a forced distantTeleport into a never-visited, ungenerated zone within the 15 s fallback on low-end hardware? The gates are clear in code but terrain-generation latency is empirical. IN-GAME: force-teleport a test player 8 km into unexplored Ashlands and time the black screen; confirm no fall damage and no '$msg_portal_blocked'.

## 175. Feedback: global keys as a world-wide state signal (and their silence)

`FEASIBLE` · `CLIENT-HONOURED` · effort: small

Server-set global keys that a vanilla client honours exactly as it honours vanilla's own boss gating — the only truly global lever, and it comes with no UI at all.

**How it works.** `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(string)` is a one-liner over `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey", name)` (:115943-115946); on the server the target resolves to itself, `RPC_SetGlobalKey` runs synchronously (:116022-116029) and calls `SendGlobalKeys(0L)`, broadcasting the WHOLE key set (:113466-113471). Each client's `RPC_GlobalKeys` clears and rebuilds its local set (:113473-113481). One routed-RPC hop, no timer — connected players update essentially instantly, no relog.

KEYS: `NoPortals` (32), `NoBossPortals` (33), `DungeonBuild` (34), `TeleportAll` (35) — all below `NonServerOption` (41), so `GlobalKeyAdd` mirrors them into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys`, persists them in the .fwl and shows them in the browser modifiers badge (:113483-113513). For a SESSION-ONLY key, call the publicized `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` + `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` instead of `SetGlobalKey`.

READS: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` checks `NoPortals` → `$msg_blocked` and `NoBossPortals && (GetBossEvent() != null || activeBosses > 0)` → `$msg_blockedbyboss`, both LIVE at the instant of transit (:143523, :143528). `Inventory.IsTeleportable` honours `TeleportAll` (:68869) — but only AFTER rejecting any item with `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` (:68862-68868), so it is not 'allow everything'.

THE UX PROBLEM, and it is severe: A VANILLA CLIENT GIVES NO WARNING. `GetHoverText` reports only connected/unconnected from `HaveTarget()` (:143453-143463) and `UpdatePortal` lights `m_target_found` purely from `IsTeleportable && TargetFound()` (:143491-143508). Neither consults either key. With `noportals` set, every portal still LOOKS connected and still glows; the player discovers the block only by walking in and getting a centre-screen `$msg_blocked`. Any affordance beyond that must come from the mod: a tag rewrite to `!CLOSED`, a sign banner, a toast on approach, or actually nulling the ZDO connections so portals visibly read `[Unconnected]`.

SECURITY: `RPC_SetGlobalKey` and `RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` have ZERO sender validation (:116022-116037). Any connected vanilla client can set or clear `noportals`/`teleportall` at will. A lockdown on these keys is one packet from being lifted unless the mod Harmony-prefixes both RPCs to drop non-server senders.

**Player experience.** A boss fight starts somewhere on the server. Every portal everywhere stops working, including yours 4 km away with no boss in sight. Your portal still glows blue and still says `[Connected]`. You walk into it and a red banner flashes: `Portals are blocked by a boss.` You walk in again to check. Same banner. No way to tell how long or why.

That is vanilla. With the mod layered on, the moment the key flips your portal's tag is rewritten to `!BOSS` and a toast reads `Portals closed: Bonemass is awake (4,100m SW). Reopens when the fight ends.` The glow is unchanged — the server cannot touch that — but you know exactly what happened.

The clearest case in this document of the mod's real job being to ADD THE MISSING FEEDBACK to a vanilla mechanism that is otherwise silently confusing.

**Failure modes.**
- Zero client-side affordance: portals still glow and read [Connected] while blocked (:143453-143508). The mod must supply every signal itself.
- `RPC_SetGlobalKey`/`RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` accept any sender (:116022-116037) — any client can lift a lockdown.
- `SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` stringifies to PascalCase `"NoPortals"` while the store holds lowercase, so `RPC_SetGlobalKey`'s dedupe guard never trips and every call re-broadcasts the whole key list. Pass lowercase literals or pre-check with `GetGlobalKey`.
- Setting a portal key at runtime permanently edits the world: `GlobalKeyAdd` mirrors ordinals <41 into `m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113511) which is written to the .fwl at the next autosave. Removing the mod later leaves `noportals` baked in.
- `ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys` wipes ordinals 0..40 on every world load (:115906-115910); mod-owned keys must be reapplied in a POSTFIX on it.
- `NoBossPortals` is a world-wide blackout the moment ANY boss anywhere is alerted, and `activeBosses` is maintained by whichever client has the boss loaded — a crash mid-fight can leave it stuck above zero and portals permanently blocked.
- `TeleportAll` does not lift the `m_toolTier >= 1000` gate (:68862-68868).

**Prerequisites.** Publicized ZoneSystem (GlobalKeyAdd / SendGlobalKeys); Postfix on ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys to re-assert; Prefix on RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey for sender hardening

**Citations.** ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115933-115946 · ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey / RPC_RemoveGlobalKey — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:116022-116037 · ZoneSystem.SendGlobalKeys / RPC_GlobalKeys — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113466-113481 · ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113483-113513 · ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115904-115931 · TeleportWorld.Teleport key checks — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143523, :143528 · TeleportWorld.GetHoverText / UpdatePortal (no key awareness) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143463, :143491-143508 · Inventory.IsTeleportable — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:68860-68880 · enum GlobalKeys — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:101270-101325

**Open questions.**
- Is `Minimap.instance` genuinely non-null on a 1.0.7 headless server? `GlobalKeyAdd` tails into `Game.UpdateWorldRates` → `UpdateNoMap` which dereferences it unguarded (:101203). Wonderland calls `GlobalKeyAdd` live on a dedicated server, which is strong indirect evidence. IN-GAME: run `setkey noportals` on the dedicated console and confirm no NRE.

## 176. Feedback: server-driven VFX/SFX at the portal

`CAVEATS` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: small

The server broadcasts `"SpawnObject"` with a vanilla effect prefab hash and a vanilla client plays it locally — the only non-textual acknowledgement available.

**How it works.** `ZNetScene.Awake` registers the routed RPC `"SpawnObject"(Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, int prefabHash)` (:81954); `RPC_SpawnObject` does a bare `UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(GetPrefab(prefabHash), pos, rot)` and logs `"Missing prefab <hash>"` on an unknown hash (:82355-82366). Server: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "SpawnObject", pos, rot, "vfx_name".GetStableHashCode())`. Wonderland ships this working in `VacuumEngine.PlayVacuumEffect` (Subsystems/ItemFlow/VacuumEngine.cs:162, RPC at :199) with `vfx_fermenter_add` / `sfx_fermenter_add`, sent per-peer to everyone within 80 m.

NEVER use a ZNetView-bearing prefab — each recipient would independently Instantiate and create a duplicate ZDO. Effect prefabs (`vfx_*`, `sfx_*`) are non-networked and safe. A server-side `Object.Instantiate` of an effect reaches nobody, so the RPC is the only path.

USE: a flare when a hub rotates, a puff when a portal locks, a sound cue confirming a gesture. This matters most for gesture inputs (jump, crouch, emote) where a corner toast is easy to miss while you are watching your own character.

IMPORTANT NON-CAPABILITY: the portal's own visual state is untouchable. `TeleportWorld.m_connected` (EffectList) and `m_target_found` (EffectFade) are driven by `UpdatePortal` on a 0.5 s `InvokeRepeating` reading `HaveTarget()` and `Player.GetClosestPlayer(...).IsTeleportable(...)` (:143491-143508), and `Update` lerps `m_colorAlpha` into the model's `_EmissionColor` (:143511-143515) — all plain Inspector references with zero networking. The server cannot make a portal glow or change colour directly.

BUT THERE IS AN INDIRECT PATH WORTH USING: `UpdatePortal` fires `m_connected.Create(...)` when `HaveTarget()` newly flips true (:143497-143500). So nulling and re-establishing a portal's ZDO connection makes every nearby client replay the portal's own 'connected' effect, in the portal's own visual language, within 0.5 s.

**Player experience.** You jump three times in front of your portal. Rather than squinting at a corner toast, you hear a soft chime and see a small puff of particles at the portal's base each time your selection advances. When you commit, a bigger flare goes off and the portal's own blue connection effect fires — the same one you see when a portal first links up — because the server briefly cleared and reset the connection.

It reads as the portal responding to you, in the portal's own visual language, with no HUD involved. The closest this toolkit ever gets to feeling like a designed feature rather than a bolted-on mod.

**Failure modes.**
- Using a ZNetView-bearing prefab creates one duplicate ZDO per recipient — permanent world pollution.
- An unknown hash silently logs `"Missing prefab"` on the client and plays nothing; the server gets no error.
- Effect prefab names are Unity asset data; a name that exists on the client may not resolve on the server for hashing purposes (hashing is name-based so it does not matter, but choosing a name requires a client-side dump).
- The indirect 'replay the connect effect' trick costs a real connection round-trip — nulling a connection makes the portal briefly unusable and, if `Game.ConnectPortals` has not been prefixed out, invites vanilla to re-pair it randomly.
- Per-peer distance gating is the mod's job; broadcasting plays the effect for players nowhere near the portal.

**Prerequisites.** ConnectedCharacters (peer resolution + distance gate); A vetted list of effect prefab names

**Citations.** ZNetScene.Awake "SpawnObject" registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81954 · ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82355-82366 · ZNetScene.GetPrefab(int) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82045-82052 · TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal (m_connected fires on HaveTarget flip) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143491-143509 · TeleportWorld.Update (_EmissionColor lerp) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143511-143515 · Wonderland VacuumEngine.PlayVacuumEffect — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/ItemFlow/VacuumEngine.cs:162, :199

**Open questions.**
- Does `RPC_SpawnObject` accept an arbitrary effect prefab hash on a 1.0.7 vanilla client with no server-side instance present? VacuumEngine only exercises two fermenter effects. IN-GAME: send a portal-flavoured vanilla effect hash at a portal position and confirm it plays; also confirm whether the prefab must exist in the SERVER's `ZNetScene.m_prefabs` for the hash to be meaningful, or only the client's.
- Which `vfx_`/`sfx_` names resolve through `GetPrefab`? IN-GAME: dump `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefabNames()` (:82345) and grep for portal-adjacent effects.

## 177. RECOMMENDED — "The Dial": tag CLI + sign terminal + map ping + gesture arming

`FEASIBLE` · `SERVER-ENFORCED` · effort: large

One coherent scheme: the portal's own rename box is the command line, a wall of signs is the screen, the map ping is the pointer, crouch arms and jumps navigate — with tag echo, HUD toasts and in-world text as three feedback layers.

**How it works.** L0 — PAIRING TAKEOVER. Harmony prefix `Game.ConnectPortals` (:100589) returning false; re-implement its two passes over `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648) for UNMANAGED portals only, faithfully including the `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` guard (:100609) and the phase-0 force-commit (:100690). This removes the 5 s tag-equality teardown (:100601) that otherwise makes per-portal display tags impossible.

L1 — STATE. Address book `{name → (worldPos rounded to 0.5 m, ownerPlayerId, locked, wardPos)}` persisted to a per-world mod file (write-temp then File.Replace). NEVER key by ZDOID — `ZDO.Load` renumbers every uid (:74552), the exact bug TortalPortal's Favorites.cs hit and fixed by switching to rounded position. Re-resolve positions to live ZDOs from `GetPortalList()` each tick.

L2 — INPUT, four channels into one dispatcher.
(a) TAG CLI (primary). Postfix `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` (:74225), filter `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(GetPrefab())` (:100021), diff `GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)`. Grammar ≤10 chars: `#NAME` name · `>NAME`/`>N` dial · `-` unlink · `!` lock · `?` help+directory · `@spawn`/`@haldor` world target.
(b) SIGN TERMINAL (rich). Same postfix on Sign prefabs, 50-char budget (:141756), full-word commands. The control sign is the lowest-y adopted sign within 8 m.
(c) MAP PING (freehand). Prefix `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` (:83646) on `"ChatMessage".GetStableHashCode()`, `type == 3`; snapshot/restore `m_parameters.GetPos()`. Route the player's last-touched portal to the nearest managed portal within 64 m of the ping x/z. Acts only while ARMED.
(d) GESTURE (hands-free). Prefix `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632) on `"SetTrigger"` for `"jump"` (:3483)/`"dodge"` (:15196); crouch bit from `characterZdo.GetInt(438569 + Animator.StringToHash("crouching"))` (:87144, :87270, :9984) at 0.2 s. Crouch within 6 m of a managed portal = ARM (15 s auto-disarm); jump = advance; un-crouch on a shown candidate = commit.

L3 — ACTION, one atomic routine: `SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` (:74627/:77362) → `SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, destId)` (:73656) → `Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, echo)` (≤10 ASCII chars, no `<`) → `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702) → `ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706) → PRE-WARM `ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, destId)` (:77714) so `TargetFound()` (:143640) succeeds on the first walk-through. Budget bulk operations at ≤256 broadcasts per sweep (Wonderland StructureUpkeep's lesson).

L4 — OUTPUT, three layers per action: TAG ECHO (instant, in-context, persistent — `GetHoverText` reads the ZDO fresh each frame, :143453); TOAST via `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "Message", 1, text, 0)` (:10072, :14820) for the detail 10 chars cannot hold; WORLD TEXT via `"RPC_DamageText"` `TextType.Bonus` at `portalPos + up*2.2` (:46352, :46494) to say WHICH portal. Plus, once per (player, portal) at naming time only, `"RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"` (:100068) for a saved map pin — never repeated, because no removal RPC exists.

PERMISSIONS from ward ZDO data: `s_creator` (:78393) + `s_permitted`/`pu_id<i>` (:78529, :137349). Never call `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` — `m_allAreas` is empty server-side and it is a silent allow-all (:137547).

DISCOVERABILITY, the honest weak point, attacked four ways: every unnamed portal gets its tag seeded to `?help`; `?` dumps the grammar as six toasts; the first sign built within 8 m of a managed portal is rewritten once into a help card; a one-line login toast `Portals: press E on any portal and type ? for help.` Four independent chances to stumble in, all inside the game.

**Player experience.** FIRST CONTACT. You log in. One line top-left: `Portals: press E on any portal and type ? for help.` You forget about it.

Later you build a portal. Hovering it, the tag reads `"?help"` — the server seeded it. You press E out of curiosity (the box is already familiar), clear it, type `?`, Enter. Six lines stack up:
`— PORTALS — you have 0 named` / `#name  name this portal` / `>name  dial to a portal` / `?  this help` / `- unlink   ! lock` / `or write a sign under it`

NAMING. You type `#Base`. The hover flips to `"#Base"` before you finish reading it. Toast: `Named: Base. Pin added to your map.` You open the map; a labelled pin sits at your base.

DIALLING. You run to your mine, build a portal, press E, type `>Base`, Enter. ~200 ms later the hover reads `">Base"`, the portal fires its blue connect effect, a toast reads `Dialed → Base · 840m · Meadows`, and an orange `→ BASE` floats over the frame for three seconds. You step through and it works first try — the destination ZDO was pre-sent.

GROWING INTO IT. Later, eleven portals. You build a column of four signs beside your hub and walk away; ten seconds later they show a live directory, page 1 of 3, updating whenever anyone changes anything. You write `dial Haldor and lock` on the bottom sign; it repaints to `→ HALDOR 1.2km LOCKED to you` and the portal follows.

SOMEWHERE NEW. You crouch at the portal (toast: `Armed`), press M, middle-click a spot in the Plains, close the map. Toast: `Dialed → Tarpit (3,410m).` You un-crouch. The arming step is what stops your hub re-routing itself every time someone pings during a raid.

HANDS FULL. Carrying a full load, you crouch at the hub and jump-jump-jump through the list watching the toast tick `1/6 Base`, `2/6 Haldor`, `3/6 Mine2`, then un-crouch on the one you want. Six seconds, no menu, no typing.

WHEN IT GOES WRONG. Typo: hover flips to `"?Halod"`, toast `No portal "Halod". Did you mean Haldor?`, nothing broke. Locked: hover reads `"!Vault"`, Center banner `Vault is locked by Bjorn.` Boss up: hover reads `"!BOSS"`, toast `Portals closed: Bonemass is awake. Reopens after the fight.` — feedback vanilla never gives you.

HONEST JANK RATING vs. a real client UI. The tag CLI is 3/10 — it reuses the exact vanilla interaction (press E on a portal, type a name) and only changes what the name MEANS, so it barely registers as a workaround. The sign terminal is 4/10 and genuinely charming. The ping is 2/10 and the fastest thing here. Crouch-and-jump is 7/10 and deliberately optional, for people who already know. TortalPortal's real client UI — a scrollable destination window with live 3D previews and favourites — is strictly better as an interface; what The Dial buys instead is that every player on the server gets it immediately with nothing to install, and the server is genuinely the authority rather than politely asking clients to behave.

**Failure modes.**
- Echo strings >10 chars are truncated in the rename dialog and can be re-submitted as garbage commands; the parser must also be idempotent on its own canonical echoes.
- Taking over `Game.ConnectPortals` means the mod now owns correctness for UNMANAGED portals too — a bug there breaks vanilla portal behaviour server-wide.
- Four input channels feeding one dispatcher creates ordering ambiguity: a player who pings while crouched and jumping produces three commands in ~200 ms. Serialize per-player with a 500 ms debounce and act on the last one.
- The armed state is the load-bearing safety mechanism; if the 15 s auto-disarm or the 6 m proximity gate is wrong, hubs re-route themselves during normal play and the mod will be perceived as haunted.
- Ownership churn: `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) returns portal ownership to nearby players every 2 s, so every write must be self-contained (claim, write, ForceSendZDO) and never assume a held claim.
- Without `SetDirtyPortals()` on every tag write, the entire naming layer silently evaporates at the next world save (:77621, :76702).
- Map pins are permanent and unremovable — a single over-eager push loop litters every player's map forever.
- Discoverability remains the genuine risk: all four bootstrap paths are passive, and a player who ignores the login toast and never presses E on a portal out of curiosity never finds the system.

**Prerequisites.** Prefix on Game.ConnectPortals plus a re-implementation of vanilla pairing for unmanaged portals; ZDO.Deserialize postfix (portal + sign prefabs); ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC and RPC_RoutedRPC prefixes; Position-keyed address book persisted per world; Wonderland Core/Data: ConnectedCharacters, PlayerNotify, ZdoSpatialQuery, and the SubsystemRegistry/Heartbeat lifecycle; Ward ZDO index for permissions

**Citations.** Game.ConnectPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589-100627, :100601, :100609, :100690 · ZDOMan.GetPortalList / SetDirtyPortals / ForceSendZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77648, :76702, :77706, :77714 · ZDO.Deserialize — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74225-74232 · ZDO.Load uid renumbering — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74552 · Game.PortalPrefabHash — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100021 · ZDO.SetConnection / SetOwner / ZDOMan.GetSessionID — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73656, :74627, :77362 · TeleportWorld.GetHoverText / TargetFound — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143464, :143640-143657 · Sign.m_characterLimit / SetText / UpdateText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:141756, :141915-141929, :141835-141865 · ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC / RPC_RoutedRPC — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83646-83665, :83632-83644 · Chat.SendPing — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:42058-42071 · ZSyncAnimation.SetTrigger / SetBool / c_ZDOSalt — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87260-87263, :87270-87281, :87144 · Character.ForceJump / Player dodge / Player.s_crouching — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:3483, :15196, :9984 · Player.Start "Message" / RPC_Message — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:10072, :14820-14825 · DamageText.Awake / RPC_DamageText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46352-46356, :46494-46510 · Game.Start / RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100068, :100823-100830 · PrivateArea.GetPermittedPlayers / CheckAccess — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:137349-137363, :137547-137593 · ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76901-76927 · Wonderland StructureUpkeep broadcast budget — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/StructureUpkeep.cs:29-40

**Open questions.**
- Does GuiInputField clamp a programmatically assigned `.text` to characterLimit? The whole ≤10-char echo discipline rests on it. IN-GAME: server-write a 20-char tag and open the dialog on a vanilla client.
- Is `PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider` null on Steam? If yes, shout becomes a free-text server input (:42002-42005) and the sign terminal and gesture layers become largely unnecessary. Highest-value single test.
- Does a client already standing at a portal pick up a server-side tag AND connection change without leaving and returning? `GetHoverText` reads live and `Teleport` re-reads the connection at transit (:143539), so it should, but confirm against a client that currently OWNS the portal ZDO.
- Which prefabs are in `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (:99828)? IN-GAME: log `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` resolved through `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)?.name` at world-ready.

# Domain notes

THE ONE LOAD-BEARING FACT. Vanilla's runtime reconciler `Game.ConnectPortals()` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589-100626, body read directly and reproduced below) never checks reciprocity. Pass 1's teardown predicate is exactly `zDO == null || zDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) != @string || zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal) == ZDOID.None` (:100600-100604) — it validates that the TARGET exists, shares the tag, and has SOME non-None connection, and nothing else. Pass 2 only touches portals whose own connection IsNone() (:100609). Consequently every non-reciprocal directed topology — fan-in stars, rings, chains with a terminator, in-trees, sinks — is a FIXED POINT of vanilla's own 5-second coroutine, requiring no Harmony patch, no faster tick and no race. That single omission is what makes a zero-client-install portal-topology mod possible at all. Contrast ZDOMan.ConvertPortals (:77812-77848), the pre-NewSaveFormat migration, which DID require `A.tag == B.tag && A.target == B && B.target == A`; the modern runtime pass deliberately relaxed it.

THE THREE INVARIANTS every managed topology must satisfy, at all times, for every member:
(1) the member's target ZDO resolves in ZDOMan;
(2) `target.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` is byte-identical to the member's own s_tag (ordinal, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant, default "" so all untagged portals are one group);
(3) `target.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != ZDOID.None`.
Violate any one and the edge is nulled within 5 s, and the freed end is then randomly re-paired inside its tag group by `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` using the shared `UnityEngine.Random` stream (:100664-100679). Invariant (3) is why every chain needs a terminator and why "just set the connection to None to disable a portal" does not work.

THE HARD CEILING. One `ZDOConnection {readonly ConnectionType m_type; readonly ZDOID m_target;}` per ZDO, stored in `ZDOExtraData.s_connections : Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` (:74794-74797, :75524-75534). One destination, ever. Every "many destinations from one place" shape in this catalogue is therefore a Portal Bank (N physical portals), a Switchboard (repointed between transits) or a Carousel (repointed on a timer). Simultaneous fan-out and simultaneous full mesh are structurally impossible, not merely unimplemented. Full mesh over S sites via banks costs S×(S−1) portals; the hub+bank hybrid costs 2S for two-hop any-to-any and is the recommended shape.

PERSISTENCE IS THE OTHER CEILING, AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE FIRST. The network wire format carries the real ZDOID (`ZDO.Serialize` writes `(byte)m_type` + `m_target`, :74169-74173) but the DISK format collapses each ZDO to one `ZDOConnectionHashData {type, int hash}` slot. `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461-75478, read directly) iterates s_connections and for each edge writes `hashData[source] = {type, h}` and then `hashData[target] = {type|Target, h}` — later edges overwrite earlier entries for any shared node. The disk format can only express a pairwise perfect matching. Therefore: rings >2 lose all but one link; one-way links come back BIDIRECTIONAL (`ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` at :77850-77893 writes both directions when it matches a hash pair); self-loops are erased outright (the source slot is immediately overwritten by the Target slot, :75472-75475); and everything left unmatched is randomly re-paired by `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()`, which `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` calls at :76523 immediately after the hash relink at :76515. **Every topology in this catalogue except the simple pair and the portal bank requires an unconditional re-assert at world load.** Put it in a postfix on Game.ConnectPortals or a one-shot after OnWorldReady, and note LoadChunks sets `DirtyPortalObjects = false` at :76527 so anything you write there needs `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`.

THE CHEAPEST WRITE WINDOW is the moment right after world load and before any peer connects: ZDOMan.ConnectPortals has just done `SetOwner(GetSessionID())` on both ends of every relinked pair (:77880-77881), `m_peers` is empty so `Game.SetConnection`'s `ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner) != null` test is always false and every write takes the immediate local path (:100641-100650), and ZDOs come back from `ZDO.Load` with `Owned = false; Owner = false` anyway (:74550-74556).

THE WRITE RECIPE, in order, for every managed edge: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, targetId); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);` — verbatim what Game.SetConnection does at :100643-100645. Ownership is not required for the write to land (no ZDO setter checks it; `ZDO.Set(int,int,bool okForNotOwner)` ignores its parameter entirely, :73648-73654) but is required to win the DataRevision race against the owning client, since `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` applies an incoming ZDO wholesale on a higher revision with no field-level merge (:77076-77139). `ZDO.SetConnection` already calls `IncreaseDataRevision()` and `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` for Portal-type writes (:73661-73664); a TAG-ONLY write does NOT, so a rename without an explicit `SetDirtyPortals()` is silently lost at the next world save because the entire ChunkPortal file is only emitted when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set (:77621-77635) and portals are explicitly excluded from ordinary chunk saves (:77572).

OWNERSHIP IS TRANSIENT. `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901-76926, driven by ReleaseZDOS every 2 s, :76872-76883) hands any persistent ZDO inside a peer's active area (~96-112 m) to that peer. Portals are included because `ZDOMan.FindObjects` merges `m_portalObjects[sectorIndex]` back into every sector query (:77367-77382). A server ownership claim near a player is revoked within 2 s. The written VALUE survives (it was already ForceSendZDO'd); only the next write must re-claim. For a hot loop, install the Wonderland `ZDO.SetOwner` Harmony prefix guard (Wonderland/Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313), fail fast on prefab hash, and never block `uid == 0` or `uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()`.

NEVER MOVE A PORTAL ZDO. `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for any prefab in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:73752-73756), so a repositioned portal stays filed in `m_portalObjects` under its creation-time sector forever: clients in the new zone never receive it through normal sector sync, `AddIfPortal` will double-file it if a position update arrives (:77738-77748), and `HandleDestroyedZDO` looks it up by the NEW sector index and fails to remove it (:76980-76987), leaking a dead ZDO that `GetPortalList()` and `Game.ConnectPortals()` keep processing forever. Destroy and recreate instead.

NEVER CACHE ZDO OBJECT REFERENCES ACROSS TICKS. `ZDOPool.Release`/`Get` recycles ZDO objects and `ZDO.Reset` sets `m_uid = ZDOID.None` (:78286-78311, :73536-73545). Vanilla itself violates this in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals`, which holds raw ZDO references for a full 5 s and force-writes through them in `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` (:100690-100698). Cache ZDOIDs, re-resolve every tick with `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id)`. And never persist a ZDOID as portal identity: `ZDO.Load` does `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)` (:74552), so every ZDOID in the world is renumbered on every load. Key mod state by rounded POSITION, by a mod-private ZDO field (which travels with the ZDO for free), or by a world global key.

TWO-PHASE COMMIT / THE DEFERRED-WRITE TRAP. `Game.SetConnection` routes `RPC_SetConnection` to the owning peer when that peer is connected (:100646-100649), leaving the server's own copy reading the OLD value. Pass 2, in the same tick and over the same snapshot, then sees `!IsNone()` and skips the portal — so a retag or re-pair near a standing player takes two or more ticks, not one. `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` force-commits the previous tick's proposals at the top of the next call (:100591, :100690-100698), so the server always wins within one extra tick regardless of what the client does. If you re-implement pass 2 yourself, reproduce the `IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal` guard (:100609, :100671) or you will double-pair portals owned by online peers.

ENFORCEMENT TIERS, precisely. Of TeleportWorld.Teleport's four gates (:143517-143537), exactly ONE is server-enforced: gate 1, `if (!TargetFound()) return;` (:143519) — a None connection, or a connection to a ZDO that does not resolve, blocks the transit on any client, modified or not, and does so SILENTLY (no player.Message on that path). Gates 2 and 3 read the server-owned global keys NoPortals / NoBossPortals and are client-HONOURED — and `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey`/`RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` have zero sender validation (:116022-116037) so any client can lift them. Gate 4 (`player.IsTeleportable(m_allowAllItems)`) is unreachable and un-influenceable per-portal: `m_allowAllItems` is a plain compiled Inspector field with no ZDO or RPC backing (:143429), as are `m_exitDistance` (:143413), `m_activationRange` (:143411) and every colour/effect reference. A server plugin writing them mutates a copy no client will ever read. The one documented escape is `ZNetView.LoadFields()` (:82669-82738, run from ZNetView.Awake), which reflects public instance fields off the ZDO under keys `"HasFields"`, `"HasFields<TypeName>"` and `"<TypeName>.<FieldName>"` — untested for TeleportWorld and applied only at instantiation, so out of scope for topology work but noted.

THE DISPLAY/ROUTING ASYMMETRY worth exploiting. Routing compares the RAW s_tag with bare `string !=` (:100601, :100669). Display runs it through `RemoveRichTextTags()` — `Regex.Replace(text, "<[\\/a-zA-Z0-9= \"\\\"''#;:()$_-]*?>", "")` (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703, read directly) — at TeleportWorld.GetHoverText:143459. So `"base<f:red>"` hovers as `base` but is a distinct network from `"base"`. That single fact underwrites invisible sharding, per-player namespaces, faction networks and the server-enforced lockdown. Budget: the client's tag editor is capped at 10 characters (`TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)`, :143482 → `m_inputField.characterLimit`, :61519) and pre-fills with the RAW tag (:143551-143554), so suffixes are visible in the edit box even though they are hidden in hover. RPC_SetTag itself applies no cap and no filter (:143587-143602), and `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is literally `return text;` in the server build (:94588-94591).

TAG CHANGES ARE NOT RELIABLY OBSERVABLE BY RPC. `TeleportWorld.SetText` routes `RPC_SetTag` to the ZDO's current OWNER (`ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string,...)` → `m_zdo.GetOwner()`, :82855-82858), and `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally and skips `RouteRPC` entirely when `targetPeerID == m_id` (:83588-83594) — so a client that owns the portal retags it with zero packets on the wire. Worse, even when the packet does cross, a dedicated server can never dispatch it, because `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` needs `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zdo)` (:83646-83663) and `m_instances` is permanently empty server-side. POLLING `s_tag` over `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` is mandatory; RPC interception at `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC`/`RPC_RoutedRPC` is a bonus that catches only the non-owner case. Note also the latent vanilla bug in RPC_SetTag: it calls `UpdateConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` BEFORE re-reading the connection to hand to `SetConnectedPortal` (:143595-143597), so the old partner is usually never told and is repaired only by the next 5 s sweep.

ENUMERATION IS FREE. `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648-77656) returns every portal in the world in a fresh List, always resident — portals live in their own `m_portalObjects` dictionary and their own `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal` save file, are removed from the ordinary sector array by `AddIfPortal` (:77732-77752), and are never unloaded or released (`ReleaseZDOS` only reassigns ownership, :76872-76883). `GetPortals()` (:77643-77646) returns the live dictionary, zero-alloc, for hot paths. `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:100021, filled in Game.Awake :100027-100032 from the Inspector list `m_portalPrefabs` :99828) is the authoritative "is this a portal" test and covers modded portal pieces for free — read it at runtime, never hard-code portal_wood/portal_stone. Prefab mixing is irrelevant to pairing: ConnectPortals never looks at the prefab, so wood, stone and modded portals pair freely inside one tag group.

THE PLAYER-EXPERIENCE CONSTANTS that shape every design: the destination is re-read at the instant of transit and never cached (:143539), so a server repoint applies to the very next walk-in; but `TargetFound()` requires the traveller's client to actually HOLD the destination ZDO and calls `RequestZDO` and returns false if not (:143646-143654), so the first walk-through after a re-pair to an unvisited region silently fails with NO message — pre-push with `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerID, targetId)` (:77714-77725). `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` is ENTER-ONLY (:143672-143681), so a player already standing in a portal's volume when it is repointed does not re-trigger. `Player.TeleportTo` refuses within 2 s of a previous teleport (:15302-15327) and `distantTeleport:true` — which portals always pass (:143546) — has a hard ~8 s black-screen floor plus an `IsAreaReady` gate and a 15 s force-land fallback (:15349-15366). Exit position is `targetPos + targetRot*forward*m_exitDistance + up*1.0`, where m_exitDistance is the DESTINATION portal's compiled 1.0 (:143542-143545, :143413). The hover text distinguishes only connected/unconnected (:143461) and the hover NAME is the hard-coded literal "Teleport" (:143466-143469).

WHAT THE SERVER CAN TELL THE PLAYER, since none of this shows up in the portal UI: a HUD toast via the per-character routed RPC "Message" (`ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "Message", (int)type, text, 0)`, Player.RPC_Message :14820-14825 — Wonderland/Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs); a global `"ShowMessage"` (MessageHud :55808, :55848); a SAVED, NAMED map pin via `"RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"` (registered on every peer at Game.Start :100068, handler :100823-100831, client Minimap.DiscoverLocation → AddPin(save:true)); floating world text via `"RPC_DamageText"` (:46352-46356, :46494-46510, 30 m cull); a VFX/SFX one-shot via `"SpawnObject"` (ZNetScene :81954, :82355-82366 — effect prefabs ONLY, never a ZNetView prefab); and server-written sign text (`ZDOVars.s_text` :78629, Sign repaints on a 2 s InvokeRepeating keyed on DataRevision, :141835-141865). What the player can tell the SERVER: a map ping, which is `Chat.SendPing` → routed `"ChatMessage"` at targetPeerID 0 carrying the clicked world Vector3 (:42058-42068) and therefore always reaches the server even solo; or an emote, polled off the character ZDO's `ZDOVars.s_emoteID`/`s_emote` (:78417-78419). Ordinary chat text is NOT a channel — `Chat.SendText`/`Talker.Say` target each other listed player individually (:41975-42043), so a lone player generates zero packets, and unknown slash commands are swallowed locally by `Terminal.TryRunCommand(silentFail:true)` (:41947-41955).

UNINSTALL BEHAVIOUR, summarised because it is the least obvious axis. Simple pairs and portal banks survive uninstall perfectly (they are vanilla shapes). Fan-in stars, rings, chains, in-trees and sinks survive until the next world RELOAD, at which point the hash-pair format collapses them into pairs plus random re-pairing. Tag-based sharding (per-player, faction, invisible suffixes) survives uninstall INDEFINITELY, because the partition lives in the saved s_tag strings — which is usually good but means a Tag-Scramble Lockdown left in place permanently bricks every portal on the server. Displaced Routing collapses within 5 SECONDS of uninstall, because vanilla's reconciler resumes and tears down every edge whose ends carry different display tags. Always restore a vanilla-legal configuration in `Plugin.OnDestroy`.

ADVERSARIAL NOTE. None of this is tamper-proof against a modified client. `Game.RPC_SetConnection(long sender, ZDOID portalID, ZDOID connectionID)` is registered on EVERY peer (outside the IsServer branch, :100066-100070), executes on the dedicated server, and performs no sender check, no ownership check and no prefab check (:100653-100662) — one packet rewires any portal to any ZDO. `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO` → `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76953, :76963-76999) is equally ungated and deletes any ZDO. `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77076-77139) applies any incoming ZDO wholesale on a higher DataRevision with no validation at all. The practical defence for a topology mod is not prevention but a per-tick audit: re-read every managed portal's connection and tag from `GetPortalList()`, compare against the intended graph held in mod-private ZDO keys, and re-assert. That loop is cheap (SetConnection/Set are no-ops when the value is unchanged, :74954-74957 and BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue in assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345, generating zero revision bumps and zero traffic) and it doubles as the destroyed-member self-heal every topology here needs anyway.

SCOPE CORRECTION ON THE CENTRAL CONSTRAINT. The commonly-cited framing — "the 0.5s UpdatePortal poll and the 5s reconciliation are the race window" — is wrong, and the correct numbers make dynamic routing far more viable than the framing suggests. Verified directly:

• The real swap race window is the ZDO PROPAGATION LATENCY, ~50-200ms. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` re-reads `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` fresh at the instant of transit (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143539) — nothing is cached. `ForceSendZDO` adds the id to every `ZDOPeer.m_forceSend` (:77706-77712), `AddForceSendZdos` inserts it at index 0 of the sync list (:77275), and `SendZDOToPeers2` services one peer per Update frame behind a 0.05s gate (:76837-76862).
• The change is ATOMIC from the client's point of view: the connection is a single `ZDOConnection{type, target}` written in one `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` call (:74951-74961) and serialized as one byte plus one ZDOID (`ZDO.Serialize` :74169-74173). There is no torn read.
• The 0.5s `InvokeRepeating("UpdatePortal", 0.5f, 0.5f)` (:143450) is COSMETIC ONLY — `m_connected` EffectList on the rising edge of `HaveTarget()`, and the `m_target_found` glow (:143491-143509). It does not gate teleporting.
• The 5s `Game.ConnectPortals` coroutine (:100580-100587) is not a race at all once its pass 1 is neutralised; it is an active adversary that must be displaced (Pairing Authority Takeover) or satisfied (identical tags + reciprocity).

THE FOUR REAL COSTS, in order of how much they hurt:
1. SILENT FAILURE. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` gate 1 returns with NO `player.Message` when `TargetFound()` is false (:143519-143522), and `TargetFound` is false whenever the client does not yet hold the destination ZDO (:143646-143654). Every cold re-point costs one completely unexplained dead walk-through unless the mod pre-warms with `ForceSendZDO(peerUid, destId)` (:77714). This is the number-one source of "the mod is broken" reports and must be engineered against from day one.
2. ENTER-ONLY TRIGGER. `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` fires on ENTER (:143673). A player standing inside the volume during a swap does not re-trigger and must step out and back in.
3. NO TRANSIT EVENT. The server learns a transit happened ~2.0-2.2s late at best, because `Player.UpdateTeleport` does not move the transform until `m_teleportTimer > 2f` (:15337) and a distantTeleport (always, :143546) does not complete until t>8s (:15349). Every "after one use" feature has a ~2s hole.
4. NO DELTA ENCODING. `ZDOMan.SendZDOs` re-serializes the whole ZDO per peer per send (:77056-77064) under a 10240-byte queue cap (:77011). Any mass rewrite needs a per-sweep budget (Wonderland's StructureUpkeep precedent: 256).

ON PER-PLAYER ROUTING — the honest answer. Divergent per-peer ZDO state is structurally impossible (one ZDO object, revision-only per-peer cache, ~50-100ms reconvergence). That leaves exactly two routes, and they compose:
• PHYSICAL (per-player terminals): fully solves the OUTBOUND leg. Identity is free — `Piece.SetCreator` already writes `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) equal to that player's `s_playerID` (:78539) on every portal they build. There is no access control (`PrivateArea.CheckAccess` returns true vacuously on a server, empty `m_allAreas` :137173/:137547), so it is convention, not enforcement. The INBOUND/return leg does NOT solve: one shared arrival portal has one connection field. Solving return properly costs one anchor per (player × destination), or falls back to (2).
• TEMPORAL (approach-triggered JIT): ~2.0-2.4s of lead time from a 12m arming radius at sprint speed, against a ~0.45s worst-case detect-and-write budget. Works beautifully for one player and breaks on contention, with only two bad options (mis-route the second player, or silently block both).
Combined — a personal terminal per player, plus JIT on the shared return gates — gets remarkably close to feeling per-player. The illusion breaks exactly when two players use the same physical frame within a couple of seconds.

RECOMMENDED BUILD ORDER: (1) Pairing Authority Takeover, (2) Phantom Anchor Fabrication, (3) Rotating Hub + Blackout Swap Protocol as the reference implementation and UX language, (4) Deterministic Assignment Replacement as a standalone quick win that needs none of the above, (5) everything else.

REUSE, DO NOT REBUILD: Wonderland (`/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/`) already ships every primitive — `Core/Data/ConnectedCharacters.cs` (peer + character ZDO pairs; `Player.GetAllPlayers()` is permanently empty server-side), `Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs` (HUD toasts), `Core/Data/EmoteSignals.cs` (the only reliable player→server channel, with the written post-mortem on why chat is not one), `Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:148` (`IsPortalTransit`, already false-positive-tuned in production), `Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301` (the `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix that holds a claim against `ReleaseNearbyZDOS`), `Subsystems/WorldGovernor/WorldRatesEngine.cs` (the GlobalKeyAdd + SendGlobalKeys write path), `Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43-58` (the `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` + `ZDO.Deserialize` pair — the ONLY server hook that sees a client-placed object appear). PortalLock (PAUSED) is the cautionary tale: it patched `Player.PlacePiece` and `ZNetScene.Instantiate` behind an `IsServer()` guard, a combination that can never fire once.

THREE TRAPS THAT WILL BITE EVERY OPTION: (a) never cache `ZDO` object references across ticks — `ZDOPool` recycles them and `ZDO.Reset` sets `m_uid = ZDOID.None` (:73536, :78286-78311); cache ZDOIDs and re-resolve. (b) Never key persistent state by ZDOID — `ZDO.Load` renumbers every ZDO on every world load (:74552); key by rounded position or `s_creator`. (c) A tag-only write is silently lost at the next world save unless you call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702) — only SetConnection/AddIfPortal/HandleDestroyedZDO set `DirtyPortalObjects`.

FOUR IN-GAME CHECKS GATE THE WHOLE DESIGN: (1) `Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs` / `PortalPrefabHash` contents at server start — decides what ZDOMan treats as a portal and what a fabricated anchor must use. (2) `ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances()` on a live server with players online — should be ~0, validating the entire ruled-out set. (3) `EnvMan.instance != null` and `GetDayFraction()` advancing headless — the whole scheduling family rests on it. (4) `ZDOVars.s_creator` on a freshly player-placed portal equalling that player's `s_playerID` — the whole per-player identity model rests on it.

THE ENFORCEMENT LADDER. Everything in this domain sits on exactly one of four rungs, and conflating them is the main way a server-only portal mod ends up shipping security theatre.

(1) SERVER-ENFORCED — the server owns the only copy of the state, or the client-side code path that would do the thing does not exist on the server. Genuinely unbypassable by a modified client. Only five mechanisms qualify: the Ownership Pin (retag/demolish/damage RPCs route to a server with no `ZNetScene` instance and are dropped — `ZNetView.InvokeRPC` :82855-82858 → `HandleRoutedRPC` :83656-83664, instances permanently empty because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins the reference position at :100465); the Managed Network Governor (the Portal connection is a server-written ZDO field and an unconnected portal cannot teleport anyone — gate 1 of `TeleportWorld.Teleport` :143519); the Destroy Veto (`ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO` :76953 is ZDO-less, so it actually runs on the server); Ungated RPC Hardening (prefixes on `RPC_SetGlobalKey`/`RPC_RemoveGlobalKey`/`Game.RPC_SetConnection`/`RPC_RequestZDO`, all of which run server-side and validate nothing today); and Creator Attestation (the server notarises identity at the one moment it holds the authenticated socket).

(2) CLIENT-HONOURED — the server broadcasts state that an unmodified client voluntarily obeys, exactly as it obeys vanilla's own boss gating. `NoPortals`/`NoBossPortals`/`TeleportAll`/`DungeonBuild` global keys and `ZNetView.LoadFields` per-portal field overrides live here. Honest servers get honest behaviour; a cheat client ignores all of it.

(3) REACTIVE-DETECTION-ONLY — "detect and revert". The malicious write lands, is real for up to one tick, and is then undone. This is the *default* rung for everything about tags, because of one structural fact: a player standing next to their portal already owns its ZDO (`ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` hands it over every 2s, :76901-76926), so `TeleportWorld.SetText` → `InvokeRPC` → `InvokeRoutedRPC(targetPeerID == m_id)` (:83588) takes the *local* branch and **no packet is ever sent**. The retag arrives at the server laundered as an ordinary `RPC_ZDOData` field push. There is no RPC to veto. Tag Watchdog, Reserved Namespace, Shadow Ward Index, Portal ACL, Anti-Grief Tag Integrity, Rate Limiting and Tag Author Rewrite are all on this rung unless paired with the Ownership Pin, which promotes them to rung 1 for the specific portals it covers.

(4) NOT ENFORCEABLE — per-player transit decisions, PINs, inventory checks, and anything requiring a prompt at the moment of use.

THE IDENTITY CHAIN, END TO END. `ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` (:83609), `RPC_SetTag`'s `authorId` (:143587), `PrivateArea`'s `playerID` payloads (:137399, :137414), `s_creator`, `s_playerID` and `peer.m_playerName` are **all client self-reports**. The single platform-verified value on the box is `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`, validated by a Steam session ticket or PlayFab auth in `ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo` (:79843-79870) — it is what vanilla's own adminlist uses (`ZNet.RPC_Kick` :81670). Two methods receive the authentic `ZRpc` and discard it: `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632) and `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77076, which even resolves the peer at :77078 and then throws it away). Those two are the *only* places identity can be recovered, and recovering it is the prerequisite for every other option here. `ZNetPeer.m_playerID` is permanently 0 — the server registers the `"PlayerID"` RPC (:79916) but no vanilla client ever invokes it. The one bridge from a piece to a verified account is `s_creatorIndex` → `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory`, because that table is built server-side from socket host names (`ZNet.UpdatePlayerList` :81270-81281, `UpdatePlayerHistory` :81436-81461) and persisted to the .fwl — which is what makes Creator Attestation possible at all.

THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE RESEARCH DIGEST, VERIFIED AGAINST THE DECOMPILE.
(a) A Harmony prefix on `ZDO.SetOwner` (:74627) does **not** stop a client claiming a ZDO. `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` applies incoming ownership by calling the public `ZDO.SetOwnerInternal` directly (:77114 and :77128), bypassing the setter entirely — and the :77112-77117 branch applies an owner change even when the incoming DataRevision is *not* newer, as long as `OwnerRevision` is higher. The Wonderland `ZdoSetOwnerPatch` pattern is necessary but insufficient; you must also guard `ZDO.SetOwnerInternal` (:74636, public) or re-assert in the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix.
(b) The Ownership Pin makes a portal **indestructible and un-demolishable**, not just un-retaggable. `WearNTear.Damage` (:150315-150321) and `WearNTear.Remove` (:150411-150416) both use `InvokeRPC(string,…)` → the ZDO owner, and the hammer's remove path calls `WearNTear.Remove()` for any WearNTear piece (`Player.RemovePiece` :12405-12408) — it only calls `ClaimOwnership()` on the non-WearNTear fallback branch (:12419). This is a feature and a trap: the legitimate owner cannot demolish their own gate either, so every pinned portal needs a server-side unpin path.
(c) `ZDO.Deserialize` does not wipe fields absent from an incoming packet — `ZDODataHelper.ReadData` (:74718-74730) calls `ZDOExtraData.Add` per key present and never clears. Mod-private ZDO keys (`tp_owner`, `tp_net`, …) written by the server therefore survive an honest client's ZDO push even when that client's copy never had them. They are still forgeable by a malicious client (no ZDO setter checks ownership — `ZDO.Set(int,int,bool okForNotOwner)` ignores its own parameter, :73648-73654), which is why they must mirror a mod-side file rather than be the authority.

RULED OUT OUTRIGHT, WITH REASONS.
• Patching `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`, `PrivateArea.RPC_TogglePermitted`/`RPC_ToggleEnabled`, or `WearNTear.RPC_Damage`/`RPC_Remove` on a dedicated server. These are ZDO-targeted RPCs; `HandleRoutedRPC` dispatches them only through `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zDO)` (:83659), which is permanently null. The patches compile, apply, and never fire once.
• `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` as an authorization primitive. It iterates the static `m_allAreas` list (:137173), appended to only in `PrivateArea.Awake` (:137197), so on a dedicated server it **returns true for every point in the world** — a silent allow-all that looks like a working check. This is the single most dangerous trap in the area.
• `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()`-based helpers (`Piece.IsCreator` :136436, `Bed.IsMine`, `TombStone.IsOwner`, `Container.CheckAccess`). `Game.Awake` creates a throwaway profile named "Stranger" with a random UID (:100047), so these return garbage rather than throwing.
• Hardening `m_senderPeerID` as a fix for the ward RPCs. `RPC_ToggleEnabled` (:137414) and `RPC_TogglePermitted` (:137399) **ignore the routed `uid` entirely** and act on the payload `playerID`; sender hardening accomplishes nothing there.
• Any per-player gate at the moment of transit (PINs, "only the builder", carrying-item checks). See the Per-Player Transit Gate option.
• Player inventories as an authorization input. Never networked in any form — `Player.Save` writes to the client's own `.fch` (:14091-14170) and `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles` collects nothing (:79653-79670).

ORDERING AND DEPENDENCY. Build in this order or you will build things that cannot work: Authentic Sender Context → Portal Record Store → Creator Attestation → Tag Watchdog → Managed Network Governor → (Ownership Pin, Destroy Veto, Ungated RPC Hardening as the enforcement layer) → policy options (ACL, wards, networks, progression, tolls, rate limits). Two cross-cutting hard rules from the decompile: **never cache a `ZDO` object reference across ticks** (`ZDOPool.Release` recycles them and `ZDO.Reset` blanks `m_uid`, :78286-78311, :73536-73545 — vanilla itself violates this in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals`), and **never key persistent state by ZDOID** (`ZDO.Load` renumbers every id on world load, :74552). Cache ZDOIDs within a session; key persistent records by rounded world position. And after **every** portal ZDO write that is not a `SetConnection(Portal, …)`, call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702) — the ChunkPortal file is only written when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set (:77621-77635), so a tag revert that skips it is silently discarded at the next world save with no error anywhere. That is the most likely shipped bug in this entire design.

ONE UNVERIFIED CAPABILITY WORTH THE EXPERIMENT. `ZNetView.LoadFields` (:82669; client copy assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82898-82970) runs in `ZNetView.Awake` on a vanilla client and overrides any public instance field of any component on the prefab from the ZDO, keyed `"<TypeName>.<FieldName>"` and gated by the ZDO bools `HasFields` / `HasFields<TypeName>`. If it works as written, a server-only mod can make `TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems` genuinely per-portal on a 100% vanilla client by writing three ZDO values — refuting the widely-repeated claim that every per-portal knob is dead. It is client-honoured, not enforced, and it applies only at instantiation. Test it first; several design choices downstream depend on the answer.

CROSS-CUTTING FINDINGS FOR THE OPS/ADMIN DOMAIN.

1. **Portals are the one ZDO family with a free, complete, always-resident server-side index.** `AddIfPortal` files them in `m_portalObjects` and removes them from the sector array (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77732-77752); they load wholesale from the dedicated `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal` file at world load (:76474-76482, :113180); they are never unloaded (`ReleaseZDOS` only reassigns ownership, :76872-76885; `FlushClientObjects` is client-only, :76180-76183). So every enumeration, health scan, audit diff and export is O(portal count) and completely independent of world ZDO count. This single fact is what makes a rich ops feature set cheap — and it is why every non-portal query (altars, beds, ships) is in a different, much more expensive cost class (`GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` walks a 512x512 = 262144-slot array, :77442-77494, :79163).

2. **Corrections to the existing TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md spec, verified this pass.**
   - The spec's Group-2 claim that `nomap` "correctly branches on IsServer()" while `noportals` does not is WRONG. `nomap`'s `IsServer()` branch is nested inside the same `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)` guard (:45261-45283). Both are equally dead on a dedicated server.
   - `Console.instance` IS non-null on a dedicated server — `Game.Awake` instantiates `m_consolePrefab` when absent (:100038-100041). That makes `RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879) a genuine, admin-gated, working command channel, which the spec does not mention at all.
   - `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(cmd)` called on the SERVER passes a null rpc (:81873) into `InternalCommand`, which dereferences `rpc.GetSocket()` unconditionally at :81893 — a guaranteed NullReferenceException. This is a new finding not in the research digest.
   - `Terminal.ConsoleCommand`'s ctor registers via an indexer assignment (`commands[command.ToLower()] = this`, :43096/:43114), NOT `.Add` — so a name collision with another mod silently clobbers rather than throwing. `ConsoleCommand.IsValid` (:43203) never reads the `OnlyAdmin` flag, and the `ConsoleEvent` overload does not even fold it into `OnlyServer` (:43120) unlike the `ConsoleEventFailable` overload (:43100).

3. **The honest limit of "orphan detection": there is no such thing as a portal in an unloaded zone.** Every portal in the save is resident in server RAM from world load onward. The real pathologies are the odd-count strand, dangling ZDOIDs, non-reciprocal links, self-loops, cross-tag links, near-duplicate tags (ordinal comparison, `ZDOExtraData.GetString` defaults to `""` so all untagged portals are one group, :75079-75082), out-of-world coordinates (`ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex` clamp, :115755-115774) and sector duplication from a repositioned portal (`AddIfPortal` :77732-77752 vs `HandleDestroyedZDO` :76980-76986).

4. **Idempotence is the performance strategy.** `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` early-returns on an unchanged value (:74951-74961) and `BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false on equality (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345), so `ZDO.Set` skips `IncreaseDataRevision`. A 2 Hz reassert loop over an already-correct network generates zero DataRevision bumps, zero network traffic and zero disk dirtying. This is what makes "re-assert everything continuously" a viable architecture rather than a resource leak.

5. **Two silent-persistence traps that will bite any ops feature.** (a) A tag-only write does NOT set `DirtyPortalObjects` — `ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision` (:73832) routes to `SetDirtySector`, and portals are explicitly excluded from ordinary chunk saves (`AddObjectsPerChunk` :77572). Always call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702). (b) `LoadChunks` ends with `DirtyPortalObjects = false` (:76474-76531), so a freshly loaded world will not rewrite the portal file until something actually changes — a restored snapshot that only re-asserts already-correct values writes nothing to disk, which is correct but can look like a failure.

6. **The complete server-side identity story for attribution.** Only `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()` is platform-verified (Steam session ticket / PlayFab auth, `ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo` :79843-79870; the same key vanilla's own admin/ban lists use, :81670). `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` (:83489) and `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`'s `authorId` (:143587-143602) are raw client self-reports. `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) is client-authored but `s_creatorIndex` (:78395) indexes the server-maintained `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` (:112396), which is fed from socket-verified PlatformUserIDs and persisted in the .fwl (:112587) — the only bridge from a built piece to an authenticated account. Any audit UI must distinguish `confirmed` from `probable`.

7. **Threading.** ZDOMan/ZDOExtraData/ZNetScene are unsynchronised static state. Vanilla's only background thread (`ZNet.SaveWorldThread` :80583) operates exclusively on a clone built on the main thread by `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` (:76197-76205). Any HTTP, webhook or serialisation work must follow the same shape: main-thread snapshot → immutable DTO → off-thread consumer. For background-thread log output, `Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog` (`public static ConcurrentQueue<string>`, :43245) is drained one line per frame by `Console.Update` into `AddString` → `ZLog.Log` (:42923-42925, :45983-45985) — vanilla's own save thread uses it for error reporting (:80675, :80710).

8. **Useful vanilla hooks nobody has used yet in this codebase.** `ZNet.WorldSaveStarted` / `WorldSaveFinished` are plain `public static Action` fields (:78989, :78991) invoked at :80524 and :80580 — `WorldSaveStarted` fires on the main thread immediately before `PrepareSave` and is the correct place to flush mod state and set the portal dirty flag. Caution: `WorldSaveFinished` is reached through `PrintWorldSaveMessage` (:80566-80581), which dereferences `MessageHud.instance` unguarded at :80574/:80578, so it may never fire headless. `ZDOExtraData.GetData(ZDOID, out floats, out vec3s, out quats, out ints, out longs, out strings, out byteArray, out connectionData)` (:75108-75119) is a public static that dumps every key on a ZDO — exactly what a `tplite.dump` diagnostic needs, and not mentioned anywhere in the research digest.

9. **The mod-removal answer, stated plainly.** Nothing corrupts. No phantom portals appear — mod-created portal-prefab ZDOs load through `LoadChunks`'s portal branch with NO `FilterZDO` call (:76474-76482) and behave as ordinary gates. Mod keys become harmless dead bytes. BUT any non-pairwise topology is lost at the FIRST RESTART after removal, silently: the on-disk format gives each ZDO one `ZDOConnectionHashData` slot (`RegenerateConnectionHashData` :75461-75478), which can only express a pairwise perfect matching, so rings collapse, one-way links come back bidirectional (`ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` writes both sides, :77879-77885) and self-loops are erased. A non-portal anchor ZDO with a fabricated prefab hash is NOT deleted — `FilterZDO` only drops the two hashes in `s_brokenPrefabsToFilterOut` (:76109, :76346-76361) and merely warns about unknown prefabs, so a bogus anchor spams the log forever. Hence `tplite.uninstall` is a required feature, not a nicety.

10. **Everything in this domain is admin-facing or server-enforced at the ZDO layer; nothing here changes the Central Constraint.** No ops feature can observe or veto the moment a player walks through a gate — `TeleportWorld.Teleport`'s only caller is `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` gated on `Player.m_localPlayer` (:143664-143682). Transit metrics are therefore heuristic and reactive, and must be labelled as such in every report an operator might show to a player.

THE CENTRAL INSIGHT, FULLY DEVELOPED.

A dedicated Valheim server holds exactly one lever over portals, and it is total: `ZDO.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, targetId)` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73656), which IS network-serialized to clients (`ZDO.Serialize` :74112/:74169) and which a vanilla client reads at the instant of transit with no cache (`TeleportWorld.Teleport` :143539). `TeleportWorld.Teleport`'s first gate is `if (!TargetFound()) return;` (:143519) — a portal with `ZDOID.None` is not "refused", it simply has nowhere to go, and no client modification can invent a destination that is not in the ZDO. This is the ONLY one of Teleport's four gates that is server-enforced; the other three read global keys or the local inventory and are client-honoured (:143523, :143528, :143533).

Therefore: **every rule of the form "should this ROUTE be open right now?" is enforceable, and every rule of the form "should this PLAYER pass right now?" is not.** The second bucket is empty for four independent reasons, each individually fatal — no transit hook exists (`TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` is the sole call site and is `Player.m_localPlayer`-gated, :143664, with `Game.FixedUpdate` pinning the server's reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) every tick at :100465 so no portal GameObject or Player ever exists server-side); no ZDO-targeted RPC dispatches server-side (`ZNetScene.FindInstance` :82229 over a permanently empty `m_instances`); a player's inventory is never networked at all (`Player.Save` :14091 → the local `.fch`; `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles` :79653 returns nothing); and transit detection is ~2s late and cannot refuse anything.

HOW MUCH GAME DESIGN FITS IN THE FIRST BUCKET

Far more than it first appears, because almost every economic or progression rule can be re-expressed route-side. The enumeration:

1. Conditional on WORLD STATE — fully enforced, zero detection, zero exploit surface: boss-key progression tiers; time-of-day and calendar schedules (`ZNet.GetTimeSeconds` :81546, persisted at :80624); weather/season; server population; event state.
2. Conditional on PHYSICAL OBJECTS AT THE PORTAL — fully enforced, read as plain ZDO fields: coins in a bound chest (`ZDOVars.s_items` :78475); a token on an item stand (`ZDOVars.s_item` :78465, one int); fuel in a brazier (`ZDOVars.s_fuel` :78433, one float); the presence and roster of a ward (`ZDOVars.s_permitted` + `pu_id<i>`, :137338); the set of building pieces within N metres.
3. Conditional on ROUTE GEOMETRY — fully enforced, computed from data the server always holds: endpoint distance; biome at either end (`WorldGenerator.GetBiome` :151725, collider-free); height, lava (`ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap` :115637), world-edge proximity; hop-count caps that force relay infrastructure.
4. Conditional on PORTAL-SIDE PERSISTED STATE — fully enforced, arbitrary mod fields on the portal ZDO which round-trip through the dedicated `ChunkPortal` save (`ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk` :77621, gated on `SetDirtyPortals()` :76702): lease expiry, cooldown-until, quota counters, tier, auction winner, chain progress.
5. Conditional on WHO BUILT IT — fully enforced, and the key move: `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) is on every player-placed piece. A per-player rule becomes a per-route rule by acting on that player's property rather than their person. "Suspend Bjorn" is impossible; "park every gate Bjorn built" is one predicate.
6. Conditional on CREATION — fully enforced, because unlike transit, creation IS server-visible: the `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` + `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix pair (Wonderland `Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43`,:58) sees every client-placed portal arrive, making a hard build cap genuinely enforceable — strictly stronger than the full client-side TortalPortal, whose cap lives in a `Player.TryPlacePiece` prefix. The PAUSED PortalLock project failed precisely by hooking `Player.PlacePiece` and `ZNetScene.Instantiate` behind an `IsServer()` guard; neither can ever fire.

The only genuinely per-player thing the server can do is REACT: toast, map pin, status effect, forced teleport, kick, ban — all after the fact. Design accordingly: make rules about routes, make consequences about property, and reserve per-player action for punishment.

FIVE RULES THAT GOVERN EVERY IMPLEMENTATION HERE

(a) `Game.ConnectPortals()` (:100589) runs every 5s server-side and its pass 1 tears down any link whose partner's `s_tag` differs or whose partner's connection is None (:100601), while pass 2 re-pairs in the SAME call (:100607). Writing `ZDOID.None` between ticks loses. You must either mutate the tag, veto the pairing, or point the gate at a decoy — nothing else holds.

(b) Ownership is transient. `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) hands portal ownership to any peer within ~96-112m every 2s. The write pattern is claim-write-forcesend and then let go: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(...); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);` — exactly `Game.SetConnection`'s own body (:100643-100645). `ZDO.SetConnection` is idempotent (`ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` :74954), so re-asserting a whole topology every tick costs nothing.

(c) Tag writes are NOT saved unless you call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702). `DirtyPortalObjects` is set only by `ZDO.SetConnection`/`UpdateConnection` for the Portal type, `AddIfPortal` (:77750) and `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76986). A rename or a custom field written alone silently vanishes at the next world save.

(d) Non-pairwise topologies are runtime-only. `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461) gives each ZDO exactly one hash slot, so across a save a ring loses a link, a one-way link becomes two-way (`ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` :77879-77885 writes both directions), and a self-loop is erased. Every managed topology must be rebuilt in an `OnWorldReady` pass. The window right after world load is also the cheapest time to do it: `m_peers` is empty so every write takes the immediate local path, and the server already owns both ends of every pair.

(e) Never cache a `ZDO` object or a `ZDOID` across a restart. `ZDOPool.Release`/`Get` recycles ZDO objects on destruction (`ZDO.Reset` sets `m_uid = ZDOID.None`, :73536) — vanilla itself has a latent bug here in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals`. And `ZDO.Load` renumbers every id at world load (`m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`, :74552), which is exactly the bug that made TortalPortal's ZDOID-keyed Favorites file forget everything between sessions. Key all persistent mod state on rounded POSITION, on `ZDOVars.s_creator`, or on a world global key.

SECURITY: THE ECONOMY SITS ON UNAUTHENTICATED FOUNDATIONS

Three holes will drain any economy built here unless closed first, and all three are closable from a server-only mod:
- `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77076) applies any incoming ZDO wholesale on a higher DataRevision with no ownership, prefab or field validation. A client can rewrite its own chest's balance, a portal's tag, or a ward's permitted list as plain data with no RPC involved.
- `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653) rewires any portal to any ZDOID with no sender check, undoing any park in one packet.
- `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey` / `RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` (:116022/:116031) let any client set or clear `noportals`, `teleportall` and every boss key.
The single hook for all of them is a prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632) — the only place the authentic `ZRpc` socket is in scope (`RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` is deserialized straight off the wire and never cross-checked, :83487). Resolve the true peer with `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)` (`ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` is private, :80504) and match against `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`, the only platform-verified identity on the server (`ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo` Steam ticket verification, :79843). Save and restore `pkg.GetPos()` when peeking or you corrupt vanilla's own dispatch. `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` needs its own prefix since it is a peer-direct ZRpc, not a routed RPC.

ENGINEERING BASELINE

Fork Wonderland's framework rather than re-deriving it: `Plugin.cs` lifecycle + `Core/SubsystemRegistry.cs` (with `SafePatch` at :99) + `Core/Heartbeat.cs`, plus `Core/Data/ConnectedCharacters.cs` (the replacement for the always-empty `Player.GetAllPlayers()`), `Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs` (the only text channel to a vanilla client), `Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs` (chest I/O), `Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs` (radius queries), `Core/Data/EmoteSignals.cs` (the ONLY reliable player→server control channel — chat is dead, since `Chat.SendText` targets each other listed player individually and a solo player generates zero packets, and an unknown slash command never leaves the client), `Core/Compat/GameShape.cs`, and `Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs` (the already-production-tuned portal-transit heuristic). Build against `libs-Tools/1.0/server/*` (the DEDICATED SERVER assemblies) with net472 and `<Publicize>true</Publicize>`, per `Wonderland.csproj` — TortalPortal's csproj points at the CLIENT assemblies and is the wrong baseline.

Two free wins before writing any code: vanilla already logs a parseable pairing audit trail (`ZLog.Log("Connected portals " + A + " <-> " + B)` at :100619 and `"[ Connected N portals ]"` at :100625), and `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (:77648) is a complete, always-resident, zero-bookkeeping census of every portal in the world with tag, position, rotation, owner, connection and `s_creator` on each — no scanner, no prefab list, no player nearby.

There is one genuine second input channel worth naming: the vanilla map ping. `Chat.SendPing` (:42058) broadcasts a `"ChatMessage"` routed RPC at `targetPeerID = 0` carrying the clicked world coordinate, from a stock client, with no permission gate and no player-count dependency. Middle-click the map, and the server gets an arbitrary player-chosen Vector3. Combined with the topology kernel that is a complete destination-selection UI — "ping where you want this gate to go, pay for the hop, the server re-routes it" — with zero client install.

Finally, two things that are NOT part of this domain and should never be promised: dungeon and crypt doors (`class Teleport` :143316 has no ZNetView, no ZDO and no RPC — its destination is the compiled Inspector reference `m_targetPoint` :143322, and a server-wide `NoPortals` lockdown does not close them and never restricted ore through them), and vanilla portal telemetry (`PlayerStatType.PortalsUsed`/`PortalDungeonIn`/`PortalDungeonOut` go to `PlayerProfile.IncrementStat` :106287 in the player's local `.fch` and never reach the server).

SCOPE NOTE ON "LOCKDOWN". There are exactly two enforcement tiers and they must never be conflated in documentation or config text.
