TIER A (client-honoured): the global-key family. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` reads `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` at :143523 and `NoBossPortals` at :143528, both live at the instant of transit, and both entirely inside a method whose only call site is `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` (:143673-143681), gated on `Player.m_localPlayer == component`. That code runs on the traveller's machine. A modified client that deletes those two `if` blocks teleports normally and the server sees nothing. This is exactly the guarantee vanilla's own boss gating has — no weaker, no stronger.

TIER B (server-enforced): the Portal connection. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` resolves its destination at :143539 with `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal))`, and `ZDOMan.GetZDO` returns null for `ZDOID.None` (:76756-76759). The whole move is then inside `if (zDO != null)` (:143540). A client with every gate removed still has no coordinate to move to. Nulling the connection server-side is therefore genuinely unbypassable *for portal-mediated travel*. It is NOT a teleport ban — a hacked client can call `Player.TeleportTo` locally with no portal involved, and can also write a connection back via the unauthenticated `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653, zero sender validation) or a higher-DataRevision ZDO push (`ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` :77107). Tier B is a read-side guarantee that must be defended on the write side.

THE CENTRAL WORLD-INTEGRITY HAZARD (verified, not inferred). `ZDO.SetConnection(Portal, ...)` calls `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:73661-73664). `DirtyPortalObjects` is the *only* thing that causes the portal chunk to be written (`ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk` :77621-77632), and that block clones EVERY portal in the world with no `Persistent` filter. The snapshot is taken synchronously on the main thread inside `ZNet.SaveWorld` (:80532 `m_zdoMan.PrepareSave()` → `GetSaveClonePerChunk` + `ZDOExtraData.PrepareSave` :75480 → `RegenerateConnectionHashData` :75461). So if an autosave lands while a force-disconnect lockdown is engaged, the world on disk has every portal connection = None. On the next load `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` calls `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` (:76523), whose phase 2 pairs same-tag portals with `UnityEngine.Random.Range` (:100678). The result is not "still locked" — it is **every portal pair in the world randomly rewired**. For tag groups of exactly 2 the random pick is a no-op; for 3+ the orphan changes and links shuffle. Any lockdown feature that does not address this will silently scramble a long-running server's portal network on the first crash.

THE FIX IS A HOOK PAIR, NOT A TIMER. `ZNet.WorldSaveStarted` is `public static Action` (:78989) invoked at :80524 on the main thread immediately before `PrepareSave`. `ZDOMan.PrepareSave()` is public (:76197). A Harmony prefix on `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` that writes the TRUE connections back, plus a postfix that re-nulls them, sandwiches the entire snapshot in one frame with no `ZDOMan.Update` send sweep in between (sends are gated on a 0.05s timer at :76843 and happen from Update, not from the save path). The lockdown then never reaches disk. Do NOT use `WorldSaveFinished` (:78991) as the closing half: it is invoked from `PrintWorldSaveMessage` (:80580) which is ~0.5s later via `UpdateSave` and which dereferences `MessageHud.instance` unguarded at :80574/:80578 — if that singleton is ever null headless, `WorldSaveFinished` never fires and the lockdown stays written.

WHAT IS DEAD ON A DEDICATED SERVER (do not build on any of it). `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick in the SERVER build only (:100465) — a line with no counterpart in the client's `Game.FixedUpdate`. Consequences: no portal/ward/player GameObject ever exists, `ZNetScene.FindInstance` is always null so every ZDO-targeted routed RPC handler (`TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`, `PrivateArea.RPC_TogglePermitted`, `WearNTear.RPC_Damage`) is unreachable server-side; `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` returns true vacuously because `m_allAreas` is empty; and every collider-based `ZoneSystem` helper (`FindFloor` :115604, `GetSolidHeight` :115525, `GetGroundHeight`, `IsBlocked`, `IsLava(Vector3)` :115647) silently returns its no-hit fallback rather than failing. Server-side geometry must be `WorldGenerator` math plus the static `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap` (:115637), which is the only lava test that works headless.

THREE TIMING CONSTANTS GOVERN EVERY DESIGN HERE. (1) `Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine` runs `ConnectPortals()` every 5.0s, started only under `if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` at `Game.Start` :100074. Phase 1 (:100594-100606) tears down any link whose partner's `s_tag` differs; phase 2 (:100607-100622) re-pairs anything left at `ZDOID.None`. Any lockdown that nulls connections is undone within 5s unless `Game.ConnectPortals` is prefixed. (2) `ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS` runs every 2s and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) hands ownership of any persistent ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer — a server ownership claim near a player evaporates in ≤2s unless guarded by a `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix. (3) `Player.m_teleportCooldown` must exceed 2f and is zeroed every tick while teleporting (`Player.UpdateTeleport` :15331-15336), so a forced teleport within ~10s of a previous one silently no-ops with no feedback anywhere.

AN IN-FLIGHT TRAVELLER CANNOT BE RECALLED. `Player.TeleportTo` snapshots the destination into `m_teleportTargetPos` at :15324 and returns true; `UpdateTeleport` then force-assigns `transform.position = m_teleportTargetPos` every FixedUpdate from t>2s (:15343) and will not complete until t>8s for a distantTeleport (:15349), force-landing at `GetSolidHeight+0.5` at t=15s (:15360-15366). Nulling the connection afterwards changes nothing, and a counter-teleport is refused by the cooldown. Every lockdown is therefore "no NEW transits", never "abort transits in progress". Design the grace window around that.

THE 10-CHARACTER TAG CAP IS A LIVE HAZARD FOR TAG-BASED LOCKDOWN. The cap exists only in the client widget — `TeleportWorld.Interact` calls `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` (:143482) and `TextInput.Show` assigns `m_inputField.characterLimit = charLimit`. `RPC_SetTag` (:143587-143602) validates nothing, so the server can write any length. But `TextInput.Show` also pre-fills the field with the existing tag. A player who opens the rename dialog on a server-written `[LOCKED]Base` tag and presses OK may save back a 10-character truncation, permanently corrupting the tag. Any quarantine-tag scheme must either keep the injected tag ≤10 chars or accept that risk.

ACTIVEBOSSES IS A LEAKY COUNTER AND WILL EVENTUALLY JAM PORTALS SHUT. `BaseAI.SetAlerted` increments `GlobalKeys.activeBosses` once per boss, guarded by the ZDO bool `s_bossCount` which it sets to `true` unconditionally on that same first call (:27256-27261) — so the intended `-1` on de-alert can never run. The only decrement is `Character.OnDeath` (:3161-3165). A boss that is alerted and then unloaded (player logs out, zone drops) leaves the counter permanently above zero, and `TeleportWorld.Teleport`'s gate at :143528 (`NoBossPortals && ... activeBosses > 0`) then blocks every portal for every player forever. A server mod that sets `NoBossPortals` at all MUST ship the watchdog that zeroes the counter when no boss is actually alive.

GLOBAL KEYS ARE NOT WHERE YOU THINK THEY ARE ON DISK. `ZoneSystem.Save` strips every key whose enum ordinal is below `NonServerOption` (41) from the .db (:113751-113755). `NoPortals`=32, `NoBossPortals`=33, `DungeonBuild`=34, `TeleportAll`=35 (enum :101304-101307) are all below that line, so their ONLY persistence is `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` in the .fwl, written by `GlobalKeyAdd` at :113511 whenever `canSaveToServerOptionKeys` is true. `ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys` wipes ordinals 0..40 and re-adds from the .fwl on every boot (:115906-115921). Practical consequences: setting `noportals` at runtime permanently edits the world file and survives uninstalling the mod; and a mod-owned key must be re-applied in a POSTFIX on `SetStartingGlobalKeys`, never a prefix, because a `preset` key causes `ServerOptionsGUI.m_instance.SetPreset` to reapply a whole key set at :115925.

THE CHEAPEST WINDOW FOR ANY BULK REWIRING IS WORLD LOAD. `ZDO.Load` resets every ZDO to `Owned=false, OwnerRevision=0, DataRevision=0`, `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (:77850, the private load-time one) then does `SetOwner(GetSessionID())` on both ends of every restored pair, `m_peers` is empty so `Game.SetConnection` always takes the immediate local-write branch (:100641 `owner == 0L`), and no client can contend. Restore-from-vault, integrity checks, and network rebuilds all belong here, not on a live tick.

TWO IDENTITY FACTS THAT BOUND THE SAFETY WORK. ZDOIDs are renumbered on every world load (`ZDO.Load` does `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`), so no persisted state may be keyed by ZDOID — key by rounded world position, which is what TortalPortal's own Favorites.cs switched to after exactly this bug. And non-pairwise topologies do not survive a save at all: `RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461-75477) gives each ZDO exactly ONE `s_connectionsHashData` slot and overwrites the source slot with the Target slot at :75474, so rings lose a link, one-way links come back bidirectional via `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals`' reciprocal writes (:77879-77885), and self-loops are erased. Any "locked" topology expressed as a ring or a self-loop is runtime-only and must be re-asserted after every load.

RULED-OUT SUMMARY, so nobody re-derives it. There is no server-side moment-of-transit hook of any kind (`TeleportWorld.Teleport` has exactly one call site, `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` :143679, triple-gated on a collider, a Player component and `Player.m_localPlayer`). There is no per-portal item policy (`m_allowAllItems` :143429 and every other TeleportWorld field is a plain compiled Inspector value with zero ZDO or RPC backing). There is no server-readable player inventory anywhere, so vanilla's ore check cannot be reproduced or audited. There is no way to block dungeon/crypt doors: `class Teleport` (:143316-143390) has no ZNetView, no ZDO, no RPC, and a destination that is a plain `Teleport m_targetPoint` Inspector reference (:143322); it never reads `NoPortals` at all and never calls `IsTeleportable`, so a full `noportals` lockdown leaves every crypt door open and ore-permissive. And retag interception at the RPC layer is unreliable because `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` skips `RouteRPC` entirely when `targetPeerID == m_id` (:83588-83594) — a client that owns the portal ZDO retags it with zero packets on the wire.

CROSS-CUTTING FINDINGS, several of which contradict or sharpen the digest.

1. THE BIGGEST UNDER-EXPLOITED MECHANISM IS ZNetView.LoadFields (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82669-82739, called from ZNetView.Awake :82631). It reflects over every public instance field of every MonoBehaviour on an instantiated prefab and overrides it from the ZDO, keyed "HasFields", "HasFields<TypeName>" and "<TypeName>.<FieldName>", for int / float / bool / Vector3 / string / GameObject / ItemDrop. This directly refutes the common conclusion that "every per-portal behavioural knob is dead to a server-only mod". Per-portal TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems, m_exitDistance, m_activationRange, m_hoverOffset, Piece.m_canBeRemoved, Piece.m_comfort and WearNTear.m_health are all reachable from a pure ZDO write on a 100 percent vanilla client. Color fields are NOT (not a supported type). The limitation is timing: it runs only at instantiation.

2. A SECOND MECHANISM THE DIGEST MISSES ENTIRELY: prefab hash 0. ZNetScene.CreateObject (:81996-82002) returns null on `prefab == 0` BEFORE the lookup and logs nothing, while an unknown non-zero hash logs "Missing prefab hash" every frame (:82004-82008). ZNetScene.IsPrefabZDOValid (:81986) also returns false for 0, so IsAreaReady skips it. And ZDO's default m_prefab is -1 (c_PrefabInvalid, :73305-73317), NOT 0 — so ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO without an explicit SetPrefab(0) produces a log-spamming ZDO, not a silent one. Explicit SetPrefab(0) is what makes a truly invisible, silent, IsAreaReady-transparent anchor.

3. A THIRD: the invalid-prefab reaper is SERVER-ONLY and only ever sees sector bucket 0. ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted's destroy branch is `else if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` (:82137-82143) — the only code in the game that reaps prefab-less ZDOs. Combined with ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex clamping every out-of-range zone to Sector 0 (:115760-115773) and Game.FixedUpdate pinning the server at (1e6,0,1e6) (:100465, zone 15625 which clamps to 0), this means: anchors at normal world coordinates are never reaped, and anything placed beyond about plus/minus 16.4 km is instantiated and/or destroyed by the server itself. ZoneSystem.PokeLocalZone uses SpawnMode.Full on the server (:114028), so the server DOES build real local zones at its pinned position — the "server instantiates nothing" conclusion is right for the wrong reason.

4. THE RICH-TEXT REGEX IS BYPASSABLE. StringExtensionMethods.RemoveRichTextTags (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703) is `Regex.Replace(text, "<[/a-zA-Z0-9= \"''#;:()$_-]*?>", "")`. The character class excludes the less-than sign and Regex.Replace makes one forward pass without re-scanning its output. Therefore the doubled form `<<color=red>color=red>` has no match at index 0, matches at index 1, and leaves exactly `<color=red>` in the output. TMP rendering of the survivor is the only open question. Separately, GetHoverText concatenates the tag INTO the string before Localization.Localize runs (:143463), so $tokens and newlines inside a tag are live.

5. FOUR THINGS ARE SERVER-ENFORCED AND EVERYTHING ELSE IS CLIENT-HONOURED. Server-enforced: the Portal connection value (TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1, :143519, reads the ZDO the server owns); ZDO existence and destruction; the tag string; and ownership. Client-honoured: NoPortals, NoBossPortals, TeleportAll, m_allowAllItems, m_canBeRemoved, everything LoadFields sets. Nothing is enforceable against a modified client, because ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77139) validates nothing at all and lets any client rewrite any field of any ZDO by bumping DataRevision, and ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO (:76953) is completely ungated on receive.

6. TWO SILENT-DATA-LOSS TRAPS DOMINATE THE FAILURE SURFACE. (a) A portal field write that is not a ConnectionType.Portal SetConnection does not set DirtyPortalObjects, so the entire ChunkPortal file is skipped at save and every portal reverts (ZDOMan.SetDirtySector :76694 dirties a chunk that AddObjectsPerChunk :77572 excludes portals from). Always call ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals(). (b) ZDOIDs are renumbered on every world load, so no mod state may be keyed by ZDOID — key by rounded position, by tag, or by a mod-written ZDO field. TortalPortal's Favorites.cs hit exactly this and switched to a position key; Wonderland's SupplySwitch is still ZDOID-keyed and masks the same bug as "the station forgot".

7. NON-PAIRWISE TOPOLOGIES ARE RUNTIME-ONLY, NOT PERSISTENT. Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 never checks reciprocity (:100601), so rings, one-way links, fan-in and self-loops all survive at runtime. But the disk format gives each ZDO exactly one ZDOConnectionHashData slot, and RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) overwrites the target's slot with the Target variant — so rings above 2 lose links, one-way links come back bidirectional via the load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77879-77885), and self-loops are erased outright. Any managed topology must be re-asserted after every world load. This is a harder constraint than "vanilla re-pairs within 5 s".

8. THE HONEST HIERARCHY OF PLAYER INPUT CHANNELS, in descending reliability: map pings (Chat.SendPing broadcasts to peer 0 with a world Vector3, no permission check, works solo — :42058-42068); emotes (character ZDO s_emote / s_emoteID, 25 values); equipped item hashes (VisEquipment writes s_rightItem etc. to the character ZDO); item stands (s_item); signs (s_text, written directly with no RPC — there is no Sign.RPC_SetText, correcting a common assumption); chest contents (s_items); look direction (s_lookTarget, 0.2 s resolution). Chat text and slash commands are NOT usable: chat is routed per-other-listed-player so a solo player generates zero packets, and an unknown slash command runs locally and prints nothing.

9. PRECISE ARRIVAL PHYSICS, which nobody else in the digest derived: FindFloor raycasts 1000 m down from target+1 (:115604), GetSolidHeight raycasts from target.y+1000 down 2000 m (:115525). So a destination up to 1000 m above terrain completes at t=8s and the player falls; 1000-2000 m above completes at t=15s with a soft landing on the ground below; above 2000 m the player is left at altitude and falls the full distance. Below ground, Character.UnderWorldCheck runs EVERY frame for players (:1062) and pops them to ground+0.5.

10. THE ONE PLACE A SERVER-ONLY MOD BEATS THE FULL CLIENT MOD: the portal cap. TortalPortal enforces it in a client-side prefix on Player.TryPlacePiece (PlacementPatch.cs:89), trivially bypassed by an unmodded client — its own comment records the effective cap drifting. The ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO plus ZDO.Deserialize postfix pair (Wonderland SpawnGovernor.cs:43/:58) is genuinely server-authoritative. PortalLock (PAUSED) is the negative control: it patched Player.PlacePiece and ZNetScene.Instantiate behind an IsServer() guard, a combination that could never fire once.

11. TWO HARD CEILINGS THAT NO AMOUNT OF CLEVERNESS MOVES WITHOUT A CLIENT: the server never sees a player's inventory (Player.Save goes to the local .fch; ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles collects nothing, :79653-79675), so vanilla's ore check is unreproducible and any server-driven teleport bypasses it; and there is no server-to-client redirect anywhere in the protocol (ZNet.RPC_Disconnect takes no destination, :80165-80177; SetServerHost is main-menu-only), so cross-server travel is impossible.

12. UNIVERSAL OPEN QUESTION GATING SEVERAL OPTIONS: the contents of Game.m_portalPrefabs (:99828) and the component composition of each portal prefab are Unity asset data. Every option that touches per-prefab behaviour, LoadFields type names, or prefab-hash filtering needs one in-game dump at first Heartbeat: log Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs names, Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash, and for each, ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash).GetComponents<MonoBehaviour>() type names plus ZNetView m_persistent / m_distant / m_type / m_syncInitialScale. That single log line resolves roughly eight of the open questions in this report at once.

CORRECTIONS TO THE RESEARCH DIGEST, verified directly against the decompile:

1. **RPC_SetTag is NOT a usable server interception point in the common case.** The digest calls a `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC`/`RouteRPC` prefix "the ONLY server-side interception point for tag changes". In practice it almost never fires. `TeleportWorld.SetText` uses `m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", …)` = `InvokeRoutedRPC(m_zdo.GetOwner(), …)` (ZNetView.InvokeRPC :82855), and `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) hands every persistent ZDO inside a peer's ~96 m active area to that peer within 2 s — so the player standing at the portal owns it, `targetPeerID == m_id`, and `InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally and SKIPS `RouteRPC` entirely (:83587-83594). Zero packets. The correct hook is a postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` (the tag arrives as ordinary ZDO data via `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` :77076-77139), or polling `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()`. Corollary in the server's favour: if the SERVER owns a portal ZDO, the retag RPC is addressed to the server, `ZNetScene.FindInstance` returns null (:83659), and the tag change is silently DROPPED — a free, total server veto on retagging, at the cost of breaking vanilla renaming for that portal.

2. **Long server-written tags and sign text are a footgun, not a feature.** `TextInput.Show` assigns `m_inputField.characterLimit = charLimit` and THEN `m_inputField.text = sign.GetText()` (:61515-61521). Unity's `InputField.text` setter clamps to characterLimit, so an 11+ char portal tag (or 51+ char sign) is silently truncated the moment a player opens the edit box — and `OnEnter` submits whatever is in the box (:61494). The digest's "long descriptive admin tags are viable" is true for display but destructive for any object a player can reach. Cancel/Escape is safe (`OnCancel` only calls `Hide()`, :61489).

3. **NEW INPUT CHANNEL: animator SetTrigger RPCs.** Not in the digest at all. `ZSyncAnimation.SetTrigger` is `m_nview.InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, "SetTrigger", name)` (:87260), i.e. `targetPeerID == 0`, which ALWAYS reaches the dedicated server via `RouteRPC`. A prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632) sees every `"jump"` (:3483), `"dodge"` (:15196), `"gpower"` (:15717), `"eat"`, `"interact"`, `"equip_hip"`, `"stagger"` from every player in real time, each carrying the character's ZDOID. A pushed, one-hop gesture channel strictly better than emote polling. The same mechanism carries ItemStand's `"SetVisualItem"` (:131849).

4. **NEW INPUT CHANNEL: animator parameters in the character ZDO.** `ZSyncAnimation.SetBool/SetFloat/SetInt` write to the owner's ZDO under `438569 + Animator.StringToHash(name)` (c_ZDOSalt :87144, writes :87270-87326). `Player.s_crouching = ZSyncAnimation.GetHash("crouching")` (:9984), so crouch state is a directly server-readable bit. With `ZDOVars.s_isBlockingHash` (:78463) and `s_stealth` (:78613) this gives a free, silent modifier-key layer. Note `IsBlocking()` forces crouch off (:15662) — crouch+block is unreachable, so three modes exist, not four.

5. **Signs are the highest-bandwidth player→server channel available, and the digest does not mention them as input at all.** `Sign.SetText` is a pure ZDO write with no RPC (:141915-141929) and the input widget allows 50 characters (`m_characterLimit`, :141756) — five times the portal tag. Full-word commands with arguments become possible.

6. **Sign author trap.** Writing `ZDOVars.s_author = "host"` makes `Sign.UpdateText` set `m_author = null`; `UpdateViewPermission` then calls `OnCheckPermissionCompleted(Denied)` and falls through with NO `return` to `if (m_author.Value.IsValid)` (:141867-141876), throwing on the nullable every 2 s on every viewing client. Always write an empty author string.

7. **Item stands cannot encode a stack count.** `ItemStand.UpdateAttach` forces `itemData.m_stack = 1` (:131843). The assignment's "item type = destination, stack count = index" works only with a Container, whose `s_items` blob does carry stacks — and a Container refuses to reload while the player has it open (`Container.Load` early-returns on `m_inUse`, :122305), so the server's reply is invisible until the chest is closed.

8. **Chat is dead as a player input, with one testable escape.** Confirmed three ways (slash commands never leave the client, :41947-41955; shout/normal are addressed per-listed-player so a solo player generates zero packets, :41996-42042 / :18942-18950; with 2+ players they are relay-only). BUT `Chat.CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync` collapses to a single `targetPeerID 0` broadcast when `PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider == null` (:42002-42005). That type lives in the Splatform assembly, absent from these decompiles. **If RelationsProvider is null on Steam, shout becomes a first-class server input even solo** — the single highest-value in-game test in this document, because it would give the mod a full-length free-text command channel and make most of the janky schemes unnecessary.

9. **Map ping is the standout input channel and is unconditional.** `Chat.SendPing` sends `InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, "ChatMessage", pos, 3, user, "")` (:42058-42071) — broadcast, so it always reaches the server regardless of player count. It is the ONLY vanilla gesture carrying an arbitrary player-chosen Vector3. Note `vector.y` is overwritten with the PLAYER's own y, so only x/z are meaningful and the destination height must be re-derived with `WorldGenerator.GetHeight` (:151944) — never `ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight`, a collider raycast that silently returns `p.y` on a dedicated server because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) (:100465).

10. **`DiscoverLocation` always toasts.** `Minimap.DiscoverLocation` calls `Player.m_localPlayer.Message(TopLeft, "$msg_pin_added: " + name, 0, sprite)` in BOTH branches (:58353, :58358), so every map-pin push also produces an iconed HUD toast for free — and `AddPin` force-enables that icon's filter (:58400-58403), so server pins cannot be filtered away.

CROSS-CUTTING UX PRINCIPLES:

**Every input channel needs an ARMED state.** Crouch, emote, jump, equip, walking onto a tile and map-pinging are all things players do constantly. Without proximity gating (<6 m of a managed portal), stationarity checks, and a short auto-disarming flag, every scheme here re-routes somebody's base portal by accident. Crouch is the cheapest gate: one free ZDO bit, one keypress, visibly signalled by the character's own posture.

**The server's real job is supplying the feedback vanilla omits.** A portal blocked by `NoPortals` still glows and still reads `[Connected]` (`GetHoverText` :143453 and `UpdatePortal` :143491 consult neither key). A retag that fails silently; a first transit that fails silently because the client lacks the destination ZDO (`TargetFound` → `RequestZDO`, :143640-143657); a forced teleport eaten by the 2 s cooldown (:15309-15316) — vanilla is full of silent failures the server CAN see and CAN narrate. Half the perceived value of a zero-client portal mod is simply telling the player what just happened.

**Pre-warm the destination ZDO on every route change.** `TeleportWorld.Teleport` re-reads the connection live at transit (:143539) so a server re-route applies immediately — but `TargetFound()` requires the client to actually HOLD the destination ZDO and returns false with no message when it does not. One `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, destId)` (:77714) after every dial eliminates the otherwise-guaranteed dead first walk-through. This single line is the difference between the feature feeling solid and feeling broken.

**Never key persistent state by ZDOID.** `ZDO.Load` does `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)` (:74552), renumbering every ZDO on every world load. TortalPortal's Favorites.cs hit this in production and switched to rounded world positions; Wonderland's SupplySwitch is still ZDOID-keyed and merely prunes the corpses. Key by rounded position or a world global key.

**Three write-back calls, always together.** Any server-side portal mutation needs `SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702 — a tag-only write never dirties the portal chunk and is silently lost at the next save, :77621) AND `ForceSendZDO` (:77706) AND, if bulk, a per-sweep broadcast budget (Wonderland's StructureUpkeep caps at 256 after a first sweep over a long-running world produced thousands of packets in one frame).

**Ranking the input channels by actual usability:** (1) map ping — one click, arbitrary destination, always reaches the server; (2) portal tag — familiar UI, 10 chars, instant echo where the player is already looking; (3) sign text — 50 chars, real commands, permanently visible; (4) equipped item — zero extra actions, physically legible; (5) item stand board — a patch panel, best-looking, high build cost; (6) build-piece socket — turns routing into architecture, latching and persistent; (7) crouch+jump — fastest hands-free, most embarrassing; (8) emote — reliable and already shipped in Wonderland but slow and gated by `CanMove`; (9) chest token — the only channel that can charge a fee; (10) positional plates — zero actions but undiscoverable and accident-prone; (11) ward toggle — better as a permissions SOURCE than as a button; (12) chat — ruled out pending the RelationsProvider test.

**Ranking the output channels:** tag echo (instant, in-context, persistent) > HUD toast (unlimited length, localized, one-way so no truncation trap) > in-world DamageText (disambiguates WHICH object, 30 m) > sign face (persistent, rich-text capable, 2 s repaint) > fabricated ChatMessage (chat line + world text + labelled pin in one packet) > VFX/SFX (non-textual acknowledgement) > saved map pin (permanent and unremovable — one shot only) > status effect (persistent but semantically borrowed, and no removal RPC exists).

**What is genuinely impossible, with citations, so nobody re-litigates it:** raising the 10-char tag cap (:143482 client-only); reading or debiting a living player's inventory (:79653-79675, :14091-14170 — the sole exception is a tombstone Container, :12702-12714); reproducing vanilla's ore/metal check for a server-issued teleport (`Inventory.IsTeleportable` :68860-68880 is client-side over data the server never holds); removing a pushed map pin (no removal RPC exists anywhere); removing a granted status effect (same); changing a portal's glow, colour, activation range, exit distance or `m_allowAllItems` at runtime (all plain Inspector fields, :143411-143431); intercepting a client's ward toggle at the RPC layer (:83659 FindInstance is always null); and slash commands from ordinary players (:41947-41955).

# Research digest

## Valheim 1.0.7 portal pairing algorithm — exact reverse-engineering of Game.ConnectPortals / ZDOMan portal bookkeeping for a server-only mod

There are three distinct "portal connect" routines and only one runs at runtime: `Game.ConnectPortals()` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589), driven by `ConnectPortalsCoroutine` (:100580) which is started once in `Game.Start()` under `if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` (:100073-100074), fires immediately and then every 5s forever, and is never stopped anywhere in the assembly. The other two — `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals()` (:77850) and `ZDOMan.ConvertPortals()` (:77812) — are private, load-time-only, and operate on save-file connection *hashes* (`s_connectionsHashData`), not on tags. The runtime tick takes a freshly-allocated, uncached, world-global snapshot from `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648, flattens `m_portalObjects` every call — there is no cache and therefore nothing to invalidate), then runs two passes over that same snapshot: a reconcile pass (:100594-100606) that clears a portal's connection if the partner ZDO doesn't resolve, has a different `tag` string, or itself has no Portal connection (reciprocity is NOT checked, so rings, chains and self-loops are stable), and a pair pass (:100607-100622) that for each still-unconnected portal picks a uniformly random same-tag unconnected partner via `UnityEngine.Random.Range` (:100664-100679). Tag equality is bare C# `string !=` — ordinal, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant, with `""` as the default, so every untagged portal in the world is one giant tag group. Writes go through `Game.SetConnection` (:100637), which writes locally (stealing ownership) when the ZDO is unowned or owned by a disconnected/absent peer, and otherwise defers to the owning client over `RPC_SetConnection`; the deferred case is force-committed locally on the *next* tick by `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` (:100690), so the server always wins ownership within ≤5s.

### Facts
- **[dedicated-server]** EXECUTABLE PSEUDOCODE — the full 5s runtime tick. // ---- every 5 s, dedicated server only ---- function Game.ConnectPortals():  (1) PHASE 0 — FORCE-COMMIT PREVIOUS TICK'S PROPOSALS: for each (A,B) in m_currentlyConnectingPortals: if A.connection(Portal) != B.uid: SetConnection(A, B.uid, force=true); if B.connection(Portal) != A.uid: SetConnection(B, A.uid, force=true); m_currentlyConnectingPortals.Clear().  (2) SNAPSHOT: portalList = ZDOMan.GetPortalList()   // new List<ZDO>, all portals in the world, no cache; num = 0.  (3) PHASE 1 — RECONCILE / SELF-HEAL: for each p in portalList (dictionary-bucket order): c = p.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal); t = p.GetString(s_tag)  // default ""; if c.IsNone(): continue; q = ZDOMan.GetZDO(c); if (q == null) OR (q.GetString(s_tag) != t) OR (q.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None): SetConnection(p, ZDOID.None, force=false).   // NOTE: no check that q.connection == p.uid.  (4) PHASE 2 — PAIR: for each p in portalList (same snapshot, same order): if IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal(p): continue; if !p.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal).IsNone(): continue; t = p.GetString(s_tag); cands = [q in portalList where (object)q != (object)p AND q.GetString(s_tag) == t AND q.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None AND !IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal(q)]; if cands.Count == 0: continue; q = cands[UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, cands.Count)]   // max-exclusive, global Unity RNG; m_currentlyConnectingPortals.Add({A:p, B:q}); SetConnection(p, q.uid, force=false); SetConnection(q, p.uid, force=false); num++; ZLog.Log("Connected portals " + p + " <-> " + q).  (5) if num > 0: ZLog.Log("[ Connected " + num + " portals ]").  // ---- the write primitive ---- function SetConnection(portal, connectionID, force=false): owner = portal.GetOwner()   // 0 if unowned; isOnlinePeer = (ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner) != null); if (owner == 0) OR (!isOnlinePeer) OR force: portal.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); portal.SetConnection(Portal, connectionID); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(portal.uid)   // applied IMMEDIATELY, locally; else: ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(owner, "RPC_SetConnection", portal.uid, connectionID)   // DEFERRED: server's own copy is unchanged this tick. — `Game.ConnectPortals / SetConnection / ForceSetConnection / FindRandomUnconnectedPortal / ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589-100627, :100629-100651, :100664-100679, :100690-100698` → This is the complete algorithm a server-only mod must either cooperate with or displace. Every step is reachable from a Harmony patch on the public Game.ConnectPortals, and every primitive it uses (GetPortalList, ZDO.SetConnection, ZDO.SetOwner, ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO) is public.
- **[dedicated-server]** EDGE-CASE TABLE (N portals sharing one tag T, all initially unconnected, stable state after ≥2 ticks). N=0 or 1: nothing happens; the lone portal's candidate list is empty (only candidate is `skip`) so FindRandomUnconnectedPortal returns null and it stays ZDOID.None forever. N=2: paired mutually on the first tick. N=3: the first portal in iteration order picks uniformly at random from the other two; the second iterated portal finds both remaining candidates excluded (both are in m_currentlyConnectingPortals and/or already non-None) and is PERMANENTLY orphaned — subsequent ticks re-confirm the surviving pair, so the orphan never rotates in. N=4: two mutual pairs, first-iterated picks randomly from 3, next unpaired picks the only remaining one. N odd: floor(N/2) pairs + exactly 1 permanent orphan. Empty tag "": every portal in the world with no `tag` string written is one single tag group — freshly placed untagged portals auto-pair with a random untagged portal anywhere in the world. Partner destroyed: phase 1 clears (GetZDO==null) within ≤5s, then re-pairs. Partner retagged: both ends cleared by phase 1 (tag mismatch is symmetric), then each re-pairs within its new tag group. Tags differ only by case or trailing space: treated as DIFFERENT groups, no pairing. A→B while B→C (ring/chain): SURVIVES phase 1 indefinitely, because phase 1 never checks reciprocity. Self-loop A→A: SURVIVES (GetZDO(A)=A, tag equals itself, connection non-None). Connection to a non-portal ZDO X: survives if X resolves, X's `tag` string equals the portal's, and X has any non-None Portal connection — and X is never itself iterated because it is not in m_portalObjects. — `Game.ConnectPortals:100594-100622 + Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal:100664-100679 + ZDOExtraData.GetString default "":75079-75082` → 3+ portals on one tag permanently strand one member — a free 'broken network' detector for an admin report. Rings, chains, self-loops and non-portal destination anchors are all stable under vanilla's own reconciler, which is the entire foundation for admin-defined fixed networks with zero client install.
- **[dedicated-server]** There are THREE distinct portal-connect routines and only one runs at runtime. `Game.ConnectPortals()` is public and runs every 5s. `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals()` is private and called exactly twice, both at world load (`ZDOMan.LoadChunks` :76515 and `ZDOMan.Load` :76653 under `version >= Version.World.NewSaveFormat`); it relinks connections from save-file hashes, not tags. `ZDOMan.ConvertPortals()` is private and called once, from `ZDOMan.Load` :76631 only when `version < Version.World.NewSaveFormat`; it is a legacy migration keyed on `ZDOVars.s_toRemoveTarget`. — `Game.ConnectPortals assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals :77850; ZDOMan.ConvertPortals :77812; call sites :76515, :76653, :76631` → A Harmony patch aimed at 'ConnectPortals' MUST specify the declaring type. Patching ZDOMan.ConnectPortals gets you nothing at runtime; patching Game.ConnectPortals gets you the whole live algorithm.
- **[dedicated-server]** The coroutine is started once, by string name, in `Game.Start()` inside `if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())`, alongside `InvokeRepeating("UpdateSleeping", 2f, 2f)`. Body: `while(true){ ConnectPortals(); yield return new WaitForSeconds(5f); }` — the first ConnectPortals() call therefore happens synchronously at Start, before the first 5s wait. — `Game.Start assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100066-100075 (StartCoroutine at :100074); Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine :100580-100587` → Period is exactly 5.0s of scaled game time, phase-locked to server start. Because it was started with the string overload, `Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")` is the clean way for a mod to take over pairing wholesale (Unity API semantics, not a decompile claim). There is no StopCoroutine for it anywhere in the assembly — it runs for the life of the Game object.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` allocates a brand-new `List<ZDO>` on every call and flattens `m_portalObjects` (a `Dictionary<ZoneSystem.SectorIndex, List<ZDO>>`) into it. There is no caching layer, no dirty flag consulted, and nothing to invalidate. — `ZDOMan.GetPortalList assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77648-77656; m_portalObjects field decl :76039` → Reads are always current — a mod can add/remove portal ZDOs and the very next tick sees them. Cost is one List allocation plus a full copy per 5s tick; acceptable to call `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` on a faster timer for instant re-pairing.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` returns the LIVE `m_portalObjects` dictionary itself, not a copy. — `ZDOMan.GetPortals assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77643-77646` → A mod can mutate the server's portal registry directly (inject or hide portal ZDOs from the pairing algorithm) without any patch at all. Dangerous but powerful — removing a ZDO from this dictionary makes vanilla's pairer blind to it while the ZDO remains live for clients.
- **[dedicated-server]** `m_portalObjects` is populated exclusively by `ZDOMan.AddIfPortal(zdo, prefabHash)`, gated on `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(prefabHash)`. It is called from `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(uid, position, prefabHashIn)` (:76689) and from the ZDO deserialize loop in `RPC_ZDOData` (:77132). AddIfPortal also calls `RemoveFromSector(zdo, zdo.GetSectorIndex())`, so portals are stored ONLY in m_portalObjects and never in m_objectsBySector. — `ZDOMan.AddIfPortal assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77732-77752; callers :76689 and :77132` → Any ZDO a mod creates with a portal prefab hash is auto-registered as a portal. Conversely, a destination-anchor ZDO created with a NON-portal prefab hash is invisible to the pairing algorithm (never iterated, never reconciled) while still being a perfectly valid teleport target.
- **[unknown-needs-ingame-check]** `Game.PortalPrefabHash` is a `List<int>` built once in `Game.Awake()` from `foreach (GameObject portalPrefab in m_portalPrefabs) PortalPrefabHash.Add(portalPrefab.name.GetStableHashCode())`. `m_portalPrefabs` is a serialized `List<GameObject>` Inspector field — no prefab name string appears anywhere in the decompiled C#. — `Game.Awake assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100027-100032; field `public List<GameObject> m_portalPrefabs;` :99828; property `public List<int> PortalPrefabHash { get; private set; }` :99847-ish` → The exact set of prefabs treated as portals is Unity asset data. PortalPrefabHash is a public get / private set List<int> — a mod CAN `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Add(hash)` at runtime (the list object is mutable even though the setter is private), which is how you would make a custom or additional prefab participate in vanilla pairing.
- **[dedicated-server]** World-load path: `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` reads the dedicated portal chunk file (`ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal = new ChunkIndex(1, 0)`) and puts those ZDOs straight into `m_portalObjects` + `m_objectsByID`, bypassing `FilterZDO` and `InitialAddToSector` entirely. It then calls `ConnectPortals()` (ZDOMan's, :76515), `ConnectSpawners()`, `ConnectSyncTransforms()`, then `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` (:76523), then sets `DirtyPortalObjects = false`. — `ZDOMan.LoadChunks assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76474-76531; ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal :113180` → Portals live in their own save chunk and are all resident in server memory from world load onward. At the moment Game.ConnectPortals runs during load, `m_peers` is empty, so `ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner)` is always null and every SetConnection takes the immediate local-write path — a mod hooking load-time pairing never has to deal with the deferred-RPC branch.
- **[dedicated-server]** Portals are never unloaded or released on the server. `ZDOMan.Update` calls `ReleaseZDOS(dt)` under `IsServer()`, but `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` only reassigns *ownership* — it never removes a ZDO. A mod wanting instant repair calls Game.instance.ConnectPortals() from ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed or a fast timer.
- **[dedicated-server]** `DirtyPortalObjects` (:76139) is a per-save-state flag array consumed ONLY by `GetSaveClonePerChunk` (:77621-77635) to decide whether to rewrite the portal chunk file. A mod re-asserting the same connection every tick costs nothing and generates no network traffic (revision unchanged means no resend), which makes a high-frequency 'integrity re-assert' loop cheap.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZDO.UpdateConnection` differs from SetConnection: it returns false and writes NOTHING if there is no existing `s_connections` entry for the ZDO. It never creates a connection, only overwrites one. — `ZDO.UpdateConnection :73668-73678; ZDOExtraData.UpdateConnection :74963-74977` → `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` uses UpdateConnection, so retagging a portal that had no connection is a pure no-op on the connection field. Do not use UpdateConnection in mod code to establish a link.
- **[dedicated-server]** The reconcile predicate is exactly `zDO == null || zDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) != @string || zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal) == ZDOID.None`. It does NOT verify that the partner points back at this portal. — `Game.ConnectPortals assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100600-100604` → Non-reciprocal topologies are fully stable in vanilla: one-way links, rings, hub fan-in, and self-loops all survive indefinitely as long as every participant shares one literal tag string and every participant's connection field is non-None. This is the single most exploitable property for a server-only portal-network mod.
- **[dedicated-server]** Tag equality uses C# `string !=` on the result of `ZDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` with `defaultValue = ""`. That is `string.Equals` ordinal semantics: case-SENSITIVE, culture-invariant, whitespace-significant, no trimming, no normalization. `ZDOVars.s_tag = "tag".GetStableHashCode()`, `s_tagauthor = "tagauthor".GetStableHashCode()`. — `Game.ConnectPortals :100597, :100601, :100611; Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100669; ZDO.GetString :73967-73970; ZDOExtraData.GetString :75079-75082; ZDOVars.s_tag :78617, s_tagauthor :78619` → 'Home' and 'home' are different networks. A tag with a trailing space is a distinct network and an easy invisible griefing/confusion vector — a server-side normalization/validation pass at write time is trivially justified. Because the default is "" (never null), untagged portals compare equal to each other and auto-pair.
- **[dedicated-server]** `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(portals, skip, tag)` builds a candidate list with `portal != skip` — REFERENCE inequality, because `ZDO` declares no `operator ==`/`operator !=` (it implements only `IEquatable<ZDO>` with `Equals(ZDO other) => m_uid == other.m_uid`). It then returns `list[UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, list.Count)]` (int overload, max-exclusive), or null on an empty list. — `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664-100679; ZDO class decl `public class ZDO : IEquatable<ZDO>` :73262; ZDO.Equals(ZDO) :73527-73534; ZDO.GetHashCode :73522` → Two distinct ZDO objects with the same m_uid would both be considered valid candidates by `!=` — which is exactly what the sector-duplication bug below produces. Note the asymmetry: `List<ZDO>.Contains`/`Remove` (used by AddIfPortal and HandleDestroyedZDO) DO use IEquatable/m_uid equality, while the pairing loop uses reference equality.
- **[dedicated-server]** Pairing selection uses the shared global `UnityEngine.Random` state, not a dedicated RNG. — `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100678` → Pairing is genuinely non-deterministic and unseeded from the mod's perspective; replacing FindRandomUnconnectedPortal with a deterministic (nearest / oldest / admin-designated) picker is a clean, well-isolated Harmony target with a simple signature.
- **[dedicated-server]** `Game.SetConnection(ZDO portal, ZDOID connection, bool forceImmediateConnection = false)` writes locally — `portal.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); portal.SetConnection(Portal, connection); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(portal.m_uid)` — when `owner == 0L || ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner) == null || forceImmediateConnection`. Otherwise it sends `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(owner, "RPC_SetConnection", portal.m_uid, connection)`. — `Game.SetConnection assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100637-100651` → CONFIRMS the central claim: the server does NOT need to own a portal ZDO to rewrite its connection — it will forcibly steal ownership whenever the ZDO is unowned or its owner is not a currently connected peer. The only case where it defers is an online player who currently owns that portal's ZDO.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZNet.GetUID()` returns `ZDOMan.GetSessionID()`, and `ZNetPeer.m_uid` is assigned from the remote's own GetUID during the PeerInfo handshake. So the test `ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner) != null` is exactly 'the ZDO's owner is a currently connected remote client'; the server's own session ID is never in ZNet's m_peers list. — `ZNet.GetUID :80866-80869; ZNet peer handshake `peer.m_uid = uid;` :79905; ZNet.GetPeer(long) :80492-80502; ZDOMan.GetSessionID :77362-77365` → A portal the server itself owns always takes the immediate local-write path (GetPeer(serverSessionID) is null), so mod writes on server-owned portals are always synchronous and visible to the very next line of code.

The server therefore ALWAYS wins the pairing decision within one tick — a client that ignores or drops RPC_SetConnection cannot prevent it.
- **[dedicated-server]** `IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal` is checked both in phase 2's loop guard (:100609) and inside FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100671). Because the list is cleared at the top of every call, it only guards WITHIN a single tick — it exists precisely because a deferred (RPC) write leaves the server's own copy of the connection reading `None`, which would otherwise let the same portal be paired twice in one pass. — `Game.ConnectPortals :100609; Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100671; Game.IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal :100700-100710` → Any mod that re-implements phase 2 must reproduce this guard or it will double-pair portals owned by online players.
- **[dedicated-server]** ORDERING TRAP: phase 1's `SetConnection(item, ZDOID.None)` is NOT force, so when the portal is owned by an online peer the clear is deferred over RPC and the server's local copy still reads the OLD connection. Phase 2, running in the same tick over the same snapshot, therefore sees `!IsNone()` and skips it. Re-pairing happens only on a later tick, after the client applies the clear and its ZDO update reaches the server. — `Game.ConnectPortals :100603 (no force) vs :100609 (IsNone check)` → Retagging a portal a player is standing next to takes 2+ ticks (up to ~10s+ round-trip) to re-pair, not 5s. A mod that wants instant retag→repair should write the tag AND clear/re-establish the connection itself with force semantics (SetOwner(sessionID) then SetConnection) rather than waiting for vanilla.
- **[zdo-owning-client]** `Game.RPC_SetConnection` is registered unconditionally in `Game.Start()` (outside the `IsServer()` block), so every vanilla client has the handler. The client-side body sets the ZDO's owner to its OWN session ID, writes the connection, and ForceSendZDO's it. — `Game.Start registration :100070; Game.RPC_SetConnection :100653-100662` → The deferred path works against 100% vanilla clients with no mod — this is vanilla's own cross-machine connection-write protocol. A server mod can invoke the same routed RPC to make an owning client write a connection on the server's behalf.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` runs on the server every 2s for the server's own reference position and for EVERY connected peer's `m_refPos`, and it reassigns ownership of persistent ZDOs — including portals, because `FindSectorObjects`→`FindObjects` explicitly merges `m_portalObjects[sectorIndex]` into the result. It releases ownership to 0 when the current owner has left the ZDO's active area, and assigns ownership to a peer when the ZDO is unowned (or its owner is out of area) and the ZDO is in that peer's active area. — `ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS :76872-76883; ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76924; ZDOMan.FindObjects portal merge :77376-77379; ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects :77142` → A server-only mod's ownership claim on a portal near an online player is stolen back within 2s. The connection VALUE it wrote survives (it was already ForceSendZDO'd), but any follow-up write must re-claim ownership. Wonderland already solves exactly this with a `ZDO.SetOwner` Harmony prefix — see /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313 (ZdoSetOwnerPatch) and its comment at line 27. That pattern is directly reusable for portals.
- **[dedicated-server]** DANGLING CONNECTIONS ARE DROPPED AT SAVE TIME, independently of the runtime reconcile. `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData()` (called from `PrepareSave`) only emits hash data for a connection when `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connection.Key) != null` AND `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connection.Value.m_target) != null` (the target exemption applies only to ConnectionType.Spawned). — `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData :75461-75478; ZDOExtraData.PrepareSave :75480-75491` → A portal pointed at a ZDOID that does not resolve loses its link permanently across a save/load cycle even if something suppressed the runtime reconcile. A mod using a custom destination-anchor ZDO must keep that anchor alive in m_objectsByID or the link will not persist.
- **[dedicated-server]** Connections are persisted as a generated INT HASH PAIR, not as ZDOIDs. `ZDO.Save` writes `(byte)connectionData.m_type` + `connectionData.m_hash`; `ZDO.Load` reads them back into `ZDOExtraData.SetConnectionData`. The source side gets `ConnectionType.Portal` (1) and the target side gets `ConnectionType.Portal | ConnectionType.Target` (0x11) with the SAME hash, generated by `GetUniqueHash` seeded from `ZDOMan.GetSessionID().GetHashCode() + s_uniqueHashes`. — `ZDO.Save :74243-74318 (connection write :74315-74317); ZDO.Load :74596-74598; ZDOExtraData.SetConnectionData :74992-74996; ZDOExtraData.GetUniqueHash :75440-75459; ConnectionType enum :74747-74754` → You cannot read a portal's saved destination out of a world file by ZDOID — you must match hash pairs the way ZDOMan.ConnectPortals does. Also: the on-disk connection is inherently directional (source vs target), even though the runtime representation is two independent one-way `s_connections` entries.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals()` (the load-time one) relinks by hash: it takes `GetAllConnectionZDOIDs(Portal)` as sources and `GetAllConnectionZDOIDs(Portal|Target)` as targets, skips any candidate whose runtime `ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionType(item2) != ConnectionType.None` (i.e. already relinked this pass), matches on `m_hash` equality, then `SetOwner(GetSessionID())` on both and writes reciprocal `SetConnection(Portal, ...)` on both, `break`ing after the first match. It does not look at tags at all and does not remove the hash data afterwards (unlike ConnectSpawners, which calls RemoveConnectionHashData at :77974). — `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals :77850-77893; ZDOExtraData.GetAllConnectionZDOIDs(ConnectionType) :75414-75427; ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionType :75104-75107` → Load-time relinking is O(sources × targets) and tag-agnostic, and it makes the server the owner of BOTH ends of every portal pair at world load. That is the cheapest possible window for a server mod to rewrite a network: right after load, before any peer connects, every portal ZDO is server-owned.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZDOMan.ConvertPortals()` (legacy pre-NewSaveFormat migration) is strictly reciprocal: it links A and B only when `A.tag == B.tag` AND `A.s_toRemoveTarget == B.m_uid` AND `B.s_toRemoveTarget == A.m_uid`, and it strips `s_toRemoveTarget` from every portal it touches whether or not the link is made. — `ZDOMan.ConvertPortals :77812-77848` → Confirms the old save format DID require mutual targeting; the modern runtime reconciler deliberately relaxed that to a one-way check. Irrelevant to a 1.0.7 world but useful for explaining why old-world imports drop asymmetric links.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID(zid, type)` returns `ZDOID.None` unless the stored connection's `m_type` matches `type` EXACTLY. `s_connections` is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` — a ZDO can hold at most ONE connection of any kind, and `ZDOConnection.m_target` is a single readonly ZDOID. — `ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID :75094-75102; class ZDOConnection :75524-75534; ZDOExtraData.SetConnection :74951-74961` → A true simultaneous multi-destination hub is structurally impossible — only one ZDOID fits. Also, writing `Portal|Target` (0x11) onto a portal makes vanilla read it as unconnected (phase 1 skips it, phase 2 re-pairs it), so do not use the Target bit on live portal ZDOs.
- **[zdo-owning-client]** `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` is gated on `m_nview.IsValid() && m_nview.IsOwner()` and is registered on the portal's ZNetView in `TeleportWorld.Awake`. A dedicated server never instantiates a portal GameObject, so no ZNetView exists and this method NEVER executes server-side. Its body clears its own connection via `UpdateConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)`, calls `SetConnectedPortal` (which either takes ownership of the partner and clears it, or RPCs `RPC_SetConnected` to the partner's owner), then writes `s_tag` and `s_tagauthor`. — `TeleportWorld.Awake registration :143447-143448; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag :143587-143602; TeleportWorld.SetConnectedPortal :143604-143620; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetConnected :143622-143629` → CONFIRMS the central constraint at the tag layer too: a Harmony patch on TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag will never fire on a dedicated server. Server-side tag interception must happen at the ZRoutedRpc relay layer instead.
- **[dedicated-server]** The server DOES see and relay every `RPC_SetTag` packet: `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` deserializes it, calls `HandleRoutedRPC` (which no-ops for ZDO-targeted RPCs because `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zDO)` returns null with no portal GameObject), then calls `RouteRPC` which forwards it to the target peer (or broadcasts if m_targetPeerID == 0). — `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC :83632-83643; ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC :83645-83663; ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC :83597-83629; ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC :83577-83595` → A prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` or `RouteRPC` keyed on `"RPC_SetTag".GetStableHashCode()` is the ONLY server-side interception point for tag changes — this is the same hook shape Wonderland already uses (`RoutedRpcHandlerPatch` on ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:315-327). Returning false from a RouteRPC prefix drops the tag change before it reaches the owning client.
- **[local-player-client]** `TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player)` reads only `GetPosition()` and `GetRotation()` off the connected ZDO and never checks its prefab. `TargetFound()` only requires `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connectionZDOID) != null` on the client, and calls `ZDOMan.instance.RequestZDO(connectionZDOID)` if it is missing. Its sole caller remains `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter`, gated on `Player.m_localPlayer`. — `TeleportWorld.Teleport :143517-143549; TeleportWorld.TargetFound :143638-143653; TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter :143672-143681; ZDOMan.RequestZDO :77687-77690; ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO :77692-77695` → CONFIRMS the central constraint verbatim, and simultaneously confirms that any ZDO with a position+rotation works as a destination for a 100% vanilla client. The client must actually hold that ZDO, which `ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO` (called by Game.SetConnection) and the RequestZDO round-trip both provide.
- **[dedicated-server]** BUG/TRAP — sector duplication: `AddIfPortal` looks up `m_portalObjects[zdo.GetSectorIndex()]` and adds the ZDO if not already in THAT bucket, but never removes it from the bucket keyed by its previous sector. `GetSectorIndex()` is derived live from `m_position`. — `ZDOMan.AddIfPortal :77732-77752; ZDO.GetSectorIndex :73776-73779; ZoneSystem.GetSectorIndex :115748-115754` → If a mod moves a portal ZDO across a 64m zone boundary (or a ZDOData update arrives with a new position), that portal appears TWICE in GetPortalList(). Because phase 2's exclusion uses reference inequality (`portal != skip`), the same ZDO object is filtered correctly — but it will be VISITED twice by both loops, and HandleDestroyedZDO will only clean one bucket, leaking the other. Never reposition a portal ZDO; create a new one instead.
- **[dedicated-server]** BUG/TRAP — pooled ZDO reuse across ticks: `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` holds raw `ZDO` object references for a full 5s. If one of those portals is destroyed in that window, `HandleDestroyedZDO` calls `ZDOPool.Release(zDO)` → `zdo.Reset()` which sets `m_uid = ZDOID.None`, and `ZDOPool.Get()` can hand the same object out for an unrelated new ZDO. The next tick's `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` then force-writes a Portal connection using a stale/recycled reference. — `Game.ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698; ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO ZDOPool.Release :76990; ZDOPool.Release/Get :78286-78311; ZDO.Reset (`m_uid = ZDOID.None`) :73536-73545` → HARD RULE for the mod: never cache `ZDO` object references across ticks. Cache `ZDOID` values and re-resolve with `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id)` every tick. Vanilla itself violates this; the blast radius is small (writes land on ZDOID.None and are filtered out at save by RegenerateConnectionHashData's `Key == ZDOID.None` guard) but it is real.
- **[dedicated-server]** Iteration order of both passes is the enumeration order of `Dictionary<SectorIndex, List<ZDO>>` buckets (hash-bucket order, perturbed by removals), then list order within each bucket. It is not sorted by position, tag, creation time, or ZDOID, and is not stable across server restarts. — `ZDOMan.GetPortalList :77648-77656; m_portalObjects :76039; ZoneSystem.SectorIndex.GetHashCode returns (int)Sector :113114-113117` → Which of 3 same-tag portals gets orphaned is effectively arbitrary and can change across a restart. Any admin-facing feature must not assume stable identity of the orphan; a deterministic replacement picker must sort the list itself.
- **[dedicated-server]** Per-pair logging: `ZLog.Log("Connected portals " + item2 + " <-> " + zDO2)` (ZDO.ToString() returns `m_uid.ToString()`, i.e. `userID:ID`), plus a per-tick `ZLog.Log("[ Connected " + num + " portals ]")` when num > 0. The load-time routines log `"ConnectPortals => Connected N portals."` and `"ConvertPortals => fixed N portals."` via UnityEngine.Debug.Log. — `Game.ConnectPortals :100619, :100625; ZDO.ToString :73514-73517; ZDOID.ToString :75884; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals :77891; ZDOMan.ConvertPortals :77845` → Vanilla already emits a parseable pairing audit trail to the dedicated server log with zero patching — usable as a cheap Discord notifier before any Harmony work is done.

### Server-callable APIs
- `public void Game.ConnectPortals()` @ assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589 — serverCallable=True; THE runtime pairing tick. Public and instance-level, so `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` can be called on demand (e.g. a 0.5s timer for instant re-pairing after a tag change) and is a clean Harmony prefix/postfix/transpiler target. Calling it out-of-band is safe and idempotent: phase 0 force-commits any pending proposals, phase 1 re-validates, phase 2 only touches ZDOID.None portals. A prefix returning false disables vanilla pairing entirely without stopping the coroutine.
- `private IEnumerator Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine()  // started via StartCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine") in Game.Start, under if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` @ assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100580 (start site :100074) — serverCallable=True; Period exactly 5.0f WaitForSeconds, first call synchronous at Start. Because it was started by string name, `Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")` stops it (Unity API semantics — verify in-game). No StopCoroutine for it exists anywhere in the assembly. Note WaitForSeconds is scaled time; Time.timeScale is 1 on a dedicated server in practice but that is an in-game assumption, not a decompile fact.
- `public List<ZDO> ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` @ assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77648 — serverCallable=True; Allocates a fresh List<ZDO> each call and flattens m_portalObjects. Returns EVERY portal in the world regardless of player proximity (the server never unloads ZDOs). No cache, no invalidation. This is the free, zero-bookkeeping world portal census — tag, position (ZDO.GetPosition), rotation, connection (GetConnectionZDOID), and owner (GetOwner) all readable off each element.
- `public Dictionary<ZoneSystem.SectorIndex, List<ZDO>> ZDOMan.GetPortals()` @ assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77643 — serverCallable=True; Returns the LIVE backing dictionary, not a copy. Mutating it changes what vanilla's pairer sees. Keyed by ZoneSystem.SectorIndex (a uint wrapping 64m zone coords, ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex :115762). Use for read-only enumeration by region; mutate only with a clear reason.
- `private ZDO Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(List<ZDO> portals, ZDO skip, string tag)` @ assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100664 — serverCallable=True; Private — reachable via Harmony with `AccessTools.Method(typeof(Game), "FindRandomUnconnectedPortal")`. A postfix that overwrites __result is the minimal, lowest-risk way to replace random pairing with nearest/oldest/admin-designated selection while leaving every other vanilla behaviour (two-phase commit, ownership handling, logging) intact.
- `private void Game.SetConnection(ZDO portal, ZDOID connection, bool forceImmediateConnection = false)` @ assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100637 — serverCallable=True; Private. Do not reimplement it badly — the exact semantics are: write locally (stealing ownership via `portal.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`) when `owner == 0L`, or the owner is not a connected ZNet peer, or force is true; otherwise send `RPC_SetConnection` to the owner. A mod that wants unconditional immediate writes should call the public primitives directly in the same order: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, targetId); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);`
- `public void ZDO.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType connectionType, ZDOID zid)` @ assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73656 — serverCallable=True; Public. Use ConnectionType.Portal (value 1). No-ops silently if type+target are unchanged. On a real change it bumps DataRevision and calls ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() for you. Do NOT use ZDO.UpdateConnection (:73668) — it refuses to create a connection where none exists.
- `public ZDOID ZDO.GetConnectionZDOID(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType type)` @ assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74002 — serverCallable=True; Public. Returns ZDOID.None unless the stored connection's type matches EXACTLY (Portal == 1; Portal|Target == 0x11 does NOT match Portal). Pair with ZDOID.IsNone() (:75950) or `== ZDOID.None` (ZDOID.operator== :75888).
- `public string ZDO.GetString(int hash, string defaultValue = "")  // hash = ZDOVars.s_tag / ZDOVars.s_tagauthor` @ assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73967; ZDOVars.s_tag :78617; ZDOVars.s_tagauthor :78619 — serverCallable=True; Public, and the write side `ZDO.Set(int hash, string value)` is equally public. Writing the tag server-side is a plain ZDO write — no RPC, no 10-char cap (that limit is client UI only), no profanity filter (client display-time only). Default is "" and never null, which is why untagged portals form one tag group.
- `public void ZDO.SetOwner(long uid)  /  public static long ZDOMan.GetSessionID()  /  public void ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(ZDOID id)` @ assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74627, :77362, :77683 — serverCallable=True; The ownership-claim triad. `ZDO.SetOwner` no-ops if the owner is unchanged; `SetOwnerInternal` sets `Owner = (uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`. ForceSendZDO(ZDOID) pushes to every peer; the `ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID)` overload (:77697) targets one peer on the server. WARNING: ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901) will reassign ownership away within 2s if a peer is near the portal — guard with a `ZDO.SetOwner` Harmony prefix (pattern: Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313).
- `public void ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals()` @ assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702 — serverCallable=True; Public. Marks the portal chunk file dirty so the next save rewrites it. ZDO.SetConnection(Portal, ...) calls this automatically; a mod writing the `tag` string alone should call it explicitly to guarantee persistence.

Using a NON-portal prefab hash yields a 'destination anchor' ZDO that TeleportWorld.Teleport will happily read position/rotation from (:143536-143543) but that vanilla's pairer never iterates. - `public List<int> Game.PortalPrefabHash { get; private set; }` @ assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:99847-ish (property), populated in Game.Awake :100029 — serverCallable=True; Private setter but the List object itself is mutable: `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Add("myprefab".GetStableHashCode())` makes that prefab participate in AddIfPortal / GetPortalList / vanilla pairing. Conversely `.Remove(hash)` at runtime does NOT retroactively un-register already-tracked ZDOs from m_portalObjects.

A prefix on RouteRPC returning false drops the tag change before any client applies it; reading `data.m_parameters` (a ZPackage, SetPos(0) already applied by InvokeRoutedRPC) yields the new tag string and the self-reported authorId.
