### Gotchas
- Two things are named ConnectPortals. `Game.ConnectPortals()` (:100589) is the public 5s runtime pairer keyed on tags. `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals()` (:77850) is private, runs only during world load, and matches save-file connection HASHES with no tag involvement. Patching the wrong one does nothing at runtime.
- Phase 1 never checks reciprocity. `A→B` survives even when `B→C`. This means rings, one-way chains, hub fan-in, and self-loops (`A→A`) are all indefinitely stable in pure vanilla — but ONLY while every participant shares one byte-identical tag string and every participant's Portal connection stays non-None. The moment one member's connection goes None, its neighbours' links get torn down by the `q.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None` clause.
- Tag comparison is `string !=` — ordinal, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant. 'Base' / 'base' / 'Base ' are three separate networks. The default value is "" (never null), so every untagged portal in the world is a single tag group and freshly-placed untagged portals auto-connect to a random untagged portal anywhere.
- 3+ portals on one tag permanently strand exactly one member. The orphan does NOT rotate in on later ticks, because the surviving pair keeps re-confirming itself. Which one is stranded depends on dictionary bucket order and is not stable across restarts.
- Phase 1's disconnect is NOT forced, so when an online player owns the portal it is deferred over RPC and the server's own ZDO still reads the old connection — phase 2 in the same tick therefore skips it. Re-pairing after a retag near a player takes 2+ ticks, not one.
- The server does not need to own a portal ZDO to rewrite it, but ownership is transient in the other direction: `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) runs every 2s and hands portal ownership to any peer in whose active area the portal sits. A mod's SetOwner claim will be stolen back within 2s unless guarded with a `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix (Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313 does exactly this for floating items).
- `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` caches raw ZDO object references for 5 seconds. `ZDOPool.Release`/`Get` recycles ZDO objects on destruction. Vanilla can therefore force-write a connection through a recycled reference. HARD RULE for mod code: cache ZDOIDs, never ZDO objects, across ticks.
- `AddIfPortal` adds a portal to the bucket for its CURRENT sector but never removes it from its old bucket. Moving a portal ZDO across a 64m zone boundary duplicates it in `GetPortalList()` and leaks a bucket entry that `HandleDestroyedZDO` will not clean. Never reposition a portal ZDO — destroy and recreate.
- `portal != skip` in FindRandomUnconnectedPortal is REFERENCE inequality (ZDO has no operator==), while `List<ZDO>.Contains/Remove` used in AddIfPortal and HandleDestroyedZDO use `IEquatable<ZDO>.Equals` (m_uid equality). Two ZDO objects with the same uid behave differently in the two places.
- A ZDO can hold exactly ONE connection (`Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>`, single readonly target ZDOID). A simultaneous multi-destination hub is structurally impossible, not merely unimplemented. Only time-sliced rotation works.
- Writing ConnectionType.Portal|Target (0x11) onto a live portal makes `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` return None, so vanilla will treat it as unconnected and re-pair it. Only use bare ConnectionType.Portal on runtime portal ZDOs; the Target bit belongs to the save-hash representation only.
- Dangling connections are dropped at SAVE time independently of the runtime reconcile: `RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461) only persists a connection when both endpoint ZDOs resolve in `m_objectsByID`. A custom destination-anchor ZDO must stay alive in ZDOMan or the link vanishes across restart even if it looked fine in memory.
- `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` is gated on `m_nview.IsOwner()` and the server never instantiates a portal ZNetView, so a Harmony patch on it NEVER fires on a dedicated server. The only server-side interception point for tag changes is the ZRoutedRpc relay (`HandleRoutedRPC` / `RouteRPC`).
- `Game.RPC_SetConnection` is registered on BOTH server and client (outside the IsServer block, :100070), and the client handler takes ownership for itself. That is vanilla's own cross-machine write protocol — but it also means a hostile client could invoke RPC_SetConnection at any peer to rewrite a portal link; nothing validates the sender. (Same trust gap class the existing spec already flags for RPC_SetTag.)
- `Game.ConnectPortals()` runs synchronously during world load from `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` (:76523) and `ZDOMan.Load` (:76658). At that moment `m_peers` is empty so every write takes the immediate local path and the server ends up owning both ends of every pair. That pre-peer window is the cheapest possible time to rewrite a network.
- The pairing loop's candidate filter also excludes portals already in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals`. Any reimplementation that drops that guard will double-pair portals owned by online players, because their connection writes are deferred and the server's copy still reads None.

### Open questions
- Which prefabs are in `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (and therefore `PortalPrefabHash`)? The list is a serialized Inspector field on the Game prefab and no prefab-name string for it appears anywhere in either decompiled assembly. IN-GAME CHECK: on a dedicated server with a mod loaded, log `string.Join(",", Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash)` in a Game.Start postfix and cross-reference against `ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs` names via GetStableHashCode — or simply log `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)?.name` for each entry. Specifically needed to confirm whether the Ashlands `portal_stone` is a separate PortalPrefabHash entry from the wood portal.
- Does `Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")` actually stop it? StartCoroutine was called with the string overload (:100074), which per Unity's API makes the string StopCoroutine valid, but this is a Unity runtime claim, not a decompile claim. IN-GAME CHECK: call it, then watch the server log for the absence of `[ Connected N portals ]` lines after deliberately placing two same-tag portals.
- What is `ZNet.GetReferencePosition()` on a dedicated server at runtime? `m_referencePosition` is declared `= Vector3.zero` (:79043) and `SetReferencePosition` (:81016) is the only writer; if it is truly never called server-side, then `ReleaseNearbyZDOS(ZNet.GetReferencePosition(), m_sessionID)` permanently treats the world origin as the server's active area, meaning the server will only auto-retain ownership of portals near (0,0,0). IN-GAME CHECK: log ZNet.instance.GetReferencePosition() every 10s on a live dedicated server.
- Timing of the ownership tug-of-war: `ReleaseZDOS` runs every 2s and `ConnectPortals` every 5s, both on the main thread but from different drivers (Update vs coroutine). The exact interleaving determines how often a server-written portal connection is followed by an ownership steal before the next write. IN-GAME CHECK: log owner transitions on one portal ZDO with a player standing next to it for 60s.
- Does a client cleanly handle a portal whose connected ZDO has a prefab hash it cannot instantiate (a pure 'destination anchor')? `TeleportWorld.TargetFound` only needs `GetZDO != null`, and `Teleport` only reads position/rotation, but `ZNetScene` will still attempt to create an object for that ZDO when the client's active area covers it. IN-GAME CHECK: create an anchor ZDO with an existing harmless prefab hash (e.g. a marker piece) vs. an unregistered hash, stand near each with a vanilla client, and watch the client log for CreateObject failures.
- Whether `WaitForSeconds(5f)` is affected by any server-side Time.timeScale manipulation (e.g. the sleep/time-skip path in Game.UpdateSleeping :100712+). IN-GAME CHECK: trigger a sleep skip on a live server and measure the interval between `[ Connected N portals ]` log lines.

### Corrections to the existing spec
- Anchor correction: the prompt lists `Game.ConnectPortals()` at :100592. The method declaration is at :100589; :100592 is the `List<ZDO> portalList = ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList();` line inside it. Phase 1 (reconcile) is :100594-100606, phase 2 (pair) is :100607-100622.
- Anchor correction: the prompt's range ':77815-77891' for 'ZDOMan-internal portal bookkeeping' actually spans two different methods — `ZDOMan.ConvertPortals()` at :77812 (legacy pre-NewSaveFormat migration keyed on ZDOVars.s_toRemoveTarget) and `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals()` at :77850 (load-time hash relinking). The true per-ZDO bookkeeping is elsewhere: `AddIfPortal` :77732, `HandleDestroyedZDO` portal branch :76980-76987, `GetPortalList` :77648, `GetPortals` :77643.
- The spec says 'Game.ConnectPortals() ... re-evaluates every same-tagged pair every 5 seconds'. More precisely: it does TWO separate things per tick — a reconcile pass over ALL connected portals (which is where 'wrongly connected' is decided) and a pairing pass over only ZDOID.None portals. Only the second is tag-driven matchmaking; the first is a validity check that also uses tag equality but as a tear-down condition.
- The spec's claim 'A ring is self-stable under vanilla's own self-heal check as long as members share a tag and stay non-None; a fan-in hub member can self-loop to stay "connected" without a real return route' is CONFIRMED exactly, and the mechanism is precisely that phase 1's predicate (:100601) checks only `q != null`, `q.tag == p.tag`, and `q.connection != None` — never `q.connection == p.uid`.
- The spec's claim 'vanilla's self-heal transitively forces every linked portal to share one literal tag string' is CONFIRMED and should be stated more strongly: the equality is ORDINAL C# string comparison with `""` as default, so case and whitespace differences break a network silently, and ALL untagged portals in the world form one implicit group.
- The spec's claim '3+ portals sharing a tag permanently strands one under vanilla's strictly-pairwise algorithm' is CONFIRMED, with the added detail that the orphan never rotates in on later ticks (the surviving pair re-confirms itself every tick) and that which portal is orphaned is dictionary-bucket-order dependent and not stable across restarts.
- The spec says the mod can rewrite connections because 'Vanilla itself already takes ownership of an offline portal's ZDO'. Sharpen this: the ownership steal is NOT limited to offline portals. `Game.SetConnection` force-writes whenever `owner == 0L` OR the owner is not a connected peer OR `forceImmediateConnection` is true — and `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` passes force=true on the very next tick for every pair proposed in the previous one. So the server unconditionally wins any pairing dispute within ≤5s, even against an online owning player.
- ADD TO THE SPEC — a mechanism it does not mention: `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) runs on the SERVER every 2s and actively reassigns portal ZDO ownership to nearby peers (portals are included via FindObjects :77376). Any 'proactive server ownership claim on placement' feature (currently listed as [Feasible, medium]) will be undone within 2s near an online player unless it also ships a `ZDO.SetOwner` Harmony prefix, exactly as Wonderland's WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313 already does for floating items.
- ADD TO THE SPEC — a concrete new design primitive it misses: a destination-anchor ZDO created with a NON-portal prefab hash is (a) never iterated by GetPortalList, (b) never reconciled by phase 1, and (c) perfectly valid as a teleport target because TeleportWorld.Teleport (:143536-143543) reads only GetPosition/GetRotation and never checks the target's prefab. A portal P pointed at such an anchor X is permanently stable under vanilla's reconciler provided X resolves, `X.tag == P.tag`, and X has any non-None Portal connection (a self-loop suffices). This makes 'Portal to any computed coordinate' materially simpler and more robust than the spec implies.
- ADD TO THE SPEC — persistence caveat for the above: `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461) refuses to persist a connection whose target ZDO does not resolve in ZDOMan at save time. Any anchor-ZDO scheme must keep the anchor alive in m_objectsByID or the link silently disappears on restart, independent of the runtime reconciler.
- REFINE the spec's Group 4 point about RPC identity: TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag is unreachable server-side (no ZNetView), so the hardening hook is NOT a patch on TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag — it must be `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC` (:83597) or `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` (:83645), matched on `"RPC_SetTag".GetStableHashCode()` and `data.m_targetZDO`. The server does relay the packet, so interception and outright dropping are both possible.
- REFINE the spec's 'Instant re-pairing after a tag change' item: calling `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` on a fast timer does NOT give instant re-pairing when the portal is owned by an online player, because phase 1's disconnect is deferred over RPC and phase 2 in the same call still sees the stale connection. For genuinely instant behaviour the mod must do the write itself with force semantics (`SetOwner(sessionID)` then `SetConnection`) rather than relying on vanilla's two-pass flow.
- REFINE the spec's 'Distinct per-portal display tags within one managed group' [Feasible-with-caveats, medium]: the specific thing that must be bypassed is the `zDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) != @string` clause at :100601. A postfix on Game.ConnectPortals cannot help (the damage is already done); the options are a prefix returning false for managed portals, a transpiler on that one clause, `StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")`, or hiding managed portals from `m_portalObjects` via the live dictionary returned by `ZDOMan.GetPortals()`.

## GlobalKeys system end-to-end (server-authoritative levers for a zero-client-install portal mod), Valheim 1.0.7

GlobalKeys is a single flat `HashSet<string>` on `ZoneSystem` whose authority is the server: only the server registers `SetGlobalKey`/`RemoveGlobalKey` routed RPCs, and every mutation ends in `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` — a full-snapshot broadcast (`ClearGlobalKeys()` + re-add on each client) that reaches already-connected vanilla clients within one network frame, with no polling interval and no relog required. All four portal-relevant keys (`NoPortals`=32, `NoBossPortals`=33, `DungeonBuild`=34, `TeleportAll`=35) sit below `GlobalKeys.NonServerOption`(41), which means they are "server option"/world-modifier keys: `GlobalKeyAdd` mirrors them into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (the .fwl file, saved on every world autosave) and `ZoneSystem.Save` deliberately strips them from the .db — so they survive relog, reappear at boot via `SetStartingGlobalKeys()`, and change the advertised server-browser "modifiers" badge. World Modifiers / `ServerOptionsGUI` / `WorldModifierOption` are NOT a separate network channel: they are a pure presentation layer that writes the same global keys (`ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeys` → `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey`), so global keys are the only vanilla-respecting global lever (the only other genuinely networked global server setting is simulation distance). The claim about the `noportals` console command is CONFIRMED — its whole body is inside `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)` so it is inert on a dedicated server — but the spec's contrast with `nomap` is WRONG: `nomap`'s `IsServer()` branch is itself nested inside the same `Player.m_localPlayer != null` guard, so `nomap` is equally inert. Every key read the client performs (`TeleportWorld.Teleport`, `Inventory.IsTeleportable`, `Player.PlacePiece`) is a live read at the moment of use, never a cached/once-at-join snapshot.

### Gotchas
- RPC_SetGlobalKey and RPC_RemoveGlobalKey have ZERO sender validation (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:116022-116037). Any connected vanilla client can set or clear `noportals` / `teleportall` on the server. Any mod feature built on these keys is trivially defeated unless the mod also Harmony-prefixes both RPCs to drop packets whose `sender` is not the server's own id.
- Setting a portal key at runtime PERMANENTLY edits the world: GlobalKeyAdd mirrors every key with ordinal < NonServerOption(41) into ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys (:113511), which is written to the .fwl on the next autosave (ZNet.SaveWorldThread :80632). Removing the mod later leaves `noportals` baked into the world. To set a key for the session only, call the publicized `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` + `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` instead of SetGlobalKey.
- ZoneSystem.Save STRIPS every ordinal < 41 from the .db (:113749-113755). Do not expect to find `noportals` in the world database — looking there and finding nothing is not evidence the key is unset.
- ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys wipes ordinals 0..40 on every world load (:115906-115910) and re-adds only what is in the .fwl. Any mod-owned world-modifier key must be reapplied in a POSTFIX on that method or it silently vanishes at boot.
- `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` stringifies to "NoPortals" (PascalCase, :115938-115941) but the store holds only lowercase, so RPC_SetGlobalKey's `!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)` guard (:116024) never trips — every call re-adds and re-broadcasts the whole key list. In a polling loop this is a broadcast storm; pass the lowercase literal or pre-check with GetGlobalKey.
- SendGlobalKeys is a full replace, not a delta: the client does ClearGlobalKeys() then re-adds (:113473-113481). It is cheap (one small string list) but it also means the server cannot push a partial update, and any client-side key state is destroyed on every server-side key change.
- NoBossPortals is a WORLD-WIDE blackout, not a per-fight lock: `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() != null || activeBosses > 0` (:143528). One player aggroing Eikthyr blocks every portal for every player on the server. Worse, `activeBosses` is maintained by whichever client has the boss loaded (BaseAI.SetAlerted :27258), so a client crash mid-fight can leave the counter stuck above zero and portals permanently blocked — a server mod should watch for and zero it.
- TeleportAll does NOT make everything teleportable: `Inventory.IsTeleportable` returns false for any item with `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` BEFORE the TeleportAll check (:68862-68869). That gate cannot be lifted by any global key.
- A vanilla client shows no sign that portals are disabled — GetHoverText still says `$piece_portal_connected` and UpdatePortal still lights the target-found effect (:143453-143508). The player only discovers the block by walking in. Any 'blocked' affordance must come from somewhere else (e.g. rewriting portal tags, or actually breaking the ZDO pairing).
- `noportals` AND `nomap` are both dead on a dedicated server console — nomap's IsServer() branch is nested inside the same `Player.m_localPlayer != null` guard (:45261-45283). Do not use nomap as the 'correct' counter-example. `remoteCommand:false` on noportals (:45298) also means an admin cannot fire it from a client console.
- World Modifiers, presets and WorldModifierOption are not a separate network channel — they are a GUI over the same keys (ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeys → ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey, :59630-59680). There is no second lever to find.
- A `preset <string>` key (GlobalKeys.Preset, ordinal 40) in the world's starting keys causes ServerOptionsGUI.SetPreset to reapply an entire slider key set at boot (:115920-115926), which can clobber a mod's portal keys. Check for it with `listkeys` before assuming your key survives a restart.
- The Steam/PlayFab browser 'modifiers' badge is snapshotted in ZNet.OpenServer (:79457) and refreshed only on the registration-retry path or a restart — a live toggle leaves the public listing stale. Cosmetic, but it will confuse operators comparing the badge to `listkeys`.
- GlobalKeyAdd unconditionally dereferences `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()` (:113506-113508) and its UpdateWorldRates tail dereferences `Minimap.instance` (:101203). These survive on a dedicated server only because the headless build instantiates the GUI scene. Any change that strips those objects (or calling GlobalKeyAdd too early in startup) turns a key write into an NRE that aborts before SendGlobalKeys.
- `setkey` from the console refuses key+value pairs the modifier GUI could not produce unless the profile is already cheat-flagged (ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeyAndValueIsCheat, :43515). A mod calling the API directly bypasses this — and every add/remove calls Achievements.MarkAchievementDifficultyDirty() (:113505), so key churn has achievement-integrity side effects for players.

### Open questions
- The exact key strings each WorldModifierOption of `WorldModifiers.Portals` writes live in `KeySlider.m_settings[].m_keys` / `KeyToggle.m_enabledKey`, which are Unity Inspector/prefab data invisible to the decompile (KeySlider.SliderSetting assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:52976-52986; KeyToggle :53266-53276). Ordinals NoPortals=32 and TeleportAll=35 both sit below NonServerOption, which strongly implies both are Portals-slider outputs, but the mapping option→key is unverified. IN-GAME CHECK: on a dedicated server console run `setworldmodifier Portals <each WorldModifierOption in turn>` then `listkeys` and read the 'Server Option Keys' block — it prints ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys verbatim.
- Which WorldModifierOption values the Portals slider actually offers (m_modifierSetups is built at runtime from prefab children in ServerOptionsGUI.Initizalize, :59762-59781). IN-GAME CHECK: `setworldmodifier Portals <garbage>` prints 'Invalid input, possible valid values are: ...' (:43571), then try each and see which report 'Missing settings for preset' from SetPreset (:59749).
- Whether `Minimap.instance` is genuinely non-null on a 1.0.7 headless dedicated server (Game.UpdateNoMap :101203 dereferences it on every key write). Strong indirect evidence yes — the sibling mod calls GlobalKeyAdd live on a dedicated server (Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/WorldRatesEngine.cs:55) — but not provable from the decompile. IN-GAME CHECK: run `setkey noportals` on the dedicated console and confirm the log shows no NullReferenceException and that connected clients immediately get `$msg_blocked` on portal entry.
- Whether `ServerOptionsGUI.GetWorldModifierSummary` works headless — it returns the literal string 'Error!' when `m_presets == null` (:59792-59796), and m_presets is populated from prefab children in Awake (:59601). FejdStartup instantiates the prefab on the server path (:97483), so it should be populated. IN-GAME CHECK: `listkeys` on the dedicated console, or inspect the log line 'Saving modifier preset:' after `setworldmodifier`.
- Whether the Steam/PlayFab listing ever re-registers after a live key change without a restart (only the failure-retry coroutine re-snapshots, :79436-79462). IN-GAME CHECK: set `noportals` at runtime on a public server, then look at the server-browser modifiers badge from a second machine before and after a restart.
- Whether a dedicated server ever instantiates a boss Character (and therefore whether the server itself can ever move the `activeBosses` counter). Game.FixedUpdate pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) every step (:100464), which should mean never — but ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects still runs and no explicit IsDedicated() guard exists on it (:82268). IN-GAME CHECK: `setkey nobossportals`, aggro a boss with one client, then read `listkeys` on the server console and watch `activeBosses` appear/decrement; also confirm it returns to 0 after the boss dies and after a client force-quits mid-fight.

### Corrections to the existing spec
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 72 is half wrong. The `noportals` claim is CONFIRMED (body entirely inside `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)`, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:45286), but the stated contrast — that `nomap` 'correctly branches on ZNet.instance.IsServer()' — is false. nomap's IsServer() branch is NESTED INSIDE the identical `Player.m_localPlayer != null` guard (:45261-45283, guard at :45263, IsServer at :45270), so nomap is exactly as inert on a dedicated server console. Rewrite as: both commands are local-player-only; neither is usable server-side; noportals additionally has remoteCommand:false so an admin cannot fire it remotely either.
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 71 ('mutate that list alongside any runtime key change') describes work vanilla already does. `ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd` automatically adds every key with ordinal < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption — which includes all of noportals/nobossportals/dungeonbuild/teleportall — into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113488, :113511), and GlobalKeyRemove removes it (:113524-113527). The real fact is the inverse problem: the mod cannot avoid persisting these keys unless it calls the publicized `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false)`. Also, the snapshot is re-taken on the Steam registration-retry path (:79436-79462), not literally 'once'.
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 65 should note that `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey` is PUBLIC and dispatches synchronously on the server (:115943, ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC :83585-83590), so the GlobalKeyAdd+SendGlobalKeys publicizer pair from WorldRatesEngine.cs is an optimization (avoids the re-broadcast and gives access to canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false), not a requirement.
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 65's TeleportAll bullet needs a carve-out: TeleportAll does NOT lift the `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` block, which is tested before the key in Inventory.IsTeleportable (:68862-68869). 'Allow-all cargo' is not literally all.
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 67 ('Auto-disable during boss fights — NoBossPortals; vanilla computes "is a boss active" itself') understates the scope. The condition is global — `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() != null || activeBosses > 0` (:143528) — so it blocks EVERY portal for EVERY player server-wide whenever any boss anywhere is alerted, not just for fight participants. It also has a second, entirely different implementation for dungeon doors that is position-based (`Teleport.Interact`, :143355), so setting the key changes two unrelated behaviours.
- Both line 66 (NoPortals) and line 70 (DungeonBuild) should state the persistence consequence explicitly: these are ordinal-<41 world-modifier keys, so enabling one rewrites the world's .fwl modifier list, changes the advertised server-browser badge, reappears automatically at next boot via SetStartingGlobalKeys, and marks achievement difficulty dirty (:113505). Turning the feature off later requires an explicit RemoveGlobalKey; simply disabling the mod leaves the key in the world.

## TeleportWorld / TeleportWorldTrigger complete anatomy (Valheim 1.0.7, server vs client assembly)

`TeleportWorld` and `TeleportWorldTrigger` are byte-identical between `assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs` (:143402-143682) and `assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs` (:144142-144422) — `diff` of the two regions is empty. The class therefore differs only in *whether it runs*, and on a dedicated server it never does: the SERVER build's `Game.FixedUpdate` (:100458-100466) pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition` to `(1000000,0,1000000)` unconditionally — a line that exists in NO form in the client assembly — so `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects`/`CreateObjectsSorted` (:82268, :82105) only ever instantiate ZDOs in a sector 1e6 metres out where no world ZDO lives. No portal GameObject, no `TeleportWorld` component, no trigger collider, no `Player` component (`Player.Awake` :10032 is what fills `s_players`) exists server-side, so `Awake`, `Update`, `UpdatePortal`, `Interact`, `GetHoverText`, `SetText`, `RPC_SetTag` and `Teleport` are all unreachable on a dedicated server. Of the 10 public fields, exactly ZERO are ZDO-backed or RPC'd — `m_allowAllItems`, `m_exitDistance`, `m_activationRange`, `m_proximityRoot`, the colours and the effect refs are plain Inspector-compiled fields, so every per-portal behavioural knob is dead to a server-only mod. What IS server-authoritative is the ZDO layer: `ZDOVars.s_tag` / `s_tagauthor` (two strings, no cap, no filter at write time — `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is literally `return text;` in the SERVER build at :94588) and the `ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal` connection, which IS network-serialized to clients (`ZDO.Serialize` :74112/:74170-74174) and is re-evaluated by the server-only `Game.ConnectPortals()` coroutine every 5s (:100074, :100589). Two genuine server→vanilla-client teleport RPCs exist and do not touch portals at all: `Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer` (:41627/:41962) and `Character.RPC_TeleportTo` (:886/:4126).

### Facts
- **[dedicated-server]** `TeleportWorld` and `TeleportWorldTrigger` are byte-for-byte identical in the server and client decompiles. Extracting server lines 143402-143690 and client lines 144142-144430 and running `diff -u` produces zero output (exit 0). ### Gotchas
- The server and client copies of TeleportWorld are IDENTICAL source — `diff` of assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143402-143690 against assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:144142-144430 is empty. Do not look for a server-specific portal code path; there isn't one. The real server/client divergence is in Game.FixedUpdate (SERVER-only reference-position pin at :100465).
- `TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player)` is `public` and shows up in any reflection dump, which makes it look callable from a server plugin. It is not usefully callable: no TeleportWorld instance ever exists server-side (no GameObject is instantiated), `m_nview` would be null, `player.Message` needs MessageHud.instance, and `Game.instance.IncrementPlayerStat` writes the server's own local profile file.
- `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` fires on ENTER only. A player already standing inside a portal's trigger volume when the server rewrites its destination will NOT re-trigger — they must step out and back in. This is the real constraint on time-sliced hub rotation, not the 0.5s UpdatePortal poll (which only drives the glow).
- Conversely, the destination is NOT cached anywhere: Teleport() re-reads `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` and the target ZDO's live position/rotation at the instant of transit (:143539-143543). A server-side re-route applies to the very next walk-through with no client refresh.
- `TargetFound()` requires the client to actually HOLD the destination ZDO, not just its id; when absent it calls `RequestZDO` and returns false (:143646-143654). The first transit after a server-side re-pair to a portal in an unvisited region can silently fail with no message at all (gate 1 returns without calling player.Message).
- `ZDO.SetSector` returns immediately for any prefab in `Game.PortalPrefabHash` (:73752-73755). A portal ZDO is filed in `m_portalObjects` under whatever sector it had when `AddIfPortal` last ran. Calling `zdo.SetPosition()` on a portal server-side therefore leaves it keyed under its OLD sector forever — clients in the new zone will never receive it through normal sector sync. Moving a portal requires manual re-filing or permanent ForceSendZDO.
- `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is `return text;` in the dedicated-server assembly (:94588-94591). A server plugin that calls it as a filter will silently filter nothing. `CensorShittyWords.Filter` (:94295) is the one that actually works server-side.
- `RPC_SetTag`'s `authorId` parameter is a raw client self-report and is never cross-checked against `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` or the owning ZNetPeer (:143587-143602). Any identity decision keyed off tagauthor is spoofable.
- There is a latent vanilla bug in `RPC_SetTag`: it calls `UpdateConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` BEFORE re-reading the connection to pass to `SetConnectedPortal` (:143595-143597), so the old partner is generally never told. Repair happens only on the next `Game.ConnectPortals()` sweep up to 5s later. Do not model a rename as an atomic two-sided unlink.
- `Game.ConnectPortals()` pass 1 tears down any connection whose partner's `s_tag` string differs (:100601). Cross-tag links, one-way links and distinct per-portal display names inside one group are all actively destroyed every 5 seconds by vanilla. A faster mod timer does not reliably win that race — patching or prefixing ConnectPortals is required.
- `GlobalKeys.TeleportAll` does NOT allow everything: `Inventory.IsTeleportable` rejects any item with `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` before it ever consults `allowAllItems` or `TeleportAll` (:68862-68870). An 'all cargo allowed' feature must carry that caveat.
- `m_allowAllItems`, `m_exitDistance`, `m_activationRange`, `m_proximityRoot` and all colour/effect refs are plain compiled Inspector fields (:143411-143431) with zero ZDO or RPC involvement. Harmony-writing any of them on the server mutates a copy no client will ever read. There is no per-portal item policy and no per-portal exit offset, full stop.
- The vanilla `noportals` console command is wrapped in `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)` (:45285) and is inert on a dedicated server console — unlike the adjacent `nomap` which correctly branches on `IsServer()` (:45270). Use `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` directly.
- `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(pos, hash)` does not set the prefab, persistence, type or rotation (:76684-76692). A portal ZDO fabricated with it alone is non-persistent and prefab-less and will vanish on world save. Replicate all five lines from ZNetView.Awake (:82616-82620).
- `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` iterates the static `m_allAreas` list of instantiated MonoBehaviours and calls `HaveLocalAccess()` (:137547-137594). On a dedicated server that list is empty, so it returns true for everything — it is not usable as a server-side authorization primitive at all.
- A server-issued forced teleport (either RPC path) silently no-ops if the target player teleported within the last 2 seconds or is mid-teleport — `Player.TeleportTo` returns false at :15308-15316 with no message on either side.

### Open questions
- Which prefabs are actually in `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:99828)? The list is Unity Inspector data and no portal prefab name string appears anywhere in the decompiles. IN-GAME CHECK: on a running dedicated server, log `string.Join(",", Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs.Select(p => p.name))` and `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` from a BepInEx plugin at first Heartbeat. This is the only authoritative answer and it also covers modded portal pieces.
- What is each portal prefab's baked `m_allowAllItems` value (the Ashlands stone portal is widely believed to be true)? Field at :143429 is Inspector data. IN-GAME CHECK: `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(<name>).GetComponent<TeleportWorld>().m_allowAllItems` on a client (the server has no prefab-instantiated components to read from a ZDO, though ZNetScene's prefab table itself may still be populated server-side — verify that too). Purely informational: the field cannot be changed over the network regardless of its value.
- What is the actual collider geometry/size on the TeleportWorldTrigger child object, and is it on a child of the TeleportWorld GameObject (Awake uses GetComponentInParent, :143670)? Unity asset data. IN-GAME CHECK: inspect the portal prefab hierarchy in a client-side Unity/ObjectDumper pass. Only matters if a mod ever wants to reason about the transit volume for a position-straddle heuristic — Wonderland's PositionWatch currently uses a flat 40 m radius instead.
- Does `ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs` / `GetPrefab()` return non-null on a dedicated server (i.e. is the prefab table loaded even though nothing is instantiated)? The decompile shows the table exists but proving the server populates it needs a runtime check. IN-GAME CHECK: log `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab("portal_wood") != null` on the server. Determines whether prefab-hash lookups by name are available server-side or whether Game.PortalPrefabHash is the only route.
- Does the dedicated server's ZoneSystem actually succeed in creating local zones at (1000000, 0, 1000000) — zone index 15625, within short range — and does that cost anything? `CreateLocalZones(ZNet.instance.GetReferencePosition())` runs at :113930. IN-GAME CHECK: log `ZoneSystem.instance.IsActiveAreaLoaded()` and `m_zones.Count` on the server. Irrelevant to portal correctness, but relevant if a mod ever wants to move the server's reference position to force server-side instantiation of a region (which would be a very different, much heavier architecture).

### Corrections to the existing spec
- REFINES the Central Constraint's reasoning. The spec says '`ZoneSystem`'s local-zone creation is gated on the same permanently-pinned reference position'. The stronger and more precise mechanism is: the SERVER assembly's `Game.FixedUpdate` contains a line that does not exist in the client assembly at all — `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100465; grep for the literal matches only the server file). Zones ARE created at that position; what makes the server instantiate nothing is that no world ZDO lives there, plus `ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted` (:82105-82112) only walks `FindSectorObjects` for that one sector. Cite :100465 as the primary proof, not the zone system.
- CORRECTS 'a player standing at the hub mid-rotation can have their destination change under them (`TargetFound`/`UpdatePortal` poll every 0.5s)'. `UpdatePortal`'s 0.5s InvokeRepeating (:143450) drives ONLY the EffectFade glow and the EffectList spawn — it has zero gameplay effect. The destination is read fresh inside `Teleport()` at :143539-143543. The real constraint is the opposite one: `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` (:143673) fires on ENTER only, so a player already standing inside the trigger volume will NOT be teleported by a rotation at all until they step out and back in.
- ADDS a hard limit the spec's 'Allow-all cargo through portals' bullet omits. `GlobalKeys.TeleportAll` is checked only AFTER an unconditional rejection loop for `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` (Inventory.IsTeleportable, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:68862-68870). Some items can never be teleported regardless of `TeleportAll` or `m_allowAllItems`. The feature must be described as 'all cargo except tool-tier-1000+ items'.
- CORRECTS the spec's 'vanilla only enforces the 10-char cap in the client UI widget and only profanity-filters at display time' — the second half understates it. On the dedicated server `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is literally `return text;` (:94588-94591), and even on a PC client it early-returns unless `ugcType == ServerName || RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering()` (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94907-94910). There is no profanity filtering on PC at display time either. The `censored` warning line is gated on `ZNet.m_onlineBackend == OnlineBackendType.PlayFab` (:143462). Also note that a server-side filter must call `CensorShittyWords.Filter` (:94295, fully implemented server-side), NOT `FilterUGC`.
- CORRECTS 'ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(pos, prefabHash) makes a real, persistent, correctly-owned ZDO with no live GameObject needed'. It does NOT make it persistent and does not even set the prefab on the ZDO — it only pools it, sets owner to the session id, calls AddIfPortal on the hash you passed, and indexes it (:76684-76692). The mod must additionally do `zdo.Persistent = true; zdo.Type = ...; zdo.Distant = false; zdo.SetPrefab(hash); zdo.SetRotation(rot);` exactly as ZNetView.Awake does (:82613-82620), or the fabricated portal disappears on the next world save.
- ADDS a gotcha the spec's 'Portal to any computed coordinate' and hub bullets need: `ZDO.SetSector` is a no-op for any prefab in `Game.PortalPrefabHash` (:73752-73755), so portal ZDOs are filed in `m_portalObjects` under the sector they had at registration time and `zdo.SetPosition()` never re-files them. Moving a portal server-side breaks its delivery to clients who enter the new zone. Create-and-destroy, don't move.
- REASSURES on a point the spec does not raise: Wonderland's `ZdoSpatialQuery` DOES find portals despite the separate `m_portalObjects` store, because `ZDOMan.FindObjects` (:77366-77381), which `FindSectorObjects` (:77142) calls, explicitly merges `m_portalObjects[sectorIndex]` in. No change needed to that helper.
- ADDS detail to the Group 3 teleport bullet. Two distinct routed RPCs work, not one: `RPC_TeleportPlayer` (Chat.Awake registration :41627, handler :41962, Vector3/Quaternion/bool, peer-targeted, no ZDO) and `RPC_TeleportTo` (Character.Awake registration :886, handler :4126, same signature, addressed to a specific character ZDO via the 4-arg InvokeRoutedRPC at :83577). The ZDO-addressed `RPC_TeleportTo` is the more precise choice since it names the character rather than trusting the receiving client's `Player.m_localPlayer`.
- REFINES 'a fan-in hub member can self-loop to stay connected'. Vanilla's pass-1 teardown at :100601 checks `zDO == null || zDO.GetString(s_tag) != ownTag || zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None`. A self-loop (portal connected to itself) passes all three checks trivially — same tag, non-None connection — so it is stable. But `TargetFound()` (:143640) would then succeed and `Teleport()` would move the player to their own portal's position + exitDistance, i.e. a visible 2-second no-op teleport, not an inert portal. That is a worse player experience than the spec implies.
- ADDS to the 'Ward-gated portal retag protection' item: the underlying `RPC_SetTag` interception is harder than the spec suggests, because `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string, ...)` routes to `m_zdo.GetOwner()` (:82855) and the server has no `TeleportWorld` component to receive it even after claiming ownership — `ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC` needs a registered instance (:82836-82848). Interception must happen at the `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC`/`ZDOMan` layer, or by simply watching `s_tag` for unexpected changes and reverting them, which is far simpler.

## rpc-teleport-paths — server→client forced teleport without portals (Valheim 1.0.7, dedicated server)

A dedicated server CAN force-move any connected vanilla client, with no client mod, via two independent routed-RPC paths that both funnel into the same method the portal itself uses (`Player.TeleportTo`): the peer-scoped `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, distantTeleport)` (handler registered in `Chat.Awake` on every vanilla client) and the ZDO-scoped `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, distantTeleport)` (handler registered in `Character.Awake`, owner-gated). Neither requires `Chat.instance` on the sender — `Chat.TeleportPlayer` is a one-line wrapper over the public `ZRoutedRpc` API, and the server never needs the method registered locally because `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC` forwards by `m_targetPeerID` without a local handler lookup. The only identifier needed is `ZNetPeer.m_uid` (a per-connection long from `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()`); `m_characterID` (ZDOID) is needed only for the ZDO-scoped variant, and the stable cross-session identity (`ZDOVars.s_playerID`) is read off the character ZDO, never used for routing. Every precondition is client-side and silent: `Player.TeleportTo` returns false (no message, no network reply) if the player is already teleporting or if `m_teleportCooldown < 2f`, and `Player.UpdateTeleport` only runs inside the `!IsDead()` branch of `Player.FixedUpdate`, so a dead player's teleport is accepted and then never executed. A `distantTeleport:true` teleport has a hard floor of ~8 seconds of black screen and is visually/audibly identical to a vanilla portal transit, because the "portal VFX" is not portal-specific — `Hud.UpdateBlackScreen` keys the teleport animation solely on `m_teleporting && m_distantTeleport`. Source dir: /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/libs-Tools/1.0/DECOMPILED/

### Facts
- **[local-player-client]** `Chat.TeleportPlayer(long targetPeerID, Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, bool distantTeleport)` contains exactly one statement: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(targetPeerID, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, distantTeleport)`. It holds no state and touches no Chat field. — `Chat.TeleportPlayer, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41957-41960` → A server-only mod never needs Chat.instance. Replicate the one line with ZRoutedRpc.instance directly; calling Chat.instance.TeleportPlayer would NRE if the GUI singleton is absent server-side, for zero benefit.
- **[local-player-client]** `Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer(long sender, Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, bool distantTeleport)` is `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport);` — no sender check, no admin check, no distance check, and the bool return of TeleportTo is discarded. — `Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41962-41968` → The receiving client gives zero feedback on success or failure. The server gets no ack. A failed teleport is indistinguishable from a delivered one except by watching the character ZDO's position afterwards.
- **[local-player-client]** The handler is registered on every vanilla client in `Chat.Awake` via `ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<Vector3, Quaternion, bool>("RPC_TeleportPlayer", RPC_TeleportPlayer)` — confirmed identical in the client assembly (class Chat : Terminal at :41507). — `Chat.Awake, assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:41627 (class at :41507); same at assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41627` → Zero client install required. The RPC name and signature are already live on every unmodified 1.0.7 client.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, string methodName, params object[] parameters)` is public and simply forwards to the 4-arg overload with `ZDOID.None` as targetZDO. — `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83554-83557` → This is the exact server-callable entry point. Signature is stable and public — no reflection needed.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, ZDOID targetZDO, string methodName, params object[] parameters)` builds a RoutedRPCData with `m_senderPeerID = m_id`, then: calls `HandleRoutedRPC` locally only if `targetPeerID == m_id || targetPeerID == 0`, and calls `RouteRPC` only if `targetPeerID != m_id`. — `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83577-83594` → Sending to a specific peer id never runs the method locally, so the server does NOT need the method registered in its own m_functions dictionary. Sending to 0 (Everybody) DOES attempt a local dispatch, which silently misses (see gotchas).
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC` on a server with `rpcData.m_targetPeerID != 0` looks up the peer via its private `GetPeer(long uid)` over `m_peers` and invokes `peer.m_rpc.Invoke("RoutedRPC", pkg)` only if `peer != null && peer.IsReady()`. An unknown or not-ready peer id is a silent drop. — `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83597-83615; ZRoutedRpc.GetPeer, :83542-83552` → Addressing one player is entirely by `long` peer id. A stale id from a disconnected player is a no-op, not an exception — safe to hold ids across ticks, but always re-resolve from ZNet.GetPeers().
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZNetPeer.m_uid` is a `public long` assigned during the handshake (`peer.m_uid = uid` at ZNet:79905) and `ZNetPeer.IsReady()` is literally `return m_uid != 0`. — `ZNetPeer.m_uid / IsReady, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78786, :78820-78823; ZNet handshake, :79905` → m_uid is the ONLY identifier RPC routing accepts. It is a per-connection session id: it changes every time the player reconnects and must never be persisted as identity.
