### Gotchas
- `PrivateArea.CheckAccess(...)` returns TRUE on a dedicated server for every point, always — not because access was granted but because `m_allAreas`:137173 is empty (nothing is ever instantiated). Calling it from server-side mod code is a silent allow-all that looks like a working permission check. (CheckAccess :137547, m_allAreas.Add only in Awake :137197.)
- A client that OWNS the target ZDO never puts the RPC on the wire: `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC`:83588 handles locally and skips `RouteRPC` when `targetPeerID == m_id`, and `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string,...)`:82855 targets `m_zdo.GetOwner()`. So RPC_SetTag, TogglePermitted and ToggleEnabled issued by the ZDO's owner are invisible to the server. Any 'veto the RPC' design fails for the most common case.
- Even when the RPC does cross the wire, the dedicated server NEVER runs the handler: `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC`:83656 requires `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zDO)`:82229 to be non-null, and `m_instances`:81927 is permanently empty. Harmony-patching `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`, `PrivateArea.RPC_TogglePermitted` or `WearNTear.RPC_Damage` on a dedicated server compiles fine and never fires.
- Hardening `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` does nothing for the three portal/ward RPCs that matter: `PrivateArea.RPC_ToggleEnabled`:137414, `RPC_TogglePermitted`:137399 and `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`:143586 all ignore the sender argument entirely and act on a payload `playerID`/`authorId`.
- The real hole is not the RPC layer at all — it is `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData`:77076, which applies any incoming ZDO wholesale on a higher DataRevision with zero validation. A client can rewrite a portal's tag, a ward's permitted list, a piece's creator and any health value as plain ZDO data, with no RPC involved.
- `ZDOMan.DestroyZDO`:76929 is owner-gated on SEND but `HandleDestroyedZDO`:76963 is completely ungated on RECEIVE. Any client can delete any portal on the server by broadcasting a forged `DestroyZDO` (registered globally at :76155). No ward check exists anywhere in that path.
- `Game.RPC_SetConnection`:100653 is an unauthenticated global routed RPC that rewires any ZDO's Portal connection to any target. A lockdown implemented by forcing every connection to `ZDOID.None` can be undone instantly by one malicious client — and vanilla's own `ConnectPortals`:100589 will then re-pair by tag 5 seconds later anyway.
- There is no `ZNetScene.RPC_Destroy` in 1.0.7. `ZNetScene.Destroy(GameObject)`:82024 needs a live GameObject and is therefore unusable server-side. The only server-reachable destruction entry point is `ZDOMan.DestroyZDO(ZDO)`.
- `pu_id0`, `pu_name0`, `pu_id1`, ... are raw runtime-concatenated string keys with NO `ZDOVars` constant (`PrivateArea.SetPermittedPlayers`:137338). Writing `ZDOVars.s_permitted` (the count) without also writing the matching indexed keys silently produces phantom or truncated entries — `GetPermittedPlayers`:137349 skips id==0 but still honours the count.
- `PrivateArea.m_radius`:137132 has a class default of 10f, but the real guard-stone value is a Unity Inspector override invisible to the decompile. Hardcoding 10f will under-cover every ward.
- `Piece.SetCreator`:136415 only writes when `m_nview.IsOwner() && GetCreator() == 0L` — it runs on the placing CLIENT, using that client's local copy of `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` to compute `s_creatorIndex`. So `creator` and `creatorIndex` are client-authored; `creatorIndex` at least points into a server-maintained table (`m_playerHistory`:112396, fed from socket-verified PlatformUserIDs at :81271-81280), so the server can validate it — `creator` (the raw playerID) it cannot.
- `ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject`:82355 really does `UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate` on the dedicated server — the one client-triggerable exception to 'the server instantiates nothing'. The object is then reaped by RemoveObjects since it sits outside the pinned active area, but it is a free unauthenticated Instantiate.
- `ZDOMan.m_deadZDOs`:76043 makes the server destroy any ZDO re-created under a previously-destroyed ZDOID (`RPC_ZDOData`:77133). A mod that deletes and then recreates a portal must use a fresh `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO`:76674 id, not the old one.
- `ZDO.Set(int hash, int value, bool okForNotOwner = false)`:73648 — the `okForNotOwner` parameter is dead in both the server and client builds. There is no ownership assertion on any ZDO setter, so a non-owning write succeeds silently and then loses a DataRevision race to the owner. Take ownership for durable writes.
- `ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc rpc)`:80504 is PRIVATE. Reproduce it with `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)` (GetPeers:81630 is public and returns the live list) rather than reflecting into it.
- `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` receives a ZPackage whose read position advances as you inspect it. A prefix that peeks at the header must save and restore `pkg.GetPos()` or the real handler will read garbage.
- `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`:143586 applies no length cap and no profanity filter at write time — the 10-char cap lives only in the client's `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)`:143444 and censoring only at display time in `GetTagInfo`:143558. A hacked client can store an arbitrarily long or hostile tag.
- `Chat.Awake`:41624 registers `ChatMessage` and `RPC_TeleportPlayer`, and `MessageHud`:55808 registers `ShowMessage`. If those singletons do not exist on a dedicated server, those global RPC hashes are simply unregistered and `HandleRoutedRPC`:83660 logs 'Failed to find rpc method' — patch targets on them would never fire. Send-side use (`ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(...)`) is unaffected.

### Open questions
- What is the actual `PrivateArea.m_radius` on the guard_stone prefab? The class default is 10f (:137132) but it is an Inspector override living in Unity asset data. Exact check: in-game, place a guard stone and binary-search the distance at which another player's build/interact is refused; or dump the guard_stone prefab from the AssetBundle and read the PrivateArea component's m_radius. A server-side ward model is wrong at every ward until this number is known.
- Does `Chat.instance` exist on a dedicated server (i.e. does `Chat.Awake`:41624 ever run)? Exact check: connect a client, send a chat message, and grep the server log for `ZLog.LogWarning("Failed to find rpc method " + hash)` from `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC`:83660 with the stable hash of "ChatMessage". Same test with "ShowMessage" for `MessageHud`:55808. Determines whether those two are patchable server-side.
- Is `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()`:100564 non-null on a dedicated server? `Piece.IsCreator()`:136436 dereferences it. Only matters if any server mod code path can reach a PrivateArea/Piece instance method, but it settles whether such a call NREs or silently compares against 0. Exact check: a trivial probe patch logging `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()?.GetPlayerID()` on server start.
- Does the guard_stone prefab set `m_enabledByDefault` false and `m_ownerFaction == 0` (Faction.Players is a different code path in `OnObjectDamaged`:137642 and short-circuits `GetHoverText`:137240 and `Interact`:137374)? Inspector data. Exact check: dump the prefab, or observe in-game whether a freshly placed guard stone is inactive until the creator interacts.
- Which ZDO actually owns a portal in steady state on a live server — the nearest client, or the server after `Game.SetConnection`:100636 claims it? This decides how often a client's RPC_SetTag is purely local (invisible to the server) versus routed. Exact check: on a running server, log `zdo.GetOwner()` versus `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` for every entry of `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` on a 10s timer with players nearby and away.
- Does `ZoneSystem`'s local-zone creation on the server ever instantiate anything near (1e6,0,1e6)? The spec asserts it does not; `Game.FixedUpdate`:100465 pins the reference position there but nothing in the decompile proves no zone is generated at that coordinate. Exact check: log `ZNetScene.instance.m_instances.Count` on a running dedicated server over time — it should be 0 or near-0.

### Corrections to the existing spec
- Group 4, bullet 1 ('Harden RPC sender identity against spoofing') is correct that `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` and `RPC_SetTag`'s `authorId` are unverified, but incomplete in a way that changes the design: the three portal/ward RPCs in question do not READ `m_senderPeerID` at all. `PrivateArea.RPC_ToggleEnabled`:137414, `RPC_TogglePermitted`:137399 and `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`:143586 ignore their sender parameter and act on a payload `playerID`/`authorId`. Cross-checking m_senderPeerID against the socket buys nothing for them; the mod must instead validate the payload playerID against a socket-anchored identity map.
- Group 4, bullet 3 ('reject an RPC_SetTag from a non-permitted player') is not achievable as an RPC veto in the general case. `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC`:83588 short-circuits to local handling and never calls `RouteRPC` when the sender owns the target ZDO, so a client that owns the portal retags it with zero packets. And even when the RPC is routed, `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC`:83656 → `ZNetScene.FindInstance`:82229 is always null on the server, so the handler is never entered there. Ward-gated retag protection must be implemented as a ZDO watcher that detects a change to `ZDOVars.s_tag`/`s_tagauthor` and reverts it (claim ownership, restore, ForceSendZDO), never as an RPC veto.
- The spec's central-constraint section attributes the no-instantiation fact to 'ZoneSystem's local-zone creation is gated on the same permanently-pinned reference position'. The precise, citable mechanism is `Game.FixedUpdate()`:100458-100465 in the SERVER build calling `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` unconditionally every physics tick — a method body that does not exist in the client build (client `Game.FixedUpdate`:100886 does respawn + ZInput instead). `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects`:82268 reads that position. Also: the consequence is broader than Teleport() — it kills EVERY ZDO-targeted routed RPC server-side via `ZNetScene.FindInstance`:82229.
- The spec does not list `Game.RPC_SetConnection`:100653 as an attack surface. It is one: an unauthenticated global routed RPC that takes ownership of any named ZDO and points its Portal connection at any other ZDOID. This directly undermines Group 2's '[Feasible, medium] genuinely unbypassable lockdown — force-disconnect every portal pair server-side': a single malicious client can re-link any pair at will. That bullet should be downgraded to 'unbypassable only if RPC_SetConnection is also vetoed by sender'.
- The spec does not list `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO`:76953 / `HandleDestroyedZDO`:76963 as an attack surface. Any client can permanently delete any portal (or any ZDO) on the server by broadcasting a forged DestroyZDO with no ward check anywhere in the path. Conversely this IS observable and vetoable server-side, which the spec also omits — `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed`:76033 is a public Action<ZDO> giving a Harmony-free 'portal destroyed' hook.
- The spec does not mention `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey`/`RPC_RemoveGlobalKey`:116022/:116031 being sender-unchecked. Every item in Group 2 (NoPortals, NoBossPortals, TeleportAll, DungeonBuild) can be set OR cleared by any connected client. These keys are not merely 'client-honored' — they are also client-writable.
- The task framing names `ZNetScene.Destroy`/`RPC_Destroy`/`ZDOMan.DestroyZDO`. There is no `RPC_Destroy` in 1.0.7 — grep returns only `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO`:76953 and the unrelated `Ship`/`Vagon` `RPC_DestroyAttachment` (:119212, :131791). `ZNetScene.Destroy(GameObject)`:82024 exists but is unusable server-side (needs a live GameObject).
- The spec's implicit assumption that portal/ward RPC handlers could be patched server-side to gain a decision point should be stated as explicitly false. The complete set of routed RPC handlers a dedicated server actually executes is the ~20 `ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register` sites (:41626, :41627, :42373, :46355, :55808, :76155, :76156, :81954, :100063-100072, :105284-105287, :106781, :113447-113448). Nothing registered on a `ZNetView` is on that list.
- Group 4's ward work should note that a ward's permitted list, creator, creatorName and enabled flag ARE fully server-readable from the ZDO with no local player (`permitted` count + `pu_id<i>`/`pu_name<i>`, per `PrivateArea.GetPermittedPlayers`:137349) — so the 'Wonderland/Lite-maintained shadow list of wards' the spec calls for is unnecessary for the permission data itself. The only thing genuinely missing from the ZDO is the radius (`PrivateArea.m_radius`:137132, a compiled Inspector field).

## target-sources-player — everything a dedicated server can locate about a player (1.0.7)

All citations are to files in /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/libs-Tools/1.0/DECOMPILED/ (SERVER = assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs, CLIENT = assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs). A dedicated server's complete live view of a player is exactly two objects: the ZNetPeer (uid, PlatformUserID via socket host name, character name, refPos refreshed every 2s, characterID) and the character ZDO behind peer.m_characterID (position/rotation at ~50ms freshness, s_playerID, s_playerName, health/stamina/eitr, s_inBed, s_dead, s_pvp, s_crowned, and every VisEquipment slot as a prefab hash). Everything a player "owns" that survives their logout is a normal persistent world ZDO and is fully server-readable: Bed s_owner/s_ownerName, every placed Piece's s_creator (= that player's profile UID) + s_creatorIndex (→ ZNet.World.m_playerHistory PlatformUserID, persisted in the .fwl), PrivateArea s_creatorName + the pu_id{i}/pu_name{i} permitted list, TeleportWorld s_tag/s_tagauthor, Tameable s_tamed/s_tamedName/s_tamedNameAuthor/s_follow, and TombStone s_owner/s_ownerName/s_timeOfDeath/s_spawnPoint plus the Container s_items blob — which is the ONE and only place a player's actual inventory is ever visible to the server. The player's live inventory, skills, recipes, unique keys, map data, custom spawn point, logout point and death point are all PlayerProfile/Player.Save state written only to that client's own .fch file; ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles merely tells each client to save its own disk file and returns nothing. The two non-obvious wins: a player's *active* bed is not stored anywhere server-side, but is inferable live from s_inBed on the character ZDO (position-matched to a bed ZDO) and from peer.m_refPos, which Game.UpdateRespawn pins to the custom spawn point while the player is dead; and ZNetPeer.m_playerID is permanently 0 because no vanilla client ever invokes the "PlayerID" RPC, so the character ZDO's s_playerID is the only server-side route to a profile UID.

### Facts
- **[dedicated-server]** Bed ownership is a pure ZDO write: RPC_SetOwner stores ZDOVars.s_owner (long = PlayerProfile UID) and s_ownerName (string = profile name) on the bed's own ZDO, gated on m_nview.IsOwner(). — `Bed.RPC_SetOwner — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:119813-119819 (registered Bed.Awake:119642, read Bed.GetOwner:119822-119829)` → Every claimed bed in the world is server-readable offline and forever: scan bed ZDOs, read s_owner/s_ownerName. No client involvement, no live player needed.
- **[local-player-client]** A player can own an unlimited number of beds. Bed.Interact only writes ownership when GetOwner()==0; claiming a second unclaimed bed does not clear the first, and nothing ever resets s_owner. — `Bed.Interact — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:119670-119725` → "The player's bed" is ambiguous server-side. Any bed-targeting portal feature must either accept the ambiguity, pick by a rule (nearest/most recent), or use the live inference channels below.
- **[local-save-only]** Which bed is the ACTIVE spawn point lives only in PlayerProfile.WorldPlayerData.m_spawnPoint/m_haveCustomSpawnPoint, keyed by world UID, in the player's local .fch file. Bed.IsCurrent() resolves it by comparing the bed's transform to Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().GetCustomSpawnPoint(). — `Bed.IsCurrent — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:119787-119795; PlayerProfile.WorldPlayerData — :105526-105545; PlayerProfile.GetCustomSpawnPoint — :106230-106233` → There is NO server-readable 'active bed' field. Confirms the existing spec's caveat, and rules out ever reading it directly.
- **[local-player-client]** Selecting a bed as your spawn point produces zero network traffic: Bed.Interact's non-claim branch calls only Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().SetCustomSpawnPoint(GetSpawnPoint()) and a local Message — no RPC, no ZDO write. — `Bed.Interact — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:119719-119725` → Not even an RPC-interception patch can observe a spawn-point change. The only signals are indirect (see the s_inBed and refPos facts).
- **[compiled-field-no-network]** Bed.GetSpawnPoint() returns m_spawnPoint.position — a Unity child Transform on the bed prefab, never written to the ZDO. ### Gotchas
- Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile() is NOT null on a dedicated server — it is a junk profile named "Stranger" with a random UID (Game.Awake:100047). Any vanilla helper that compares against it (Bed.IsMine :119801, Bed.IsCurrent :119787, Piece.IsCreator :136436, TombStone.IsOwner :19865, Container.CheckAccess :122090) silently returns garbage server-side rather than throwing. Never call them.
- ZNetPeer.m_playerID is permanently 0: the "PlayerID" RPC is registered by both sides (SERVER:79916, CLIENT:80108) but never invoked by any vanilla client. Reading it looks correct and yields nothing.
- ZDOVars.s_owner is shared between Bed/TombStone (PlayerProfile UID) and GrapplingPoint (a ZDOID.ID, :127909). A global s_owner query mixes incompatible value spaces — always filter by prefab hash.
- Piece.SetCreator only writes when GetCreator() == 0 and m_nview.IsOwner() (:136417) — pre-existing world-gen structures and anything placed before the check have s_creator == 0, i.e. Piece.IsPlacedByPlayer() == false. Do not treat missing s_creator as 'owned by nobody in particular' without checking that.
- s_creatorIndex is FindIndex(...) against ZNet.World.m_playerHistory at placement time and is -1 when the placer is not yet in the history (:136421). It is also a positional index into a list that only ever grows by append — safe across restarts, but useless if it is -1.
- ZNet.GetPlayerList()[i].m_position is zero for any player with public position disabled (:81256-81259). peer.m_refPos is populated unconditionally (:80401). Using the former for positions silently produces (0,0,0) targets.
- peer.m_refPos is the client's ZNet reference position, NOT the character position — during respawn/loading it is the spawn point, and during normal play it lags the true position by up to 2s. Use the character ZDO position for anything precise.
- ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles() sounds like it collects profiles; it does the opposite (tells each client to save its own disk file, :79653). No data comes back.
- Character ZDOs are non-persistent and are destroyed on disconnect (ZDOMan.RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS :77406). A per-player cache keyed on the ZDOID or on peer.m_uid dies with the session — key on s_playerID or PlatformUserID and re-resolve every connect.
- ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash is a full nested scan (:75707) with no index behind it, and only Float/Long/Int/String are implemented — Vec3/Quat/ByteArray log an error and return empty (:75403-75406). It looks like a cheap query and is not.
- The server has no Bed, PrivateArea, TeleportWorld, Container, TombStone or Player GameObject anywhere near a player (Game.FixedUpdate pins refPos to 1e6, :100464). PrivateArea.m_allAreas, Player.GetAllPlayers() and Piece.s_allPieces are all permanently empty; every static-list-based vanilla helper is a silent no-op.
- Bed's spawn position is a child Transform (Bed.GetSpawnPoint :119796), not ZDO data. A 'teleport to their bed' feature lands on the bed ZDO's origin, which is not exactly where vanilla respawns them.
- A dead player's tombstone Container ZDO is the ONLY server-visible inventory. It is a live Container though — respect ZDOVars.s_inUse before writing (Wonderland ZdoInventoryIO.IsBusy), and it self-destructs once emptied (TombStone.UpdateDespawn :19875-19890).
- Tameable's s_follow holds a character NAME string, not an id (:19457), and is cleared to "" when the creature is told to stay (:19444). Name collisions between two characters called the same thing are indistinguishable, and a tame that is not currently following has no owner marker at all.
- TeleportWorld.s_tagauthor and Piece.s_creator can disagree about 'whose portal this is' — the first is the last person to set the tag (a PlatformUserID string), the second is the builder (a profile UID long). They are different value types and different semantics; pick one deliberately.

### Open questions
- Is the Player prefab's ZNetView m_persistent actually false? RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS (:77406) only destroys non-persistent ZDOs of a departed peer, and the design clearly assumes character ZDOs are among them, but m_persistent is Inspector data (ZNetView.Awake :82616 copies it). IN-GAME CHECK: connect a client, record its character ZDOID, disconnect, then call ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(thatId) from a server-side timer a few seconds later — null means non-persistent as assumed.
- What is the vanilla tombstone prefab's exact name/hash? Player.m_tombstone is an Inspector GameObject reference (:9594) and the string never appears in either decompile. IN-GAME CHECK: kill a character, then log the prefab hash of the new ZDO carrying both s_ownerName and s_timeOfDeath, and compare against "Player_tombstone".GetStableHashCode().
- Which bed prefabs exist and do they all carry both a Piece and a Bed component (i.e. do all beds have s_creator as well as s_owner)? Prefab composition is asset data. IN-GAME CHECK: place each bed variant, then dump the ZDO's field set and confirm s_creator, s_owner and s_ownerName all appear on the same ZDO.
- Does the tombstone's Container write s_items promptly on creation, or only on the first OnContainerChanged after a client instantiates it? Container.Save runs from OnContainerChanged when IsOwner (:122287-122300), and the grave is filled by MoveInventoryToGrave on the dying client (:12709). IN-GAME CHECK: die, then read the fresh tombstone ZDO's s_items from the server within a second — if empty, the blob only lands once the owning client's Container ticks.
- How quickly after a peer becomes ready does its character ZDO actually arrive server-side with s_playerID populated? The ordering is guaranteed client-side (Game.SpawnPlayer :100692-100698) but the wire delay is not derivable. IN-GAME CHECK: on RPC_CharacterID, poll GetZDO(peer.m_characterID).GetLong(s_playerID) each frame and log the number of frames until non-zero.
- Do all shoulder/back/trinket VisEquipment slots get written for a Player specifically, or are some gated by m_isPlayer/m_isArmorStand paths that a real Player never takes? The read-back at :20857-20885 branches on m_isPlayer (an Inspector bool). IN-GAME CHECK: equip each slot in turn and dump the character ZDO's int fields.

### Corrections to the existing spec
- REFINE — 'Portal to a player's claimed bed … "currently active" bed with multiple beds lives only in that player's local, non-networked save data.' The premise is correct (Bed.IsCurrent :119787 reads PlayerProfile.GetCustomSpawnPoint, and Bed.Interact's spawn-set branch :119719 emits no RPC and no ZDO write), but two live inference channels exist and should be listed: (a) ZDOVars.s_inBed on the character ZDO, which vanilla's own server code already reads via GetAllCharacterZDOS (Game.EverybodyIsTryingToSleep :100735) — position-match the sleeping character to a bed ZDO; (b) peer.m_refPos while the player is dead, because Game.UpdateRespawn pins the reference position to the custom spawn point (:100349) and it is reported to the server every 2s (:80395). Neither is instantaneous, but both turn 'impossible' into 'observable over time'.
- ADD — the spec never mentions that EVERY placed structure carries a builder record in its ZDO: Piece.SetCreator writes ZDOVars.s_creator (the placer's PlayerProfile UID, identical to their character ZDO s_playerID) plus s_creatorIndex (→ ZNet.World.m_playerHistory PlatformUserID, persisted in the .fwl) — Piece.SetCreator :136415, Player.PlacePiece :12514. This makes 'a player's own portals', 'a player's own beds' and 'a player's own wards' server-answerable offline and persistently, which is a stronger basis for per-player portal features than s_tagauthor and should be added to Group 1 and Group 4.
- REFINE — 'the server can't inspect a player's inventory anyway (never networked)'. True for a living player's inventory (Player.Save → PlayerProfile.m_playerData → local .fch, :14091/:105706; ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles sends nothing back, :79653). Two carve-outs belong in the text: equipped/visible gear IS in the character ZDO as prefab hashes (VisEquipment :20569-20708, incl. back and utility slots), and a DEAD player's entire inventory IS server-readable from the tombstone Container's s_items blob together with s_owner/s_ownerName/s_timeOfDeath/s_spawnPoint (TombStone.Setup :19845, TombStone.Awake :19732). Neither enables vanilla's ore check (which is against the full inventory), but both are real server-side data the spec currently denies exists.
- REFINE — Group 5's 'portal toll via an adjacent chest … never the traveling player's own inventory'. Correct, and the set of server-writable inventories should be stated as 'any Container-family ZDO', which includes the player's own tombstone — Container.Save is the single s_items writer in the assembly (:122294), with ZdoInventoryIO already implementing the read/claim/write cycle.
- ADD to Group 4 — the identity-hardening item says RPC sender identity is unverified but does not say what to check it against. The answer is concrete: peer.m_socket.GetHostName() is the PlatformUserID the connection authenticated with (Steam session ticket / PlayFab check in ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo :79836-79868), reverse-lookupable via ZNet.GetPeerByHostName (:80480), and RPC_SetTag's authorId is a PlatformUserID string in exactly that format (TeleportWorld.SetText :143579). Cross-checking the two is the whole fix. Also note ZNetPeer.m_playerID is always 0 (no client ever invokes the "PlayerID" RPC) so it cannot be part of any identity check.
- ADD to Group 4 — PrivateArea's permission data needs no 'shadow list' to READ: s_creator (owner), s_creatorName (PrivateArea.Setup :137446), s_enabled, and the permitted roster as s_permitted + "pu_id{i}"/"pu_name{i}" (SetPermittedPlayers :137338, GetPermittedPlayers :137349) are all plain ZDO fields. The shadow list is only needed because no PrivateArea GameObject exists server-side to run the checks — the data itself is fully available, which makes that item smaller than 'large'.

## Dungeon teleport (class Teleport) vs TeleportWorld, plus a complete inventory of every non-locomotive character position change in Valheim 1.0.7

`class Teleport` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143316) is architecturally the *opposite* of `TeleportWorld`: it has no `ZNetView`, no `ZDO`, no RPC, no Awake, and no networked state whatsoever — its destination is a plain serialized Unity Inspector reference `public Teleport m_targetPoint` (:143322) resolved through `Transform` math at `GetTeleportPoint()` (:143372). Server and client decompiles are byte-identical for this class. Its NoBossPortals gate (:143355) blocks ONLY the outbound leg (it requires `character.InInterior()`, i.e. the player's current y > 3000f) and its third conjunct `Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` (:133631) dereferences `EnemyHud.instance` — a pure client HUD singleton — so on any headless context it returns false. Dungeon doors deliberately skip *both* `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` and `Player.IsTeleportable` (the ore check), which `TeleportWorld.Teleport` (:143515) applies — so a server-wide `NoPortals` lockdown does NOT close crypt doors and ore always passes through them. The stats (`PortalDungeonIn`=83, `PortalDungeonOut`=84, `PortalsUsed`=15 in `PlayerStatType` :106499) land in `PlayerProfile.m_playerStats` (`IncrementStat` :106287), a local `.fch` save structure that is never networked. Nothing in `Teleport` is server-reachable, readable, or writable — but a dungeon transit IS server-*detectable* after the fact, because the player's character ZDO position y crosses the 3000f interior threshold. Counting every path, there are **five** distinct transform-level relocation mechanisms plus several physics/rescue snaps; only two of them (`Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer` and `Character.RPC_TeleportTo`) are reachable from a dedicated server, and both bypass every vanilla portal rule.

### Facts
- **[compiled-field-no-network]** `class Teleport` declares exactly four fields — m_hoverText, m_enterText, `public Teleport m_targetPoint`, m_hoverOffset — and has NO ZNetView field, NO Awake(), NO m_nview, NO ZDO access and NO RPC registration anywhere in the class body (lines 143316-143390 inclusive). — `Teleport (class body) assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143316-143390` → There is zero networked state for dungeon doors. A server-only mod cannot read, write, redirect, log, or veto a dungeon door by any ZDO or RPC means, because none exists. Unlike TeleportWorld (which has s_tag/s_tagauthor/ConnectionType.Portal), Teleport is invisible to ZDOMan entirely.
- **[compiled-field-no-network]** The dungeon exit point is a Unity Inspector object reference (`public Teleport m_targetPoint`) plus Transform math: `GetTeleportPoint() => transform.position + transform.forward - transform.up`. No paired ZDO, no ZDOID, no connection type. — `Teleport.m_targetPoint assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143322; Teleport.GetTeleportPoint assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143372-143375` → Contrast with TeleportWorld, whose destination is `ZDO.GetConnectionZDOID(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal)` and IS server-rewritable. Dungeon destinations are baked into the location prefab asset; rewriting one requires a client-side asset/Harmony patch, which is out of scope for server-only. Also note GetTeleportPoint() is private and is called on *another* instance (`m_targetPoint.GetTeleportPoint()`), which is legal C# but means the exit offset is not overridable via any public surface.
- **[dedicated-server]** The server and client decompiles of `class Teleport` are textually identical (client copy at assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:144056-144130). The only difference is line offset. — `Teleport (class body) assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:144056-144130 vs assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143316-143390` → No server-specific stub or IL stripping to exploit; the code exists on the server binary but is unreachable there for the reasons below. Any Harmony patch on Teleport.Interact WILL compile and apply on a dedicated server and will simply never fire.
- **[local-player-client]** `Teleport.OnTriggerEnter` requires `Player.m_localPlayer == component`; `Teleport.Interact` is reached from `Player.Update()` -> `Interact(m_hovering, ...)`, which sits behind `!m_nview.IsOwner() -> return` and raw ZInput button reads. — `Teleport.OnTriggerEnter assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143336-143343; Player.Update assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:10239, gate at :10257, call at :10291 and :10300` → Both entry points into Teleport.Interact are local-player-only, same as TeleportWorldTrigger. - **[local-player-client]** `Teleport.Interact`'s boss gate is a three-way AND: `GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoBossPortals) && character.InInterior() && Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon(character.transform.position)`. `Character.InInterior(Vector3 position) => position.y > 3000f`. — `Teleport.Interact assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143355; Character.InInterior assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:4538-4541` → Because the second conjunct tests the player's CURRENT altitude, the check can only ever be true when the player is already inside an interior. It blocks OUTBOUND (dungeon -> surface) only. The inbound leg (surface, y<3000) is never blocked by NoBossPortals. This refines the existing spec's wording from 'the outbound trip from inside an active boss's own dungeon' to the precise mechanic.
- **[local-player-client]** `Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` first dereferences `EnemyHud.instance` and returns false if it is null; `EnemyHud.instance` is set only in `EnemyHud.Awake` on the HUD prefab and its `m_huds` dictionary is filled in `EnemyHud.LateUpdate` from `Character.GetAllCharacters()` relative to `Player.m_localPlayer.transform.position`. — `Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133631-133645; EnemyHud.instance assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46669; EnemyHud.LateUpdate assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46686-46704; EnemyHud.GetActiveBoss assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46873-46884` → The dungeon NoBossPortals check is doubly client-bound: it depends on a UI singleton and on which boss HUD bars that specific client is currently showing. A server-only mod can neither evaluate nor influence it beyond setting the global key. It is 'vanilla-respecting' in the weakest sense — it is honored per-client, based on per-client HUD state.
- **[local-player-client]** The boss-proximity test inside `IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` is `ZoneSystem.GetZone(point) == ZoneSystem.GetZone(activeBoss.transform.position)`, and `GetZone` uses only x and z (64m grid, `FloorToInt((point.x+32)/64)`), plus the boss must have `m_bossEvent.Length > 0`. — `Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133635-133642; ZoneSystem.GetZone assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115741-115746` → Y is ignored, which is exactly why the check works at all — the interior is at zoneCenter XZ with y+5000, so it shares the boss's XZ zone. - **[local-player-client]** `Teleport.Interact` never consults `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` and never calls `Player.IsTeleportable(...)`. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` does both (NoPortals at :143523, IsTeleportable at :143533). — `Teleport.Interact assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143345-143370; TeleportWorld.Teleport assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143515-143549` → MAJOR for TortalPortal Lite: a server-wide `NoPortals` lockdown closes constructed portals but leaves every crypt/dungeon door fully working, including with ore in inventory. ### Gotchas
- A server-wide `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` lockdown does NOT close dungeon/crypt doors. `Teleport.Interact` (:143345-143370) never reads NoPortals at all. Marketing a 'disable all portals' feature as total is wrong; say 'disable all constructed portals'.
- Ore/metal restriction has never applied to dungeon doors. `Teleport.Interact` never calls `Player.IsTeleportable`, unlike `TeleportWorld.Teleport` (:143533). There is nothing to 'enforce server-side' for dungeon doors because vanilla itself does not restrict them.
- `Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` (:133631) returns false whenever `EnemyHud.instance` is null. That makes the dungeon boss gate not merely client-honored but client-HUD-honored: it depends on which boss health bars that specific player currently has on screen (within EnemyHud.m_maxShowDistanceBoss=100f and alerted, EnemyHud.TestShow :46706-46728).
- The dungeon boss gate blocks only the OUTBOUND leg. `character.InInterior()` tests the player's current altitude, so a player standing outside (y<3000) is never blocked from entering. Do not describe it as 'blocks the dungeon while a boss is alive'.
- `Teleport` has no ZNetView, so there is no ZDO, no s_tag, no connection, no owner, and no ZDOMan registry entry for a dungeon door. There is literally nothing for a server-only mod to read or write. Do not look for a 'dungeon portal list' — none exists at any layer.
- A server-issued teleport (either RPC) bypasses NoPortals, NoBossPortals, PrivateArea, and IsTeleportable entirely — the client-side RPC_TeleportPlayer body has no checks at all (:41962-41968). Any rule TortalPortal Lite wants applied to a server-driven warp must be implemented in the mod itself.
- `Player.TeleportTo` silently returns false if `m_teleportCooldown < 2f` (:15311-15314). A server sending two teleports inside 2s gets one honored and one dropped with no error, no message, and no way for the server to learn which. Rate-limit on the server side.
- `distantTeleport: false` (what dungeon doors use) makes `Player.UpdateTeleport` restore the player to m_teleportFromPos with '$msg_portal_blocked' if ZoneSystem.FindFloor fails, instead of y-snapping to solid ground (:15359-15376). If a mod reuses distantTeleport:false for a long-range warp into unloaded terrain, the player is silently bounced back.
- `Game.instance.IncrementPlayerStat` writes only to the local `PlayerProfile`. PortalsUsed / PortalDungeonIn / PortalDungeonOut never leave the client (:100569 -> :106287). Do not plan a server leaderboard on vanilla stats; the only client->server per-player dictionary is ZNet.m_serverSyncedPlayerData, which vanilla fills with three unrelated keys (:79212, :11095, :11400).
- The dedicated server DOES instantiate GameObjects — during SpawnMode.Ghost world-gen around each peer's reference position (ZoneSystem.Update :113930-113939). They are destroyed the same frame (SpawnZone :114093-114100), and SpawnLocation only ever instantiates ZNetView-bearing children (:115229), so Teleport/Ladder colliders still never appear. 'The server instantiates nothing' is the right conclusion from the wrong premise.
- `Character.TeleportTo` is a `return false` stub; only `Player` overrides it (verified in both assemblies). RPC_TeleportTo aimed at a creature, tame, or ship ZDO does absolutely nothing — it is not a general entity-relocation primitive.
- Vanilla's `recall` and `goto` console commands both dereference `Player.m_localPlayer` (:44551, :44562) and are dead from a dedicated server's own console, exactly like `noportals` (:45287). Invoke the routed RPC directly instead of shelling to a command.
- `Ladder.Interact` (:132074) relocates a character instantly with no cooldown and no checks whatsoever. It is the cheapest vanilla-legitimate teleport in the game, and it will produce position jumps that any server-side portal-transit detector will misattribute.
- Server-side writes to a player's ZDO position are futile: the owning client's `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` rewrites `zDO.SetPosition(GetPosition())` every frame (:87533). ZDO position is a read-only view of a player from the server's perspective.

### Open questions
- Does the `Teleport` component sit on a GameObject that also carries a ZNetView in the shipped dungeon-entrance prefabs? The decompile cannot say (Unity asset data). It does not change the conclusion (CreateLocationProxy passes spawnNow=false in Ghost mode so the visual prefab never expands server-side), but it would settle whether a Teleport ever exists for a single frame during ghost world-gen. Check: in-editor/AssetRipper inspection of `dungeon_*` entrance prefabs, or a dedicated-server Harmony prefix on `Teleport.Awake`-equivalent (there is none; patch `OnTriggerEnter` and log) and confirm zero hits over a world-gen pass.
- Which prefabs are in `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (the List<GameObject> feeding `Game.PortalPrefabHash` at :100029-100032)? This determines exactly which placed objects ZDOMan tracks as portals. Check in-game: log `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Count` and cross-reference against `ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs` name hashes at server start.
- Which creature/attack prefab actually uses `TeleportAbility` (:25523) and what `m_targetTag` does it search for? Inspector data. Check in-game: log from a Harmony postfix on TeleportAbility.Setup on a client and note the owner's prefab name.
- Does `Player`'s prefab have `ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync` enabled? This gates whether `Player.GetRelativePosition` (:16551) ever writes ConnectionType.SyncTransform + s_relPosHash into the character ZDO, which the existing spec's 'portal to a player's live-attached ship' item depends on. Check in-game: read `ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID(playerZdoId, ConnectionType.SyncTransform)` server-side while a player is confirmed seated on a moving karve.
- Empirically, how large is the position delta and how many physics ticks elapse for a dungeon transit as seen in the character ZDO? Needed to size the y>3000 crossing detector's polling interval. Check in-game: server-side poll of ConnectedCharacters positions at 0.1s and log every sample where |Δy| > 1000.
- Does the Ashlands `portal_stone` prefab ship with `m_allowAllItems = true`? Still unresolved (Inspector/AssetBundle data, as the existing spec notes). Check in-game: carry iron through a portal_stone pair on an unmodified client.

### Corrections to the existing spec
- The spec's closing section says the dungeon mechanism 'shares the NoBossPortals key'. True, but it must be qualified: `Teleport` ALSO ignores `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` entirely. A 'disable all portals server-wide [Feasible, small]' item under Group 2 is therefore incomplete — it closes constructed portals only, and dungeon/crypt doors keep working. The Group 2 'genuinely unbypassable lockdown' item (force SetConnection to ZDOID.None) is likewise portal-only and has no dungeon-door analogue at any layer.
- The spec says the dungeon check 'blocks only the outbound trip from inside an *active* boss's own dungeon'. Refine: (a) 'outbound' is correct and is caused specifically by the `character.InInterior()` conjunct testing the player's CURRENT y > 3000f; (b) it is not 'the boss's own dungeon' but 'the same 64m XZ zone column as the boss' (ZoneSystem.GetZone ignores y); (c) the check additionally requires `EnemyHud.instance != null` and a boss present in that client's own m_huds with m_bossEvent.Length > 0 — so it is client-HUD-state-dependent, a strictly weaker guarantee than the spec's 'vanilla-respecting' framing implies.
- The spec says dungeon doors send a character 'to a fixed Transform-based exit point (no paired ZDO)'. Correct, and it should be stated more strongly: `class Teleport` has no ZNetView, no ZDO, no RPC and no Awake at all (:143316-143390). It is not merely unpaired — it is entirely absent from the network layer, so unlike TeleportWorld there is no partial server visibility to exploit.
- The spec frames Group 5 portal-use detection as needing the `PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit` position-straddle heuristic. For the DUNGEON mechanism specifically there is a better, heuristic-free signal: `Character.InInterior(pos) => pos.y > 3000f` (:4538) against the character ZDO position, since interiors are placed at +5000f (Location.Awake :133512). Dungeon in/out logging should be listed as [Feasible, small] with no false-positive class, separate from the portal-transit heuristic.
- The spec's 'One More Mechanism To Track Separately' should be 'Three More'. `Ladder.Interact` (:132064-132079) instantly relocates a Humanoid with no TeleportTo, no cooldown, no key check and no item check, and `TeleportAbility.Setup` (:25533-25550) writes `m_owner.transform.position` directly. Both are as server-invisible as `Teleport`, but any audit/lockdown claim of covering 'all teleports' is false without them.
- Group 3's 'reuse vanilla's RPC_TeleportPlayer ... bypassing Chat.instance entirely' is confirmed correct and the reasoning can be tightened: `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(targetPeerID, ...)` with targetPeerID != m_id never calls HandleRoutedRPC locally (:83585-83591), so the server genuinely needs no Chat registration. Add: a second, more precisely addressed path exists via `Character.RPC_TeleportTo` (registered unconditionally for any Character with a ZDO, :886) using the ZDO-targeted overload with peer.m_characterID. Also add the hard constraint that neither path applies ANY vanilla portal rule.
- Group 5's portal-toll item should note that `Teleport`/dungeon transits cannot be tolled by the same mechanism in any meaningful way, since the dungeon exit is a fixed prefab transform and there is no per-door ZDO to attach a toll chest to.

## Ships & moving platforms as portal destinations; moving portal ZDOs (Valheim 1.0.7, server-only)

A dedicated server can read exactly which ZNetView-bearing Rigidbody a player is riding, because the rider's own client writes it into the rider's ZDO as a `ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.SyncTransform` connection plus `relPos`/`relRot`/`attachJoint` fields, and that connection is serialized into the network ZDO blob the server receives (`ZDO.Serialize`:74169 / `ZDO.Deserialize`:74229). Ship and Vagon both carry ZNetView and Rigidbody on the same GameObject (`Ship.Awake`:140444-140445, `Vagon.Awake`:147437/147447), so the connection target is the vehicle's own ZDO — but the whole mechanism is gated on `ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync`:87362, an Inspector bool the decompile cannot read; the fully-confirmed fallback is `ZDOVars.s_user` on the Ship's ZDO, which only identifies the helmsman (`ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl`:141332). A portal's ZDO position CAN be rewritten server-side (`ZDO.SetPosition`:73729) but three things break: the write only bumps DataRevision if the server owns the ZDO (:73740) and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS`:76901 hands portal ownership to any peer within ~96m every 2s; portal ZDOs are permanently exempt from sector re-registration (`ZDO.SetSector`:73754) so `m_portalObjects` stays keyed by the creation-time sector and normal sector-based sync stops reaching the new location; and the new position is never saved (portals are excluded from chunk saves at :77572 and the ChunkPortal file only emits when `DirtyPortalObjects`:77621, which a position write never sets). A vanilla client does NOT rubber-band or re-instantiate on a moved portal ZDO — `ZNetScene.CreateObject`:82011 applies position only at Instantiate and `ZNetView.Awake` never applies it — so the mesh and the TeleportWorldTrigger collider stay put until the instance is destroyed and recreated, at which point it pops. The one genuinely live-following thing is the *destination*: `TeleportWorld.Teleport`:143539 reads the target ZDO's position at the instant of transit with no prefab validation, so a portal pointed at a Ship ZDO teleports to wherever that ship currently is — except `Player.UpdateTeleport`:15343-15349 pins the player at a frozen snapshot for ≥8 seconds, by which time the ship has sailed.

### Facts
- **[compiled-field-no-network]** `Character.m_characterParentSync`, `Character.SetCharacterParent` and `RPC_SetCharacterParent` do not exist anywhere in 1.0.7. The only `m_characterParentSync` in the entire codebase is a public serialized bool on `ZSyncTransform`. — `ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87362 (grep for SetCharacterParent returns 0 hits in all four decompiles)` → Any design doc naming Character.m_characterParentSync or RPC_SetCharacterParent is referencing a pre-1.0 API. The correct handle is the ZSyncTransform component on the Player prefab.
- **[zdo-owning-client]** `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` — which runs only on the ZDO-owning client — writes the parent as a real ZDO connection: `zDO.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.SyncTransform, m_tempParent)`, plus `s_attachJointHash` (string), `s_relPosHash` (Vector3), `s_relRotHash` (Quaternion). All of this is inside `if (m_characterParentSync)`. — `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87542-87562 (SetConnection at :87548)` → The rider's own client authors the ship-attachment record. A server-only mod reads it, never writes it.
- **[dedicated-server]** The connection ZDOID is serialized into the network ZDO packet (`ZDO.Serialize` writes `(byte)connectionData.m_type` then `connectionData.m_target` as a raw ZDOID) and re-applied on receipt (`ZDO.Deserialize` reads the byte + ZDOID and calls `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection`). — `ZDO.Serialize, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74169-74172; ZDO.Deserialize, :74229-74231` → CONFIRMED: the parent-sync link reaches the dedicated server verbatim as a ZDOID. No RPC interception, no live GameObject, no ownership needed to read it.
- **[dedicated-server]** The disk save path is different from the network path: `ZDO.Save` writes `connectionData.m_hash` (an int from `ZDOConnectionHashData`), not the ZDOID, and `ZDOMan.ConnectSyncTransforms` re-pairs SyncTransform connections by hash on world load. — `ZDO.Save, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74313-74314; ZDOMan.ConnectSyncTransforms, :78232-78257` → SyncTransform parentage survives a server restart. A logged-out player's ZDO can still claim a ship parent after a restart — always cross-check the live world positions before trusting it.
- **[zdo-owning-client]** `Character.GetRelativePosition` returns the parent only when `IsOnGround() && m_lastGroundBody` and the ground body has a valid ZNetView; `m_lastGroundBody` is `m_lastGroundCollider.attachedRigidbody`, refreshed in `UpdateGroundContact`, which `Character.CustomFixedUpdate` calls only when `zDO.IsOwner()`. — `Character.GetRelativePosition, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:4423-4437; Character.UpdateGroundContact, :2933/:2943; Character.CustomFixedUpdate, :982/:987/:1001` → Parent detection is physics-derived on the rider's machine. Anything the rider stands on that has Rigidbody+ZNetView becomes the parent — carts, Leviathans, tamed mounts — so the connection target must be prefab-checked against Ship before it means 'on a ship'.
- **[zdo-owning-client]** `Player.GetRelativePosition` overrides the ground path when `m_attached` is set (sitting at a helm, on a chair, in a bed): it uses `m_attachPoint.GetComponentInParent<ZNetView>()`. `ShipControlls` has no ZNetView of its own — `ShipControlls.Awake` does `m_nview = m_ship.GetComponent<ZNetView>()` — so a helmsman's parent ZDOID resolves to the Ship's own ZDO. — `Player.GetRelativePosition, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:16551-16576; ShipControlls.Awake, :141260` → Both the standing passenger and the seated helmsman produce the same parent ZDOID (the Ship). - **[zdo-owning-client]** When the parent is a Character (a ridden creature), `attachJoint` is set to `m_attachPoint.name` and relPos/relRot are zeroed; for a non-Character parent (a ship), `attachJoint` is `""` and relPos/relRot carry real local-space values. — `Player.GetRelativePosition, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:16558-16571` → Server-side, a non-empty `ZDOVars.s_attachJointHash` string on a player ZDO means 'riding a creature'; an empty one with a non-None SyncTransform connection means 'on a vehicle/platform'. - **[dedicated-server]** Ship carries its ZNetView and Rigidbody on the same GameObject (`m_nview = GetComponent<ZNetView>(); m_body = GetComponent<Rigidbody>();`), and so does Vagon. — `Ship.Awake, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:140444-140445; Vagon.Awake, :147437/:147447` → `m_lastGroundBody.GetComponent<ZNetView>()` in Character.GetRelativePosition WILL resolve for both ships and carts. Its `NoBossPortals` check additionally reads `EnemyHud.instance` via `Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` (:133631) — a client-only UI singleton.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZDOExtraData.UpdateConnection` returns false and writes nothing if the ZDO has no existing connection entry, whereas `SetConnection` always writes. — `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74951-74960; ZDOExtraData.UpdateConnection, :74962-74975` → A rider's first-ever dismount is a silent no-op (ZSyncTransform uses UpdateConnection for the detach path at :87568). A player ZDO can therefore have NO connection entry at all rather than an explicit None — treat 'missing' and 'None' as the same 'not attached' state.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea` uses Chebyshev distance <= 1.5 * 64m (=96m) from the zone centre at the default simulation distance, tightened to a 112m disc when NearSimulationDistance==2 and non-classic. — `ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82297-82320; SimulationDistance.OriginalDistance, :117898` → Quantifies the ownership-steal radius in ReleaseNearbyZDOS and the create/destroy boundary that makes a moved portal pop. ~96-112m around each peer.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<Vector3, Quaternion, bool>("RPC_TeleportPlayer", ...)` is a global routed-RPC registration made in `Chat.Awake`, and `Chat.TeleportPlayer` is nothing but `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(targetPeerID, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, distantTeleport)`. — `Chat.Awake, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41627; Chat.TeleportPlayer, :41957-41960; Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer, :41962-41968` → Confirms the existing spec: a server-only mod can invoke the routed RPC by name without touching Chat.instance. This is the only way to actually put a player onto a moving ship — send the RPC repeatedly with the ship's CURRENT position, not once.
- **[local-player-client]** On a client, receiving a moved portal ZDO runs `AddIfPortal` again, which looks up `m_portalObjects[zdo.GetSectorIndex()]` using the NEW sector and appends the ZDO under a second key without removing the old entry. — `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77128-77132; ZDOMan.AddIfPortal, :77732-77750` → Every sector boundary a moved portal crosses adds a duplicate entry to each receiving client's portal registry, which then appears twice in FindObjects results. Unbounded growth on long-lived client sessions.

### Gotchas
- The moving-portal idea fails on the client before it fails anywhere else: `ZNetScene.CreateObject`:82011 sets the transform at Instantiate and `ZNetView.Awake`:82566 never touches position again. Absent a ZSyncTransform on the portal prefab, a vanilla client's portal mesh AND its TeleportWorldTrigger collider stay frozen at the build site no matter what the server writes. It does not rubber-band, it does not re-instantiate — it just ignores you until the instance is destroyed and recreated, at which point it pops.
- `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73754), so `m_portalObjects` stays keyed by the sector the portal was created in. `CreateSyncList`→`FindSectorObjects`→`FindObjects`(:77376) therefore keeps delivering a moved portal to peers near its ORIGINAL location and never to peers at its new one. Every moved portal needs per-tick `ForceSendZDO`.
- Moving a portal across a 64m sector boundary permanently corrupts the portal registry: `HandleDestroyedZDO`:76979 removes it using the recomputed current sector index, which no longer matches the dictionary key, so a destroyed portal ZDO leaks into `m_portalObjects` forever and `Game.ConnectPortals()` keeps trying to pair a dead object.
- Moved portal positions are not saved. `AddObjectsPerChunk`:77572 excludes portal prefabs from chunk files and the ChunkPortal file is only written when `DirtyPortalObjects`:77621 — which a position write never sets. Every relocation reverts on restart unless you also touch the Portal connection in the same save window.
- `ZDO.InternalSetPosition`:73740 only bumps DataRevision when `IsOwner()`. Writing a position you do not own is a completely silent no-op on the wire, and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS`:76901 revokes server ownership of anything within ~96-112m of a player every 2 seconds. A moving-portal loop that forgets to re-claim ownership appears to work in the logs and does nothing in the world.
- On the CLIENT, every sector boundary a moved portal crosses adds a duplicate entry to `m_portalObjects` (`AddIfPortal`:77738 keys on the new sector and never removes the old one). Unbounded registry growth on long client sessions.
- The whole parent-sync read depends on `ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync`:87362 being ticked on the Player prefab — Inspector data, invisible to the decompile. Wonderland's ShipAttachment.cs header records a live test of the adjacent ground-body approach that was 'granted once, then never again', which is a warning sign even though the mechanism it tested was different.
- The SyncTransform connection is a latch, not a heartbeat: `OwnerSync` only rewrites it `if (m_tempParent != m_tempParentCached)`:87546. It persists across restarts via the hash path (`ZDO.Save`:74313 + `ConnectSyncTransforms`:78232), so a disconnected or crashed player's ZDO can keep claiming a ship parent indefinitely. Always cross-check `shipZdo.GetPosition() + shipRot*relPos ≈ playerZdo.GetPosition()`.
- A rider's parent is whatever Rigidbody+ZNetView they stand on — carts (Vagon), tamed mounts, Leviathans (Character.CustomFixedUpdate references Leviathan at :1598), moving props. The connection target MUST be prefab-checked for a Ship component before it means 'on a ship'.
- Pointing a portal at a Ship's ZDO works at the client transit site (`TeleportWorld.Teleport`:143539 does a bare GetZDO with no prefab validation), but `Game.ConnectPortals`:100597-100604 nulls the connection within 5 seconds because the ship has no matching `s_tag` and no reciprocal Portal connection. You must either fake both on the ship ZDO, out-write the 5s pass, or patch ConnectPortals.
- `TeleportWorld.TargetFound`:143653 requests a missing destination ZDO exactly once (`RequestZDO`→`ForceSendZDO`, which `SendZDOs`:77048 consumes). After that the client never re-requests, so a distant moving destination goes stale immediately. Only continuous server-side ForceSendZDO keeps it fresh.
- Even with a perfectly fresh destination, arriving 'on' a moving ship is impossible in vanilla: `Player.UpdateTeleport`:15343 force-assigns a FROZEN snapshot position every FixedUpdate, and for distantTeleport (which portals always pass, :143546) completion is blocked until t>8s AND IsAreaReady (:15349). The traveller is nailed to an 8-second-old coordinate.
- `ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask`:113424 omits the "vehicle" layer that `BaseAI`:25909 explicitly adds, so `FindFloor`/`GetSolidHeight` do not see a ship hull. Over water they hit the seabed instead, and the 15s fallback (:15363) drops the player to seabed height. Landing someone on a deck is not something vanilla's teleport can do.
- Vanilla bug to not build on: `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` writes relative velocity to `s_velHash` (:87561) while `SyncPosition` reads `s_velRelHash` (:87647). `velRel` is never written by anything. And `vel` is session-only (`s_sessionHashes`:78691), so it is absent from disk.
- `ZDO` holds exactly ONE connection (`s_connections`:74794 is one value per ZDO). Writing a Portal connection onto a player's ZDO would wipe their SyncTransform parentage. Ships are safe because they never have a parent.
- `ZDOExtraData.UpdateConnection`:74962 silently does nothing when no entry exists, so a player who has never boarded anything has NO connection record rather than an explicit None. Treat missing and None identically.
- `ZDOMan.SendZDOs`:77053 re-serializes the ENTIRE ZDO (every float/vec3/quat/int/long/string/byte[]) on every send — there is no delta encoding — and a permanently-incrementing DataRevision makes `ZDOPeer.ShouldSend`:76003 true forever, so each moving portal permanently occupies a slot in every peer's sync list under the 10240-byte queue cap (:77010).

### Open questions
- Is `m_characterParentSync` ticked on the Player prefab's ZSyncTransform? In-game check: have a player board a karve/longship, then from server code read `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID).GetConnectionType()` and `.GetConnectionZDOID(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.SyncTransform)`. A type of `SyncTransform` (2) with a non-None target proves it. Corroborate with `GetVec3(ZDOVars.s_relPosHash)` returning a non-zero deck-local offset and `GetString(ZDOVars.s_attachJointHash)` returning "". Repeat while the player walks, stands still, jumps, and sits at the helm, and again after they step onto the dock (should latch to None).
- Does the portal prefab (portal_wood, and Ashlands portal_stone) carry a ZSyncTransform with m_syncPosition? This is the single decisive unknown for 'moving portals'. In-game check: with a player standing next to a portal, run server-side `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetPosition(pos + Vector3.up*3f); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);` every tick for 3 seconds. If the mesh glides upward and the walk-through trigger follows, ZSyncTransform is present (expect a 20%/FixedUpdate lerp with a 5m snap, :87715). If nothing visible happens until the player walks ~120m away and back, it is absent and moving portals are dead.
- What exactly is in `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (:99828)? It decides which ZDOs get sector-exemption, m_portalObjects registration and chunk-save exclusion. Check: at server start, log every hash in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` resolved through `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash).name`.
- Can a portal even be built on a ship's deck, and if so does its ZDO position track the ship? Check: build a portal on a longship, sail 300m, then read that portal ZDO's `GetPosition()` server-side. If it is frozen at the build coordinate, ship-mounted portals are useless as destinations and effectively invisible to the portal registry's location logic.
- What Unity layer are Ship hull/deck colliders on? `ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask`:113424 omits "vehicle" while `BaseAI`:25909 includes it. Check: force-teleport a player (via the RPC_TeleportPlayer route) to 1m above a stationary boat's deck and observe whether `UpdateTeleport` completes at deck height (FindFloor hit the hull) or the player falls through into the water (it did not).
- Ship top speeds (m_sailForceFactor, m_force, mass) are all Inspector values, so the exact drift distance during the ≥8s teleport hold cannot be computed from the decompile. Check: record a longship's ZDO position server-side at 1Hz under full sail and measure metres travelled in 8 seconds — that number is the minimum miss distance for any ship-as-destination feature.
- Does `GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild` actually let a vanilla client place a portal inside a crypt, or does the portal piece's `m_allowedInDungeons` Inspector bool already permit it? Check: set the global key server-side and try placing a portal inside a burial chamber on an unmodified client.

### Corrections to the existing spec
- The spec's phrasing around the ship-attach feature is right in substance but names the wrong member. The flag is `ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync` (:87362), a component-level Inspector bool — there is no `Character.m_characterParentSync`, and `SetCharacterParent`/`RPC_SetCharacterParent` return zero grep hits across all four 1.0.7 decompiles. `Character.m_lastAttachBody` (:600) is a private Rigidbody used only for local anti-slide force on a deck (:2106-2143) and is never networked.
- The spec lists 'Portal to a player's live-attached ship' as [Feasible-with-caveats, small] pending only the Inspector check. Two additional blockers were not captured: (a) `Game.ConnectPortals`:100597-100604 will null any portal→ship link within 5 seconds because the ship carries no matching `s_tag` and no reciprocal Portal connection; (b) `TeleportWorld.TargetFound`:143653 fetches a distant target ZDO exactly once via a one-shot ForceSendZDO, so without continuous server-side `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(shipUid)` the client teleports to a stale ship position. This is medium effort with a live tick loop, not small.
- The spec does not state that a ship destination is unusable even when technically wired up. `Player.UpdateTeleport`:15343-15349 pins the arriving player at a frozen snapshot coordinate for at least 8 seconds (distantTeleport is always true for portals, :143546), and `ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask`:113424 cannot see the vehicle layer, so the traveller lands in open water behind the boat rather than on the deck. 'Portal to a player's live-attached ship' should be re-scoped to 'portal to the water beside where the ship was ~8s ago', or paired with a follow-up `RPC_TeleportPlayer` (:41627) issued after arrival.
- The spec's 'Portal to any computed coordinate' via `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` is correct, but should carry the caveat that such a portal can never be MOVED afterwards by the normal sync path: `ZDO.SetSector`:73754 freezes the sector key and `m_portalObjects` is never re-keyed, `AddObjectsPerChunk`:77572 plus the `DirtyPortalObjects` gate at :77621 mean the new position is never saved, and `HandleDestroyedZDO`:76979 leaks the ZDO if it crossed a sector boundary. Created portals should be treated as immutable in position.
- The spec correctly notes vanilla takes ownership before writing portal fields, but does not state the mechanical reason: `ZDO.InternalSetPosition`:73740 skips `IncreaseDataRevision()` entirely when the server is not the owner, so a non-owner position write never reaches any client. Combined with `ReleaseNearbyZDOS`:76901 stealing ownership every 2s for any ZDO within ~96-112m of a peer, ownership re-claiming is mandatory per write, not merely 'more reliable' as the Group 1 'Proactive server ownership claim' line implies.
- Add to the 'Ruled Out' list: **moving/following portals of any kind**. Not because the ZDO cannot be written, but because (a) vanilla clients never reposition an existing instance (`ZNetScene.CreateObject`:82011 / `ZNetView.Awake`:82566 apply position only at Instantiate), (b) the sector key is frozen so normal sync stops reaching the new location, (c) the move is not persisted, and (d) crossing a sector boundary permanently leaks the ZDO in `m_portalObjects` on destroy. Only the *destination* can meaningfully move, never the gate itself.
- The spec's dungeon coverage can be simplified: dungeon interiors need no special server-side handling at all. Zones are 2D x/z only (`ZoneSystem.GetZone`:115741), interiors sit at surface `y + 5000f` (`Location.Awake`:133512) and `InInterior` is just `y > 3000f` (:4538), so a crypt portal occupies the SAME sector as the ground above it and `Game.ConnectPortals` pairs it identically. The only dungeon-specific lever really is the client-honoured `GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild` (:13353), exactly as listed.
- `Wonderland/Core/Data/ShipAttachment.cs` deserves promotion in the spec from an implementation detail to the recommended primary mechanism for anything ship-related, because `ZDOVars.s_user` on the Ship ZDO (`ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl`:141332) is fully confirmed from code with no Inspector dependency, whereas the SyncTransform-connection path is not. The trade is coverage: s_user sees only the helmsman, never passengers.

## target-sources-world — what world-static things a dedicated server can locate and point a portal at (Valheim 1.0.7)

The dedicated server has exactly two rich, zero-player, whole-world target registries, and they are world-gen data, not ZDOs: `ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances` (every location in the world — boss altars, StartTemple, traders, crypts, dungeons, runestone camps — with a ground-height-resolved position, persisted in the world save and fully populated before any player connects) and `World.m_biomeData` (`AltBiomeWorldData`: a 2048x2048 / 12m biome+height grid plus flood-filled `BiomeSector`s with world-space `Center`, bbox, height min/max/avg, neighbours, and per-biome `AllPoints`/`AllPointsAboveSeaLevel`). Everything collider-based in `ZoneSystem` (`GetGroundHeight`, `GetSolidHeight`, `IsBlocked`, `FindFloor`, `GetGroundData`, `IsLava(Vector3)`) is **dead on a dedicated server**, because `Game.FixedUpdate` (server build, :100463) pins `ZNet.m_referencePosition` to `(1e6,0,1e6)` every physics tick, so the only Heightmap colliders that ever exist sit 1,000,000 m from the world. Server-side position validation must therefore be pure procedural math: `WorldGenerator.GetHeight/GetBiome/GetNormal/GetTerrainDelta`, sea level 30, `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap` (static, WorldGenerator-only), `WorldGenerator.worldSize/waterEdge`, plus `AltBiomeWorldData.PointHeights` as an O(1) cached 12m height lookup. Object-level targets (a specific altar bowl, a chest, a dungeon room) are ZDOs that only exist after a peer's ghost-zone generation has run for that zone, are found only via the resumable `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` (there is no `GetAllZDOsWithPrefab`), and require prefab names that live in Unity asset data. Finally, two vanilla server→client channels already push world coordinates onto a vanilla client's map: the `LocationIcons` routed RPC (also the authority for where a vanilla client respawns, via `Game.m_StartLocation` = "StartTemple") and `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` (arbitrary saved pin, name, type, position).

### Facts
- **[dedicated-server]** On a dedicated server `Game.FixedUpdate` unconditionally sets `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick. The client build's `Game.FixedUpdate` has no such line. — `Game.FixedUpdate, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100463-100466 (compare assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:100885)` → Every server subsystem keyed off the reference position operates around (1e6,0,1e6): `ZoneSystem.CreateLocalZones` (:113930), `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` (:82270), `ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted` (:82112), `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76880). No terrain collider and effectively no GameObject ever exists near real world coordinates.
- **[dedicated-server]** Every ground/solid/blocked helper on ZoneSystem is a `Physics.Raycast` against layer masks built in `ZoneSystem.Awake` (terrain / Default / static_solid / Default_small / piece). — `ZoneSystem.Awake :113419-113425; IsBlocked :115496; GetGroundHeight :115502 and :115513; GetSolidHeight :115525, :115536, :115548, :115574; GetStaticSolidHeight :115590; FindFloor :115604; GetGroundData :115667; IsLava(Vector3) :115647` → All of these silently return the fallback (`p.y`, or false) on a dedicated server because no Heightmap/piece collider exists at real world coordinates. They are NOT usable for validating a portal destination. Do not call them and do not trust a `false`/`p.y` result as 'no ground'.
- **[dedicated-server]** Ghost-mode zone spawning does instantiate a Heightmap (`SpawnZone` instantiates `m_zonePrefab` for every mode) but immediately `Destroy`s the root and all spawned objects at the end of the same call when mode == Ghost. — `ZoneSystem.SpawnZone :114071, instantiate :114085, ghost teardown :114094-114102; Heightmap.OnEnable→Regenerate :128417-128429; Heightmap.Regenerate→RebuildCollisionMesh :128521-128527` → There is a sub-frame window where a peer's ghost zone has a real terrain collider, but it is gone by the next frame. Not a usable query surface; do not design around it.
- **[world-gen-data]** `ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances` is a public `Dictionary<Vector2s, LocationInstance>` holding one entry per zone for EVERY location in the whole world, and it is written to and read from the world save (`Save`/`Load`). — `ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances :113295; PrepareSave :113734; Save :113742 (locations written :113762-113770); Load :113782 (RegisterLocation replay :113801-113815)` → This is the primary server-side world-target registry: complete, whole-map, available at world load with zero players connected, survives restarts, costs one dictionary read. This — not a ZDO scan — is how a server-only mod enumerates boss altars, the start temple, traders, crypts and dungeon sites.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZNet.ServerLoadWorld` calls `AltBiomeWorldData.VerifyBiomeData(m_world)` and then `ZoneSystem.instance.GenerateLocationsIfNeeded()` immediately after loading the world db, before any peer can connect. — `ZNet.ServerLoadWorld :79273-79285; WorldGenerator.Initialize :79200` → Both the location registry and the biome grid are guaranteed populated by the time a mod's first tick runs on a dedicated server. No 'wait for a player' gating is needed.
- **[world-gen-data]** `LocationInstance.m_position.y` is set to `WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(x, z)` during location generation, and altitude checks in the same loop compare `y - 30.0`. — `ZoneSystem.GenerateLocationsTimeSliced :114639, y assignment :114735, altitude test :114736-114742; LocationInstance struct :113001` → Every stored location position already carries a procedurally-valid ground height with sea level = 30. A portal target at a location needs no extra height resolution — only a +1..2 m lift. Caveat: it is the PRE-flattening height; a location with `m_clearArea`/terrain modifiers ends up a metre or two off.
- **[dedicated-server]** `ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(name, out pos)` and `GetLocationIcons(dict)` branch on `ZNet.instance.IsServer()`: the server branch reads `m_locationInstances` directly and emits entries whose `ZoneLocation.m_iconAlways` is true, or `m_iconPlaced` is true AND the instance is already placed. The client branch reads the RPC-received `m_locationIcons` dictionary. — `ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon :115422-115447; GetLocationIcons :115450-115467; m_locationIcons (client-only store) :113303` → `GetLocationIcons` on the server is the ready-made 'world landmark registry': {world position -> location prefab name} for every icon-flagged location (in vanilla: start temple, boss altars, traders). O(number of location instances), no allocation beyond the dict, no players needed. Cache it; don't call it per frame.

- **[dedicated-server]** `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type, hash)` supports only Float/Long/Int/String and logs an error for anything else (ByteArray included).
