### Gotchas
- The single biggest trap: `ZoneSystem.instance.GetGroundHeight/GetSolidHeight/IsBlocked/FindFloor/GetGroundData/IsLava(Vector3)` all COMPILE and all RUN on a dedicated server — they just always return the no-hit fallback, because Game.FixedUpdate (:100463) pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) so no terrain collider exists near real coordinates. They will not throw and will not log. A `GetGroundHeight` that returns `p.y` unchanged looks like a valid answer.
- There is no `ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefab`. Only `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative(string, List<ZDO>, ref int)` (:77442). Existing specs that say 'a plain spatial ZDO scan finds every altar' are describing an API that does not exist in 1.0.7.
- `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` re-scans `m_objectsBySector[0]` on its terminal call (:77445-77455), so any ZDO in sector index 0 — zone (-256,-256) AND the out-of-range fallback bucket that every coordinate beyond +/-16384 m falls into — is returned twice per full pass. Deduplicate.
- Portal ZDOs are invisible to `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` until its FINAL call, because they live in `m_portalObjects`, not `m_objectsBySector` (AddIfPortal :77732 removes them from the sector array). An abandoned scan reports zero portals.
- `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752). Moving a portal ZDO with SetPosition leaves the m_portalObjects key stale: the new sector never sees it in FindObjects, and HandleDestroyedZDO (:76980) can never remove it. Create a fresh target ZDO instead of relocating one.
- `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` does not set `Persistent` and does not write the prefab into the ZDO body — `ZNetView.Awake` (:82612-82620) normally does both. A hand-made non-portal target ZDO with Persistent=false is never written to the save (GetSaveClonePerChunk filter :77572). Portal-prefab ZDOs escape this because the portal chunk is saved wholesale (:77621).
- `BiomeSector.MinZone`/`MaxZone` are garbage: GenerateSectors computes both from `sector.Min`, and passes the y value into `new Vector3(x, y)` so `GetZone` reads z = 0 (:92577-92578). Compute zone bounds from Min/Max yourself.
- `BiomeSector.Center` is the centroid of the region's PERIMETER cells (only cells adjacent to a different sector contribute, :92531-92535), not its area centroid. For a crescent or ring-shaped biome region the centre can land in a different biome entirely. Always re-check `WorldGenerator.GetBiome` at the chosen point.
- A location's ZDOs (the altar bowl's parent piece, the trader, the runestone, the chests) do NOT exist until that zone has been ghost-generated, which only happens once a peer's reference position brings it inside `CreateGhostZones`' simulation distance (:113934). The LocationInstance exists from world creation; the objects inside it do not. Never assume a boss altar ZDO is findable on a fresh server.
- `ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon` returns the FIRST dictionary match, not the nearest, and silently returns false for any location whose `m_iconAlways`/`m_iconPlaced` flags are unset — those flags are Unity Inspector data on the ZoneLocation.
- `LocationInstance.m_position.y` is the PRE-placement `WorldGenerator.GetHeight`. `PlaceLocations` re-resolves it with a raycast at spawn time and forces y = 30 for `m_snapToWater` locations (:114963-114968). Expect a metre or two of error, and treat ocean locations as sitting at exactly 30.
- `mask.a` from `WorldGenerator.GetHeight(x, z, out Color mask)` means lava only in the Ashlands (GetAshlandsHeight :152224). In Mistlands and Deep North the same channel carries an unrelated mask, and ZoneSystem's own location generator reads it as a 'vegetation' value (:114780-114792). Do not treat mask.a > 0.6 as lava outside the Ashlands — use `IsLavaPreHeightmap`, which biome-gates first.
- `class Teleport` (dungeon doors) stores its destination in `public Teleport m_targetPoint` — a compiled Inspector reference with zero networking (:143322). Dungeon entrance/exit pairing is permanently invisible to a server-only mod.
- `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash` cannot search ByteArray fields (:75403), so there is no global way to find every `DungeonGenerator` by its `s_roomData` payload. You must reach dungeon generators via prefab name or via their LocationProxy.
- `Minimap.UpdateLocationPins` silently drops any LocationIcons entry whose name has no sprite in `Minimap.m_locationIcons` (GetLocationIcon returns null, assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57594). Invented location names produce no pin and no error on a vanilla client.
- Leviathans have a Rigidbody, are owner-simulated every FixedUpdate, and self-destruct on the `submerged` animation state (:132218-132229). They are not a stable portal target.
- The `IsDiscovered` pass in GenerateSectors (:92605-92612) calls `ZoneSystem.instance.IsZoneLoaded` while iterating the broken MinZone/MaxZone range — it is effectively always false on a server. Do not read `BiomeSector.IsDiscovered`.

### Open questions
- Which vanilla location prefab names correspond to each boss altar, the traders and the Bog Witch? These live in the LocationList Unity assets, not the C# decompile. In-game check: on a running dedicated server with the mod loaded, dump `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locations` — for each entry log `m_prefab.Name`, `m_biome`, `m_quantity`, `m_unique`, `m_iconAlways`, `m_iconPlaced`, `m_exteriorRadius` — and separately dump `GetLocationIcons()` on a generated world. The icon-flagged set is the landmark list; cross-reference names against `m_quantity == 1 && m_unique` for boss altars.
- Does `SoftReference<GameObject>.Name` (used by FindClosestLocation/FindLocations and GetLocationIcon) resolve without loading the asset, and is it cheap? SoftReference lives in an assembly not present in this decompile set. In-game check: time 10,000 `FindClosestLocation` calls on a dedicated server and watch for asset-load log spam; if it is expensive, key the mod's index off `ZoneLocation.m_prefabName` (a plain string, :112892) instead.
- Which prefabs are in `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (:99828, hashed into `PortalPrefabHash` in Game.Awake :100029)? Inspector data. This decides whether a mod-created target ZDO enters `m_portalObjects` (always resident, always saved, force-sendable) or the ordinary sector array. In-game check: log `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` against `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefabNames()` hashes at server start.
- Does a mod-created target ZDO actually have to be a portal-prefab ZDO for `TeleportWorld.Teleport` to use it? The method only reads GetPosition/GetRotation off the connection target (:143536-143541), but `Game.ConnectPortals` (:100589) prunes based on the target's tag and reciprocal connection, and only iterates GetPortalList. In-game check: create a non-portal-prefab ZDO at a target coordinate, SetConnection both ways, and see whether a vanilla client teleports and whether the link survives the 5 s coroutine.
- Does the vanilla zone prefab's Heightmap GameObject carry a MeshCollider on the DEDICATED SERVER build (Heightmap.Awake does `GetComponent<MeshCollider>()` and RebuildCollisionMesh null-checks it, :128368/:128897)? Only matters if someone tries to salvage the sub-frame ghost-zone collider window. In-game check: log `Heightmap.GetAllHeightmaps()` count and each one's transform.position on a dedicated server — expect a handful, all near (1e6, *, 1e6).
- How many location instances does a full vanilla 1.0.7 world actually hold, and how long does one `GetLocationIcons`/`FindClosestLocation` pass take on server hardware? This sets whether the mod can query live or must cache. In-game check: log `m_locationInstances.Count` and Stopwatch one full `FindLocations` pass at server boot.
- Are `AllPoints`/`AllPointsAboveSeaLevel` lists retained in memory after `GenerateSectors`, and how large are they (2048*2048 = 4.2M cells distributed across biomes)? Memory cost matters before leaning on `GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel`. In-game check: log `ZNet.World.m_biomeData.Biomes[b].AllPoints.Count` per biome and the process RSS delta at server start.
- Which location-icon names does the stock client's `Minimap.m_locationIcons` list actually contain (:56373)? This bounds what a server can render as a location pin without a client mod. In-game check: connect a vanilla client and log the names for which `Minimap.GetLocationIcon` returns non-null, or inspect the Minimap prefab in the shipped assets.

### Corrections to the existing spec
- SPEC (Group 1): 'Portal to nearest/named boss altar — the real altar is `OfferingBowl`, an always-present world-gen ZDO ... a plain spatial ZDO scan finds every altar with zero new bookkeeping.' — WRONG on three counts. (1) `OfferingBowl` is a plain MonoBehaviour with no ZDO of its own; it does `GetComponentInParent<ZNetView>()` in Start (:135652-135661), so the ZDO belongs to the altar piece. (2) That ZDO is NOT always present — it is created only when the zone is ghost- or full-generated, which needs a peer's reference position nearby (`ZoneSystem.CreateGhostZones` :113934, `SpawnLocation` ghost path :115234). On a fresh server, no altar ZDO exists anywhere. (3) There is no 'plain spatial ZDO scan' for a prefab — only the resumable `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` (:77442), and it needs the altar prefab NAME, which is Unity asset data. The correct, always-available, zero-player source is `ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances` / `FindClosestLocation(altarLocationName, ...)` (:113295, :115707) — world-gen data persisted in the save.
- SPEC (Group 1): 'Portal to any computed coordinate — `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(pos, prefabHash)` makes a real, persistent, correctly-owned ZDO.' — REFINE. `CreateNewZDO` (:76674/:76684) sets the owner to the session ID and calls `AddIfPortal(zdo, prefabHash)`, but it does NOT set `Persistent` (default false, :73323) and does NOT write the prefab into the ZDO body (`SetPrefab` :73808 is a separate call `ZNetView.Awake` makes, :82615-82620). A non-portal-prefab ZDO left at Persistent=false is dropped from the world save (`GetSaveClonePerChunk` persistence filter :77572). A portal-prefab ZDO escapes that because the whole `m_portalObjects` set is saved into the dedicated ChunkPortal file with no Persistent check (:77621-77636) — but only when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set, which `AddIfPortal` (:77748) does.
- SPEC (Group 1) implicitly: relocating a portal server-side. ADD A HARD WARNING. `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for any portal-prefab ZDO (:73752-73757), so `SetPosition` (:73729) does not re-file it: `m_portalObjects` keeps the OLD sector key. Consequences: `FindObjects` for the new sector never includes it (:77376), and `HandleDestroyedZDO` looks it up by the NEW sector index and silently fails to remove it, leaking it in m_portalObjects forever (:76980-76986). Create a fresh ZDO at the destination rather than moving an existing portal.
- SPEC (Central Constraint): 'ZoneSystem's local-zone creation is gated on the same permanently-pinned reference position.' — CORRECT, and now precisely citable: the pin is `Game.FixedUpdate` in the SERVER build setting `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` unconditionally every physics tick (:100463-100466); the client build's FixedUpdate has no equivalent line (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:100885). Worth stating the consequence explicitly in the spec: every `Physics.Raycast`-backed ZoneSystem helper (GetGroundHeight, GetSolidHeight, IsBlocked, FindFloor, GetGroundData, IsLava(Vector3)) silently returns the no-hit fallback on a dedicated server rather than failing loudly.
- SPEC (Group 1): 'Portal to world spawn / start location, via `ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(m_StartLocation)`' — CORRECT, with two caveats worth adding: on the server that method takes the `m_locationInstances` branch and requires the location's `m_iconAlways`/`m_iconPlaced` flag (:115424-115436), and it returns the FIRST dictionary match rather than the nearest. Also worth adding as a feature the spec does not list: the same `LocationIcons` payload is what a vanilla client uses to decide where to respawn (`Game.FindSpawnPoint` client-side :100796), so a server can relocate the world spawn for vanilla clients with no client mod.
- SPEC MISSING ENTIRELY — two server→client map channels that are directly relevant to 'show a player where their portal now points', both vanilla-respecting and needing no client install: (a) `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse(pinName, pinType, pos, showMap)`, registered on both sides in Game.Start (:100068) and handled client-side by `Minimap.DiscoverLocation` → `AddPin(..., save: true, ...)` (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:58394) — an arbitrary SAVED pin at an arbitrary coordinate with a HUD message and optional map-open; (b) the `LocationIcons` routed RPC (`ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons` :113581), which gives the server full authority over the location-icon pin set on every vanilla client, refreshed every 5 s (Minimap.UpdateLocationPins, assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57551).
- SPEC MISSING — the biome-region target source. `ZNet.World.m_biomeData` (`AltBiomeWorldData`, :92332, built by `ZNet.ServerLoadWorld` :79283) is a disk-cached 2048x2048 / 12 m grid of biome + height, plus flood-filled `BiomeSector` regions carrying world-space `Center`, bbox, height min/max/avg, neighbours and size, plus per-biome `AllPoints`/`AllPointsAboveSeaLevel`. It makes 'portal to a random/nearest Plains region, on land' and 'portal to a biome centroid' one-call operations with zero players and O(1) height lookups, and it is the cheapest server-side 'is this coordinate land' filter available.
- SPEC MISSING — the server-side position-validation recipe, which the spec never states. On a dedicated server, validate a candidate (x,z) with: (1) `x*x + z*z <= WorldGenerator.waterEdgeSqr` (110250000, :151122) for in-world; (2) `float h = WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(x, z)` (:151944) and require `h > 30f + margin` for dry land (sea level ZoneSystem.c_WaterLevel = 30f, :113228); (3) `!ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap(new Vector3(x, h, z))` (:115637) for the Ashlands; (4) `WorldGenerator.instance.GetTerrainDelta(p, r, out delta, out _)` (:152364) with delta <= ~2 for flatness, or `GetAverageNormal` (:151905) for slope; (5) reject `y > 3000f` per `Character.InInterior` (:4538); (6) reject candidates inside any `LocationInstance`'s `m_location.m_exteriorRadius` (:112930) using the location registry; (7) `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear` (Wonderland Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs, over `ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects` :77142) to reject spots occupied by pieces or wards. Steps 2-4 are blind to player terraforming and to a location's own flattening — always add >= 1 m clearance.

## Existing-codebase assets for TortalPortal Lite: Wonderland server-only engine inventory, full TortalPortal feature classification, PortalLock post-mortem, loader stack

Wonderland is a complete, production server-only mod framework that TortalPortal Lite should fork wholesale rather than re-derive: a Heartbeat + SubsystemRegistry tick/lifecycle, a hot-reloading ServerSync'd config with Bind helpers, and ten Core/Data utilities that already solve every server-only primitive a portal mod needs — sector-bounded and time-budgeted ZDO scanning (ZdoSpatialQuery), the per-peer character-ZDO view that replaces the always-empty Player.GetAllPlayers() (ConnectedCharacters), server->vanilla-client toast messages (PlayerNotify), the only reliable vanilla-client->server control channel (EmoteSignals), a routed-RPC status-effect grant (StatusEffectRpc), and a compat shim for the 1.0 sector API (GameShape). Three Wonderland engines are direct portal analogues: WaterBuoyancyEngine's ZDO ownership-claim / SetOwner-block / ForceSendZDO pattern, WorldRatesEngine's GlobalKeyAdd+SendGlobalKeys write path (the mechanism for NoPortals/TeleportAll/NoBossPortals), and SpawnGovernor's ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO+ZDO.Deserialize pair — the ONLY server-side hook that sees a client-placed object appear, which is what a server-enforced portal cap must be built on. Two under-documented capabilities found in Wonderland that the Lite spec does not currently mention: FirstSpawnGrant pushes a real, persistent map pin to a 100%-vanilla client via the routed RPC "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse", and VacuumEngine plays vanilla VFX/SFX on vanilla clients via the routed RPC "SpawnObject" — partial server-side replacements for TortalPortal's PortalMapPins and runic-gateway VFX. Of full TortalPortal's ~22 features, 4 are fully replicable server-side, 8 partially (degraded), and 10 are impossible without a client. PortalLock (PAUSED) attempted a server-side portal cap by patching Player.PlacePiece and ZNetScene.Instantiate — both dead on a dedicated server — which is exactly the trap Wonderland's SpawnGovernor documents and avoids.

### Facts
- **[dedicated-server]** Wonderland's lifecycle is: BepInEx Awake -> GameShape.Detect() -> ConfigSync built -> WonderlandConfig.Bind -> RegisterSubsystems -> Subsystems.InitializeAll(config, configSync, harmony) -> a Harmony postfix on ZNetScene.Awake drives OnWorldReady; Update() calls PollConfigFile(), Heartbeat.OnUpdate(dt), Subsystems.OnUpdate(). A Lite mod should copy this shape verbatim. — `WonderlandPlugin.Awake + WonderlandPlugin.Update + WorldReadyHook.Postfix, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Plugin.cs:35, :71, :151` → Lite needs no new lifecycle design; copy Plugin.cs, Core/IWonderlandSubsystem.cs, Core/SubsystemRegistry.cs, Core/Heartbeat.cs and rename. OnWorldReady is the only safe point for ZNetScene/ObjectDB prefab reads.
- **[dedicated-server]** IWonderlandSubsystem is a 4-method contract (Initialize/OnWorldReady/OnUpdate/Shutdown) plus Name/IsEnabled; SubsystemRegistry wraps every call in try/catch so one failing subsystem cannot take the mod down, and SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch(harmony, patchType) applies a Harmony patch set with a logged warning instead of an exception on failure. — `IWonderlandSubsystem, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/IWonderlandSubsystem.cs:7; SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/SubsystemRegistry.cs:99` → Lite subsystems (PortalNetwork, PortalGovernor, PortalNotify) drop straight into this registry. SafePatch is the required wrapper for every portal-related Harmony patch.
- **[dedicated-server]** ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(worldPos, radiusMeters, reuseBuffer) returns every ZDO within a real metre radius by calling ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects with SimulationDistance(area, 0, classic:true) and post-filtering by squared distance; it never uses Physics.OverlapSphere because no collider exists server-side away from the pinned reference position. — `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25` → This is the ready-made 'find portals / altars / beds / ships near point X' primitive for every Lite destination-resolution feature (portal-to-nearest-altar, portal-to-bed, portal-to-ship). Reuse, do not rewrite.
- **[dedicated-server]** ZdoSpatialQuery has two unanchored whole-map scanners: PrefabSetScanner round-robins ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative across a set of prefab NAMES one chunk per Advance(); PrefabSetSweeper walks ZDOMan.m_objectsBySector directly against a HashSet of prefab HASHES with an explicit sectorBudget, returning true when a full map pass completes. The header records that the name-based scanner re-walks all 512*512=262144 sector slots per prefab and ran to hours for ~800 prefabs, which is why the hash-set sweeper exists. — `ZdoSpatialQuery.PrefabSetScanner, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:92; ZdoSpatialQuery.PrefabSetSweeper.Advance, same file :135 and :153` → For portals specifically NEITHER is needed: ZDOMan.GetPortalList() already returns every portal ZDO in the world for free. Use the sweepers only if Lite needs to scan a non-portal prefab family (OfferingBowl altars, Bed, Ship).
- **[dedicated-server]** ConnectedCharacters.All() returns (ZNetPeer, character ZDO) pairs for every ready peer via ZDOMan.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID), and the struct exposes PlayerId (ZDOVars.s_playerID - the STABLE identity to persist, not peer.m_uid and not the ZDOID), Name (ZDOVars.s_playerName with peer.m_playerName fallback) and Position. Its header records that Player.GetAllPlayers() is always empty on a dedicated server and that six Wonderland subsystems silently did nothing in their first version because of it. — `ConnectedCharacters.All, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/ConnectedCharacters.cs:56; ConnectedCharacter.PlayerId :30` → Every Lite per-player feature (per-player portal cap, portal-use logging, named warps, 'who owns this gate') must go through this, keyed on s_playerID. It is exactly what TortalPortal's own server-side PlayerNames.HarvestPeers re-implements independently.
- **[dedicated-server]** PlayerNotify.Toast(who, message, center) sends a server->client message to a 100%-vanilla client by invoking the routed RPC "Message" on the player's own character ZDO with (int type, string msg, int amount); the client's Player.RPC_Message hands it to MessageHud.ShowMessage which Localizes it first, so "$piece_portal" arrives translated. — `PlayerNotify.Toast, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs:15` → This is Lite's entire player-facing text channel: 'Portal locked', 'Destination rotated to X', 'Portal cap reached (6)'. It replaces TortalPortal's MessageHudPatch/centre messages with zero client install, and it is how a cap refusal or a PIN failure gets communicated.
- **[dedicated-server]** EmoteSignals is the only reliable vanilla-client->server control channel. It polls every connected character's ZDOVars.s_emoteID counter at 0.25s and dispatches the new ZDOVars.s_emote string to registered handlers. Its header documents why chat is NOT usable: a stock client runs an unknown slash command locally and prints 'not a recognized command', and plain chat is sent as one routed RPC per OTHER listed player, so a player alone on the server produces no chat traffic at all. — `EmoteSignals.OnUpdate, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/EmoteSignals.cs:46; EmoteSignals.Register :38; EmoteSignals.Is :125` → Any Lite player-triggered portal action (cycle this gate's destination, lock/unlock, request the portal list as toasts) must be emote-driven, not chat-driven. CacheClaimControl.cs is the worked example of a full emote-command subsystem in ~45 lines.

### Gotchas
- RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse pins are added with save:true — they land permanently in the player's own saved pin list and the server has NO removal RPC. A Lite 'portal map pins' feature cannot un-pin a demolished portal, and re-pushing after a rename creates a SECOND pin (HaveSimilarPin matches on name AND type AND position-within-1m). Treat it as a one-shot discovery push, not a live-synced pin set like TortalPortal's PortalMapPins, which adds/removes client-side pins every 2s (PortalMapPins.Rebuild, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PortalMapPins.cs:89).
- ZDOIDs are renumbered on every world load — ZDO.Load does m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID) — so any Lite state file keyed by ZDOID silently points at nothing after a restart. TortalPortal's Favorites.cs hit exactly this (stars vanished between sessions, Favorites.cs:109-124) and switched to a rounded-position key; Wonderland's SupplySwitch is still ZDOID-keyed and prunes dead ids on save, which masks the same bug as 'the station forgot'. Key Lite portal state by position, or by world global key.
- PortalLock's failure mode is the canonical trap: patching Player.PlacePiece / Player.TryPlacePiece / ZNetScene.Instantiate with an `if (!ZNet.instance.IsServer()) return true;` guard produces code that can never execute. The server has no Player instance and never instantiates a client-placed piece. Use the ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO + ZDO.Deserialize pair instead.
- A Harmony postfix on ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO ALONE always sees GetPrefab()==0 on the network-receive path — the prefab hash only arrives in the subsequent ZDO.Deserialize. SpawnGovernor's header records this as a shipped bug in its own first version (SpawnGovernor.cs:16-24).
- ServerSync's CustomSyncedValue<string> — TortalPortal's entire portal-index delivery mechanism — is invisible to a vanilla client (no ConfigSync RPC is registered there). Anything Lite wants a player to SEE must go through PlayerNotify toasts, RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse pins, or SpawnObject effects. There is no fourth channel.
- A stock client never sends a slash command to the server (Chat.InputText runs it locally and prints 'not a recognized command') and plain chat is routed only to OTHER listed players, so a lone player generates zero chat traffic. Emotes (ZDOVars.s_emoteID / s_emote on the character ZDO) are the only reliable player->server signal. Documented at length in EmoteSignals.cs:8-27, and independently confirmed by CacheClaimControl's header, which records replacing a '/cache claim' chat hook that could never run.
- ObjectDB.instance is frequently still null at the ZNetScene.Awake postfix this codebase treats as 'world ready' — live-confirmed 2026-09-11. BuffRosterEngine retries once per tick from OnUpdate until it resolves (BuffRosterEngine.cs:83-96); WaterBuoyancyEngine's ObjectDB read at the same hook silently no-ops and is masked only because its ZNetScene prefab loop finds everything anyway. Any Lite OnWorldReady code touching ObjectDB must retry.
- On mono, a compile-time binding to a member the loaded assembly lacks throws at JIT of the CALLING method — a try/catch inside that method does not save it. Version-sensitive calls must live in their own method only invoked after a reflection-based detection confirms the shape (GameShape.cs:29-48). Separately, Type.GetMethod's single-result overload throws AmbiguousMatchException when a compatibility patcher injects a same-name/same-parameter overload differing only in return type — enumerate with GetMethods() and filter by hand.
- ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID and RPC_SetTag's authorId are raw, unverified client self-reports; nothing cross-checks them against the ZNetPeer that owns the connection the packet arrived on. Any Lite feature trusting a player identity carried in a portal-adjacent RPC needs its own peer cross-check first. TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md Group 4 flags this; the Wonderland codebase contains no hardening for it yet.
- Wonderland's ZdoSetOwnerPatch is an unconditional prefix on ZDO.SetOwner — a global hot path touched by ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS on every peer move. If Lite forks it for portals, the predicate must fail fast on prefab hash before anything else, and must never block uid==0 or uid==ZDOMan.GetSessionID().
- TortalPortal's cap is CLIENT-enforced (Player.TryPlacePiece prefix) and its own LogRefusal comment records the effective cap 'wandered between values nobody had deliberately set' before a locking config entry existed. Do not port that design into Lite — the SpawnGovernor destroy-on-arrival cap is both server-authoritative and simpler.
- StructureUpkeep caps routed broadcasts at 256 per sweep because a first pass over a long-running world turned up thousands of dirty ZDOs, each becoming a packet to every peer in one frame. Any Lite sweep touching many portals at once (mass re-tag, network rebuild, a lockdown nulling every connection) needs the same per-sweep broadcast budget.
- TortalPortal's SnapGuard and TraderRepair depend on Heightmap.FindHeightmap / a loaded collider, so they are client-only in practice on a dedicated server despite patching types the server also loads. 'The server loads this type' does not mean 'the patch fires'.
- Wonderland's SecuritySubsystem.Initialize carries a written post-mortem of a patch that shipped dead: a DamagePlausibility postfix on Character.RPC_Damage could never run server-side, because a damage RPC is routed to the victim's OWNING peer (ZRoutedRpc only handles a routed RPC locally when it is the target or the target is Everybody), and even a locally-handled ZDO RPC needs a live instance via ZNetScene.FindInstance, which the server never has away from its pinned reference position. The same two conditions kill any Lite plan to intercept a per-portal, per-player RPC.
- PortalLock detected portals by a case-insensitive 'portal' substring on the GameObject name plus GetComponent("Portal") — vanilla's component is TeleportWorld, so that component test never matched anything. Portal identity should come from ZDOMan's own registry (Game.PortalPrefabHash-backed GetPortalList/GetPortals), which also picks up modded portal pieces for free.

### Open questions
- Does RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse actually render on a PlayFab/Xbox crossplay client identically to Steam? Wonderland ships it behind StarterBoatMapPin (default on) but -NextSteps.md carries no live-test note for it, unlike the Moder/RequireBoat entries which are explicitly dated 2026-09-11. IN-GAME CHECK: connect a vanilla client, have the server invoke the RPC at a known coordinate, confirm the pin appears, log out and back in to confirm save:true really persisted, then re-send the identical payload and confirm HaveSimilarPin suppresses a duplicate.
- Does ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject accept an arbitrary effect prefab hash from a routed RPC on a 1.0.7 vanilla client with no server-side instance present? VacuumEngine only exercises vfx_fermenter_add / sfx_fermenter_add. IN-GAME CHECK: server-invoke "SpawnObject" with a portal-flavoured vanilla effect hash at a portal position and confirm a vanilla client plays it; also confirm whether the prefab must exist in ZNetScene.m_prefabs on the SERVER for the hash to be meaningful, or only on the client.
- Can the server destroy a client-created portal ZDO inside ZDO.Deserialize's own postfix without a client-side desync? The placing client already has a live GameObject. SpawnGovernor does exactly this for creatures and is shipped, but a Piece/WearNTear-bearing object may behave differently. IN-GAME CHECK: set a cap of 1, place a second portal on a vanilla client, and observe whether the ghost portal disappears cleanly, leaves an orphaned local instance until the zone reloads, or refunds/consumes the build materials.
- Whether a portal ZDO whose connection the server force-writes to ZDOID.None is reliably re-broadcast to a nearby client that currently OWNS that ZDO, or whether the owning client's next push overwrites the server's write. WaterBuoyancyEngine solves the analogous problem with a SetOwner block plus ForceSendZDO; whether portals need the same is untested. IN-GAME CHECK: stand at a portal, have the server null its connection, and watch whether the gate reads as disconnected and stays that way for 60s.
- Whether a client already standing at a portal picks up a server-side ZDOVars.s_tag change without a zone reload. TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal runs on a 0.5s InvokeRepeating so the connection state probably refreshes, but the hover text goes through a separate GetTagInfo read. IN-GAME CHECK: stand at a gate, server-write a new tag, and see whether the hover text and the connected/unconnected state both update without walking away.
- Whether ZDOVars.s_creator is reliably populated on a player-placed portal in 1.0.7. TortalPortal's PortalExport and PortalRegistry both treat creator==0 as 'admin-spawned or older than the field', which implies usually non-zero but not always — and a server-enforced per-player cap is only as good as this field. IN-GAME CHECK: place a portal on a vanilla client, dump s_creator server-side, and confirm it equals the same value that lands in ZDOVars.s_playerID on that player's character ZDO.
- Whether ZNetScene.m_prefabs on the DEDICATED SERVER build contains the portal prefabs with usable components (Wonderland's ContainerRegistry and StructureUpkeep both enumerate ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs server-side and find real components, so this is very likely yes, but Lite depends on it for any GetComponent<TeleportWorld>() prefab test). IN-GAME CHECK: log ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab("portal_wood")?.GetComponent<TeleportWorld>() at OnWorldReady on the dedicated server and confirm non-null, along with m_activationRange / m_exitDistance / m_allowAllItems values.

### Corrections to the existing spec
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 61 says 'Every Portal in the Realm, Listed' is 'admin/Discord-facing only, not an in-game player UI'. Too strong. Two in-game, zero-client-install channels exist and are already shipped in Wonderland: (a) PlayerNotify.Toast pushes arbitrary localized text to a vanilla player's MessageHud (Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs:15), so an emote can make the server toast a paged portal list; (b) ZRoutedRpc "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse" pushes a REAL map pin with a chosen name and Minimap.PinType to a vanilla client (FirstSpawnGrant.cs:253-263, registration assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100068, client body assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:101265). Lite can therefore give a vanilla player named portal markers on their own map — a genuine partial replication of PortalMapPins. Unavoidable caveat: the pin is save:true and there is no removal RPC.
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md has no entry for server-side portal VFX. Wonderland's VacuumEngine.PlayVacuumEffect (Subsystems/ItemFlow/VacuumEngine.cs:162) shows the server can play any vanilla effect prefab on vanilla clients by broadcasting the native "SpawnObject" routed RPC per nearby peer. This does not replicate the procedural runic gateway, but it makes 'a visible/audible cue when a hub rotates, a gate is locked, or a lockdown starts' feasible. Add as [Feasible, small].
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 55 proposes detecting 'a player's live-attached ship' via the ZSyncTransform / ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.SyncTransform link and flags it as needing an in-game Inspector check (whether Player's prefab has m_characterParentSync enabled). Wonderland already ships a BETTER, decompile-confirmed, live-tested signal needing no Inspector data: ShipAttachment.IsSteeringShip reads ZDOVars.s_user (hash of "user") off the Ship's own ZDO, written by ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl and zeroed by RPC_ReleaseControl (Core/Data/ShipAttachment.cs:12-19, :31). It answers 'is actively steering' rather than 'is standing on', which is the sharper question. Downgrade line 55's caveat and line 56's cruder proximity fallback accordingly.
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md has no per-player portal cap entry at all, yet it is the single most valuable server-only portal feature and the one thing Lite would do BETTER than full TortalPortal (whose cap is client-enforced in a Player.TryPlacePiece prefix, PlacementPatch.cs:89, and whose own log comment records the effective cap wandering because any client's config could override it). Mechanism: Wonderland's SpawnGovernor ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO + ZDO.Deserialize pair (SpawnGovernor.cs:43/:58), ZDOMan.GetPortalList() counted by ZDOVars.s_creator, destroy-over-limit plus a PlayerNotify.Toast refusal. Add as [Feasible, medium].
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 62 lists 'Proactive server ownership claim on placement' as [Feasible, medium] citing WaterBuoyancyEngine generically. The concrete three-part recipe is worth recording: zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) + zdo.DataRevision += 4096 + ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid) to push; a prefix on ZDO.SetOwner returning false to stop ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS handing the portal back to a nearby client; and a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC keyed on "RPC_RequestOwn".GetStableHashCode() to grant a temporary window when a client legitimately needs ownership (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:158-164, :251, :301, :315).
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 76 says self-service named warps should use 'an emote or item-interaction trigger, not a slash command'. Correct, but it understates what exists: EmoteSignals (Core/Data/EmoteSignals.cs) is a complete shipped emote-command bus with per-character counter tracking, disabled-state reseeding and departed-peer pruning, and CacheClaimControl.cs:16 is a 47-line worked example of a full emote command with nearest-target search, a range config and a toast reply. The effort estimate for any emote-triggered Lite feature should drop accordingly.
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md says nothing about where per-portal mod-side state should live, and two shipped precedents conflict. SupplySwitch persists per-object state to a ZDOID-keyed file (SupplySwitch.cs:100-165), while TortalPortal's Favorites.cs documents that ZDO.Load does m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID) on every world load and switched to a rounded-position key for exactly that reason (Favorites.cs:109-124). Lite must key portal state by position or by world global key, never by bare ZDOID. Add this as an explicit design constraint.
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md describes Wonderland only as a source of patterns. It is in fact a directly forkable chassis: Plugin.cs (lifecycle + 5s config hot-reload), Core/IWonderlandSubsystem.cs, Core/SubsystemRegistry.cs (incl. SafePatch), Core/Heartbeat.cs, Core/WonderlandDebug.cs, Core/SafeMath.cs, Core/WonderlandConfig.cs's Bind helper block, Core/Compat/GameShape.cs, Shared/ServerSync.cs, six of the ten Core/Data utilities, AuditLog.cs and the whole DiscordNotify subsystem are portal-agnostic and transfer with a namespace rename — roughly 1,400 lines of already-live infrastructure Lite does not need to write. It should also copy Wonderland.csproj (net472, libs-Tools/1.0/server assemblies), NOT TortalPortal.csproj (net48, client assemblies).
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md's provenance note says it came from a 13-agent audit of the decompiles. It should also record that PortalLock (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/PAUSED/PortalLock/) is a prior, abandoned attempt at exactly the Group-1 portal-cap feature, and that its entire hook set (Player.*PlacePiece*, ZNetScene.Instantiate, ZNetScene.Destroy, Player.IsAdmin, ZDOID-keyed YAML, name-substring portal detection) is dead on a dedicated server. That negative result belongs in the Ruled Out section as the empirical counterpart to the Central Constraint.
- TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md's 'Every Portal in the Realm, Listed' entry does not mention that the whole-world portal enumeration AND its JSON export already exist and already run server-only in the full mod: PlacementPatch.GetAllPortals (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PlacementPatch.cs:195) and PortalExport (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PortalExport.cs:32, :75, writing barrkbot_portals.json atomically with per-creator counts, at_cap/over_cap flags and an online set). Effort for that item is near zero — it is a file copy, not a build.

## player-input-surfaces: what a dedicated Valheim 1.0.7 server can observe a vanilla client doing, and what it can show back, with zero client mod

The single decisive finding is that **the vanilla map ping is a free, always-delivered, coordinate-bearing player→server channel**: `Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick`/`OnMapDblClick` call `Chat.SendPing`, which invokes the routed RPC `"ChatMessage"` at `targetPeerID = 0` (Everybody) with **no permission check and no player-count dependency**, so the dedicated server receives the exact world Vector3 plus the sender's peer id and PlatformUserID every single time. That is a complete destination-selection UI on a stock client: open map → middle-click a spot → server picks the nearest portal. Ordinary chat text is *not* equivalent — `Chat.SendText`/`Talker.Say` target each *other* listed player individually, so with one player online nothing goes on the wire at all, and with 2+ players the packets only pass through the server as **relay traffic** (visible via a Harmony hook on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC`/`RouteRPC`, never via a registered handler). The second-tier input channels are all ZDO-poll based and rock solid: emotes (`s_emote`/`s_emoteID`), equipped items (`VisEquipment` writes `s_rightItem`/`s_leftItem`/`s_helmetItem`… into the character ZDO), item stands (`s_item` = prefab hash), sign text (`s_text`), portal tags (`s_tag`, max 10 chars from the client UI), chest contents (`s_items` blob), position/look-direction (`s_lookTarget`), and every piece built or destroyed (hook `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` + `ZDO.Deserialize`, read `s_creator`). Output back to a vanilla client is richer than expected: `"ShowMessage"` (MessageHud TopLeft/Center), the per-character `"Message"` RPC, `"RPC_DamageText"` (floating world text at any position, any string), `"RPC_TeleportPlayer"` **and** `Character.RPC_TeleportTo` (two independent, completely ungated server→client teleports), `"RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"` (a **named, saved map pin** at any position), a fabricated `"ChatMessage"` of type Shout or Ping (chat line + in-world text + a labelled animated map pin), `"LocationIcons"` (icon-only overlay), status effects, `"SpawnObject"` for VFX prefabs, and portal-tag/sign-text rewriting as persistent in-world text. The two hard walls: the server can never see a player's inventory (never networked — so no ore check is reproducible), and `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` strips server ZDO ownership near any player every 2s.

### Facts
- **[local-player-client]** The vanilla map ping is a broadcast routed RPC with NO permission gate and NO player-count dependency: Chat.SendPing sends "ChatMessage" to targetPeerID 0 (ZRoutedRpc.Everybody) carrying the clicked world position (x/z from the map click, y forced to the player's own y), type 3 (Talker.Type.Ping), the sender's UserInfo, and empty text. — `Chat.SendPing, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:42058-42068 (identical at assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:42058)` → THE destination-selection surface. A dedicated server receives an arbitrary player-chosen world coordinate from a 100% vanilla client, always, even with a single player online. Middle-click the map = 'send me here'.
- **[local-player-client]** A vanilla player triggers SendPing three ways, all in the stock map UI: middle-click on the large map (Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick), double-click on the map while the Ping pin type is selected (Minimap.OnMapDblClick), and gamepad JoyButtonX while the large map is open (Minimap.UpdateMap, pings the view centre). — `Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:58580-58584; Minimap.OnMapDblClick :58538-58548; Minimap.UpdateMap :57058-57062` → No keybind config, no client mod, no chat syntax to teach. Mouse and gamepad both covered. Precision is whatever the map zoom allows.
- **[dedicated-server]** ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC only puts a packet on the wire when targetPeerID != m_id; a message addressed to the sender's own id is handled purely locally. — `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83576-83592 (the `if (targetPeerID == m_id || targetPeerID == 0L) HandleRoutedRPC` / `if (targetPeerID != m_id) RouteRPC` pair)` → This is the rule that kills chat as a control channel and saves the ping channel. Self-addressed = invisible to the server; 0 = always visible; other-peer = relayed through the server but not locally handled.
- **[local-player-client]** Chat.SendText (Shout) and Talker.Say (Normal/Whisper) both route through Chat.CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync, which sends ONE RPC to the sender's own UserID plus one to each OTHER listed player's characterID.UserID — never to the server as a distinct target. Only the `PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider == null` branch collapses to a single broadcast at targetPeerID 0. — `Chat.SendText assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41975-41994; Chat.CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync :41996-42043; Talker.Say :18942-18950` → With exactly one player online, chat text produces ZERO network traffic and the server is blind. With 2+ players it only appears as relay traffic. A registered server-side "ChatMessage" handler will NOT fire for chat text on Steam. Confirms and sharpens Wonderland's EmoteSignals.cs warning.
- **[dedicated-server]** The dedicated server relays every routed RPC it does not handle locally: ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC deserializes the package, calls HandleRoutedRPC only when m_targetPeerID is the server or 0, and then calls RouteRPC for anything not addressed to itself. — `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83637-83648; ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC :83594-83635` → A Harmony prefix on RPC_RoutedRPC (or on the private RouteRPC(RoutedRPCData)) sees 100% of peer-to-peer traffic, including whispers, shouts, RPC_SetTag, ward toggles, door use — everything. This is the universal observation hook and needs no RPC-name registration.
- **[dedicated-server]** ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC receives a fully deserialized RoutedRPCData (m_senderPeerID, m_targetZDO, m_methodHash, m_parameters as a ZPackage positioned at 0) and is called for every RPC addressed to the server or to Everybody, regardless of whether any handler is registered. — `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83650-83668; RoutedRPCData.Deserialize :83478-83486` → Collision-free alternative to ZRoutedRpc.Register for capturing pings: Harmony-prefix HandleRoutedRPC, snapshot data.m_parameters.GetPos(), read, then SetPos back so vanilla's own dispatch still works.
- **[dedicated-server]** ZDOID.UserID resolves to the ZDOMan session id of the client that minted the ZDO, and ZNet.GetUID() == ZDOMan.GetSessionID() == the value a peer reports as ZNetPeer.m_uid. — `ZDOID.UserID assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75830; ZDOMan.m_sessionID :76035; ZDOMan.GetSessionID :77362; ZNet.GetUID :80866` → A chat/ping RPC's `sender` argument and a character ZDO's m_uid.UserID are the same number as ZNetPeer.m_uid, so a received ping maps directly to a ZNetPeer and therefore to a ConnectedCharacter.
- **[zdo-owning-client]** Player emotes are pure ZDO writes on the character ZDO: Player.StartEmote sets s_emote (string), bumps s_emoteID (int), and sets s_emoteOneshot; StopEmote bumps the counter with an empty name. There are 25 vanilla emotes (Emotes enum), all reachable from the emote wheel or by typing /<emote> in chat. — `Player.StartEmote assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15585-15598; Player.StopEmote :15600-15608; Emote.DoEmote :6206-6214; enum Emotes :6216-6246` → A 25-value discrete selector that always reaches the server regardless of player count, exactly as Wonderland/Core/Data/EmoteSignals.cs polls it. Combine with the equipped-item channel below for a 2-axis menu.
- **[zdo-owning-client]** VisEquipment mirrors every visible equipped item into the character's own ZDO as a prefab hash: s_rightItem, s_leftItem (+Variant/+Quality), s_chestItem, s_legItem, s_helmetItem, s_shoulderItem (+Variant/+Quality), s_utilityItem, s_beardItem, s_hairItem, plus s_modelIndex/s_skinColor/s_hairColor. — `VisEquipment assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:20120; ZDO writes at :20569-20571, :20590-20591, :20632, :20644, :20656, :20670-20672, :20684, :20696, :20708` → 'Hold item X' is a fully server-readable selector on a vanilla client. Equipping a specific weapon/cape/utility + emoting gives a large, discoverable command space with zero UI work.
- **[zdo-owning-client]** An ItemStand stores what is mounted on it as plain ZDO ints: ZDOVars.s_item (prefab stable hash), s_variant, s_quality, s_type (orientation). — `ItemStand assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:131475; ZDO writes at :131795 (s_item = stableHashCode), :131570/:131600 region; field reads at :131649-131651` → An item stand is a physical radio button the server can read with one ZDO poll. A row of stands next to a portal is a zero-mod destination picker with an in-world, self-documenting UI.
- **[zdo-owning-client]** A Sign's text is written straight into its own ZDO by the local client — Sign.SetText calls m_nview.ClaimOwnership() then zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_text, text) plus s_author/s_authorDisplayName. There is NO Sign RPC; Sign.Awake registers none. — `Sign.SetText assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:141913-141928; Sign.Awake :141772-141781; Sign.UpdateText :141835-141865 (InvokeRepeating every 2s, redraw gated on ZDO DataRevision)` → Corrects the assignment's premise of a `Sign.RPC_SetText`: sign text is observed by polling s_text, not by intercepting an RPC. It is also a bidirectional surface — the server can rewrite s_text and every client repaints within 2s. Default m_characterLimit is 50.
- **[zdo-owning-client]** A portal tag is set by TeleportWorld.SetText -> m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", tag, authorId), which targets the ZDO's current OWNER; the handler applies only if m_nview.IsOwner(), and writes s_tag + s_tagauthor after clearing the portal's connection. — `TeleportWorld.SetText assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143575-143581; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag :143583-143598; ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string,...) :82855-82858` → The server can observe retags either by polling s_tag on ZDOMan.GetPortalList() or by watching relayed RPC_SetTag traffic. CRITICAL: if the SERVER owns a portal ZDO, the RPC routes to the server, ZNetScene.FindInstance returns null (no GameObject), and the tag change is silently dropped — server ownership of a portal breaks vanilla retagging.
- **[local-player-client]** The client's portal-tag text box is hard-capped at 10 characters: TeleportWorld.Interact calls TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10), and TextInput.Show assigns that straight to m_inputField.characterLimit. — `TeleportWorld.Interact assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143470-143483; TextInput.RequestText :61509-61513; TextInput.Show :61515-61522` → A tag-as-command-line gets 10 characters, period. Enough for 'go:mine' or a short destination name, not for structured syntax. Also: the dialog pre-fills with the existing tag, so a long server-written tag risks being clamped and saved back truncated if the player opens the dialog.
- **[zdo-owning-client]** Container contents live in the container's own ZDO as a single serialized Inventory blob under ZDOVars.s_items, written by Container.Save() whenever the owning client's inventory changes, with ZDOVars.s_inUse flagging an open UI. — `Container.Save assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:122294-122301; Container.Load :122303-122322; UpdateUseVisual (s_inUse) :121990-122000` → 'Put item X in chest Y' is a fully server-readable input, exactly as Wonderland/Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs already implements (Load/Save/IsBusy). Slower and clunkier than a ping but unambiguous, and it is the only channel that can also charge a toll.
- **[dedicated-server]** Player character inventories are NEVER in any ZDO. Character/Humanoid/Player write only s_health, s_maxHealth, s_stamina, s_eitr, s_dead, s_pvp, s_stealth, s_inBed, s_playerName, s_playerID, s_noise, s_lookTarget, s_bodyVelocity, s_emote*, s_crowned, s_adrenaline, s_dodgeinv, s_weaponLoaded, s_isBlockingHash, s_wakeup, s_baseValue, s_cheated to their ZDO. — `exhaustive scan of `Set(ZDOVars.s_*)` inside Character :178-6796, Humanoid :6796-9414 and Player :9414-16500 of assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs; ZdoInventoryIO.cs documents the same conclusion` → The server cannot reproduce TeleportWorld's ore/metal check under any circumstances, and cannot charge a player's own inventory. Any server-driven teleport therefore bypasses the item restriction entirely.

- `ZNet.instance.GetPeers() : List<ZNetPeer>  — ZNetPeer.m_uid, m_characterID (ZDOID), m_playerID, m_playerName, m_refPos, m_publicRefPos, m_socket.GetHostName(), m_serverSyncedPlayerData; ZNet.instance.GetPeer(long uid); ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(string hostName)` @ ZNetPeer fields :78778-78805; ZNet.GetPeers :81630-81633; ZNet.GetPeer :80492; ZNet.IsAdmin :81811-81814 — serverCallable=True; Peer -> character ZDO resolution for every output RPC above. Wonderland/Core/Data/ConnectedCharacters.cs already packages this, including the IsReady()/m_characterID.IsNone() guards.
- `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey(string name) / SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys key) / SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys key, float value) / RemoveGlobalKey / GetGlobalKey` @ ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey :115933-115947; RPC_SetGlobalKey (server handler, re-broadcasts via SendGlobalKeys(0L)) :116022-116029 — serverCallable=True; Works end-to-end from the server: InvokeRoutedRPC targets GetServerPeerID() == the server's own id, handled locally, then broadcast. Client-honored gating only (NoPortals, NoBossPortals, TeleportAll).
- `Harmony postfix on ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int) [private] + postfix on ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` @ ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID,Vector3,int) :76684-76692; pattern implemented in Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43-70 — serverCallable=True; The only reliable 'a client just created an object' hook. prefabHash == 0 distinguishes the network-receive path; the prefab is only known after Deserialize. Use for build-a-piece / drop-an-item input detection.

### Gotchas
- Chat text is NOT a server input. With exactly one player online, Chat.SendText/Talker.Say produce literally zero packets (targetPeerID == the sender's own id, and ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC only routes when targetPeerID != m_id, :83576-83592). Any design that depends on 'player says a keyword' is broken for a solo player and only works as relay sniffing otherwise.
- Slash commands are dead. Chat.InputText strips the '/' and hands the rest to Terminal.TryRunCommand with silentFail:true (:41947-41955, :45734-45758). An unknown command name does nothing and prints nothing; only commands already compiled into the client AND flagged RemoteCommand reach the server, and ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand then rejects non-admins (:81879-81889).
- Claiming server ownership of a portal ZDO silently breaks vanilla retagging. TeleportWorld.SetText invokes RPC_SetTag at the ZDO's owner (:143575-143581, ZNetView.InvokeRPC :82855-82858); if that owner is the dedicated server, ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC looks up ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zdo), gets null (no GameObject exists server-side), and drops the RPC with no error (:83650-83668, :82229-82236).
- Server ZDO ownership is revoked automatically. ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS runs every 2s; because the server's reference position is pinned at (1e6,0,1e6) (Game.FixedUpdate :100465), any server-owned persistent ZDO inside a player's active area fails IsInPeerActiveArea and is handed to that player (:76901-76927). Write-then-release, and re-apply on a tick; never assume a held claim.
- The server can never see a player's inventory. No character ZDO carries s_items; the exhaustive Character/Humanoid/Player ZDO-write scan yields only vitals, identity, emote and pose fields. TeleportWorld's ore/metal restriction is therefore unreproducible server-side, and a server-issued teleport (RPC_TeleportPlayer / RPC_TeleportTo) bypasses it entirely — you will let players portal with iron and there is no way to detect it.
- Portal tags are capped at 10 characters by the client's text widget (TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10) :143481 -> m_inputField.characterLimit :61519). Worse, TextInput.Show pre-fills the field with the existing tag — if the server has written a longer tag for display, a player opening the dialog may save back a truncated version.
- Portal tags are not rich-text capable in hover: TeleportWorld.GetHoverText runs the tag through .RemoveRichTextTags() (:143458, assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700). And vanilla shows portal tags NOWHERE on the map — only on hover.
- Chat text has '<' and '>' replaced with spaces in Chat.OnNewChatMessage (:41795-41796), so fabricated chat output cannot use colour or size markup either.
- A fabricated Shout/Ping ChatMessage produces its map pin only if Chat.AddInworldText runs, which is skipped when Minimap.m_mode == MapMode.None AND the position is more than m_nomapPingDistance (50f) from the viewer (:41808, :56396). Normal play has the small minimap up (m_mode == Small), so this only bites in nomap worlds or with the HUD hidden.
- Registering a routed-RPC name the dedicated server already has throws. ZRoutedRpc.Register uses Dictionary.Add (:83680-83716). Vanilla code at :80258-80281 calls MessageHud.instance.MessageAll UNGUARDED under IsDedicated(), and ZNet.InternalCommand calls Console.instance.TryRunCommand ungated (:81894) — both imply GUI singletons may exist headless. Probe ZRoutedRpc.instance's private m_functions before Register, or patch HandleRoutedRPC instead.
- MapTable-based pin delivery is destructive: Minimap.AddSharedMapData marks every pin whose m_ownerID is non-zero and not the reader's own for deletion, keeping only those re-listed in the incoming blob (:58824-58875). A crafted blob that omits a player's shared pins wipes them. It also throws/rejects unless the explored bool array length exactly matches the client's Minimap.m_textureSize^2.
- Minimap.AddPin forces any type outside [Icon0, m_visibleIconTypes.Length) to Icon3 (:58375-58382), and DiscoverLocation refuses to add a pin if one with the same name+type already sits within 1m (HaveSimilarPin :58363-58374) — repeated server pushes of the same pin are silently no-ops.
- Player.TeleportTo refuses while IsTeleporting() or while m_teleportCooldown < 2f (:15309-15316), returning false with no message on either side. Rapid server-issued teleports vanish without a trace.
- ZNetScene 'SpawnObject' broadcast-instantiates on every recipient: using it with a ZNetView prefab creates one duplicate ZDO per client (:82355-82366). VFX/SFX prefabs only.
- Server->client ZDO writes only reach a client whose simulation area covers that ZDO (ZDOMan.CreateSyncList :77212-77241). Rewriting a far portal's tag as a message to a player does nothing until they walk there, unless you call ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerUid, zdoid).
- ZNet.RemotePrint output lands in the client's Console buffer (:81650-81656), which most players never open — treat it as an admin-only channel, not player feedback.
- Map pings are public: Chat.SendPing broadcasts to targetPeerID 0, so every other online player sees the ping marker and its map pin. A ping-driven destination picker is a visible, shared gesture, and is trivially spammable — debounce per player and rate-limit before acting on it.

### Open questions
- Does a dedicated server instantiate the GUI hierarchy? Specifically: are Chat.instance, MessageHud.instance, Minimap.instance, DamageText.instance, Console.instance null or non-null? The decompile is contradictory — Game.UpdateSaving guards with `(bool)MessageHud.instance` (:100474) while ZNet.LowDiskLeftInformer calls MessageHud.instance.MessageAll unguarded under IsDedicated() (:80258, :80280) and ZNet.InternalCommand calls Console.instance.TryRunCommand unguarded (:81894). IN-GAME CHECK: at BepInEx plugin Awake+30s on the dedicated server, log the null-ness of all five singletons, AND dump the key set of ZRoutedRpc.instance's private m_functions (AccessTools.Field(typeof(ZRoutedRpc),"m_functions")) checking for "ChatMessage".GetStableHashCode() and "ShowMessage".GetStableHashCode(). This decides Register-vs-Harmony for the ping hook.
- Is PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider null on a Steam client? It is implemented in the platform assemblies, which are not in this decompile set. If it IS null, Chat.SendText collapses to a single broadcast at targetPeerID 0 (:42002-42005) and ordinary chat text becomes a first-class server input even solo. IN-GAME CHECK: register/patch a server-side "ChatMessage" handler, have a SOLO player type a plain sentence and a /s shout, and see whether the handler fires.
- Does the Player prefab have CharacterAnimEvent.m_headRotation enabled and m_head assigned? Both are serialized Inspector fields gating the ZDOVars.s_lookTarget write (:5043). IN-GAME CHECK: poll s_lookTarget on a connected character ZDO for 10s while the player spins in place; a changing non-zero Vector3 confirms the look-direction channel.
- What is Minimap.m_textureSize on the shipped Minimap prefab? The C# default is 256 (:56287) but the Inspector may override it, and Minimap.GetSharedMapData/AddSharedMapData require an exploration bool array of exactly m_textureSize^2 (:58739-58748, :58777-58795). Without this number a server-crafted MapTable blob cannot be built. IN-GAME CHECK: on a client, log Minimap.instance.m_textureSize and Minimap.instance.m_explored.Length.
- What location-icon names exist in the Minimap prefab's compiled m_locationIcons sprite list (Minimap.GetLocationIcon :58363-58374)? These are Unity asset entries, invisible to the decompile, and they bound what the "LocationIcons" server-push overlay can render. IN-GAME CHECK: on a client, enumerate Minimap.instance.m_locationIcons and log every m_name.
- Is the emote list in the emote wheel the full 25-value Emotes enum on every platform/input device, or is the wheel a subset with the rest reachable only by typing /<emote>? Affects how large a practical emote-based command alphabet is. IN-GAME CHECK: open the emote wheel on a vanilla client and count entries against the enum at :6216-6246.
- Does GuiInputField (Valheim's InputField subclass) clamp a programmatically assigned .text to characterLimit? TextInput.Show assigns m_inputField.text = existingTag AFTER setting characterLimit = 10 (:61519-61520). If it clamps, any server-written portal tag longer than 10 chars gets silently truncated the moment a player opens the tag dialog and saves. IN-GAME CHECK: server-write a 20-char tag, then open and confirm the dialog on a vanilla client and re-read s_tag.
- Does the dedicated server's ZNetScene ever instantiate a GameObject for a ZDO, or is FindInstance always null? The RPC_SetTag drop-on-server-ownership gotcha depends on this being always-null. IN-GAME CHECK: log ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances() (:82334) on a running dedicated server with players online.

### Corrections to the existing spec
- Group 3 says 'Chat-command parsing is unreliable server-side — an emote or item-interaction trigger is the safer entry point, not a slash command.' That is right about slash commands but MISSES the strongest channel in the game: the vanilla MAP PING. Chat.SendPing invokes "ChatMessage" at targetPeerID 0 with no permission check and no player-count dependency (:42058-42068), delivering an arbitrary player-chosen world coordinate to the dedicated server. Middle-click the map (or double-click with the Ping pin selected, or gamepad JoyButtonX) is a complete, precise, zero-mod destination picker. Self-service warps and player-driven portal retargeting are therefore genuinely player-driven, not admin-only.
- The spec is silent on WHY chat text fails. The reason is not 'parsing': Chat.SendText and Talker.Say address one RPC per OTHER listed player plus one to the sender (:41996-42043), so a solo player generates no packets at all, and multi-player chat only appears as relay traffic visible through a ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC patch — never through a registered handler. Worth stating precisely, because the relay path IS usable when 2+ players are online.
- The assignment brief (and by implication the spec's mental model) names `Sign.RPC_SetText` and `ZDOVars.s_text` as an RPC surface. In 1.0.7 there is NO Sign RPC at all — Sign.Awake registers none and Sign.SetText does ClaimOwnership + zdo.Set(s_text, ...) directly (:141772-141781, :141913-141928). Sign text is a POLLED ZDO field in both directions, and it is also a server-writable in-world display that repaints on every client within 2s (Sign.UpdateText InvokeRepeating 2f).
- Group 1's 'Direct tag write/rename bypassing the RPC and the 10-character text-entry UI entirely' is correct but incomplete: because RPC_SetTag is delivered to the portal ZDO's OWNER and the dedicated server has no TeleportWorld GameObject, a mod that takes server ownership of a portal ZDO makes vanilla retagging silently fail (ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC -> ZNetScene.FindInstance == null, :83660-83667). This directly contradicts Group 1's last bullet, 'Proactive server ownership claim on placement — makes RPC interception more reliable' — it does the opposite for RPC_SetTag. Intercept via ZDO polling or a RPC_RoutedRPC relay patch instead, and never hold portal ownership.
- Group 1's ownership-claim bullet also underestimates ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS: any server-owned persistent ZDO inside a player's active area is reassigned to that player every 2 seconds (:76871-76927), because the server's own reference position is pinned at (1e6,0,1e6). A 'proactive claim' cannot be held; it is only ever a momentary write window.
- The Ruled Out entry 'no server-pushed map pins' is not stated in the spec, but the spec's 'Every Portal in the Realm, Listed' bullet asserts an in-game player-facing listing is 'unavoidably client work'. That is too strong. Four server-only map surfaces exist on a vanilla client: (a) "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse" -> Minimap.DiscoverLocation adds a NAMED, SAVED pin of any PinType at any position and can center the player's map (:100068, :100822-100829, :58334-58360); (b) a fabricated Shout/Ping "ChatMessage" gives a 5s labelled animated pin at any position (:41775-41816, :57591-57650); (c) "LocationIcons" rewrites the client's whole location-icon overlay (:113595-113607); (d) MapTable's s_data blob delivers a full named pin set to any player who reads a cartography table (:133831-133865, :58797-58875). An in-game, per-player portal map is achievable without a client mod — just not as a live interactive picker window.
- Group 5's toll bullet says 'debit a nearby server-visible container, never the traveling player's own inventory (which is never networked to the server at all)'. Correct, and the reason is now pinned exactly: an exhaustive scan of every `Set(ZDOVars.s_*)` in Character/Humanoid/Player shows no s_items on any character ZDO; the only player-carried thing the server CAN see is what is visibly equipped, via VisEquipment's s_rightItem/s_leftItem/s_helmetItem/s_chestItem/s_legItem/s_shoulderItem/s_utilityItem writes into the character ZDO (:20569-20708). That is also a usable player-input alphabet the spec does not mention.
- Group 3's 'bypassing Chat.instance entirely' advice is right, and there is a second, independent teleport RPC the spec already names but does not distinguish operationally: "RPC_TeleportPlayer" needs only the peer uid (Chat-registered, global, :41627/:41962) while Character's "RPC_TeleportTo" is per-character-ZDO (:886/:4126). Both are completely ungated on the client — no item check, no boss check, no NoPortals check — and both no-op silently inside the 2s cooldown.
